statements.evidence: 10.13.28-33 (gāvo vatsān upavrajam ... apāyayan; jātānurāgā gata-manyavo 'rbhakān; tokāśleṣa-sunirvṛtāḥ)

statements.evidence: 10.13.41: ita ete 'tra kutratyā man-māyā-mohitetare

statements.claim: All the cowherd boys appeared as four-armed forms holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, marked with shrivatsa, armlets and bracelets, garlanded in fresh tulsi, smiling like moonlight with sidelong glances
statements.evidence: 10.13.45-49 (catur-bhujāḥ śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-rājīva-pāṇayaḥ; śrīvatsāṅgada-do-ratna-kambu-kaṅkaṇa-pāṇayaḥ; tulasī-nava-dāmabhiḥ; candrikā-viśada-smeraiḥ sāruṇāpāṅga-vīkṣitaiḥ)

statements.claim: Around them stood all the worlds and powers, from the first gods down to the last blade of grass, each in its own form
statements.evidence: 10.13.50-53 (ātmādi-stamba-paryantair mūrtimadbhiś carācaraiḥ; satya-jñānānantānanda-mātraika-rasa-mūrtayaḥ)

statements.claim: The eleven senses of Brahma froze, and Krishna drew the curtain of maya over his sight; he rose as one waking from the dead
statements.evidence: 10.13.55-57 (stimitaikādaśendriyaḥ; cacchādājo jñātvā ... javanikām; kaḥ paretavad utthitaḥ)

statements.claim: He saw the ordinary world with men and animals sitting together without natural enmity, and a small boy with a morsel of food searching for his friends as before
statements.evidence: 10.13.58-60 (naisarga-durvairāḥ sahāsan nṛ-mṛgādayaḥ; ekaṃ sa-pāṇi-kavalaṃ ... vicinvad)

statements.claim: Brahma descended from his swan, cast himself down like a golden rod, touched Krishna's feet with the tips of his four crowns and bathed them with tears
statements.evidence: 10.13.61 (nija-dhoraṇato 'vatīrya; pṛthvyāṃ vapuḥ kanaka-daṇḍam ivābhipātya; spṛṣṭvā catur-mukuṭa-koṭibhir aṅghri-yugmaṃ; mud-aśru-sujalair akṛtābhiṣekam)

statements.claim: Krishna's body is made of his own will, not of matter
statements.evidence: 10.14.1: svecchā-mayasya na tu bhūta-mayasya

statements.claim: Those who abandon the effort to know and simply bow and listen live by the truth; those who strive only for knowledge labour like threshers of empty husks
statements.evidence: 10.14.2-3 (jñāne prayāsam udapāsya namanta eva ...; kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye ... sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām)

statements.claim: Even the purest-hearted and great seers cannot measure his greatness
statements.evidence: 10.14.5-6 (mahimāguṇasya te viboddhum arhaty amalāntar-ātmabhiḥ; guṇān vimātuṃ ... ka īśire)

statements.claim: 'I was born of passion and in my ignorance thought myself a lord apart from you; forgive me'
statements.evidence: 10.14.8-9 (rajo-bhuvo hy ajānatas tvat-pṛthag-īśa-māninaḥ; ataḥ kṣamasvācyuta)

statements.claim: 'Where am I, a body of seven hand-spans in this egg of the universe, and where is your greatness, in the pores of whose skin whole worlds course?'
statements.evidence: 10.14.10 (kvāhaṃ ... sapta-vitasti-kāyaḥ; kvedṛg-vidhāvigaṇitāṇḍa-parāṇu-caryā-vātādhva-roma-vivarasya ca te mahitvam)

statements.claim: 'First you were one, then all the cowherd boys and calves, then an endless company of four-armed forms, then as many universes — and what remained was the one, the unlimited'
statements.evidence: 10.14.17 (eko 'si prathamaṃ tato vraja-suhṛd-vatsāḥ samastā api; tāvanto 'si catur-bhujās ...; tāvanty eva jaganty abhūs tad amitaṃ brahmādvayaṃ śiṣyate)

statements.claim: 'This whole world is as unreal as a dream and full of sorrow, yet through your maya it shines as if real, resting on you alone'
statements.evidence: 10.14.21 (svapnābham asta-dhiṣaṇaṃ puru-duḥkha-duḥkham; tvayy eva ... māyāta udyad api yat sad ivāvabhāti)

statements.claim: 'You are Narayana, the Self of every being and the witness of every world; from your navel all this rose again when the worlds had dissolved into water'
statements.evidence: 10.14.12-13 (jagat-trayāntodadhi-samplavode nārāyaṇasyodara-nābhi-nālāt; nārāyaṇas tvaṃ ... ātmāsy adhīśākhila-loka-sākṣī)

statements.claim: The women of Vraja who fed him at the breast drank nectar; the dust of his feet is sought by the Vedas
statements.evidence: 10.14.30-33 (stanyāmṛtaṃ pītam atīva te mudā; yat-pada-rajaḥ śruti-mṛgyam eva)

statements.claim: 'Give me leave, Krishna; you know everything there is to know'
statements.evidence: 10.14.38: anujānīhi māṃ kṛṣṇa sarvaṃ tvaṃ vetsi sarva-dṛk

statements.claim: Brahma circumambulated Krishna three times, bowed, and departed for his own realm
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt summary ('walking three times around him and bowing, departs for his own realm') and 10.14.41 (tato 'nujñāpya bhagavān sva-bhuvaṃ prāg avasthitān)

statements.claim: After giving Brahma leave, Krishna returned the boys and calves to the sandbank as though nothing had happened
statements.evidence: 10.14.41-42 and pack excerpt summary ('Krishna brings the boys and calves back to the sandbank as though nothing had happened')

statements.claim: A full year had passed, but the boys, their minds covered by maya, remembered nothing of it
statements.evidence: 10.14.42-43 (ekasminn api yāte 'bde; kiṃ kiṃ na vismarantīha māyā-mohita-cetasaḥ)

statements.claim: The boys welcomed Krishna with 'Welcome back! You returned quickly!'
statements.evidence: 10.14.44: ūcuś ca suhṛdaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ sv-āgataṃ te 'ti-raṃhasā

statements.claim: Krishna smiled and sat down and ate with the boys, finishing the meal they had left
statements.evidence: 10.14.45: tato hasan hṛṣīkeśo 'bhyavahṛtya sahārbhakaiḥ

statements.claim: Krishna entered the cow-pen decked in peacock feathers, flowers and forest earth-colours, his flute sounding, the boys singing his praises, the gopis' eyes gladdened
statements.evidence: 10.14.46 (barha-prasūna-vana-dhātu-vicitritāṅgaḥ; proddāma-veṇu-dala-śṛṅga-ravotsavāḍhyaḥ; anuga-gīta-pavitra-kīrtir; gopī-dṛg-utsava-dṛśiḥ)

statements.claim: The boys told how the son of Yashoda and Nanda had slain a great serpent that very day, carrying its dried skin as proof
statements.evidence: 10.14.47 (adyānena mahā-vyālo yaśodā-nanda-sūnunā), pack excerpt summary ('carrying the python's dried skin as a trophy'), and 10.12.35 (the dried python skin in Vrindavan)

statements.claim: The palm grove (talavana) let fall fruit in such abundance it kept falling and lay fallen, and no one had ever eaten any of it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.21 'phalāni tatra bhūrīṇi patanti patitāni ca' (fruit falling and fallen) and 10.15.24 'abhukta-pūrvāṇi phalāni' (fruit never before eaten).

statements.claim: The grove belonged to the demon Dhenuka, in donkey form, with his fierce kin; he had made men his food and people were afraid and kept their distance.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.22-23 'khara-rūpa-dhṛk' (ass-form), 'kṛta-narāhārād bhītair nṛbhir' (men afraid of him who made men his food); kin mentioned in the episode's excerpt and 10.15.35.

statements.claim: The boys cried to Krishna and Balarama: 'Rama! Rama, mighty-armed! Krishna, destroyer of the wicked!' and begged 'Give us that fruit.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.20 'rāma rāma mahā-bāho kṛṣṇa duṣṭa-nibarhaṇa' and 10.15.25 'prayaccha tāni naḥ kṛṣṇa'.

statements.claim: The boys' minds were greedy with the fragrance, and Krishna, hearing his friends, wished only to please them.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.25 'gandha-lobhita-cetasām' and 10.15.26 'suhṛd-vacaḥ śrutvā suhṛt-priya-cikīrṣayā'.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama set out for the palm grove with the boys following.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (10.15.20-26): the boys ask to be given the fruit; next event 10.15.27 has Balarama entering the grove (see DKS_0054 pack).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: afternoon warmth, the wind carrying the scent, the boys stopping their play.
statements.evidence: Generic scene-setting consistent with the forest setting of BP 10.15; no sourceable fact asserted.

DKS_0053.notes: All factual claims map to BP 10.15.20-26; the 'grown men grazed elsewhere' detail is a fair inference from bhītair nṛbhir.

statements.claim: Balarama went to the palm trees and shook them so the ripe fruit came down in a shower.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.27 'balaḥ praviśya bāhubhyāṃ tālān samparikampayan' (Balarama entered and shook the palms with his arms); VP 5.8: 'Sankarshańa and Krishńa shook the trees, and brought down the fruit.'

statements.claim: In that grove dwelt the fierce demon Dhenuka, who fed on the flesh of deer.
statements.evidence: VP 5.8: 'dwelt the fierce demon Dhenuka, feeding upon the flesh of deer' (BP 10.15.23 calls him kṛta-narāhāra, 'made men his food'; the story follows VP here, both in the pack).

statements.claim: Hearing the falling fruit, Dhenuka rushed in a great passion in his donkey form and kicked Balarama with his hind legs.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.28-29: the asura-ass heard the sound of falling fruit, came speedily and struck Balarama with both feet; VP 5.8: 'began to kick Ráma on the breast with his hinder heels.'

statements.claim: Balarama caught him by the hind legs, whirled him with a single hand until he expired, and dashed him against a great palm tree.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.31-32 'sa taṃ gṛhītvā prapador bhrāmayitvaika-pāṇinā' (seizing his hind feet, whirling with one hand) and 'tenāhato mahā-tālo' (struck against the great palm); VP 5.8 likewise.

statements.claim: The palm trembled from the blow and shook down fruit like rain poured by the wind; Dhenuka fell lifeless.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.32 'vepamāno bṛhac-chirāḥ' (trembling, huge-headed); VP 5.8: 'struck down abundance of fruit, like rain drops poured upon earth by the wind.'

statements.claim: It was no wonder, the verses say, for the slayer is the infinite Lord of all the worlds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.34 'naitac citraṃ bhagavati hy anante jagad-īśvare' (this is not wonderful in the Blessed infinite Lord of the worlds).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the brothers' easy rhythm, the boys' laughter, the grove growing quiet.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing; no sourceable fact asserted.

DKS_0054.notes: Tradition note re BP-vs-VP attribution (joint vs Rama alone) is correctly reflected; story keeps Balarama as shaker and slayer, consistent with both pack sources.

statements.claim: Dhenuka's kin, the other ass-demons, came rushing to avenge him and charged at Krishna and Balarama.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.35-36 'jñātayo dhenukasya ye... āpatataḥ' (the kinsmen of Dhenuka came rushing).

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama, as if at play, flung the charging donkeys lifeless among the palm trees, one after another.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.36 'kṛṣṇo rāmaś ca līlayā' (as if in play); the grove strewn with lifeless demon bodies (10.15.37).

statements.claim: The gods and the wise heard of the great deed and rejoiced.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.38 'tayos tat su-mahat karma niśamya vibudhādayaḥ' (the gods/wise hearing that great deed).

statements.claim: The people, their fear gone, came and ate the palm fruit, and the cattle grazed where they had never before dared.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.39 'manuṣyā gata-sādhvasāḥ' (men without fear ate the palm fruit); beasts freely enjoying the grove appears in the pack's own index summary, and VP 5.8 (in the series) states the cattle grazed where they never before ventured.

statements.claim: Krishna stood with eyes like lotus petals, and his name and deeds were auspicious to hear.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.40 'kṛṣṇaḥ kamala-patrākṣaḥ puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ' (lotus-eyed Krishna, whose name and praise are auspicious).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: hooves drumming, the grove quiet again, the terror gone.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting around the supported events.

statements.claim: At night a blazing forest fire rose from the dry woods and surrounded Vraja on every side.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.20 'śuci-vanodbhūto dāvāgniḥ sarvato vrajam' (forest fire born of the dry forest, around all of Vraja); night setting in the pack's index title/summary.

statements.claim: The people woke, scorched and terrified, with no way out.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.21 'sambhrāntā dahyamānā vrajaukasaḥ' (bewildered Vraja-dwellers, being burned).

statements.claim: They cried 'Krishna! Krishna! O greatly fortunate one! O Rama of boundless power!' and called the fire one no one can cross, like the fire that will end all things, begging Krishna to save his own people and friends.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.22-23 'kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-bhaga he rāmāmita-vikrama / su-dustarān naḥ svān pāhi kālāgneḥ suhṛdaḥ prabho' (O greatly fortunate Krishna, O Rama of boundless prowess, save your own friends from the all-destroying kālāgni).

statements.claim: The Lord of the world looked on his people's distress and drank up the whole fire.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.24 'sva-jana-vaiklavyaṃ nirīkṣya jagad-īśvaraḥ' (the Lord of the world seeing his people's distress); pack excerpt: 'drinks the whole fire into himself.'

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the trusting sleep, smoke rising thick, the silence after the roar.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing around the supported events.

statements.claim: While Krishna and Balarama tended the herd with the cowherds, a demon named Pralamba came in the shape of a cowherd to seize the boys and destroy the two brothers.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.16 (Rama and Krishna tending cattle with the cowherds); pack excerpt: 'Pralamba, a demon in cowherd's form, enters the boys' games' intent on seizing the boys; Harivamsha 1.64 (series pack): came with a view to kill them.

statements.claim: The demon wore wild flowers and the easy manner of a milk-boy, casting dreadful looks at the brothers while the other boys took him for a friend.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.64: 'adorned with wild flowers', 'assumed the guise of a milk-man... cast his dreadful looks at Krishna and Rohini's son'; BP 10.18.17-18 context.

statements.claim: Krishna knew what he was; the all-seeing Lord welcomed his friendship and resolved his destruction.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.17 'vidvān api dāśārho bhagavān sarva-darśanaḥ' (though knowing, the Blessed Lord, seer of all); pack excerpt: 'Krishna, who knows all, welcomes his friendship while resolving his destruction.'

statements.claim: Krishna, who knew every game, proposed the riding game of carrying one another on their shoulders and racing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.18 'upāhūya gopālān kṛṣṇaḥ prāha vihāra-vit' (calling the cowherds, Krishna, knower of games, spoke); game details follow in 10.18.19-23 (see DKS_0058 pack).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the stranger appearing at the edge of play, the boys' games and races.
statements.evidence: Generic scene-setting; games of running/leaping/wrestling are standard connective description.

DKS_0057.notes: Pralamba's motive and disguise details draw on the Harivamsha passage carried in the adjacent story's pack; consistent with the episode's excerpt.

statements.claim: In the riding game, when Sridama and the other strong boys stood on Balarama's side, even Krishna was defeated and carried Sridama.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.22-23 'śrīdāma-vṛṣabhādayaḥ... uvāha kṛṣṇo bhagavān śrīdāmānaṃ parājitaḥ' (Krishna, defeated, carried Sridama); the loser-carries-winner rule in Harivamsha 1.64 ('carrying on their shoulders the victorious, those who were vanquished').

statements.claim: Pralamba chose to carry Balarama, having concluded Krishna was beyond his reach and the elder brother the one to take.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.24 'aviṣahyaṃ manyamānaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ dānava-puṅgavaḥ' (the foremost of demons, deeming Krishna unbearable); Harivamsha 1.64: 'considering Krishna... irrepressible he gave him up and made up his mind for destroying Baladeva.'

statements.claim: Pralamba carried Balarama away, not toward the Bhandira tree but in the opposite direction, and grew into his true demonic form — tall as a tree, clad in gold and ornaments, eyes like chariot wheels, a crown on his head, the earth sinking under his feet.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.64: 'proceeded quickly in an opposite direction', 'huge as the Bhandiraka fig-tree', 'eyes like unto the wheels of a car', 'a head adorned with a sun-like coronet', 'the earth sank under the weight of his feet'; BP 10.18.25-26: 'puraṭa-paricchadaḥ' (clad in gold), blazing with ornaments, bracelets, crown, earrings; carried like a cloud with the moon.

statements.claim: Balarama called out asking Krishna how to overcome the demon, and Krishna answered with a smile that he knew what Balarama truly was and to remember his own strength.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.64 verses 31-35: 'O Krishna, I am being carried away by this Daitya... How shall I vanquish him?' and Krishna, knowing Rohini's son's strength, smilingly told him to meditate on his own Nārāyaṇa nature.

statements.claim: Balarama struck Pralamba once on the head with a fist like a thunderbolt; the skull shattered, blood ran from his mouth, and he fell dead like a toppled mountain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.27-28 'sa āhataḥ sapadi viśīrṇa-mastako mukhād vaman rudhiram' (struck, skull shattered, vomiting blood from the mouth); Harivamsha 1.64: 'with his well-formed fist resembling a thunder-bolt struck the wicked Pralamva on the head'; VP 5.9 and BP 10.18.29 for the fall.

statements.claim: The cowherd boys came running and saw him slain; the brothers returned unhurried.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.29 'dṛṣṭvā pralambaṃ nihataṃ' (seeing Pralamba slain); the unhurried return is connective.

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the startled moment of the plow-bearer, the laughter of the games.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.26 'haladhara īṣad atrasat' (the plow-bearer was somewhat startled) supports the startle; rest is framing.

DKS_0058.notes: Fist-on-head version follows BP and Harivamsha (VP's knees/eyes variant noted in pack but story uses the primary source).

statements.claim: While the boys played, the cows, goats and buffaloes wandered from one grove to the next, and the boys found the herd gone.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.1-2 'ajā gāvo mahiṣyaś ca nirviśantyo vanād vanam / te 'paśyantaḥ paśūn gopāḥ' (goats, cows and buffaloes entering forest after forest; the cowherds not seeing the cattle).

statements.claim: They searched by reading the ground: grass cut by hooves and hoof-prints led them on.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.3 'tṛṇais tat-khura-dac-chinnair goṣ-padair aṅkitair gavām' (marked by grass cut by hooves and hoof-prints of the cows).

statements.claim: The trail led into a dense thicket of munja grass where the herd was found lost and lowing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.4 'muñjāṭavyāṃ bhraṣṭa-mārgaṃ krandamānaṃ sva-godhanam' (in the munja forest, the herd off the path, lowing).

statements.claim: Krishna called to the cows with a voice deep as a cloud, and they began to quiet.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.5 'tā āhūtā bhagavatā megha-gambhīrayā girā' (they were called by the Lord with a voice deep as a cloud); the calming is connective.

statements.claim: A wildfire with smoke for its banner sprang up around them on every side, as if by accident — the destroyer of all that lived in the forest — and the boys and cattle were ringed by flame.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.6-7 'dava-dhūmaketur yadṛcchayābhūt kṣaya-kṛd vanaukasām... tam āpatantaṃ parito davāgniṃ gopāś ca gāvaḥ... bhītāḥ' (a wildfire with smoke for banner arose by chance, destroyer of forest-dwellers; seeing it approaching all around, cowherds and cows were frightened).

statements.claim: They cried 'Krishna! Krishna! Great hero! O Rama, whose strength never fails!'
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.8 'kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-vīra he rāmāmogha vikrama' (Krishna! Krishna! Great hero! O Rama of infallible prowess).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: wind driving the fire forward, tall sharp-bladed munja reeds, the silence of the search.
statements.evidence: Wind and reed-height are generic description; the fire's 'accidental' origin (yadṛcchayā) is supported.

statements.claim: In the rains the forest was the best of forests, heavy with ripening dates and jambu fruit, and Krishna and Balarama led the herd into it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.24 'vanaṃ tad varṣiṣṭhaṃ pakva-kharjura-jambumat' (that forest, best in the rains, full of ripe dates and jambu); leading the herd in the pack's index summary.

statements.claim: The cows walked slowly because their udders were heavy with milk.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.25 'dhenavo manda-gāminya ūdho-bhāreṇa bhūyasā' (cows slow-moving by the great burden of their udders).

statements.claim: The forest-dwellers were delighted, the trees let fall their honey-sweet blossoms, and the boys sheltered under a tree or in a cave when a shower broke.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.26-27 'vanaukasaḥ pramuditā vana-rājīr madhu-cyutaḥ / kvacid vanaspati-kroḍe guhāyāṃ cābhivarṣati' (forest-dwellers delighted, trees shedding honey; when it rained, in a tree-hollow or cave).

statements.claim: They ate a meal of curd and rice set out on a flat stone near the water, sitting on the green grass, and afterward watched the cows chew their cud with half-closed eyes.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.28-29 'dadhy-odanaṃ samānītaṃ śilāyāṃ salilāntike / śādvalopari saṃviśya carvato mīlitekṣaṇān' (curd-rice brought, on a stone near the water; seated on the fresh grass, chewing with half-closed eyes).

statements.claim: It was, the verses say, a beauty of the rains that brings happiness in every season.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.30 'prāvṛṭ-śriyaṃ... sarva-kāla-sukhāvahām' (the glory of the rains, bringing happiness at all times).

statements.claim: No demon, fire or danger came that day; the afternoon passed peacefully.
statements.evidence: Negative framing consistent with the pack — the entire episode 10.20.24-30 is idyllic with no adversary; framing device, no contrary fact asserted.

statements.claim: The cowherds of Vrindavan marvelled that a child of seven had held up a great mountain with one hand.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.2: 'yaḥ sapta-hāyano bālaḥ kareṇaikena līlayā' (a seven-year-old boy, with one hand, playfully [held up the mountain]); pack summary: cowherds wondered how a seven-year-old boy could hold up a great mountain.

statements.claim: Putana, the demon woman, came to Vrindavan in the shape of a nurse, took the child to her breast, and the babe whose eyes were barely open drew out her life.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.3-4: 'tokenāmīlitākṣeṇa pūtanāyā mahaujasaḥ' (by the child with barely opened eyes, of mighty Putana [her life was drawn out]).

statements.claim: A whirlwind snatched him up when he was a year old and carried him high into the sky.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.5: 'eka-hāyana āsīno hriyamāṇo vihāyasā' (one-year-old, seated, carried through the sky).

statements.claim: His mother Yashoda caught him stealing butter and bound him to a heavy grinding mortar.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.6: 'kvacid dhaiyaṅgava-stainye mātrā baddha udūkhale' (once, for butter-theft, bound by his mother to a mortar).

statements.claim: A demon slipped among the calves in the form of a calf; the donkey demon and all his kindred were killed; and Pralamba was thrown down by Balarama.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.7-10: 'vatseṣu vatsa-rūpeṇa praviśantaṃ jighāṃsayā', 'hatvā rāsabha-daiteyaṃ tad-bandhūṃś ca', 'pralambaṃ ghātayitvograṃ balena bala-śālinā'.

statements.claim: The serpent Kaliya, whose venom poisoned the river, was subdued and driven out of the lake by the boy.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.11: 'āśī-viṣatamāhīndraṃ damitvā vimadaṃ hradāt' (the great serpent-king of poisonous venom subdued and dispirited from the lake).

statements.claim: Nanda quieted the cowherds by recalling Garga's prophecy: the child was once born of Vasudeva, takes a body each age, has many names and forms, is the delight of cowherds and cattle, will be their welfare, will stand between them and danger, and is equal to Narayana in qualities; Garga then returned home.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.15-22 (Nanda's speech): 'prāgayaṃ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ', 'bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te', 'eṣa vaḥ śreya ādhāsyad gopa-gokula-nandanaḥ', 'sādhavo dasyu-pīḍitāḥ', 'nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ', 'garge ca sva-gṛhaṃ gate' (Garga gone to his own house).

statements.claim: The cowherds' deep affection for the boy was hard to set aside even amid their wonder.
statements.evidence: BP 10.26.12: 'dustyajaś cānurāgo 'smin sarveṣāṃ no vrajaukasām' (the love for him, hard to give up, of all us Vraja-dwellers).

statements.claim: Nanda had called Garga to Vrindavan to give the child his name; Garga told Nanda in confidence what he could not say loudly.
statements.evidence: Pack confirms Garga foretold about the child to Nanda and returned home; the naming-ceremony framing is standard traditional background, not contradicted by the pack.

DKS_0062.notes: Story follows the Bhagavata turn (Nanda recalls Garga's prophecy) as the tradition_note states; no unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Nanda bathed in the Yamuna at night, alone.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'While Nanda bathed in the Yamuna at night'; BP 10.28.1 context.

statements.claim: A servant of Varuna seized Nanda and carried him to Varuna's abode.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.1: 'taṃ gṛhītvānayad bhṛtyo varuṇasyāsuro 'ntikam' (seizing him, the servant/demon of Varuna brought him near [to Varuna]).

statements.claim: The cowherds, missing Nanda, cried out 'Krishna! Rama!'
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.2: 'cukruśus tam apaśyantaḥ kṛṣṇa rāmeti gopakāḥ' (not seeing him, the cowherds cried 'Krishna! Rama!').

statements.claim: Krishna came at the sound and entered the water, going down to Varuna's court.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.3: 'prāptaṃ vīkṣya hṛṣīkeśaṃ' (seeing Hrishikesha [Krishna] arrived); pack summary: Krishna went to Varuna's abode.

statements.claim: Varuna rose, honored Krishna with offerings and worship, bowed, and spoke words of praise and apology.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.3-7: 'loka-pālaḥ saparyayā' (the world-protector with worship); Varuna's speech: 'namas tubhyaṃ bhagavate brahmaṇe paramātmane' (obeisance to you, the supreme Self), 'ajānatā māmakena mūḍhenākārya-vedinā' (by my fool servant who did not know what was right), 'mamāpy anugrahaṃ kṛṣṇa kartum arhasy aśeṣa-dṛk' (grant me grace, O all-seeing Krishna).

statements.claim: Krishna accepted the honor without anger, and Varuna returned Nanda to him.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Varuna, honoring him, returned Nanda with apologies.'

statements.claim: Krishna brought his father back up through the water to the bank where the cowherds waited.
statements.evidence: Implied by BP 10.28.1-8 rescue sequence; pack summary: Krishna freed Nanda.

statements.claim: Nanda was silent for a long moment after climbing out, having seen the lord of the waters bow to the boy.
statements.evidence: Connective coda consistent with pack; Nanda's telling is the premise of DKS_0064 (BP 10.28.9).

DKS_0063.notes: All event claims match BP 10.28.1-8; Varuna's quoted speech mirrors the Sanskrit verses closely.

statements.claim: Nanda told his kinsmen how the lord of the waters had honored Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.9: 'nandas tv atīndriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam' (Nanda, having seen the extraordinary majesty of the world-protector [told it]); pack summary.

statements.claim: The cowherds' minds grew eager, wondering if the child was the Lord himself.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.10: 'te cautsukya-dhiyo rājan matvā gopās tam īśvaram' (the cowherds, their minds eager, thinking him the Lord).

statements.claim: Krishna, the all-seeing one, perceived the desire of his people and, being full of mercy, resolved to grant it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.11-13: 'sa bhagavān vijñāyākhila-dṛk svayam', 'iti sañcintya bhagavān mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ' (the all-seeing Lord perceived; the greatly merciful Hari reflected).

statements.claim: He reflected that people in this world are caught in ignorance, desire, and karma, unable to see the eternal.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.12: 'jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ' (people in this world, by ignorance, desire and karma).

statements.claim: He led the cowherds to the lake of Brahman, let them sink beneath it, and revealed his own abode — the eternal light of Brahman, which is truth, knowledge, and the infinite.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.14-15: 'satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ yad brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam' (the eternal Brahman-light, truth, knowledge, infinite); 'te tu brahma-hradam nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ' (taken to the lake of Brahman, immersed, and raised up by Krishna).

statements.claim: The light was not the light of sun or moon, but the light from which all lights are born, without beginning or end.
statements.evidence: Doctrinal elaboration of 'brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam'; consistent with the pack's eternal-light claim, not asserted verbatim in it.

statements.claim: The cowherds were filled with supreme bliss beyond anything the world could give, and Krishna drew them up again to the bank.
statements.evidence: BP 10.28.15-16: 'coddhṛtāḥ' (raised up by Krishna); 'nandādayas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramānanda-nivṛtāḥ' (Nanda and the others, having seen, filled with supreme bliss).

DKS_0064.notes: Theological elaboration of the Brahman-light is benign framing, not a factual divergence.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama went into the forest with the women of Vraja in the evening and began to sing, honouring the night as the moon and stars rose.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.19-21: 'govindo rāmaś cādbhuta-vikramaḥ', 'upagīyamānau lalitaṃ strī-janair baddha-sauhṛdaiḥ', 'niśā-mukhaṃ mānayantāv uditoḍupa-tārakam' (honouring the face of night, moon and stars risen).

statements.claim: The song was sweet and slow and auspicious to the mind and ear of every living thing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.20-22: 'lalitaṃ' (sweet/graceful); 'jagatuḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ manaḥ-śravaṇa-maṅgalam' (they sang what was auspicious to the mind and hearing of all beings).

statements.claim: The gopis, listening, went still and forgot themselves, as if entranced.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.23: 'gopyas tad-gītam ākarṇya mūrcchitā nāvidan' (hearing the song the gopis swooned and knew not [themselves]).

statements.claim: The demon Shankhachuda, a servant of Kubera, seized the gopis and carried them off while the brothers sang.
statements.evidence: Pack summary and BP 10.34.24-25: 'evaṃ vikrīḍatoḥ svairaṃ gāyatoḥ sampramatta-vat', 'tan-nāthaṃ pramadā-janaṃ' (the women whose lord was him); excerpt: 'the demon Shankhachuda, servant of Kubera, carried off the women'.

statements.claim: The gopis cried out 'Krishna! Rama!' as they were carried away.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.26: 'krośantaṃ kṛṣṇa rāmeti' (crying 'Krishna! Rama!').

statements.claim: The brothers cried 'Do not fear!', tore up sal-tree trunks as clubs, and plunged after the demon like two lions.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.27: 'mā bhaiṣṭety abhayārāvau śāla-hastau tarasvinau' ('Do not fear' — the two giving fearlessness, sal-trees in hand, impetuous); excerpt: 'pursued him like two lions'.

DKS_0065.notes: All details map to BP 10.34.19-27; 'of the kind that had troubled Vrindavan before' is generic connective.

statements.claim: The demon Shankhachuda had carried the gopis off into the forest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.24-26 (preceding verses in pack's cited range); pack summary for DKS_0065/DKS_0066.

statements.claim: Looking back, the demon saw Krishna and Balarama coming together and perceived them as Time and Death themselves.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.28: 'sa vīkṣya tāv anuprāptau kāla-mṛtyū ivodvijan' (seeing the two arrived, trembling as if [they were] Time and Death).

statements.claim: Krishna ran after him wherever he ran.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.29: 'tam anvadhāvad govindo yatra yatra sa dhāvati' (Govinda ran after him wherever he ran).

statements.claim: Krishna overtook the fleeing demon and, with a single blow of his fist to the head, struck him down and killed him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.30: 'avidūra ivābhyetya śiras tasya durātmanaḥ' (approaching as if near, [struck] the head of that evil one); pack excerpt: 'struck his head with his fist'.

statements.claim: Krishna took the bright jewel from the fallen demon's crest and gave it to his elder brother Balarama, while the women looked on.
statements.evidence: BP 10.34.31: 'śaṅkhacūḍaṃ nihatyaivaṃ maṇim ādāya bhāsvaram' (having slain Shankhachuda thus, taking the bright jewel); pack excerpt: 'gave it to his elder brother Balarama while the women looked on'.

statements.claim: The women he had taken were safe and saw the whole exchange.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'while the women looked on'; implied by the rescue of the abducted gopis.

DKS_0066.notes: The chase imagery and 'not spoil' commentary are connective; all factual beats are in BP 10.34.28-31.

statements.claim: The demon Arishta came in the shape of a savage bull.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14: 'the demon Arisht́a, disguised as a savage bull'; BP 10.36.1-14.

statements.claim: The Vishnu Purana describes him with the colour of a cloud charged with rain, vast horns, eyes like two fiery suns, tongue licking his lips, erect tail, an enormous hump between his shoulders, low-hanging dewlap, and a face scarred from butting trees; his hooves ploughed up the earth.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14 verbatim: 'colour was that of a cloud charged with rain; he had vast horns, and his eyes were like two fiery suns... his tongue was repeatedly licking his lips; his tail was erect... a hump of enormous dimensions... his dewlap hung low, and his face was marked with scars from butting against the trees... he ploughed up the ground with his hoofs.'

statements.claim: He was a demon who haunted the forests in the shape of a bull, destroying hermits and ascetics.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14: 'the demon who perpetually haunts the forests in the shape of a bull, destroying hermits and ascetics.'

statements.claim: The cows fled in fear, abandoning the herd.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.4: 'paśavo dudruvur bhītā rājan santyajya go-kulam' (the cattle fled in fear, abandoning the herd).

statements.claim: Krishna called the creature out — 'what is this, you lowest of beings, terrifying the cowherds and their animals?' — and slapped his arms together to goad him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.6-7: 'gopālaiḥ paśubhir manda trāsitaiḥ kim asattama' (what is this, O lowest one, the cowherds and animals terrified), 'ity āsphotyācyuto 'riṣṭaṃ tala-śabdena kopayan' (thus slapping his arm, enraging Arishta with the sound).

statements.claim: Arishta pawed the ground, lowered the points of his horns, fixed his reddened eyes on Krishna, and charged.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.8-9: 'khureṇāvanim ullikhan' (pawing the earth with his hoof), 'agra-nyasta-viṣāṇāgraḥ stabdhāsṛg-locano' (horn-points lowered, eyes fixed and bloodshot).

statements.claim: Krishna waited, smiling, for the bull to reach him, then seized him by the horns and flung him a full eighteen paces.
statements.evidence: VP 5.14: 'smiling in sport and derision, awaited the near approach of the bull'; BP 10.36.10: 'gṛhītvā śṛṅgayos taṃ vā aṣṭādaśa padāni' (seizing him by the horns, eighteen paces [he flung him]).

statements.claim: The demon rose and charged again, and Krishna took hold of him by the horns, forced him down, and pressed him to the ground with his foot, killing him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.11-12: 'punar utthāya satvaram', 'sa nigṛhya śṛṅgayoḥ padā samākramya nipātya bhū-tale' (seizing him by the horns, pressing with his foot, throwing him to the ground).

statements.claim: He died vomiting blood, kicking out his feet, his eyes rolling and finding no rest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.13: 'asṛg vaman mūtra-śakṛt samutsṛjan kṣipaṃś ca pādān anavasthitekṣaṇaḥ' (vomiting blood, excreting urine and dung, kicking his feet, eyes unsteady).

statements.claim: The gods praised Krishna with a shower of flowers, and the herdsmen glorified him as the celestials of old praised Indra over the demon Jambha.
statements.evidence: BP 10.36.14: 'stūyamānaḥ dvijātibhiḥ' (praised by the twice-born/gods); pack excerpt: 'the gods praised Krishna with showers of flowers'; VP 5.14: 'the herdsmen glorified Krishńa, as the companies of the celestials of old praised Indra, when he triumphed over the Asura Jambha.'

DKS_0067.notes: Story follows the Bhagavata killing method (fling + press down), as its tradition_note declares; the VP horn-tearing variant is not asserted.

statements.claim: Keshi came to Vrindavan in the shape of a horse, sent by Kamsa, who wanted Krishna dead.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP): 'sent by Kamsa'; Harivamsha 1.79: 'king Kansa sent an emissary to Keshi for destroying Krishna.'

statements.claim: His mane tossed like a storm-cloud and his neighing was itself a terror.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.1: 'vāla-vighūrṇitāmbudam' (clouds whirled by his mane); Harivamsha 1.79: 'trifle at the wind with his neighing'.

statements.claim: The Harivamsha says he was born along with Kamsa, as dear to the king as his own life, a peerless fighter who had never met his equal.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'peerless in battle, is born with Kansa, and is his life though ranging outward... the foremost of the sinful.'

statements.claim: He killed the cows and the cowherds and fed on them, and wherever he ranged the forest fell empty: people and cattle withdrew, paths went unused, and animals could no longer travel the forest roads.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'Killing the cows and cow-herds... began to feed on beef... continually fed on human flesh', 'made the forest empty', 'the Gopas, who derive their sustenance through woods and the kine left it', 'the animals could not wend the forest roads.'

statements.claim: Following the sound of men, the horse came to the settlement of the cowherds; the women, boys and men set up a cry and fled to Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'following in anger the noise of men... arrived at the settlement of the milk-men', 'the Gopa-women, with their children, and the Gopas, setting up a cry, fled away to their master Krishna.'

statements.claim: Krishna promised them safety and went out to meet the demon, despite cowherds urging him back — 'you are only a boy, and this one is beyond the strength of all.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.79: 'Krishna promised them safety and went out to meet Keshi'; 'thou art a boy and that one of evil ways is beyond the power of all.'

statements.claim: The horse charged with his mouth open as if to drink the sky, eyes and teeth bared, neck raised; Krishna roared like a lion and met the rush.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.1-2: 'upāhvayat sa vyanadan mṛgendra-vat' (he called out roaring like a lion), 'makhena khaṃ pibann ivābhyadravad' (rushing with mouth as if drinking the sky); Harivamsha: 'expanding his eyes and teeth and raising up his neck.'

statements.claim: The horse struck at him with his fore-hooves, and Krishna slipped aside, caught hold of him, whirled him around, and hurled him to the ground.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.2-3: 'jaghāna padbhyām' (he struck with his feet); 'tad vañcayitvā tam adhokṣajo ruṣā pragṛhya dorbhyāṃ parividhya pādayoḥ' (having deceived him, seized him with his arms, whirled him by the feet).

statements.claim: Keshi rose again, angrier than before, and came at him with jaws stretched open to bite; Krishna, smiling, thrust his arm into the open mouth, like a hand thrust down a serpent's hole.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.4: 'labdha-saṃjñaḥ punar utthito ruṣā vyādāya keśī tarasāpatad harim', 'so 'py asya vaktre bhujam uttaraṃ smayan praveśayām āsa yathoragaṃ bile' (smiling, he put his arm into his mouth as into a serpent's hole).

statements.claim: The demon's teeth met the arm and dropped out as though they had touched hot iron, and the arm swelled until it filled the creature and stopped his breath; Keshi choked, kicked, and fell dead.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.5-6: 'dantā nipetur... tapta-maya-spṛśo yathā' (teeth fell as if touching molten metal), 'bāhuś ca tad-deha-gato... saṃvavṛdhe' (the arm within the body grew), 'niruddha-vāyuś caraṇāṃś ca vikṣipan' (breath stopped, kicking his feet).

statements.claim: His body split open like a ripened gourd — one source says torn asunder like a tree struck by lightning — and Krishna drew his arm out.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.7: 'tad-dehataḥ karkaṭikā-phalopamād vyasor apākṛṣya bhujaṃ mahā-bhujaḥ' (withdrawing his arm from the body like a karkaṭikā fruit); VP 5.16: 'fell down, torn asunder like a tree struck by lightning.'

statements.claim: The gods showered flowers upon him, and because he had slain Keshi the world would call him Keshava.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP): 'the gods showered flowers on Krishna'; Harivamsha 1.79: 'Since thou hast slain Keshi, thou shalt pass by the name of Keshava'; VP 5.16: 'thou shalt be known in the world by the name of Keśava.'

DKS_0068.notes: Blends BP, Harivamsha and VP as the pack does; every cited detail (born with Kamsa, empty forest, serpent-hole simile, Keshava name) is in the pack.

statements.claim: The boys of Vrindavan played a game on the slopes of the hill where the herd grazed, some as keepers of the calves and some as thieves.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.25-26: 'te paśūn pālāś cārayanto 'dri-sānuṣu' (herding cattle on mountain slopes), 'tatrāsan katicic corāḥ pālāś ca katicin' (some there were thieves, some keepers).

statements.claim: Vyoma, the son of Maya, a demon and master of deception, dressed as a cowherd boy and was taken for one of the boys.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.27: 'maya-putro mahā-māyo vyomo gopāla-veṣa-dhṛk' (Vyoma, son of Maya, of great illusion, wearing a cowherd's garb).

statements.claim: One by one he led boys away and sealed them in a cave in the mountain, so the game went on around the empty places where they had been.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.28: 'giri-daryāṃ vinikṣipya nītaṃ nītaṃ mahāsuraḥ' (sealing them in a mountain cave, the great demon carried them away one by one).

statements.claim: Krishna, whom the verses call the giver of refuge to the good, saw what was happening and understood at once.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.29: 'tasya tat karma vijñāya kṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇa-daḥ satām' (Krishna, the refuge-giver to the good, knowing that deed).

statements.claim: Krishna left off the shape and size of a boy and stood in his own form, vast and strong as a king among mountains.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.30: 'sa nijaṃ rūpam āsthāya girīndra-sadṛśaṃ balī' (assuming his own form, mighty, like a king of mountains).

statements.claim: He seized Vyoma with both hands, threw him down upon the earth, and ended him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.31: 'taṃ nigṛhyācyuto dorbhyāṃ pātayitvā mahī-tale' (seizing him with his arms, throwing him on the ground).

statements.claim: Krishna broke through the covering that sealed the cave and brought the boys out, one after another, into the light.
statements.evidence: BP 10.37.32: 'guhā-pidhānaṃ nirbhidya gopān niḥsārya kṛcchrataḥ' (breaking the cave's covering, bringing the cowherds out with difficulty).

DKS_0069.notes: Every claim maps to BP 10.37.24-32; 'the mountain gave back everyone it had taken' is connective coda.

statements.claim: Krishna went into the forest alone, not with Balarama (Sangkarshana)
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66 (Dutt): 'without being united with Sangkarshana, began to range alone in that charming forest'

statements.claim: He was dark as a rain-cloud, wore a crow's feather in his hair, and garlands of new kadamba and arjuna buds
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66: 'dark-blue hue of the clouds of the rainy season', 'wearing a feather of crow', 'Garlands of new grown buds of Arjuna, Kadamba and Nipa flowers'

statements.claim: The forest was resonant with peacocks and low thunder among the hills, with plantain groves, new grass, lotuses and hidden fountains
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66: 'resonant with the notes of peacocks', 'caves echoed with the muttering of clouds', 'adorned with plantain trees... new grown grass, twigs and lotuses', 'abounded in many fountains'

statements.claim: He used to stop under the great Bhandiraka fig tree, tall enough to brush half the sky, while cowherd boys amused him and he answered on his flute
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66: 'Beholding this Bhāndiraka fig-tree... traversed half of the sky'; 'the other cow-herds amused him with various wild plays... Krishna, too at times, played on his flute'

statements.claim: He came to the Yamuna bank, which was embellished with lilies and lotuses, swans and cranes, smooth landing-stairs, strong sweet current and many lakes
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66 (vv.28-31): 'embellished with lilies and lotuses', 'resonant with the notes of swans, Karandavas and Sārasas', 'landing stairs were well-levelled and her water was sweet; she had many lakes and her current was strong'

statements.claim: Kaliya the serpent-king lived in a lake beside the Yamuna and his venom had made the water unfit to drink
statements.evidence: Index summary: 'Finding the Yamuna's lake poisoned by the serpent-king Kaliya'; excerpt: 'jump into the lake and vanquish Kalya'

statements.claim: Krishna quietly resolved: 'I should vanquish this king of serpents... I shall climb the Kadamba tree, and jump into the lake, and vanquish Kaliya'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66 excerpt (verbatim): 'I should, however, vanquish this king of serpents... I shall climb this Kadamba tree, jump into the lake and vanquish Kalya.'

DKS_0070.notes: All setting details and the resolve are drawn directly from Harivamsha 1.66. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: The cowherds and cattle, distressed by the summer heat, came to the Yamuna and drank
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.47: 'gāvaś ca gopāś ca nidāghātapa-pīḍitāḥ' (cows and cowherds distressed by the heat of summer)

statements.claim: The poisoned water struck down their minds and they fell lifeless, as if by fate
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.48: 'viṣāmbhas tad upaspṛśya daivopahata-cetasaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'fall lifeless'

statements.claim: Krishna, master of all yoga and of the masters of yoga, restored them with a single nectar-showering glance
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.49-51: 'kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ... govindānugrahekṣitam'; pack excerpt: 'restores them with a single nectar-showering glance'

statements.claim: The cowherds rose from the water's edge with memory restored and knew it was Govinda's grace
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.50-51: 'te sampratīta-smṛtayaḥ samutthāya jalāntikāt / anvamaṃsata tad rājan govindānugrahekṣitam' (with restored memory they rose and deemed it Govinda's gracious look)

statements.claim: They were given back as if waking from a dreamless sleep, with no ordinary medicine involved
statements.evidence: Framing of the recovery scene consistent with the pack; no sourceable fact asserted

DKS_0071.notes: Faithful rendering of BP 10.15.46-51; 'no one left standing to raise a cry' is consistent with all falling. No unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna bound his cloth tightly, climbed the tall kadamba tree, slapped his arms and dived headlong into the poisoned pool
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.5: 'kṛṣṇaḥ kadambam adhiruhya tato 'ti-tuṅgam āsphoṭya gāḍha-raśano nyapatad viṣode'; Harivamsha 1.67: 'Tying his cloth firmly... emitting a leonine roar... jumped headlong down into the lake'

statements.claim: The water overflowed its banks like scattering clouds and the serpent's abode was shaken
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'The water thereof overflowed (on all sides) like scattering clouds. The huge abode of the serpent was shaken by that sound.'

statements.claim: The serpents rose with eyes red with anger, Kaliya at their head, dark as clouds with five hoods and a fiery face and tongue
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'serpents, with their eyes reddened with anger, rose up'; 'king of serpents Kālya... hue of clouds... five hoods, a fiery countenance and tongue and effulgent like the flames of fire'

statements.claim: The whole surface of the pool was covered by his burning hoods; the water boiled and the Yamuna fled in its opposite course
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'The entire lake was covered with his hood burning like fire... water there appeared as if boiling and the river Yamunā, stricken with fear, flew in her opposite course'

statements.claim: Kaliya loosed winds of fire; sparks and smoke poured from him and the great trees on the bank were consumed
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'powerful winds issue out of his mouth filled with the fire of anger. Scintiliations of fire, accompanied by smoke... All the huge trees... were in no time consumed'

statements.claim: His son Dara and his servant serpents rose with him, vomiting venom and flame
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'his son Dāra and his servants, the other leading serpents... vomitting the dreadful fire of venom accompanied by smokes'

statements.claim: Krishna sported in the water as if at play and was untouched by fire, venom and the serpent fury
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'sporting like a boy'; 'The powerful Krishna however did not die'

DKS_0072.notes: The story stops before the coiling (correctly deferred to DKS_0073); variant_note about VP including the biting is respected. No issues.

statements.claim: Kaliya bit Krishna, the tender boy in yellow cloth with the Srivatsa mark, smiling face and lotus-soft feet, and wound his coils about him, holding him motionless
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.8: 'śrīvatsa-pīta-vasanaṃ smita-sundarāsyam... krīḍantam apratibhayaṃ kamalodarāṅghriṃ sandaśya marmasu ruṣā bhujayā cachāda'; v.9: 'nāga-bhoga-parivītam adṛṣṭa-ceṣṭam' (wrapped in the serpent's coils, motionless)

statements.claim: The cowherd boys on the bank, seeing him bound, were overcome with grief, terror and sorrow and dropped where they stood
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.9: 'tat-priya-sakhāḥ paśupā bhṛśārtāḥ... duḥkhānuśoka-bhaya-mūḍha-dhiyo nipetuḥ'

statements.claim: The cows, bulls and young calves lowed and cried out in their distress
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.10: 'gāvo vṛṣā vatsataryaḥ krandamānāḥ su-duḥkhitāḥ'

statements.claim: Three kinds of terrible omens appeared in Vraja, and the cowherds, led by Nanda, with children, old men and women, went out in fear
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.11-14: 'mahotpātās tri-vidhā hy ati-dāruṇāḥ'; 'gopā nanda-purogamāḥ'; 'ā-bāla-vṛddha-vanitāḥ sarve 'ṅga paśu-vṛttayaḥ'

statements.claim: Balarama went with them, seeing them so distressed
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.15: 'tāṃs tathā kātarān vīkṣya bhagavān mādhavo balaḥ'

statements.claim: They followed Krishna's footprints stamped with lotus, barley-grain, goad, thunderbolt and banner, and found him in the pool wrapped in the serpent's coils
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.16-18: 'sūcitayā padaiḥ'; 'abja-yavāṅkuśāśani-dhvajopapannāni padāni'; 'antar hrade bhujaga-bhoga-parītam... kṛṣṇaṃ nirīham upalabhya'

statements.claim: The gopis remembered his friendship, smile, looks and words, and saw the three worlds empty
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.19: 'tat-sauhṛda-smita-viloka-giraḥ smarantyaḥ... śūnyaṃ priya-vyatihṛtaṃ dadṛśus tri-lokam'

statements.claim: The gopis held up Yashoda, who had run after her child, shared her pain, told the old stories of Vraja with eyes fixed on Krishna's face, looking like the dead
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.20: 'kṛṣṇa-mātaram apatyam anupraviṣṭāṃ tulya-vyathāḥ samanugṛhya śucaḥ sravantyaḥ... vraja-priya-kathāḥ kathayantya āsan kṛṣṇānane 'rpita-dṛśo mṛtaka-pratīkāḥ'

DKS_0073.notes: All beats of BP 10.16.8-20 rendered faithfully. 'Lived by Krishna as cattle live by grass' is a devotional gloss on paśu-vṛttayaḥ (living by cattle), connective.

statements.claim: Kaliya lay with his hoods crushed by the blows of Krishna's feet
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.30: 'pārṣṇi-prahāra-parirugna-phaṇātapatram' (hood-umbrella broken by heel-blows)

statements.claim: His wives came forward with loosened hair and slipping garments, children placed before them, and bowed with folded hands
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.30-31: 'ślathad-vasana-bhūṣaṇa-keśa-bandhāḥ'; 'puraskṛtārbhāḥ... kṛtāñjali-puṭāḥ'

statements.claim: They declared the punishment just, since Krishna's descent is to subdue the wicked, and that he looks with equal eyes even on his enemies' children
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.32: 'nyāyyo hi daṇḍaḥ kṛta-kilbiṣe 'smiṃs tavāvatāraḥ khala-nigrahāya / ripoḥ sutānām api tulya-dṛṣṭiḥ'

statements.claim: They said the punishment itself was grace, washing away the stain of the wicked
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.33: 'anugraho 'yaṃ bhavataḥ kṛto hi no daṇḍo 'satāṃ te khalu kalmaṣāpahaḥ'

statements.claim: They praised Krishna as the great Soul, storehouse of knowledge and wisdom, the Infinite One of unbroken power; Time, navel of time, witness of its parts; the Self behind elements, senses, breath, mind and heart
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.38-41: 'puruṣāya mahātmane... jñāna-vijñāna-nīdhaye... ananta-śaktaye / kālāya kāla-nābhāya kālāvayava-sākṣiṇe / bhūta-mātrendriya-prāṇa-mano-buddhy-āśayātmane'

statements.claim: They hailed him as the subtle, unchanging seer, source of scripture; homage to Krishna, Rama, son of Vasudeva; the lamp that lights the strands of the world and hides them
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.42-45: 'sūkṣmāya kūṭa-sthāya vipaścite... śāstra-yonaye / namaḥ kṛṣṇāya rāmāya vasudeva-sutāya ca / namo guṇa-pradīpāya guṇātma-cchādanāya ca'

statements.claim: His play lies beyond all that is made, yet through him everything made comes to be; though desiring nothing, he holds the powers of action and time; he knows the highest and lowest and oversees all
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.46-48: 'avyākṛta-vihārāya sarva-vyākṛta-siddhaye / parāvara-gati-jñāya sarvādhyakṣāya... guṇair anīho 'kṛta-kāla-śakti-dhṛk'

statements.claim: All beings of the three worlds — peaceful, restless, bewildered — are his forms; the peaceful are dear to him, and he came to guard them and uphold what is right
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.49: 'śāntā aśāntā uta mūḍha-yonayaḥ... śāntāḥ priyās te hy adhunāvituṃ satāṃ sthātuś ca te dharma-parīpsayehataḥ'

statements.claim: They pleaded that a wrong done once by a husband should be borne as one bears with one's own children, and that the serpent was giving up his life
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.50-51: 'aparādhaḥ sakṛd bhartrā soḍhavyaḥ sva-prajā-kṛtaḥ / anugṛhṇīṣva bhagavan prāṇāṃs tyajati pannagaḥ'

statements.claim: They asked Krishna to tell his servants what to do
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.52: 'vidhehi te kiṅkarīṇām anuṣṭheyaṃ tavājñayā'

DKS_0075.notes: The praise-hymn and plea track BP 10.16.30-52 point by point. No issues.

statements.claim: Kaliya, regaining his senses and breath, slowly lifted his head and spoke to Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.54: 'pratilabdhendriya-prāṇaḥ kāliyaḥ śanakair harim'

statements.claim: Kaliya acknowledged the world was brought forth by Krishna, that serpents are fierce by birth, and that Krishna is the cause of everything, all-knowing, lord of the world
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.56-58: 'tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ... vayaṃ ca tatra... sarpā jāty-uru-manyavaḥ / bhavān hi kāraṇaṃ tatra sarva-jño jagad-īśvaraḥ'

statements.claim: Krishna spared him and ordered him to leave the water and go to the ocean with his wives and kin
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'O serpent, I do not wish to allow you to live in this water of Yamuna. Therefore repair to the ocean with your wife and kinsmen'; Vishnu Purana 5.7: 'Hari set the snake-king at liberty'

statements.claim: The marks of Krishna's feet on the serpent's heads would protect him from Garuda
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt summary (BP 10.16.53-67 rendered): 'declaring that the mark of Krishna's feet will protect him from Garuda'

statements.claim: Whoever remembered this command or bathed in that pool and offered water to the gods would be freed of sin
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.60-61: 'ya etat saṃsmaren martyas tubhyaṃ mad-anuśāsanam / yo 'smin snātvā mad-ākrīḍe devādīṃs tarpayej jalaiḥ'

statements.claim: Kaliya worshipped Krishna with divine garments, garlands and fine gems, honouring him whose banner is Garuda, then departed with wife, kin and sons to the island of the ocean
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.64-66: 'divyāmbara-sraṅ-maṇibhiḥ parārdhyair api bhūṣaṇaiḥ pūjayitvā jagan-nāthaṃ prasādya garuḍa-dhvajam / sa-kalatra-suhṛt-putro dvīpam abdher jagāma ha'

statements.claim: He went to Ramanaka island, the very island he had left before taking refuge in this pool
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.62: 'dvīpaṃ ramaṇakaṃ hitvā hradam etam upāśritaḥ'

statements.claim: The poison lifted, the Yamuna ran sweet again, and the cattle that had been perishing were restored
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.30 (Uddhava): 'vipannān viṣa-pānena nigṛhya bhujagādhipam utthāpyāpāyayad gāvas tat toyaṃ prakṛti-sthitam' (the cows perishing from the poisoned drink he restored, and made the water natural again)

statements.claim: Long afterward Uddhava remembered this among the wonders of Krishna's childhood
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.30, Uddhava's recollection; variant_notes: 'bpc1_035 is Uddhava's recollection'

DKS_0076.notes: tradition_note correctly defers the dance-on-hoods to the previous episode per BP chronology. No issues.

statements.claim: A king listening to the tale asked how Kaliya came to live in the Yamuna, and the sage answered
statements.evidence: BP 10.17 opens with Śuka's narration (śrī-rājovāca at 10.16.67 closes the prior chapter); the question-and-answer frame is consistent with the text

statements.claim: The serpents owed Garuda a share, paid at every change of the moon
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.2: 'svaṃ svaṃ bhāgaṃ prayacchanti nāgāḥ parvaṇi parvaṇi'

statements.claim: Kaliya, son of Kadru, intoxicated with his venom's power, withheld the tribute
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.3: 'viṣa-vīrya-madāviṣṭaḥ kādraveyas tu kāliyaḥ'

statements.claim: Garuda, dear to the Lord, heard and was furious
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.4: 'tac chrutvā kupito rājan bhagavān bhagavat-priyaḥ'

statements.claim: Kaliya rose to meet him with many heads raised and venom as his weapon, but the son of Tarkshya struck him with his left wing shining like gold, and Kaliya was dazed
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.5-7: 'viṣāyudhaḥ pratyabhyayād utthita-naika-mastakaḥ / taṃ tārkṣya-putraḥ... pakṣeṇa savyena hiraṇya-rociṣā jaghāna kadru-sutam'; 'suparṇa-pakṣābhihataḥ kāliyo 'tīva vihvalaḥ'

statements.claim: Garuda is the vehicle of Vishnu (Madhusudana)
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.6: 'madhusūdanāsanaḥ' (seated on Madhusudana's vehicle)

statements.claim: Garuda once came to that spot wanting to eat a fish; the sage Saubhari saw the fish distressed when their king was slain and laid a curse: if Garuda entered that pool, his life would end
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.8-10: 'jala-caraṃ garuḍo bhakṣyam īpsitam / mīnān su-duḥkhitān dṛṣṭvā dīnān mīna-patau hate / atra praviśya garuḍo yadi matsyān sa khādati'; pack excerpt names Saubhari

statements.claim: Only Kaliya among the serpents knew this, and took refuge there
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.11: 'tat kāliyaḥ paraṃ veda nānyaḥ kaścana lelihaḥ'

DKS_0077.notes: The sage who answers is Śuka, consistent with the framing; Saubhari named in the pack's excerpt summary. No issues.

statements.claim: Krishna emerged from the pool wearing a divine garland, fragrant and finely dressed
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.12: 'kṛṣṇaṃ hradād viniṣkrāntaṃ divya-srag-gandha-vāsasam'

statements.claim: Seeing him, all rose as though their breath had returned
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.13: 'upalabhyotthitāḥ sarve labdha-prāṇā ivāsavaḥ'

statements.claim: Yasoda, Rohini, Nanda, the gopis and the cowherds embraced him
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.14: 'yaśodā rohiṇī nando gopyo gopāś ca kaurava'

statements.claim: Balarama, embracing Krishna, laughed, knowing his power
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.15: 'rāmaś cācyutam āliṅgya jahāsāsyānubhāva-vit'

statements.claim: The brahmanas, elders with their families and wives, came to Nanda and asked him to give gifts to the twice-born for Krishna's deliverance
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.16-17: 'nandaṃ viprāḥ samāgatya guravaḥ sa-kalatrakāḥ / dehi dānaṃ dvi-jātīnāṃ kṛṣṇa-nirmukti-hetave'

statements.claim: Nanda gave cows and gold in thanksgiving
statements.evidence: Pack index summary and excerpt: 'Nanda gives cattle and gold to the brahmanas... bestows cows and gold upon the brahmanas'

statements.claim: Yasoda, the fortunate one who had lost and regained her child, held Krishna close
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.18: 'yaśodāpi mahā-bhāgā naṣṭa-labdha-prajā satī'

statements.claim: The river ran sweet behind them, the poison gone with the serpent
statements.evidence: Arc continuity: BP 10.16.67/3.2.30 (water restored to its natural state once Kaliya departed)

statements.claim: The village vigil: no one had seen the serpent go and none dared believe the boy would come back up
statements.evidence: Scene-setting atmosphere of the reunion; no sourceable fact asserted either way

DKS_0078.notes: Opening vigil is connective atmosphere (pronoun 'him' refers to the serpent's unseen departure). All substantive claims supported by BP 10.17.12-18.

statements.claim: Krishna came before the elders, Nanda at their head, bowed low, and asked what ceremony they had undertaken.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.1-2: Krishna, bowing humbly, asked the elders led by Nanda: 'kathyatāṃ me pitaḥ ko 'yaṃ sambhramo...' (verse 2).

statements.claim: He asked four things: what the ceremony is, its fruit, for whom it is meant, and by what means it is accomplished.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.2: 'kiṃ phalaṃ kasya voddeśaḥ kena vā sādhyate makhaḥ'.

statements.claim: His eagerness to hear was real and large; he asked as one who truly wished the answer.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.3: 'etad brūhi mahān kāmo mahyaṃ śuśrūṣave pitaḥ'.

statements.claim: The text marks that he was the Lord who knows all things, the Self of every being, the one who sees everything.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.1: 'tad-abhijño 'pi bhagavān sarvātmā sarva-darśanaḥ'.

statements.claim: People perform their rites whether they understand them or not, and acting with understanding is not the same as acting without it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.5: 'jñatvājñātvā ca karmāṇi jano 'yam anutiṣṭhati'; viduṣaḥ karma-siddhiḥ syād yathā nāviduṣo bhavet.

statements.claim: Before anything else he wanted to know what the elders had settled upon, and why.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.6: 'tatra tāvat kriyā-yogo bhavatāṃ kiṃ vicāritaḥ'.

statements.claim: The sacrifice had come down from the elders' fathers and their fathers before them, season after season.
statements.evidence: Inherited tradition is the story's framing; the 'paramparyāgata' dharma is stated in Nanda's speech (10.24.10).

statements.claim: The question hung in the air over Vraja, simple and unsettling.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere; no sourceable fact asserted.

DKS_0079.notes: Every factual claim tracks BP 10.24.1-6 closely; no unsupported or contradicted material.

statements.claim: Indra is lord of the clouds and rain, king of the celestials; the clouds are his own forms.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.7 (in pack passage): 'parjanyo bhagavān indro meghās tasyātma-mūrtayaḥ'.

statements.claim: This season the cowherds, at a boy's word, carried their offerings to a hill instead of Indra.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.30-37 in pack; 10.25.1: 'indras tadātmanaḥ pūjāṃ vijñāya vihatāṃ'.

statements.claim: The boy had argued beings are born and perish by their own deeds, clouds rain by nature, and forest people should honour what they live by.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.13-23 (karmaṇaiva, rajasā coditā meghā, vanaukasas... vana-śaila-nivāsinaḥ).

statements.claim: The cowherds walked in a circle around the hill, cows and brahmins, the women of Vraja singing of the boy's deeds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.32-33: 'giriṃ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam'; 'gopyaś ca kṛṣṇa-vīryāṇi gāyantyaḥ'.

statements.claim: The boy came before the hill, said 'I am the mountain,' and in a great form received the offerings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.34: 'śailo 'smīti bruvan bhūri balim ādad bṛhad-vapuḥ'.

statements.claim: When Indra understood his worship had been cut off, he grew angry with the cowherds whose lord was Krishna, Nanda and the rest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.1: 'gopebhyaḥ kṛṣṇa-nāthebhyo nandādibhyaś cukopa ha'.

statements.claim: Indra had come to expect the cowherds' homage season after season, an old arrangement.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the inherited Indra-yajna tradition (10.24.8-10, Harivamsha 1.70).

statements.claim: The anger gathered over Vraja like a storm not yet broken.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric framing of the following beat.

DKS_0080.notes: Faithful expansion of BP 10.25.1 plus recapitulation fully grounded in 10.24 passages included in the pack.

statements.claim: Nanda told Krishna that Indra is the lord of the clouds, and the clouds are his very selves, raining down the delight and life of all beings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.7: 'parjanyo bhagavān indro meghās tasyātma-mūrtayaḥ / te 'bhivarṣanti bhūtānāṃ prīṇanaṃ jīvanaṃ payaḥ'.

statements.claim: He and all other men worship Indra with offerings produced by his own rain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.8: 'vārmucāṃ patim īśvaram / dravyais tad-retasā siddhair yajante kratubhir narāḥ'.

statements.claim: On what remains after the offering the people live, pursuing the good things a life is meant to hold.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.9: 'tac-cheṣeṇopajīvanti tri-varga-phala-hetave' (tri-varga = the three aims of life).

statements.claim: It is a dharma that has come down from the fathers and the fathers' fathers, handed down without a break.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.10: 'dharmaṃ paramparyāgataṃ'.

statements.claim: A man may abandon it out of desire, hatred, fear or greed, but the one who sets it aside does not come to anything good.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.10: 'kāmād dveṣād bhayāl lobhāt sa vai nāpnoti śobhanam'.

statements.claim: Without the rain the grass would not grow, the cows would not graze, the milk would not come.
statements.evidence: Natural elaboration of verse 7's claim that rain is the life of beings; no specific verse asserts the milk detail.

statements.claim: Nanda gave the answer simply, without pride, and waited to see what the boy would make of it.
statements.evidence: Narrative characterization; consistent with the speech's tone.

DKS_0081.notes: Direct, faithful rendering of BP 10.24.7-10; all doctrinal content sourced.

statements.claim: A being is born by its own actions and comes to its end by them; joy, sorrow, fear and safety are all reached through one's deeds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.13: 'karmaṇā jāyate jantuḥ karmaṇaiva pralīyate / sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayaṃ kṣemaṃ karmaṇaivābhipadyate'.

statements.claim: A lord who hands out the fruits of others' deeds only follows the actor; he has no power over one who has done nothing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.13: 'asti ced īśvaraḥ... kartāraṃ bhajate so 'pi na hy akartuḥ prabhur hi saḥ'.

statements.claim: Among tilling, trading, tending cattle and lending, the cowherds' livelihood has always been cattle.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.20: 'kṛṣi-vāṇijya-go-rakṣā kusīdaṃ... vayaṃ go-vṛttayo 'niśam'.

statements.claim: The clouds rain not by a king's command but driven by rajas, nature's restless force, in every direction.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.21-22: 'sattvaṃ rajas tama iti... rajasā coditā meghā varṣanty ambūni sarvataḥ'.

statements.claim: Whoever thrives by one thing and bows to another finds no security; whoever is helped by one and worships another meets calamity in this world and the next.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.18 ('na tasmād vindate kṣemaṃ'); Harivamsha 1.71: 'visited by twofold calamities in this world, and in the next after death'.

statements.claim: He compared such a man to a faithless woman who leaves her own home for strangers and keeps nothing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.18: 'jārān nāry asatī yathā'.

statements.claim: We have no cities, no towns, no walled houses; we are people of the forest who live among forests and hills.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.23: 'na naḥ purojanapadā na grāmā na gṛhā vayam / vanaukasas... vana-śaila-nivāsinaḥ'.

statements.claim: Let the sacrifice be for the cows, the brahmins and the hill.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.24: 'tasmād gavāṃ brāhmaṇānām adreś cārabhyatāṃ makhaḥ'.

statements.claim: He prescribed the details: take the offerings gathered for Indra, cook the rich dishes and milk-rice, brahmins feed the fires, food to every guest even the lowliest, fodder to the cows, oblation to the hill, then circumambulate the cows, brahmins, fire and mountain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.25-28: pāyasa/saṃyāva, 'hūyantām agnayaḥ... brāhmaṇair', 'annaṃ bahu-guṇaṃ tebhyo deyaṃ', 'anyebhyaś cāśva-cāṇḍāla-patitebhyo yathārhataḥ', 'yavasaṃ ca gavāṃ dattvā giraye dīyatāṃ baliḥ', 'pradakṣiṇāṃ ca kuruta go-viprānala-parvatān'.

statements.claim: 'This is my thought, father... Do it, if it pleases you. This sacrifice to the cows, the brahmins and the hills is dear to me.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.29: 'etan mama mataṃ tāta kriyatāṃ yadi rocate / ayaṃ go-brāhmaṇādrīṇāṃ mahyaṃ ca dayito makhaḥ'.

statements.claim: He was the Lord of time itself who had set out to break Indra's pride.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.31: 'kālātmanā bhagavatā śakra-darpa-jighāṃsayā'.

statements.claim: The cowherds agreed to do exactly as he said.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.31: 'sādhv agṛhṇanta tad-vacaḥ'.

DKS_0082.notes: Dense but every claim maps to 10.24.13-29 or the parallel Harivamsha/VP excerpts; zero drift.

statements.claim: Every year the people of Vraja set aside a day for Indra; this year, at a boy's urging, they set it aside instead and prepared to honour Govardhana.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.30-32; index summary 'Nanda and the cowherds accept Krishna's words and perform the sacrifice to Govardhana hill'.

statements.claim: They brought offerings to the hill, to the cows and to the brahmins.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.31-32: 'upahṛtya balīn samyag... yavasaṃ gavām'.

statements.claim: The villagers climbed onto their decorated bullock carts and, with their cattle before them, walked around Govardhana keeping the hill on their right.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.32-33: 'go-dhanāni puraskṛtya giriṃ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam'; 'anāṃsy anaḍud-yuktāni te cāruhya sv-alaṅkṛtāḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna took on another form, vast and still, stood upon the summit of the hill and said 'I am the hill.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.34: 'kṛṣṇas tv anyatamaṃ rūpaṃ... śailo 'smīti bruvan... bṛhad-vapuḥ'; VP 5.10: 'Upon the summit of Govarddhana, Krishńa presented himself, saying "I am the mountain"'.

statements.claim: That form began to eat, consuming the abundant offerings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.34: 'bhūri balim ādad'; VP 5.10: 'partook of much food presented by the Gopas'.

statements.claim: The people of Vraja bowed low and murmured 'Behold, the hill has favored us.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.24.35-36: 'tasmai namo vraja-janaiḥ saha cakra'; 'aho paśyata śailo 'sau rūpī no 'nugrahaṃ vyadhāt'.

statements.claim: Krishna had argued the hill's grass nourished the cows and its slopes held the clouds.
statements.evidence: Recap of the preceding argument (10.24.17-24); the cloud-holding detail is a nature description, not a pack claim.

statements.claim: The walking-around was an old gesture that bound them to the hill.
statements.evidence: Reflective framing of the circumambulation.

DKS_0083.notes: Worship and manifestation beats both match BP 10.24.30-37; summit detail corroborated by VP 5.10.

statements.claim: Indra, furious, summoned the Samvartaka clouds, the storm-clouds of dissolution kept for the ending of an age.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.1: 'gaṇaṃ sāṃvartakaṃ nāma meghānāṃ cānta-kārīṇām'; Harivamsha 1.73: 'the clouds called Samvartaka'.

statements.claim: He told them: if you respect your king, Nanda and these cowherds have grown hostile to my festival.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'if you cherish any respect for your king... Nanda and other Gopas have grown inimical towards my festival'.

statements.claim: Within seven nights they were to afflict with rain and wind the precious cattle, the animals from which the cowherds take their very name.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'within seven nights, distress, with rain and winds, the precious kine which constitute their life-long subsistence and for which they pass by the name of Gopas'.

statements.claim: Indra himself would ride his elephant Airavata and pour down rain and wind flashing like thunder and lightning.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'I myself, stationed on (my elephant) Airavata, shall discharge dreadful rain, winds and showers effulgent like thunder and lightning'.

statements.claim: The clouds would drive the cattle to destruction.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'you will kill all the kine and the inhabitants of Vraja'; BP 10.25.1-8 excerpt.

statements.claim: The clouds rolled up dark-blue and vast as mountains, muttering, some like elephants, some like sea-creatures, some like serpents, and made an unfair day.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'dreadful dark-blue clouds, resembling a mountain in size and muttering awfully... some resembling the elephants, some the Makaras and some the serpents... created a very unfair day'.

statements.claim: Lightning flared without pause; they wrapped the heavens in darkness, adorned with Indra's rainbow bow.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'Producing lightnings continually the clouds, adorned with the bow of Indra, enshrouded the welkin with darkness'.

statements.claim: The sun and moon vanished; the stars were swallowed.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'The planets and stars disappearing from view, the sky, shorn of the rays of the sun and the moon'.

statements.claim: Earth, horizon and sky were blended into one by the heavy shower, and people took it for a deep, unpassable ocean in the sky.
statements.evidence: VP 5.11: 'the earth, the points of the horizon, and the sky, were all blended into one by the heavy and incessant shower'; Harivamsha 1.73: 'a deep, unpassable and limitless ocean stationed in the sky'.

statements.claim: Rain fell in columns thick as pillars and streams wide as an elephant's trunk; rivers swelled and tore away bank trees.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: showers 'resembling... the trunks of elephants and some bamboos'; 'the rivers, increasing their size, carried away the trees grown on their banks'.

statements.claim: Grass and trees trembled as if rebuked by thunder; birds could not leave their nests; animals fled; peacocks cried out.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: grass and trees 'began to tremble'; 'the birds could not come out of their nests and the animals began to fly away'; 'The peacocks began to cry aloud'.

statements.claim: The cowherds, drenched and terrified, said the end of the world was at hand and the earth would become one sheet of water.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'We think the end of the world is at hand and the earth will be converted into one sheet of water'.

statements.claim: The cows stood motionless and lowed in distress, soaked, trembling, hair standing up; some died of exhaustion, some fled, some sank down in the cold with their calves.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: cows 'stood motionless and began to cry aloud... the hairs stood erect... Some died out of exhaustion, some took to their heels in fear and some with their calves sank under frost'.

statements.claim: The cows and calves looked toward Krishna and cried 'Save us! Save us!'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: 'looked towards Krishna and cried "Save us! Save us!"'.

statements.claim: Krishna understood why the storm had come and had already begun to plan.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.73: Krishna 'greatly worked up with anger... meditating for a while... "To protect them... I will uproot this best of mountains Govardhana"'.

statements.claim: He was not a god who forgave such things; his fury rose.
statements.evidence: Characterization consistent with 10.25.1 (cukopa) and the Harivamsha mandate.

DKS_0084.notes: Storm sequence tracks Harivamsha 1.73 nearly line-for-line; counts (seven nights) and cattle-death details match. 'Kept apart for the ending of an age' is a fair reading of cānta-kārīṇām/Samvartaka.

statements.claim: Krishna had uprooted Govardhana and lifted it over the cowherds like an umbrella; villagers and cattle crowded beneath it.
statements.evidence: Recap of the immediately preceding canonical beat (previous story 'Krishna Lifts Govardhana Hill'); BP 10.25.20 addresses the held hill ('mad-dhastādri-nipātanāt').

statements.claim: Hunger and thirst pressed on them; they set aside hunger, thirst, aches and longing for comfort.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.22: 'kṣut-tṛḍ-vyathāṃ sukhāpekṣāṃ hitvā'.

statements.claim: Krishna told them there was nothing to fear; the hill would not fall on them while he held it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.20: 'na trāsa iha vaḥ kāryo mad-dhastādri-nipātanāt'.

statements.claim: Their minds steadied by his word, they went in and stayed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.21: 'nirviviśur gartaṃ kṛṣṇāśvāsita-mānasaḥ'.

statements.claim: Seven days Krishna stood holding the hill without moving from his place.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'he held the mountain for seven days without moving from his place' (BP 10.25, verses 19-23 rendering).

statements.claim: Indra, seeing the cowherds sheltered by a mountain held by a boy, was astonished; his anger gave way and he checked his clouds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.23: 'kṛṣṇa-yogānubhāvaṃ taṃ niśamyendro 'ti-vismitaḥ'; excerpt: 'Indra, astonished, checked his clouds'.

statements.claim: The rain slackened, the wind died, the clouds drew apart and the sun came out.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.24: 'khaṃ vyabhram uditādityaṃ vāta-varṣaṃ ca dāruṇam' (sky cloudless, sun risen, fierce wind and rain gone).

statements.claim: The cowherds were told to come out, leaving fear behind, with their women, wealth and children.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.25: 'niryāta tyajata trāsaṃ gopāḥ sa-strī-dhanārbhakāḥ'.

statements.claim: The cowherds he meant to destroy were sheltered and dry; the boy had not stirred.
statements.evidence: Consistent with 10.25.23 (astonishment at Krishna's power) and the sheltered state; 'dry' is an implied corollary of the shelter.

DKS_0086.notes: All claims grounded in BP 10.25.20-25; the lifting recap matches the corpus chain's prior beat.

statements.claim: The cowherds came out from beneath the hill, each gathering up what was his — the goods and the cattle.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.26: 'niryayur gopāḥ svaṃ svam ādāya go-dhanam'.

statements.claim: Krishna set the mountain back down in its own place, as it had stood before.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.27: 'śailaṃ sva-sthāne pūrva-vat'.

statements.claim: Nanda, Yashoda, Rohini and Balarama came to him and embraced him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.28-29: 'yaśodā rohiṇī nando rāmaś ca balināṃ varaḥ'; 'samīyuḥ parirambhaṇādibhiḥ'.

statements.claim: The gopis welcomed him with curd and unbroken rice, showering blessings with glad hearts.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.28: 'gopyaś ca sa-sneham apūjayan mudā dadhy-akṣatādbhir yuyujuḥ sad-āśiṣaḥ'.
