statements.claim: In heaven the hosts of gods — siddhas, sadhyas, gandharvas and charanas — rained flowers down on him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.30: 'divi deva-gaṇāḥ siddhāḥ sādhyā gandharva-cāraṇāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'the gods rained flowers'.

statements.claim: Conches and drums sounded in the sky.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.31: 'śaṅkha-dundubhayo nedur divi'.

statements.claim: Krishna, surrounded by the devoted cowherds, set out with Balarama for his own cow-pen.
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.32: 'anuraktaiḥ paśupaiḥ pariśrito... sva-goṣṭhaṃ sa-balo 'vrajad dhariḥ'.

statements.claim: The land that had sheltered them closed over the gap where they had hidden.
statements.evidence: Imagery consistent with restoring the hill to its place; not a separate sourceable fact.

DKS_0087.notes: Restoration, embrace and heavenly rejoicing all map to BP 10.25.26-32; characters and actions exact.

statements.claim: For seven days Indra poured thunder, wind and water over Vrindavan because the cowherds, at a boy's urging, had turned their worship away from him and toward a hill.
statements.evidence: Storm and its cause are the established preceding event in the arc (prev story DKS_0087); SB 10.27.11 has Indra say 'by me this cowherd home was about to be destroyed by wind and rain', and the Harivamsha passage in the adjacent pack (1.74) gives 'excessive rain extending over seven nights'.

statements.claim: Indra came down quietly, alone, approaching in seclusion, ashamed, his offense heavy on him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.1: 'vivikta upasaṅgamya vrīḍītaḥ kṛta-helanaḥ' — approached in seclusion, ashamed, having committed an offense.

statements.claim: He had seen and heard enough of Krishna's boundless power to know who stood before him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.2: 'dṛṣṭa-śrutānubhāvo 'sya kṛṣṇasyāmita-tejasaḥ' — having seen and heard of Krishna's boundless power.

statements.claim: Indra touched Krishna's feet with his crown.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Indra, ashamed, approached Krishna in seclusion, touched his feet with his crown' (rendered from verses 1-15).

statements.claim: "I was drunk on my own lordship... I did not know your power, and so I offended you. Forgive me, Lord. Let such a wish never rise in me again."
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'I, intoxicated by my sovereignty, have offended you, not knowing your power; forgive me, Lord, and may such evil intention never arise in me again.'

statements.claim: A man intoxicated with rule and riches cannot see the hand that holds the rod of chastisement.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.15: 'mām aiśvarya-śrī-madāndho daṇḍa-pāṇiṃ na paśyati'.

statements.claim: He named Krishna the father and teacher of all the worlds, the lord before whom all must bow, with time holding its punishment ready.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.5: 'pitā gurus tvaṃ jagatām adhīśo duratyayaḥ kāla upātta-daṇḍaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna had come down to lighten the burden of the earth, a burden the gods could not lay down.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.8: 'tavāvatāro 'yam adhokṣajeha bhuvo bharāṇām uru-bhāra-janmanām' — this descent to lighten the earth's heavy burden.

statements.claim: "By me this home of the cowherds was about to be destroyed by wind and rain. And by you I have been spared. My arrogance is broken. My effort has come to nothing."
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.11-12: 'mayedaṃ bhagavan goṣṭha-nāśāyāsāra-vāyubhiḥ / tvayeśānugṛhīto 'smi dhvasta-stambho vṛthodyamaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna replied, "Go, Shakra. May all be well with you. Do what I ask of you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.16: 'gamyatāṃ śakra bhadraṃ vaḥ kriyatāṃ me 'nuśāsanam'.

statements.claim: The forest was quiet after the rain, leaves wet and ground soft, with no witness to the meeting.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric setting consistent with Indra approaching in seclusion (10.27.1); no sourceable fact asserted.

DKS_0088.notes: All claims map directly to SB 10.27.1-16 or the established preceding storm narrative; no unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Surabhi, the divine cow, stepped forward to praise Krishna.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.17-18: 'athāha surabhiḥ kṛṣṇam abhivandya manasvinī' — Surabhi, wise, bowed to and addressed Krishna.

statements.claim: Surabhi is the mother of all the cattle of heaven and earth.
statements.evidence: Traditional epithet of Surabhi (the divine cow per pack); the pack itself calls her 'the divine cow' — epithet, not a sourceable event in the pack.

statements.claim: "You are our highest deity... You are our very Indra, lord of the world. Urged by Brahma, we shall now consecrate you as Indra."
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.19-20: 'tvaṃ naḥ paramakaṃ daivaṃ tvaṃ na indro jagat-pate / indraṃ nas tvābhiṣekṣyāmo brahmaṇā coditā vayam'.

statements.claim: Indra was urged on by Surabhi and the divine mothers, and came with the sages of the gods, Tumburu, Narada, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Siddhas and Charanas.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.22-23: 'indraḥ surarṣibhiḥ sākaṃ codito deva-mātṛbhiḥ / tatrāgatās tumburu-nāradādayo gandharva-vidyādhara-siddha-cāraṇāḥ'.

statements.claim: Indra brought the water of the celestial Ganga and bathed Krishna with it, giving him the name Govinda.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Indra, with the waters of the celestial Ganga, bathed Krishna and named him Govinda' (10.27.20-22); SB 10.27.27: 'iti go-gokula-patiṃ govindam abhiṣicya saḥ'.

statements.claim: "The people of this world will sing of you as Govinda," spoken in the words of the older account.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.74: 'the people of this world will hymn thee as Govinda'; Vishnu Purana 5.12: 'as the Indra of the cows, thou shalt be called Govinda'.

statements.claim: The assembled gods praised Krishna and showered him with wonderful flowers from the sky.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.24: 'taṃ tuṣṭuvur deva-nikāya-ketavo hy avākiraṃś cādbhuta-puṣpa-vṛṣṭibhiḥ'.

statements.claim: When Krishna was consecrated, the rivers ran with many kinds of sweetness and the trees oozed honey.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.25: 'nānā-rasaughāḥ sarito vṛkṣā āsan madhu-sravāḥ'.

statements.claim: The name Govinda — lord of the cows and cowherds — stuck and never left him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.27 ('go-gokula-patiṃ govindam'); Vishnu Purana 5.12 ('Indra of the cows... called Govinda'); closing reflection is commentary, not a factual assertion.

DKS_0089.notes: Clean; ceremony details (celestial Ganga, Govinda naming, flower showers, honey-dripping trees) all in SB 10.27.17-27 / Harivamsha 1.74 / VP 5.12.

statements.claim: Krishna's flute song awakened remembrance of him in the gopis, and they began to describe him to one another.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.2-3: 'veṇu-gītaṃ smarodayam... tad varṇayitum ārabdhāḥ smarantyaḥ kṛṣṇa-ceṣṭitam'.

statements.claim: He wore a peacock feather, golden-yellow cloth, and a garland of forest flowers, and filled the flute with the nectar of his lips, with cowherd boys around him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.4: 'barhāpīḍaṃ... vāsaḥ kanaka-kapiśaṃ vaijayantīṃ ca mālām... adhara-sudhayāpūrayan... gopa-vṛndair'.

statements.claim: His music was pleasing to every living thing.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.5: 'veṇu-ravaṃ rājan sarva-bhūta-manoharam'.

statements.claim: Even the dull-witted deer stopped to listen and worshipped him with looks of love.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.10: 'dhanyāḥ sma mūḍha-gatayo 'pi hariṇya etā... pūjāṃ dadhur viracitāṃ praṇayāvalokaiḥ'.

statements.claim: The women of heaven in their flying chariots went still, flowers falling loose from their hair.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.11: 'devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā bhraśyat-prasūna-kabarā mumuhur vinīvyaḥ'.

statements.claim: The cows drank the music with lifted ears, and calves with milk still on their mouths stood motionless with tears in their eyes, holding Govinda in their hearts.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.12: 'gāvaś ca... pīyūṣam uttabhita-karṇa-puṭaiḥ pibantyaḥ / śāvāḥ snuta-stana-payaḥ-kavalāḥ sma tasthur govindam ātmani dṛśāśru-kalāḥ'.

statements.claim: Birds and sages climbed the branches and listened with closed eyes, without a word.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.13: 'vihagā munayo vane 'smin... āruhya ye druma-bhujān rucira-pravālān śṛṇvanti mīlita-dṛśo vigatānya-vācaḥ'.

statements.claim: The rivers, their current broken, reached out with arms of water to touch his feet, offering lotuses.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.14: 'nadyas tadā... bhagna-vegāḥ... āliṅgana-sthagitam ūrmi-bhujair murārer gṛhṇanti pāda-yugalaṃ kamalopahārāḥ'.

statements.claim: A single cloud stayed over Krishna and his friends like an umbrella as they walked the herds in the heat of the day.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.15: 'dṛṣṭvātape vraja-paśūn saha rāma-gopaiḥ... vyadhāt sva-vapuṣāmbuda ātapatram' — a cloud made an umbrella of its body; verse places the walk in the heat with Rāma and the cowherds.

statements.claim: Govardhana is the greatest of his servants because his feet touched it and it feeds him and his cattle with water, grass and roots.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.17: 'hantāyam adrir abalā hari-dāsa-varyo yad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparaśa-pramodaḥ... pānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kandamūlaiḥ'.

DKS_0090.notes: Every image (deer, goddesses, cows, calves, birds/sages, rivers, cloud, hill) maps to a specific verse in SB 10.21.1-19.

statements.claim: The young unmarried girls of Vrindavan went down to the Yamuna before dawn and bathed in it.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.1: 'āplutyāmbhasi kālindyā jalānte codite 'ruṇe' — bathing in the waters of the Kalindi (Yamuna) at the rise of dawn.

statements.claim: The verses call them kumaryas — young girls, not yet married.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.4: 'evaṃ māsaṃ vrataṃ ceruḥ kumāryaḥ kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ'.

statements.claim: Through the first month of winter they performed the vow every morning.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.4 ('for a month they performed the vow'); index summary: 'Through the first month of winter the gopis keep their vow, bathing before dawn in the Yamuna'.

statements.claim: At the water's edge they made an image of the goddess Katyayani and worshipped her with fragrant paste, garlands, offerings, incense and a burning lamp.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.2: 'gandhair mālyaiḥ surabhibhir balibhir dhūpa-dīpakaiḥ'; pack excerpt: 'worshipping an image of the goddess'.

statements.claim: Their single prayer was: "O Katyayani... make Nanda's son my husband."
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.3 addresses Katyayani as 'mahā-māye mahā-yoginy adhīśvari'; pack excerpt: 'with the single prayer that Nanda's son become their husband'; 10.22.4: 'kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ' — minds fixed on Krishna.

statements.claim: They rose at dawn and went linked arm in arm with one another.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.5: 'ūṣasy utthāya gotraiḥ svair anyonyābaddha-bāhavaḥ' — rising at dawn, holding one another's arms.

statements.claim: They asked for nothing else — not riches, long life, or good fortune.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the pack's single-prayer emphasis (10.22.4); negative framing is narrative, not a separately sourceable claim.

statements.claim: Their mothers knew and said nothing.
statements.evidence: Minor narrative texture; not in the pack's verses 1-5 but contradicts nothing.

statements.claim: By the time the sun was fully up they would be dressed and turning for home.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric continuation of the pre-dawn bathing scene; no factual assertion in the pack to verify.

DKS_0091.notes: Core vow details all supported by SB 10.22.1-5; remaining items are connective texture.

statements.claim: The girls laid their clothes on the riverbank and entered the water, as before.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.6: 'nadyāḥ kadācid āgatya tīre nikṣipya pūrva-vat' — coming to the river, placing clothes on the bank as before.

statements.claim: Krishna understood what their discipline was for; the verses call him the master of all masters of yoga.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.7: 'bhagavāṃs tad abhipretya kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ'.

statements.claim: He gathered up their garments and quickly climbed a kadamba (nīpa) tree.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.8: 'tāsāṃ vāsāṃsy upādāya nīpam āruhya satvaraḥ'.

statements.claim: Laughing, he called down: come, one by one, and take back what is yours.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.9: 'atrāgatya... kāmaṃ svaṃ svaṃ vāsaḥ pragṛhyatām'; the jest (kṣvelita) at 10.22.11.

statements.claim: The gopis knew he had never once spoken an untruth to them, and found no cruelty in the jest.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.10: 'na mayodita-pūrvaṃ vā anṛtaṃ tad ime viduḥ' — they knew he had never uttered an untruth before; 10.22.11 'kṣvelitaṃ' — play/jest.

statements.claim: The gopis were flooded with love, like a lamp flaring when a hand is cupped near it.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.11: 'tasya tat kṣvelitaṃ dṛṣṭvā gopyaḥ prema-pariplutāḥ' — seeing his jest, the gopis were flooded with love; lamp simile is narrative embellishment of 'flooded with love'.

statements.claim: The kadamba tree stood close to the water, and the girls stood waist-deep in the cold river looking up at him.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting consistent with 10.22.6-11 (clothes on the bank, tree climbed, girls in the water); physical details are atmosphere.

DKS_0092.notes: All plot points map directly to SB 10.22.6-11.

statements.claim: The gopis answered from the water, calling him the dear son of Nanda, the dark and beautiful one, saying they were his maidservants and would do whatever he asked.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.13-14: 'mānayaṃ bhoḥ kṛthās tvāṃ tu nanda-gopa-sutaṃ priyam / śyāmasundara te dāsyaḥ karavāma tavoditam'.

statements.claim: All the girls came out of the water together, trembling with cold, and stood before him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.16: 'tato jalāśayāt sarvā dārikāḥ śīta-vepitāḥ'.

statements.claim: Their hands pressed together above their heads as they stood before him.
statements.evidence: Gesture not stated in the pack passage (10.22.16 only says they came out trembling with cold); descriptive detail, contradicts nothing in the pack.

statements.claim: Krishna, pleased by the purity of their hearts, told them that bathing naked while keeping their vow showed disregard for the gods, which had to be answered.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.17-18: 'śuddha-bhāva-prasāditaḥ... yūyaṃ vivastrā yad apo dhṛta-vratā vyagāhataitat tad u deva-helanam'.

statements.claim: "Your resolve is known to me. This worship of me — I have seen it."
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.24: 'saṅkalpo viditaḥ sādhvyo bhavatīnāṃ mad-arcanam'.

statements.claim: "Go back to Vraja now. The nights you have wished for will come to you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.26: 'yātābalā vrajaṃ siddhā mayemā raṃsyathā kṣapāḥ' — go to Vraja, successful; with me you will enjoy these nights.

statements.claim: They felt no resentment and were joyful in the company of their beloved.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.21-22: 'nābhyasūyan priya-saṅga-nirvṛtāḥ... paridhāya sva-vāsāṃsi preṣṭha-saṅgama-sajjitāḥ'.

DKS_0093.notes: All substantive claims (maidservant reply, coming out shivering, deva-helana rebuke, resolve known, nights to come, joy) map to SB 10.22.12-27.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama were pasturing cattle not far from home with the cowherd boys, and hunger came over them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.6: 'gāś cārayantāv avidūra odanaṃ rāmācyutau vo laṣato bubhukṣitau' — pasturing cows not far away, Rāma and Acyuta, hungry, want cooked rice.

statements.claim: A company of brahmanas, learned and well-versed in the Vedas, had gathered to perform a sacrifice.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.2: 'prayāta deva-yajanaṃ brāhmaṇā brahma-vādinaḥ' — the brahmanas, speakers of Brahman, went to the sacrificial site; pack excerpt: 'performing the Angirasa sacrifice'.

statements.claim: Krishna sent the boys to them with the request for food in his name.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.3-4: 'tatra gatvaudanaṃ gopā yācatāsmad-visarjitāḥ / ity ādiṣṭā bhagavatā gatvā yācanta te tathā'.

statements.claim: The boys asked: "O gods of the earth, listen to us: we come at Krishna's bidding. While pasturing the cows not far from here, Balarama and Krishna have grown hungry, and they ask for food."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.5-6: 'he bhūmi-devāḥ śṛṇuta kṛṣṇasyādeśa-kāriṇaḥ / gāś cārayantāv avidūra odanaṃ rāmācyutau vo laṣato bubhukṣitau'.

statements.claim: The brahmanas neither said yes nor no; they simply did not heed the request.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.8: 'iti te bhagavad-yācñāṃ śṛṇvanto 'pi na śuśruvuḥ'; 10.23.11: 'na te yad om iti procur na neti ca'.

statements.claim: Their attention was wholly on the sacrifice — place, time, materials, mantras, rituals, priests, fires.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.9: 'deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṃ mantra-tantrartvijo 'gnayaḥ'.

statements.claim: They did not recognize the supreme Brahman, the Lord, who stood before them, hidden by their own learning.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.10: 'taṃ brahma paramaṃ sākṣād bhagavantam adhokṣajam' — the supreme Brahman, directly the Lord Adhokṣaja; pack excerpt: 'proud of their learning, do not recognize the Lord'.

DKS_0094.notes: Refusal episode matches SB 10.23.1-11 exactly, including the 'neither yes nor no' detail.

statements.claim: When Krishna heard what had happened, the master of the whole world laughed, without anger.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.12: 'tad upākarṇya bhagavān prahasya jagad-īśvaraḥ' — hearing this, the Lord, master of the world, laughed.

statements.claim: He said: go to their wives, and tell them that I have come, with Balarama.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.13: 'māṃ jñāpayata patnībhyaḥ sa-saṅkarṣaṇam āgatam' — announce to the wives that I have come with Saṅkarṣaṇa.

statements.claim: The boys bowed to the wives and said: "Obeisance to you, wives of the brahmanas; listen to our words. While pasturing the cows with the cowherds, he has come from far away, with Balarama — and he is hungry."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.14-16: 'namo vo vipra-patnībhyo nibodhata vacāṃsi naḥ / gāś cārayan sa gopālaiḥ sa-rāmo dūram āgataḥ'; hunger from 10.23.6.

statements.claim: The wives, who had always longed for Krishna's sight, heard that Acyuta had come and rose at once.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.17: 'śrutvācyutam upāyātaṃ nityaṃ tad-darśanotsukāḥ' — hearing Acyuta had come, they who were always longing for his sight.

statements.claim: They filled vessels with food of four kinds, rich and fine, and hurried toward him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.18: 'catur-vidhaṃ bahu-guṇam annam ādāya bhājanaiḥ' — taking four kinds of excellent food in vessels.

statements.claim: Their husbands, brothers, kinsmen and sons tried to stop them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.19: 'niṣidhyamānāḥ patibhir bhrātṛbhir bandhubhiḥ sutaiḥ'.

statements.claim: Not one of them turned back; they went like rivers running to the sea.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'hurry to him like rivers to the sea, heedless of husbands and kinsmen who would stop them' (rendered from 10.23.12-19).

statements.claim: They left houses, husbands and kin without a backward look, running toward him as toward a light.
statements.evidence: Devotional framing of the 'heedless of husbands and kinsmen' detail (10.23.19); the 'light/arrival' imagery is narrative commentary, not a factual claim.

DKS_0095.notes: Wives episode matches SB 10.23.12-19; no unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: The women had left their husbands' great sacrifice, carried food through the forest, and fed Krishna and his cowherd companions with their own hands.
statements.evidence: Preceding event in the arc (SB 10.23.1-19, prev story DKS_0095 'The Brahmanas' Wives Bring Food to Krishna'); DKS_0097's pack confirms the wives 'had gone instead, carrying food through the woods' and SB 10.23.35: 'bhagavān api govindas tenaivānnena gopakān' — Govinda fed the cowherd boys with that very food.

statements.claim: They stood before him in a grove on the banks of the Yamuna, where the ashoka trees were tipped with fresh young leaves.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.20: 'yamunopavane 'śoka nava-pallava-maṇḍite' — in the Yamuna pleasure-grove adorned with ashoka trees in fresh leaf.

statements.claim: They had known him before they ever saw him — their hearts already sunk in him, their ears filled with the nectar of hearing about him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.22: 'prāyaḥ-śruta-priyatamodaya-karṇa-pūrair yasmin nimagna-manasas' — minds immersed in him through hearing of the dearest one.

statements.claim: Krishna stood like a dancer at ease — one hand on a companion's shoulder, the other twirling a lotus, dark skin, gold garments, forest-flower garland, peacock feather, earrings, lotus-bright smiling face.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.21: 'śyāmaṃ hiraṇya-paridhiṃ vanamālya-barha-dhātu-pravāla-naṭa-veṣam anavratāṃse vinyasta-hastam itareṇa dhunānam abjaṃ karṇotpalālaka-kapola-mukhābja-hāsam' — dark, gold-clad, forest garland and peacock feather, dancer's garb, hand on a companion's shoulder, twirling a lotus with the other, earrings at cheeks, lotus-face with a smile.

statements.claim: The women drank him in through their eyes, and the sorrow that had followed them from home left them, the way the wise give up their false ideas of self.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.22: 'antaḥ praveśya su-ciraṃ parirabhya tāpaṃ prājñaṃ yathābhimatayo vijahur' — taking him in through the eyes, they abandoned their sorrow as the wise abandon their misconceptions.

statements.claim: Krishna said: "You are welcome. Sit. Tell me what I can do for you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.24: 'svāgataṃ vo mahā-bhāgā āsyatāṃ karavāma kim'.

statements.claim: The wise see what is best for themselves and give him all they have — breath, mind, intelligence, wife, children, wealth.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.25-26: 'nanv addhā mayi kurvanti kuśalāḥ svārtha-darśinaḥ / prāṇa-buddhi-manaḥ-svātma dārāpatya-dhanādayaḥ'.

statements.claim: He told them to return to the place of sacrifice, since their husbands were brahmanas.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.27: 'tad yāta deva-yajanaṃ patayo vo dvijātayaḥ'.

statements.claim: The women answered: "Do not speak such cruel words. We have left everyone — fathers, husbands, sons, brothers — so that we might carry on our heads the tulasi garland fallen from your feet. Neither they nor any stranger will take us back; for us who have fallen at your feet there is no other refuge. Grant us this."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.28-29: 'maivaṃ vibho 'rhati bhavān gadituṃ nṛ-śaṃsaṃ ... prāptā vayaṃ tulasi-dāma padāvasṛṣṭaṃ keśair nivoḍhum atilaṅghya samasta-bandhūn / gṛhṇanti no na patayaḥ pitarau sutā vā na bhrātṛ-bandhu-suhṛdaḥ kuta eva cānye tasmād bhavat-prapadayoḥ patitātmanāṃ no nānyā bhaved gatir ... tad vidhehi'.

statements.claim: Krishna was pleased and granted them the grace they asked, teaching that he is won by remembrance — hearing, seeing, holding him in the mind, speaking of him — not by bodily nearness, and sent them home with hearts fixed on him.
statements.evidence: Index summary: 'Krishna, pleased with their devotion, assures them of his grace and sends them back with their minds fixed on him'; pack excerpt: 'teaching that he is won by remembrance rather than by nearness'; SB 10.23.31 + 10.23.32: 'na prītaye 'nurāgāya hy aṅga-saṅgo ... / śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo 'nukīrtanāt'.

DKS_0096.notes: All plot points map directly to SB 10.23.20-31; the food-carrying opening is the established preceding event (10.23.1-19, DKS_0095).

statements.claim: The sacrifice had the right place, hour, offerings, mantras, and fires tended by priests who knew every rule.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.47 (the brahmanas' own enumeration): 'deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṃ mantra-tantrartvijo 'gnayaḥ'.

statements.claim: When a young cowherd came asking for food, sent by his companion Krishna who waited hungry in the forest with his friends, they waved him away.
statements.evidence: Established preceding event (SB 10.23.1-19, prev story DKS_0095); pack excerpt: 'the Lord they had spurned'; SB 10.23.8/11: they did not heed the request.

statements.claim: It was their wives who had gone instead, carrying food through the woods to Krishna and his friends, and Krishna fed the cowherds with that very food.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.35: 'bhagavān api govindas tenaivānnena gopakān' — Govinda fed the cowherds with that same food.

statements.claim: Even the one wife whose husband had held her back by force was not stopped; she closed her eyes and went to Krishna in her mind, meditating on the Lord as she had heard of him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.34: 'tatraikā vidhṛtā bhartrā bhagavantaṃ yathā-śrutam' — one held back by her husband [meditated on] the Lord as she had heard; cf. 10.23.32 'śravaṇād darśanād dhyānāt'.

statements.claim: The one they had refused was Vishnu himself — the Lord standing in the forest in the shape of a cowherd boy.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.48: 'sa eva bhagavān sākṣād viṣṇur yogeśvareśvaraḥ'; 10.23.36: 'līlā-nara-vapur nr-lokam anuśīlayan' — playing a human form.

statements.claim: "Shame on our birth, and on its threefold aims. Shame on our vows. Shame on our great learning."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.39: 'dhig janma nas tri-vṛd yat tad dhig vrataṃ dhig bahu-jñatām'.

statements.claim: The Lord's power to delude could bewilder even the wise, even the yogis.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.40: 'nūnaṃ bhagavato māyā yoginām api mohinī'.

statements.claim: The women had no initiation into the brahminical way and no long years of study in a guru's house, yet they loved Krishna, the teacher of all the worlds, with a love that shamed the men's learning.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.41-43: 'aho paśyata nārīṇām api kṛṣṇe jagad-gurau / nāsāṃ dvijāti-saṃskāro na nivāso gurāv api / tathāpi hy uttamaḥ-śloke kṛṣṇe yogeśvareśvare'.

statements.claim: The place, the hour, the separate offerings, the mantras, the priests, the fires — all were Krishna himself; he is whom the goddess of fortune serves, ever longing for the touch of his feet; he needs nothing yet grants liberation.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.45-48: 'anyathā pūrṇa-kāmasya kaivalyādy-aśiṣāṃ pateḥ / hitvānyān bhajate yaṃ śrīḥ pāda-sparśāśayāsakṛt / deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṃ mantra-tantrartvijo 'gnayaḥ / sa eva bhagavān sākṣād viṣṇur yogeśvareśvaraḥ'.

statements.claim: "Salutations to the Lord Krishna, whose wisdom never falters. He is Vishnu himself, the lord of all lords of yoga, the first being of all — and it is his own power that keeps our minds deluded."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.49-50: 'tasmai namo bhagavate kṛṣṇāyākuṇṭha-medhase / sa vai na ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sva-māyā-mohitātmanām'.

statements.claim: They remembered their fault and the insult they had offered him, and longed to see him — but they did not go, because Kamsa ruled nearby and they were afraid.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.51: 'iti svāgham anusmṛtya kṛṣṇe te kṛta-helanāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'yearn for his sight yet do not dare approach, fearing Kamsa'.

DKS_0097.notes: All claims map to SB 10.23.32-51; the cowherd-refusal opening is the established preceding event (10.23.1-19, DKS_0095).

statements.claim: The moon rose full over Vrindavan, painting the sky with red light.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.1-2: 'tadoḍurājaḥ kakubhaḥ karair mukhaṃ prācyā vilimpann aruṇena' — the moon tinting the directions with red rays; 'akhaṇḍa-maṇḍalaṃ ... nava-kuṅkumāruṇam' — full disc, red like fresh kumkum.

statements.claim: When Krishna's flute sounded, the women of Vraja heard it amid their ordinary tasks and set them down — one left milking, another left milk half-boiled over the fire, another turned from a husband she was serving, another from a child she was feeding.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.3-6: 'niśamya gītāṃ ... vraja-striyaḥ kṛṣṇa-gṛhīta-mānasāḥ ... duhantyo 'bhiyayuḥ kāścid dohaṃ hitvā ... payo 'dhiśritya ... pariveṣayantyas tad dhitvā pāyayantyaḥ śiśūn payaḥ śuśrūṣantyaḥ patīn kāścid aśnantyo 'pāsya bhojanam'.

statements.claim: Some came with their clothes and ornaments half arranged, so great was their haste.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.6: 'vyatyasta-vastrābharaṇāḥ kāścit kṛṣṇāntikaṃ yayuḥ' — some went to Krishna with clothes and ornaments askew.

statements.claim: Some who were shut inside their houses stood where they were, closed their eyes, and held him in their minds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.8: 'antar-gṛha-gatāḥ kāścid gopyo 'labdha-vinirgamāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ tad-bhāvanā-yuktā dadhyur mīlita-locanāḥ'.

statements.claim: Their families called them back, but they did not turn — Krishna had taken their minds, and they went where the music led.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.7: 'tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ'.

statements.claim: Pride rose in the gopis out of their good fortune — the sense that they, of all people, possessed him.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (SB 10.29.47): 'Seeing the pride that had arisen in the gopis from their good fortune'.

statements.claim: Where he had been, there was nothing — he vanished then and there, in the middle of the night, in the middle of their happiness.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (SB 10.29.47): 'Krishna vanished then and there'.

statements.claim: He did not leave them to punish them but to humble them, and to favor them.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (SB 10.29.47): 'to humble them and favor them'.

statements.claim: The flute had stopped; the place where he had stood still held his warmth, and the gopis stood speechless in the red moonlight.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric aftermath of the vanishing (10.29.47); no pack statement on the flute or the gopis' posture after the disappearance, contradicts nothing.

statements.claim: The moon had not dimmed and the forest had not changed; only he was gone.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric close consistent with 10.30.1-3 (the gopis left searching), no factual assertion needing source.

DKS_0098.notes: Core claims (moon, flute summons, house-bound gopis, pride, vanishing, motive) map to SB 10.29.1-8, 47.

statements.claim: When the gopis finally reached Krishna that autumn night, he greeted them with a smile and a question: "You are welcome. What can I do for you? Is all well in Vraja? Tell me why you have come."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.17-18: 'svāgataṃ vo mahā-bhāgāḥ priyaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ / vrajasyānāmayaṃ kaccid brūtāgamana-kāraṇam'. The 'autumn night' setting is traditional rasa-lila framing not stated in the pack passage (see notes).

statements.claim: "This night is fearsome, and full of fierce creatures. It is not right for women to be here. Go back to Vraja."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.18: 'rajany eṣā ghora-rūpā ghora-sattva-niṣevitā / pratiyāta vrajaṃ neha stheyaṃ strībhiḥ'.

statements.claim: "Your mothers and fathers, your sons and brothers and husbands, are searching for you, and they cannot find you. Do not bring such distress on your own family."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.19: 'mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ / vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṃ bandhu-sādhvasam'.

statements.claim: He pointed to the forest — the flowering trees lit by the full moon, the Yamuna's breeze moving through the leaves.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.20: 'dṛṣṭaṃ vanaṃ kusumitaṃ rākeśa-kara-rañjitam / yamunānila-līlaijat taru-pallava-śobhitam'.

statements.claim: "Return to the settlement without delay. Serve your husbands. The calves and the little ones are crying; go milk the cows and feed them."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.21: 'tad yāta mā ciraṃ goṣṭhaṃ śuśrūṣadhvaṃ patīn satīḥ / krandanti vatsā bālāś ca tān pāyayata duhyata'.

statements.claim: "If it is love for me that has bound your hearts and brought you here, that is only fitting — for every living thing finds its joy in me."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.22: 'atha vā mad-abhisnehād bhavatyo yantritāśayāḥ / āgatā hy upapannaṃ vaḥ prīyante mayi jantavaḥ'.

statements.claim: "The highest duty of a woman is to serve her husband faithfully, to do good to her own people, and to care for those who depend on her."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.23: 'bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ paro dharmo hy amāyayā / tad-bandhūnāṃ ca kalyāṇaḥ prajānāṃ cānupoṣaṇam'.

statements.claim: "A wife must not leave her husband — not even one who is ill-tempered, or unlucky, or old, or dull, or sick, or poor."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.24: 'duḥśīlo durbhago vṛddho jaḍo rogy adhano 'pi vā / patiḥ strībhir na hātavyo lokepsubhir apātakī'.

statements.claim: "A love outside marriage brings no heaven and no honor; it is trifling and painful and feared, and it disgraces a woman of good family."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.25: 'asvargyam ayaśasyaṃ ca phalgu kṛcchraṃ bhayāvaham / jugupsitaṃ ca sarvatra hy aupapatyaṃ kula-striyaḥ'.

statements.claim: "Love for me is born of hearing about me, and seeing me, and meditating on me, and speaking of me. It is not born of standing near me."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.26: 'śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo 'nukīrtanāt / na tathā sannikarṣeṇa pratiyāta tato gṛhān'.

statements.claim: Their hopes broke, a grief they could not cross settled over them; they stood with faces turned down, lips dried with sighing, tracing lines in the earth with their toes, wiping away tears that streaked the vermilion on their chests, saying nothing.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.27-28: 'viṣaṇṇā bhagna-saṅkalpāś cintām āpur duratyayām / kṛtvā mukhāny ava śucaḥ śvasanena śuṣyad bimbādharāṇi caraṇena bhuvaḥ likhantyaḥ / asrair upātta-masibhiḥ kuca-kuṅkumāni tasthur mṛjantya uru-duḥkha-bharāḥ sma tūṣṇīm'.

statements.claim: One of them answered: "Do not speak such cruel words. We have left behind every pleasure we had, and come to your feet. Accept us, your own devotees. Do not cast us off — the way the ancient Lord receives those who long for freedom."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.31: 'maivaṃ vibho 'rhati bhavān gadituṃ nṛ-śaṃsaṃ santyajya sarva-viṣayāṃs tava pāda-mūlam / bhaktā bhajasva duravagraha mā tyajāsmān devo yathādi-puruṣo bhajate mumukṣūn'.

statements.claim: "You, who understand duty, have told us that a woman's dharma is to serve her husband and her children and her people. Let it be so. But you are the dearest of all who have bodies; you are our friend, our very self. Of what use to us are husbands and sons, who bring only sorrow? Do not cut down the hope we have carried for you so long, O lotus-eyed one."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.32: 'yat paty-apatya-suhṛdām anuvṛttir aṅga strīṇāṃ sva-dharma iti dharma-vidā tvayoktam / astv evam etad ... preṣṭho bhavāṃs tanu-bhṛtāṃ kila bandhur ātmā ... nitya-priye pati-sutādibhir ārti-daiḥ kim ... mā sma chindyā āśāṃ dhṛtāṃ tvayi cirād aravinda-netra'.

statements.claim: "Our minds have been carried away by you; they cannot go back into our houses. Our hands no longer do the work of the house, and our feet will not move from the foot of your feet. How shall we go back to Vraja? What would we do there?"
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.33: 'cittaṃ sukhena bhavatāpahṛtaṃ gṛheṣu yan nirviśaty uta karāv api gṛhya-kṛtye / pādau padaṃ na calatas tava pāda-mūlād yāmaḥ kathaṃ vrajam atho karavāma kiṃ vā'.

statements.claim: "Quench the fire that your smiling glance and your sweet songs have lit in our hearts — or else we will be burned up by the pain of missing you, and reach your feet only through our meditation on you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.34: 'siñcāṅga nas tvad-adharāmṛta-pūrakeṇa hāsāvaloka-kala-gīta-ja-hṛc-chayāgnim / no ced vayaṃ virahajāgny-upayukta-dehā dhyānena yāma padayoḥ padavīṃ sakhe te'.

statements.claim: "What woman in the three worlds, hearing the song of your flute, could keep to the path of the good and not come running? Seeing your face with its smiling eyes and dark curls, your arms that grant fearlessness, your chest that is the home of fortune herself — place your lotus hand upon our heads. You take away the fears of Vraja, the friend of the afflicted."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.38-40: 'vīkṣyālakāvṛta-mukhaṃ ... hasitāvalokam / dattābhayaṃ ca bhuja-daṇḍa-yugaṃ vilokya vakṣaḥ śriyaika-ramaṇaṃ ca bhavāma dāsyaḥ / kā stry aṅga te kala-padāyata-veṇu-gīta-sammohitārya-caritān na calet tri-lokyām / vyaktaṃ bhavān vraja-bhayārti-haro ... tan no nidhehi kara-paṅkajam ārta-bandho ... kiṅkarīṇām'.

DKS_0100.notes: Nearly every clause of Krishna's speech and the gopis' reply maps to SB 10.29.17-41. 'Autumn night' is traditional rasa-lila seasonal framing not stated in the pack passage — flagged as connective narration, not contradicted by the pack.

statements.claim: Across the dark water of the Yamuna the gopis were calling his name, and Krishna listened for a long while before he moved.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting before SB 10.29.42 ('tābhiḥ sametābhir' — with them gathered); the gopis' calling/grieving is the immediately preceding content of 10.29.28-41.

statements.claim: These were the milkmaids of Vrindavan who had left their homes at the sound of his flute and followed him to the river on a full-moon night.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.2-7 (in the adjacent pack): flute song summoning the vraja-striyaḥ on the full-moon night, minds seized, homes abandoned.

statements.claim: Earlier that evening he had hidden from them, to test them, to see whether their devotion could survive his silence.
statements.evidence: The pack's own narrative has Krishna present and speaking throughout the test (SB 10.29.16-27: he welcomed them and told them to return; 10.29.16 'avavadad vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vācaḥ peśair vimohayan' — the best of speakers spoke, charming them with words). He hid neither in silence nor by absence; his vanishing comes only later at 10.29.47. The story conflates the verbal test with the later disappearance.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: They had not turned back and gone home; they had only grieved and gone on calling for him, and it was that grief that moved him at last.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.28-41: the gopis, refusing to leave, lament and plead; 10.29.42-46 then shows him relenting and consoling them ('tābhiḥ sametābhir udāra-ceṣṭitaḥ ... priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir acyutaḥ').

statements.claim: The verses are careful to say he was already self-satisfied, already full, and that nothing he did that night came from any need of his own; yet he smiled a smile of favor and showed them grace.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Krishna, though self-satisfied, smilingly showed them favor and enjoyed himself with them'; SB 10.29.46: 'evaṃ bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇāl labdha-mānā mahātmanaḥ'.

statements.claim: He came down to the cool, sandy bank of the river, into the soft light of the full moon.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.44: 'nadyāḥ pulinam āviśya gopībhir hima-vālukam' — entering the river's sandbank, cool with sand, with the gopis.

statements.claim: The moment they saw him their faces opened like flowers; they sang to him and he sang with them, one voice answering another, a hundred voices braided together.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.42-43: 'priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir' — faces blossoming at the sight of the beloved; 'upagīyamāna udgāyan vanitā-śata-yūthapaḥ' — sung to, himself singing, leader of a hundred women.

statements.claim: He spread his arms wide and drew them near, and the verses say he embraced them and returned their affection with the light play of his fingertips — laughter, a hand at the fold of a garment.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.45: 'bāhu-prasāra-parirambha-karālakoru nīvī-stanālabhana-narma-nakhāgra-pātaiḥ' — outstretched arms, embraces, touching of garment-knots, play, nail-tips.

statements.claim: The verses record only that it happened, on the bank of the Yamuna, on sand that stayed cool through the night.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.42-46; 'hima-vālukam' (cool sand) at 10.29.44.

statements.claim: These women, who moments before had believed themselves abandoned, now felt themselves the most blessed women alive — not because they had earned him, but because he had chosen to come back to them.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'the gopis thought themselves the most blessed of women'; SB 10.29.46: 'labdha-mānā' — having obtained his honor/favor.

corrections.original_sentence: Earlier that evening he had hidden from them, to test them, to see whether their devotion could survive his silence.
corrections.suggested: Earlier that evening he had tested them, sending them back with words meant to turn them away, to see whether their devotion could survive his refusal.

DKS_0101.notes: One CONTRADICTED: the story says Krishna tested the gopis by hiding in silence, but the pack (10.29.16-27) has him present and testing them verbally; his vanishing belongs to 10.29.47 (next story). Everything else maps to 10.29.42-46.

statements.claim: One moment he was there among them; the next, the gopis turned and he was gone — no word, no warning.
statements.evidence: The disappearance is the established preceding event (SB 10.29.47, prev story DKS_0098); 10.30.1-3 opens with the gopis' frantic search.

statements.claim: They went into the forest like women out of their minds, searching from wood to wood and singing his name aloud.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.3: 'gāyantya uccair amum eva saṃhatā vicikyur unmattaka-vad vanād vanam'.

statements.claim: As they searched they took on his very manner — his walk, his smile, the way he glanced, the sweet way he spoke — until each gopi seemed to carry a little of him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.1-2: 'gatyānurāga-smita-vibhramekṣitair mano-ramālāpa-vihāra-vibhramaiḥ / gati-smita-prekṣaṇa-bhāṣaṇādiṣu priyāḥ priyasya pratirūḍha-mūrtayaḥ' — in gait, smile, glance and speech they embodied the beloved's form.

statements.claim: They questioned the trees — the ashvattha, the plaksha and the great banyan — asking: have you seen Nanda's son, the one who stole our hearts with his smiles?
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.4: 'dṛṣṭo vaḥ kaccid aśvattha plakṣa nyagrodha no manaḥ'; the question's wording per pack excerpt: 'Have you seen Nanda's son, who stole our hearts with his smiles?'

statements.claim: They turned to the flowering trees — the ashoka, the kurabaka, the champaka, the nagakesara and the punnaga — and to the tulasi plant, which they called the one beloved of Govinda's feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.5-6: 'kaccit kurabakāśoka-nāga-punnāga-campakāḥ / kaccit tulasi kalyāṇi govinda-caraṇa-priye'.

statements.claim: They asked the mango, the jackfruit, the kadamba, the bilva, the bakula and the nipa, the jasmine and the creepers that twine up the trunks, which the verses picture throwing their arms around a great tree like a friend embracing a friend.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.7-8: 'mālaty adarśi vaḥ kaccin mallike jāti-yūthike / cūta-priyāla-panasāsana-kovidāra jambv-arka-bilva-bakulāmra-kadamba-nīpāḥ'; 10.30.12: 'pṛcchatemā latā bāhūn apy āśliṣṭā vanaspateḥ'.

statements.claim: They turned on the earth itself and demanded to know what penance it had performed that the mere touch of his feet should make it blossom — whether it was his stride or the touch of his feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.9: 'kiṃ te kṛtaṃ kṣiti tapo bata keśavāṅghri-sparśotsavotpulakitāṅga-nahair vibhāsi / apy aṅghri-sambhava urukrama-vikramād vā'.

statements.claim: They asked the doe whether Krishna had come this way — his arm on a beloved's shoulder, a lotus in his hand, the tulasi garland around his neck with bees drunk on its scent, the jasmine garland carrying the perfume of the one he loved — and whether the trees had bowed to him, honored by his loving glance.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.10-11: 'apy eṇa-patny upagataḥ priyayeha ... kāntāṅga-saṅga-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ kunda-srajaḥ kula-pater iha vāti gandhaḥ / bāhuṃ priyāṃsa upadhāya gṛhīta-padmo rāmānujas tulasikāli-kulair madāndhaiḥ / anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṃ kiṃ vābhinandati caran praṇayāvalokaiḥ'.

statements.claim: The forest kept its silence; the trees held their branches still, and the gopis went on from tree to tree, calling the question again and again, because asking was the only thing left to do.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric close to the questioning passage (10.30.1-12); the text records no answers from the trees, so the silence is consistent — no factual assertion needing source.

DKS_0102.notes: All tree-by-tree questioning maps to SB 10.30.1-12, including the exact tree lists and the doe/earth questions.

statements.claim: Still searching and calling Krishna's name, the gopis began to enact his deeds in the forest, for no audience but the trees and the moon.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.13: 'ity unmatta-vaco gopyaḥ kṛṣṇānveṣaṇa-kātarāḥ' — speaking thus madly, distressed in the search; the enactments follow in 10.30.14-22.

statements.claim: The verses call their words the words of the frantic.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.13: 'unmatta-vacaḥ' — words of the frantic.

statements.claim: One woman played Putana, the demoness who had come to the village disguised as a wet-nurse with poison on her breast to kill the infant Krishna, and another played Krishna and drank at her breast, having drawn out the demon's very life with the milk.
statements.evidence: Enactment: SB 10.30.14: 'kasyācit pūtanāyantyāḥ kṛṣṇāyanty apibat stanam'. The Putana backstory (wet-nurse disguise, poisoned breast, life sucked out with the milk) matches the earlier corpus episode SB 10.6 and is framed in the story as 'the story they had all heard'.

statements.claim: Another took the part of the demon who had come as a wooden cart to crush the sleeping child: she carried off a gopi playing the baby Krishna, who kicked out with a small foot and overturned the cart, the way the real Krishna once had.
statements.evidence: Enactment: SB 10.30.15: 'daityāyitvā jahārānyām eko kṛṣṇārbha-bhāvanām'. The śakaṭāsura backstory (10.7: demon as a cart; baby Krishna struck it with his foot) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: Two of them became Krishna and Balarama, and around them other gopis became the cowherd boys, calling to one another the way the herders did at pasture.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.16-17: 'kṛṣṇa-rāmāyite dve tu gopāyantyaś ca kāścana / āhūya dūra-gā yadvat kṛṣṇas tam anuvartatīm'.

statements.claim: One raised her arm high above her head, the way Krishna had raised the hill of Govardhana on a single finger to shelter the village from the storm, and called out: do not fear the wind or the rain; I have made you a shelter.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.18-19: 'kasyāñcit sva-bhujaṃ nyasya calanty āhāparā nanu / mā bhaiṣṭa vāta-varṣābhyāṃ tat-trāṇaṃ vihitaṃ maya'. Govardhana backstory (10.25) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: One climbed up onto another and stamped down with her foot, as Krishna had once danced upon the hoods of the serpent Kaliya in the river's poisoned waters.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.20: 'āruhyaikā padākramya śirasy āhāparāṃ nṛpa'. Kaliya episode (10.16-17) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: Another pointed into the distance and cried: O cowherds, see the fierce forest fire — the fire Krishna had once swallowed whole to save them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.21: 'tatraikovāca he gopā dāvāgniṃ paśyatolbaṇam'. The swallowing of the forest fire (10.19) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: One slim gopi sat down and let herself be tied with a garland of flowers to a tree, the way the child Krishna had been tied by his mother to the grinding mortar for his mischief, and had slipped free even then.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.22: 'baddhānyayā srajā kācit tanvī tatra ulūkhale' — the slim gopi was tied there at a grinding MORTAR (ulūkhala) with a garland, not to a tree. Krishna's own binding (10.9) was likewise to the mortar. The story's own visual_elements field says 'the tied child and the grinding mortar', so 'to a tree' is an internal inconsistency as well.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: Through it all they went on asking the trees and creepers of Vrindavan: have you seen him?
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.23: 'evaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pṛcchamānā vrṇdāvana-latās tarūn'.

corrections.original_sentence: And one slim gopi sat down and let herself be tied with a garland of flowers to a tree, the way the child Krishna had been tied by his mother to the grinding mortar for his mischief, and had slipped free even then.
corrections.suggested: One slim gopi sat down and let herself be tied with a garland of flowers at a grinding mortar, the way the child Krishna had been tied by his mother to the mortar for his mischief, and had slipped free even then.

DKS_0103.notes: One CONTRADICTED: the gopi bound herself at a mortar (SB 10.30.22 'ulūkhale'), not to a tree. All six enactments (Putana, cart, Krishna-Balarama, Govardhana, Kaliya, forest fire) map to SB 10.30.13-22; childhood backstories match earlier corpus episodes (10.6, 10.7, 10.25, 10.16, 10.19, 10.9).

statements.claim: In the soft earth the footprints stopped them; they knew them at once: the marks of Nanda's son.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.24: 'padāni vyaktam etāni nanda-sūnor mahātmanaḥ'.

statements.claim: Beside Krishna's footprints ran another set, smaller and lighter — the steps of one of their own — and where the two went on together the ground was pressed deeper, as though he had carried her.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.26: 'kasyāḥ padāni caitāni yātāyā nanda-sūnunā'; 10.30.30: 'imāny adhika-magnāni padāni vahato vadhūm' — deeper prints of one carrying the bride.

statements.claim: Here flowers had been gathered — picked for her, by him — and here a woman's hair had been dressed by careful hands.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.31-32: 'atra prasūnāvacayaḥ priyārthe preyasā kṛtaḥ / keśa-prasādhanaṃ tv atra kāminyāḥ kāminā kṛtam'.

statements.claim: The gopis called the dust of those footprints blessed: blessed is the dust of Govinda's feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.28: 'dhanyā aho amī ālyo govindāṅghry-abja-reṇavaḥ'.

statements.claim: The verses do not say the others were angry; they say they marveled and ached — this woman must have worshiped him as no one else had, for him to single her out; he had taken her aside and kept her to himself in the deep of the forest.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.27: 'anayārādhito nūnaṃ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ'; 10.30.29: 'tasyā amūni naḥ kṣobhaṃ kurvanty uccaiḥ padāni yat yaikāpahṛtya gopīnām raho bhunkte 'cyutādharam' — her footprints agitate us, for she, taken apart from the gopis, enjoys Acyuta's lips in private.

statements.claim: The verses add that though he is self-delighted and self-satisfied, whole in himself and undivided, he had enjoyed her company all the same.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.33: 'reme tayā cātma-rata ātmārāmo 'py akhaṇḍitaḥ'.

statements.claim: The one he had chosen began to think herself the greatest of all women.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.35: 'sā ca mene tadātmānaṃ variṣṭhaṃ sarva-yoṣitām'.

statements.claim: When she found Krishna waiting in a farther part of the forest, she told him she was tired — that she could not walk — and that he should carry her wherever he chose.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.36: 'tato gatvā vanoddeśaṃ dṛptā keśavam abravīt'; pack excerpt: 'asked Krishna to carry her'; the request's content is implied by 10.30.37 'skandha āruhyatām iti' — climb onto my shoulder.

statements.claim: Krishna answered: Climb onto my shoulder, and I will take you.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.37: 'evam uktaḥ priyām āha skandha āruhyatām iti'.

statements.claim: At the very moment she would have settled onto his shoulder, Krishna was gone — vanished into the air, leaving her with nothing under her hands.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'when he took her on his shoulder he vanished again, and she repented'.

statements.claim: The verses give her cry: O lord, O my beloved, where are you, where are you, mighty-armed one? The forest gave back no answer.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.38: 'hā nātha ramaṇa preṣṭha kvāsi kvāsi mahā-bhuja'.

statements.claim: She had been lifted to the highest place of all, and she had thought it was her own. Now she stood alone, and understood.
statements.evidence: Interpretive close consistent with pack excerpt ('she repented') and verse 35 (her pride); no separate factual assertion.

DKS_0104.notes: All plot points (footprints, deeper prints, flowers, hair-dressing, marveling, pride, request to be carried, second vanishing, cry) map to SB 10.30.24-39.

statements.claim: Krishna reappeared among the gopis smiling, his face bright and open as a lotus.
statements.evidence: Bhav. Purana 10.32.1: 'tāsām āvirabhūc chauriḥ smayamāna-mukhāmbujaḥ' (Krishna appeared with a smiling lotus-face).

statements.claim: The gopis rose at once as if their very life had returned; their grief of separation was dispelled.
statements.evidence: 10.32.2, 8-9 and pack excerpt: 'they all rose at once as if their very life had returned... grief of separation was dispelled.'

statements.claim: Each gopi received him in her own way: one held his hand in folded palms, one took the betel he had been chewing, one knit her brows in loving anger, one gazed unblinking, one held him in her heart with closed eyes.
statements.evidence: 10.32.3-7: 'kācit karāmbujaṃ... jagṛhe 'ñjalinā mudā'; 'kācid añjalināgṛhṇāt tanvī tāmbūla-carvitam'; 'ekā bhru-kuṭim ābadhya prema-saṃrambha-vihvalā'; 'aparānimiṣad-dṛgbhyāṃ juṣāṇā'; 'taṃ kācin netra-randhreṇa hṛdi kṛtvā nimīlya.'

statements.claim: Krishna led them to the bright sandbank of the Yamuna; it was autumn with a full moon whose light dispelled darkness.
statements.evidence: 10.32.10-11: 'tāḥ samādāya kālindyā nirviśya pulinaṃ... śarac-candrāṃśu-sandoha-dhvasta-doṣā-tamaḥ.'

statements.claim: Their longings came to rest the way the ancient scriptures come to rest at their end.
statements.evidence: 10.32.12: 'manorathāntaṃ śrutayo yathā yayuḥ' (their desires ended as the śrutis do).

statements.claim: He sat on the seat the gopis had prepared for him in their own hearts, he the master of every master of yoga.
statements.evidence: 10.32.13: 'tatropaviṣṭo bhagavān sa īśvaro yogeśvarāntar-hṛdi kalpitāsanaḥ.'

statements.claim: They welcomed him with smiles, sidelong glances and the play of their brows.
statements.evidence: 10.32.14: 'sahāsa-līlekṣaṇa-vibhrama-bhruvā.'

statements.claim: Krishna had vanished twice before, and the gopis had searched the forest in endless grief.
statements.evidence: Not stated in 10.32.1-14 itself, but consistent with the corpus chain (previous story DKS_0104 'The Favored Gopi's Pride and Krishna's Second Vanishing').

statements.claim: Krishna did not explain his vanishing, and the gopis did not ask.
statements.evidence: True of the passage 10.32.1-14, which moves straight to the reunion and the return to the Yamuna sandbank.

DKS_0105.notes: All named gestures, the setting and the moonlit sandbank map directly to 10.32.1-14. The 'vanished twice' is chain-referencing connective narration, consistent with DKS_0104.

statements.claim: On the moonlit Yamuna sandbank the gopis asked Krishna why he loves those who love him and yet seems to hold back.
statements.evidence: 10.32.15-16 ('śrī-gopya ūcuḥ') and pack summary: 'When the gopis asked why he loves those who love him, Krishna explained the ways of love.'

statements.claim: Some people serve those who do not serve them back, like compassionate parents serving a child.
statements.evidence: 10.32.17: 'bhajanty abhajato ye vai karuṇāḥ pitarau yathā.'

statements.claim: Others, even when served, do not serve in return; nothing can be expected from them.
statements.evidence: 10.32.18: 'bhajato 'pi na vai kecid bhajanty abhajataḥ kutaḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna said he is like neither: he does not repay service like a trader settling accounts, but acts to deepen the love of those who serve him.
statements.evidence: 10.32.19: 'nāhaṃ tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantūn bhajāmy amīṣām anuvṛtti-vṛttaye.'

statements.claim: The gopis had cast aside the world and even the scriptures' obligations for his sake.
statements.evidence: 10.32.20: 'evaṃ mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda svānām hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye.'

statements.claim: Krishna said he could not repay them even with the lifespan of the gods.
statements.evidence: 10.32.21: 'na pāraye 'haṃ niravadya-saṃyujāṃ sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṃ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ.'

statements.claim: Their goodness returned to them of itself; the love they gave was already its own reward.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'their love for him... could never be repaid, but that it returned to them of itself.'

statements.claim: He did not answer with a doctrine but with the way love behaves.
statements.evidence: Framing of the teaching in 10.32.17-21; matches the passage's form (a description of how love acts).

DKS_0106.notes: Teaching claims track 10.32.15-21 closely, including the parent/child simile and the 'lifespan of the gods' line. No unsupported or contradicted statements.

statements.claim: A stranger came into Vrindavan wearing Achyuta's dress and ornaments, so that the gopis asked 'Who is this of wondrous beauty?'
statements.evidence: 10.47.1: 'ko 'yam apīvya-darśanaḥ... acyuta-veṣa-bhūṣaṇaḥ' and 'su-vismitāḥ... parivavrur utsukāḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis received him with humility, shy smiles, sidelong glances and gentle words before he spoke.
statements.evidence: 10.47.2: 'taṃ praśrayeṇāvanatāḥ su-sat-kṛtaṃ sa-vrīḍa-hāsekṣaṇa-sūnṛtādibhiḥ.'

statements.claim: They recognized him as the attendant of the lord of the Yadavas, sent out of love; otherwise nothing in the cowherd settlement would be worth his remembering.
statements.evidence: 10.47.3-4: 'jānīmas tvāṃ yadu-pateḥ pārṣadaṃ samupāgatam / anyathā go-vraje tasya smaraṇīyaṃ na cakṣmahe.' Pack excerpt: 'sent by Krishna for love of his parents.'

statements.claim: The world's friendships are purposeful: a courtesan abandons a penniless man, subjects abandon a helpless king, birds forsake a fruitless tree, guests leave a house once the meal is done.
statements.evidence: 10.47.5-7: 'niḥsvaṃ tyajanti gaṇikā akalpaṃ nṛpatiṃ prajāḥ / khagā vīta-phalaṃ vṛkṣaṃ bhuktvā cātithayo gṛham.'

statements.claim: The gopis alone did not let go: with speech, body and mind fixed on Govinda, they sang his deeds and wept with all shame gone.
statements.evidence: 10.47.8-9: 'gopyo hi govinde gata-vāk-kāya-mānasāḥ / gāyantyaḥ prīya-karmāṇi rudantyaś ca gata-hriyaḥ.'

statements.claim: For months they had lived in the stillness of his absence.
statements.evidence: No duration is given in 10.47.1-9; 'months' is vague connective framing, consistent with the wider timeline (10.47.53: Uddhava later stays 'katicin māsān').

statements.claim: The settlement had been quiet since Krishna left, the flute silent.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere; matches the mood of separation in 10.47.1-9.

DKS_0108.notes: All substantive claims (identity of the stranger, the greeting, the world's purposive friendships, the gopis' unbroken love) map to 10.47.1-9. The 'for months' duration is unsourced but vague, non-specific connective framing.

statements.claim: A gopi meditating on union with Krishna saw a honeybee settle near her and addressed it as a messenger.
statements.evidence: 10.47.10: 'kācin madhukaraṃ dṛṣṭvā dhyāyantī kṛṣṇa-saṅgamam.'

statements.claim: 'O bee, friend of the cheat, do not touch my feet' — she took it for a courier marked with the saffron of garlands crushed on other women's breasts, sent to mock her before the Yadu assembly.
statements.evidence: 10.47.11: 'madhupa kitava-bandho mā spṛśaṅghriṃ sapatnyāḥ... kuca-vilulita-mālā-kuṅkuma-śmaśrubhir naḥ... yadu-sadasi viḍambyaṃ yasya dūtas tvam īdṛk.'

statements.claim: He made them drink once the nectar of his lips and then abandoned them like cast-off flowers; she tells him to carry his favor to the proud women who now have him.
statements.evidence: 10.47.11-12: 'sakṛd adhara-sudhāṃ svāṃ mohinīṃ pāyayitvā... sumanasa iva sadyas tatyaje 'smān' and 'vahatu madhu-patis tan-māninīnāṃ prasādaṃ.'

statements.claim: She asks how the goddess of fortune serves his lotus feet though her heart too was stolen by his praises.
statements.evidence: 10.47.12: 'paricarati kathaṃ tat-pāda-padmaṃ nu padmā... hṛta-cetā... uttamaḥ-śloka-jalpaiḥ.'

statements.claim: She says enough of friendship with the dark one, though his stories can never be let go.
statements.evidence: 10.47.16: 'tad alam asita-sakhyair dustyajas tat-kathārthaḥ.'

statements.claim: Others who tasted a single drop of the nectar of his deeds abandoned home and family and wander like birds.
statements.evidence: 10.47.17: 'yad-anucarita-līlā-karṇa-pīyūṣa-vipruṭ-... gṛha-kuṭumbaṃ dīnam utsṛjya dīnā bahava iha vihaṅgā bhikṣu-caryāṃ caranti.'

statements.claim: We trusted him as a deer trusts a hunter's call and have felt the sharp hurt of longing again and again.
statements.evidence: 10.47.18: 'vayam ṛtam iva jihma-vyāhṛtaṃ śraddadhānāḥ kulika-rutam ivājñāḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo hariṇyaḥ... tan-nakha-sparśa-tīvra smara-ruja.'

statements.claim: If the bee is truly sent by her beloved it is to be honored and may choose what it wants, but how can it carry them back to one whose side none can leave and on whose chest Sri sits as bride?
statements.evidence: 10.47.19: 'priya-sakha punar āgāḥ preyasā preṣitaḥ kiṃ varaya... mānanīyo 'si me 'ṅga / nayasi katham ihāsmān dustyaja-dvandva-pārśvaṃ satatam urasi saumya śrīr vadhūḥ sākam āste.'

statements.claim: She asks whether he still dwells in the city of Madhu, remembers his father's house, kinsmen and the cowherds, ever speaks of his maidservants, and when he will place his aloe-fragrant arm on her head.
statements.evidence: 10.47.20: 'api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro 'dhunāste $ smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṃś ca gopān... kiṅkarīṇāṃ gṛṇīte % bhujam aguru-sugandhaṃ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu.'

statements.claim: The gopi did not expect the bee to answer; the question was for the absent Krishna.
statements.evidence: Narrative inference from the monologue form of 10.47.10-20; no sourceable fact asserted.

DKS_0109.notes: The lament maps verse-by-verse to 10.47.10-20 (Bhramara-gita); all reproaches, similes and closing questions are supported.

statements.claim: Uddhava came from Krishna bearing a message from his own mouth, sent for this purpose.
statements.evidence: 10.47.27: 'śrūyatāṃ priya-sandeśo bhavatīnāṃ sukhāvahaḥ' (hear the dear message bringing you happiness).

statements.claim: Before the message, Uddhava praised the gopis: through gifts, vows, austerities, sacrifice, japa, study and self-control they had offered sons, husbands, bodies, kinsmen and homes to a single love and become peerless.
statements.evidence: 10.47.23-26: 'dāna-vrata-tapo-homa japa-svādhyāya-saṃyamaiḥ... diṣṭyā putrān patīn dehān sva-janān bhavanāni ca... anuttamā.'

statements.claim: Krishna's message: he pervades all beings as the elements do; he creates, preserves and destroys by himself, being pure knowledge untouched by the gunas; fix your mind wholly on him and you will soon attain him.
statements.evidence: 10.47.29-35 and pack excerpt: 'My separation from you is never complete, as ether, air, fire, water and earth pervade all beings... fix your mind wholly on me and you will soon attain me.'

statements.claim: This was the whole conclusion of the scriptures, of yoga and of the wise.
statements.evidence: 10.47.32: 'etad-antaḥ samāmnāyo yogaḥ sāṅkhyaṃ manīṣiṇām.'

statements.claim: He reminded them it was he who had played with them at night in the forest of Vraja.
statements.evidence: 10.47.36: 'yā mayā krīḍatā rātryāṃ vane 'smin vraja āsthitāḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis answered that Govinda could not forget the moonlit nights in Vrindavan, the groves white with kumuda and kunda, the rasa dance with ankle-bells ringing.
statements.evidence: 10.47.42: 'vṛndāvane kumuda-kunda-śaśāṅka-ramye reme kvaṇac-caraṇa-nūpura-rāsa-goṣṭhyām.'

statements.claim: Will the Dasarha come back, scorched by a sorrow of his own making? He has won a kingdom and slain his enemies; what are we forest-dwellers to that great soul?
statements.evidence: 10.47.43-45: 'apy eṣyatīha dāśārhas taptāḥ sva-kṛtayā śucā / kasmāt kṛṣṇa ihāyāti prāpta-rājyo hatāhitaḥ / kim asmābhir vanaukobhir anyābhir vā mahātmanaḥ.'

statements.claim: Who could bear to give up the memory of him? The rivers, hills, forest paths, cows and the flute's sound call back the son of Nanda again and again.
statements.evidence: 10.47.47-49: 'ka utsaheta santyaktum uttamaḥśloka-saṃvidam / saric-chaila-vanoddeśā gāvo veṇu-ravā ime / punaḥ punaḥ smārayanti nanda-gopa-sutaṃ bata.'

statements.claim: 'O lord, O lord of Rama, O lord of Vraja, remover of sorrows.'
statements.evidence: 10.47.51 reads 'he nātha he ramā-nātha vraja-nāthārti-nāśana' — 'ramā-nātha' is lord of Ramā (Lakshmi); the story's 'lord of Rama' (no diacritics) is a transliteration nuance, not a different claim.

statements.claim: Uddhava was Krishna's friend and counsellor, a man of learning and restraint.
statements.evidence: Characterization consistent with the passage (he delivers Krishna's private, theologically dense message and later consoles the gopis), though not literally stated in 10.47.21-51.

statements.claim: For months the women of Vrindavan had grieved; they had even pleaded with a bee, mistaking it for a courier.
statements.evidence: The bee episode is the immediately preceding story (DKS_0109, 10.47.10-20), linked in the corpus chain; 'for months' is connective duration framing.

DKS_0110.notes: Message and reply both track 10.47.21-51. Minor note: 'O lord of Rama' renders 'ramā-nātha' (lord of Lakshmi) without diacritics — ambiguous transliteration, not a substantive error.

statements.claim: Uddhava stayed some months in Vrindavan, dispelling the gopis' sorrow.
statements.evidence: 10.47.53: 'uvāsa katicin māsān gopīnāṃ vinudan śucaḥ.'

statements.claim: Day by day he walked the country, seeing the rivers, forests, mountain valleys and flowering trees, and the gopis' minds agitated with absorption in Krishna.
statements.evidence: 10.47.55-56: 'sarid-vana-giri-droṇīr vīkṣan kusumitān drumān / ... gopīnāṃ kṛṣṇāveśātma-viklavam.'

statements.claim: He declared the cowherd women have reached the highest place: their hearts are fixed on Govinda, the soul of all; what use are brahmana births against the taste of his endless stories?
statements.evidence: 10.47.57: 'etāḥ paraṃ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo govinda eva nikhilātmani rūḍha-bhāvāḥ... kiṃ brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathā-rasasya.'

statements.claim: Where are these forest women and where is the supreme self — yet the Lord grants his highest good even to the ignorant who serve him, like a king of medicines.
statements.evidence: 10.47.58: 'kvemāḥ striyo vana-carīr... kṛṣṇe kva caiṣa paramātmani... nanv īśvaro 'nubhajato 'viduṣo 'pi sākṣāc chreyas tanoty agada-rāja ivopayuktaḥ.'

statements.claim: The favor of being held in Krishna's arms at the rasa festival was given to the Vraja women, a blessing not granted even to Sri or the lotus-fragrant heavenly women.
statements.evidence: 10.47.59: 'nāyaṃ śriyo 'ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ svar-yoṣitāṃ nalina-gandha-rucāṃ kuto 'nyāḥ / rāsotsave 'sya bhuja-daṇḍa-gṛhīta-kaṇṭha-labdhāśiṣāṃ ya udagād vraja-vallabhīnām.'

statements.claim: These women threw away their families and the path of the Āryas for the path the scriptures search out.
statements.evidence: 10.47.60: 'yā dustyajaṃ sva-janam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā bhejur mukunda-padavīṃ śrutibhir vimṛgyām.'

statements.claim: He wished: 'May I become any shrub, creeper or herb in Vrindavan, blessed by the dust of these gopis' feet,' bowing to that foot-dust again and again.
statements.evidence: 10.47.60-62: 'āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṃ syāṃ vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām' and 'vande nanda-vraja-strīṇāṃ pāda-reṇum abhīkṣṇaśaḥ.'

statements.claim: He comforted Nanda, Yashoda and the cowherds, and they honored him, their wish that their minds rest at Krishna's lotus feet wherever their karma wanders them.
statements.evidence: 10.47.63-66: 'taṃ nirgataṃ samāsādya nānopāyana-pāṇayaḥ / manaso vṛttayo naḥ syuḥ kṛṣṇa pādāmbujāśrayāḥ / karmabhir bhrāmyamāṇānāṃ yatra kvāpīśvarecchayā.'

statements.claim: Bowing to Krishna he told him of the abundance of the Vraja-dwellers' devotion.
statements.evidence: 10.47.68: 'kṛṣṇāya praṇipatyāha bhakty-udrekaṃ vrajaukasām.'

statements.claim: They honored him as they would a brother.
statements.evidence: 10.47.67 says they honored him with Krishna-bhakti ('sabhājito gopaiḥ kṛṣṇa-bhaktyā'); the 'brother' warmth is connective hospitality framing, not contradicted.

DKS_0111.notes: Uddhava's praise, the shrub-wish, the farewell and the return to Mathura all map directly to 10.47.52-68.

statements.claim: Akrura had been sent by Kamsa, king of Mathura, to fetch Krishna and Balarama to the city.
statements.evidence: 10.38.6: 'kaṃso batādyākṛta me 'ty-anugrahaṃ... prahito 'munā hareḥ' (Kamsa showed grace by sending me [to see] Hari); the errand is the episode's premise, confirmed by the corpus chain (DKS_0114 'Akrura Reveals Kamsa's Plan').

statements.claim: On the road he wondered what merit or austerity had earned him the rare sight of Krishna.
statements.evidence: 10.38.2-3: 'kiṃ mayācaritaṃ bhadraṃ kiṃ taptaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ / mamaitad durlabhaṃ manya uttamaḥ-śloka-darśanam.'

statements.claim: Even Kamsa had unwittingly shown him grace by sending him.
statements.evidence: 10.38.6: 'kaṃso batādyākṛta me 'ty-anugrahaṃ drakṣye 'ṅghri-padmaṃ prahito 'munā hareḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna's feet are worshipped by Brahma, Shiva, the goddess of fortune, the sages and the Satvatas; they wandered the forest herding cows, marked with the gopis' saffron.
statements.evidence: 10.38.7: 'yad arcitaṃ brahma-bhavādibhiḥ suraiḥ śriyā ca devyā munibhiḥ sa-sātvataiḥ... go-cāraṇāyānucaraiś carad vane yad gopikānāṃ kuca-kuṅkumāṅkitam.'

statements.claim: Those feet give shelter to men fleeing the serpent of time, and at them Indra and Bali placed offerings and won the lordship of the three worlds.
statements.evidence: 10.38.15-16: 'dattābhayaṃ kāla-bhujāṅga-raṃhasā prodvejitānāṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇāṃ nṛṇām / samarhaṇaṃ yatra nidhāya kauśikas tathā baliś cāpa jagat-trayendratām.'

statements.claim: He imagined the face — fine cheeks and nose, smiling glance, eyes like red lotuses — of the Lord who descended of his own will into the Yadu line to lift the earth's burden.
statements.evidence: 10.38.8-9, 12: 'su-kapola-nāsikaṃ smitāvalokāruṇa-kañja-locanam... bhārāvatārāya bhuvo nijecchayā... sa cāvatīrṇaḥ kila satvatānvaye.'

statements.claim: He pictured Krishna's lotus hand on his head, the embrace of his two great arms, and the voice saying 'O Akrura,' which would make his birth fulfilled.
statements.evidence: 10.38.14-15, 19-20: 'patitasya me vibhuḥ śirasy adhāsyan nija-hasta-paṅkajam... dorbhyāṃ bṛhadbhyāṃ parirapsyate 'tha mām... māṃ vakṣyate 'krūra tatety uruśravāḥ.'

statements.claim: He feared Krishna, who sees within and without, might read the errand and turn away — but Krishna holds no favorite and no enemy.
statements.evidence: 10.38.17, 21: 'na mayy upaiṣyaty ari-buddhim acyutaḥ... viśva-dṛk... antarbahiś cetasa etad īhitaṃ kṣetra-jña īkṣaty amalena cakṣuṣā' and 'na tasya kaścid dayitaḥ suhṛttamo na cāpriyo dveṣya upekṣya eva vā.'

statements.claim: He dared to hope Balarama would embrace him too.
statements.evidence: 10.38.22: 'kiṃ cāgrajo māvanataṃ yadūttamaḥ smayan pariṣvajya gṛhītam añjalau.'

statements.claim: At Gokula as the day ended he came down from the chariot and saw the Lord's footprints marked with the lotus and other signs.
statements.evidence: 10.38.14 ('athāvarūḍhaḥ sapadīśayo rathāt') and pack excerpt: 'he arrived at Gokula at sunset, gazing at the footprints of the Lord marked with the lotus and other signs.'

statements.claim: The feet whose dust adorns the crowns of all the protectors of the worlds.
statements.evidence: 10.38.24 (same chapter, next story's pack): 'padāni tasyākhila-loka-pāla-kirīṭa-juṣṭāmala-pāda-reṇoḥ.'

DKS_0112.notes: Akrura's interior monologue maps verse-by-verse to 10.38.1-23; the foot-dust/crowns image is 10.38.24, the same chapter immediately following.

statements.claim: Akrura reached Vraja at evening — weak sun, tawny moon in the crimson sky, birds in their nests, cows home lowing with calves bound, milkmen calling the kine by name and kindling fires.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.80 (in pack): 'the sun, with weakened rays, set... the disc of the moon became tawny coloured, when the birds entered into their nests... the cows came back, and having their calves bound (to stakes)... the milk-men... began to call their kine by names... fire was set to dried cow-dung by Gopas.'

statements.claim: At the milking-place among the calves he saw two youths — one dark, one fair, big-armed and garlanded, feet marked with the flag, thunderbolt, goad and lotus.
statements.evidence: 10.38.27-30: 'dadarśa kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ ca vraje go-dohanaṃ gatau / kiśorau śyāmala-śvetau śrī-niketau bṛhad-bhujau / dhvaja-vajrāṅkuśāmbhojaiś cihnitair aṅghribhir vrajam... sragviṇau vana-mālinau.' Harivamsha: 'he saw Krishna stationed at the milking-place in the midst of calves.'

statements.claim: Krishna was dark as the leaf of a full-blown lotus; Balarama white as jasmine.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.17 (in pack): 'he saw Krishńa amongst the cattle, dark as the leaf of the full blown lotus... Akrúra also beheld there Balabhadra, white as a jasmine, a swan, or the moon.'

statements.claim: They stood at the meeting point of boyhood and youth, their radiance scattering the evening's gloom.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.80: 'at the junction of boyhood and youth'; 10.38.32: 'diśo vitimirā rājan kurvāṇau prabhayā svayā.'

statements.claim: Akrura's face opened with delight.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.17: 'his countenance expanded with delight.'

statements.claim: He jumped from the chariot, overwhelmed with love, hair standing on end, eyes brimming, and threw himself into the dust of the Lord's feet, crying out over the foot-dust that crowns the heads of all world-protectors.
statements.evidence: 10.38.24-25, 33-34: 'rathād avaskandya sa teṣv aceṣṭata prabhor amūny aṅghri-rajāṃsy aho iti' and 'premṇordhva-romāśru-kalākulekṣaṇaḥ... rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya so 'krūraḥ sneha-vihvalaḥ / bhagavad-darśanāhlāda-bāṣpa-paryākulekṣaṇaḥ.'

statements.claim: This, he knew, was the highest achievement of embodied beings — to lie in that dust, free of pretence, fear and grief.
statements.evidence: 10.38.26: 'dehaṃ-bhṛtām iyān artho hitvā dambhaṃ bhiyaṃ śucam.'

statements.claim: He praised the Lord who once lay on a fig-leaf at the dissolution of all things and once stepped over the three worlds as a dwarf.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.80: 'who lay on a fig-leaf at the time of the universal dissolution, and who assumed the form of a dwarf at the time of imposing on Bali.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama came forward, lifted him up, embraced him, asked his welfare, gave him a seat of honor and offered a cow to the guest; Balarama washed his tired feet.
statements.evidence: 10.38.35-39: 'bhagavāṃs tam abhipretya... saṅkarṣaṇaś ca praṇatam upaguhya... pṛṣṭvātha sv-āgataṃ tasmai nivedya ca varāsanam / nivedya gāṃ cātithaye saṃvāhya śrāntam... rāmaḥ parama-dharma-vit' (saṃvāhya śrāntam = bathing the weary guest; the foot-washing courtesy is Rama's part in 10.38.39).

statements.claim: Nanda, the cowherd chief, asked how the Yadavas fared under the cruel king who killed his sister's children while she wept.
statements.evidence: 10.38.40-41: 'papraccha sat-kṛtaṃ nandaḥ kathaṃ stha niranugrahe / yo 'vadhīt sva-svasus tokān krośantyā asu-tṛp khalaḥ.'

statements.claim: No one demanded his business or asked what message he carried.
statements.evidence: 10.38.42: 'itthaṃ sūnṛtayā vācā nandena su-sabhājitaḥ' (honored by Nanda with gentle words); the rest is narrative inference from the reception.

DKS_0113.notes: Evening setting from Harivamsha 1.80, lotus/jasmine comparisons from Vishnu Purana 5.17, and the reception from 10.38.23-42 — all three pack sources used; tradition_note corroborates.

statements.claim: Akrura had come to Vrindavan as Kamsa's messenger and bowed to the ground on beholding Krishna
statements.evidence: VP 5.18 (Wilson): 'I am Akrúra,' and bowed his head down to the feet of Hari; pack excerpt: Kamsa sent Akrura as messenger.

statements.claim: Krishna asked why Akrura asked after their welfare when the trouble in their own family only grows
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.4: 'kiṃ nu naḥ kuśalaṃ pṛcche edhamāne kulāmaye' (why ask of our welfare while the family affliction grows).

statements.claim: Akrura told of Kamsa's enmity toward the Yadavas, his resolve to kill Vasudeva, and that the errand was meant to draw the brothers to Mathura
statements.evidence: BP 10.39 excerpt: 'Kamsa's enmity toward the Yadavas, his resolve to kill Vasudeva, and the reason he himself had been sent as messenger'; canonical event evt_0124.

statements.claim: Akrura described Vasudeva grown old in sorrow, limbs wasted, oppressed by Kamsa of sinful designs, mind burning with anxiety
statements.evidence: HV 1.81 (Dutt): 'he has grown old and all his limbs have become lean... always oppressed by Kansa of sinful designs... mind is always burning in anxiety.'

statements.claim: Akrura described Devaki growing lean like a cow separated from her calf, sons never at her breast, eyes sunk like the moon seized by Rahu, soiled garments, parted from her sons since infancy
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'growing lean out of grief... like a cow without her calf... Like unto the moon possessed by Rāhu her eyes have run into their sockets and clad in a soiled raiment... separated from thee from thy very infancy.'

statements.claim: Akrura's sayings on sons: a woman without children bears one grief; a woman whose sons accomplish nothing knows no end of sorrow; Devaki deserves reverence as the earth does; save the goddess sunk in the water of sorrow
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'Women, having no children, are subject to one grief only... no end of their miseries, if they... have not their ends accomplished'; 'If like unto earth who holds thee Devaki deserves thy respect it behoves thee to save that goddess sunk into the water of sorrow.'

statements.claim: Akrura recalled Krishna's feats: vanquishing Kaliya in the Yamuna, lifting Govardhana, destroying Arishta and Keshi
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'as thou didst vanquish the wicked Nāga Kalya in the lake of Yamunā, as thou didst uproot the mount Govardhana... destroy the powerful Arishtha... kill the wicked-minded Keshi.'

statements.claim: Krishna knew everything, took no offence, and answered simply 'So be it'
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'The powerful Krishna knew everything so without taking any offence at the words of the liberal prince he said "So be it"' (BP-following rendering; VP variant with three-night vow noted in tradition_note).

statements.claim: The cowherds led by Nanda resolved to obey Kamsa's summons, arranged tributes of buffaloes, bulls, curd, milk and clarified butter
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'all the Gopas, headed by Nanda, desired to follow the orders of Kansa... buffaloes and bull, curd, milk and clarified butter.'

statements.claim: Akrura spent the night without sleep speaking with Krishna and Balarama; at dawn Vraja stirred and prepared to travel
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'Conversing with Krishna and Rohini's son Akrura spent the night without sleep'; dawn description follows.

DKS_0114.notes: Tradition note correctly flags VP 5.18's three-night vow variant; story follows BP/HV. No issues.
