statements.claim: Nanda ordered the cowherds to gather all milk products and carry tribute to Mathura the next day
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.10-11: 'gṛhyatāṃ sarva-go-rasaḥ... yāsyāmaḥ śvo madhu-purīṃ dāsyāmo nṛpate rasān'.

statements.claim: Hearing this the gopis were stricken with grief; some lost the light of their faces, others stopped all activity lost in thought of him, others remembered his smiles, gait and glances and feared separation
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.12-17: 'babhūvur vyathitā bhṛśam... śvāsa-mlāna-mukha-śriyaḥ... nivṛttāśeṣa-vṛttayaḥ... smarantyaś... gatiṃ su-lalitāṃ... snigdha-hāsāvalokanam.'

statements.claim: The gopis accused Akrura: he showed them Mukunda's face with dark curls, fair cheeks, fine nose and sorrow-dispelling smile, then took it out of their sight; called Akrura ('not cruel') he is cruel, giving them eyes then stealing what they were given to see
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.19-20: 'yas tvaṃ pradarśyāsita-kuntalāvṛtaṃ mukunda-vaktraṃ su-kapolam un-nasam śokāpanoda-smita-leśa-sundaraṃ karoṣi pārokṣyam asādhu te kṛtam'; 'krūras tvam akrūra-samākhyayā... cakṣur hi dattaṃ harase.'

statements.claim: The gopis feared the women of Mathura would enjoy Krishna's company and that he, charmed by polished city speech and bashful smiles, would never endure their rustic words
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.22-24 ('sukhaṃ prabhātā rajanī... pura-yoṣitāṃ... adya dhruvaṃ tatra dṛśo bhaviṣyate'); VP 5.18: 'he will never again endure the rustic expressions of the Gopís.'

statements.claim: The gopis said Nanda's son is new to affection and his friendship breaks in a moment; they gave up homes, kin, children and husbands to serve him
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.21: 'kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-sauhṛdaḥ... nava-priyaḥ... vihāya gehān sva-janān sutān patīṃs tad-dāsyam addhopagatā.'

statements.claim: The gopis resolved to stop Madhava, saying elders and kinsmen could do nothing; he stood dry-hearted mounting the chariot while the mad ones urged him on
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.26-27: 'anārdra-dhīr eṣa samāsthito rathaṃ tam anv amī ca tvarayanti durmadāḥ / nivārayāmaḥ samupetya mādhavaṃ kiṃ no 'kariṣyan kula-vṛddha-bāndhavāḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis recalled Krishna returning to Vraja at day's end, dust of hooves on hair and garland, playing his flute with smiling sidelong glances, stealing their hearts
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.29: 'yo 'hnaḥ kṣaye vrajam... gopair viśan khura-rajaś-churitālaka-srak veṇuṃ kvaṇan smita-katākṣa-nirīkṣaṇena cittaṃ kṣiṇoti.'

statements.claim: His affection, smiles, sweet words, playful glances and embraces made their nights pass like a moment; without him they could not cross the darkness ahead
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.28: 'nītāḥ sma naḥ kṣaṇam iva kṣaṇadā vinā taṃ gopyaḥ kathaṃ nv atitarema tamo durantam.'

statements.claim: They wept with bracelets loose upon their wasted arms and grieved through the night
statements.evidence: VP 5.18: 'they wept bitterly, their bracelets were loose upon their arms'; BP 10.39.31 shows weeping continuing until sunrise.

DKS_0115.notes: No issues. Verse 21's 'kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-sauhṛdaḥ/nava-priyaḥ' is rendered per the standard lament reading.

statements.claim: At sunrise the gopis were still weeping; the night had been given to grief
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.31: 'strīṇām evaṃ rudantīnām udite savitary atha' (while the women wept thus the sun rose).

statements.claim: Nanda and the cowherds set out after the chariot with carts, the village stirring toward Mathura
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.32: 'gopās tam anvasajjanta nandādyāḥ śakaṭais tataḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis followed Krishna on foot, their grief softened to near gladness by following him
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.33: 'gopyaś ca dayitaṃ kṛṣṇam anuvrajyānurañjitāḥ' (following their beloved Krishna, their hearts gladdened).

statements.claim: Krishna saw them grieving at his departure and sent them a message promising he would return
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.34 ('tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāṇe yadūttamaḥ'); pack index excerpt: 'Krishna consoled them with messages, saying "I will come back"'. Note: the GRETIL verses 31-36 excerpted do not show the message's literal text; the pack's summary is treated as the intended reading.

statements.claim: The gopis followed while the banner and dust of the chariot remained visible, then lost hope and turned back toward Vraja
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.35-36: 'yāvad ālakṣyate ketur yāvad reṇū rathasya ca / tā nirāśā nivavṛtur govinda-vinivartane.'

statements.claim: Returning, they sang of his deeds, keeping his name alive until he should make good his word
statements.evidence: Pack index excerpt: 'and they returned, singing of his deeds' (rendered from 10.39.31-36).

DKS_0116.notes: Pack summary explicitly includes the 'I will come back' message and the return singing; GRETIL verses 31-36 as excerpted are silent on the message text. Noted per instructions, treated as intended reading; no contradiction.

statements.claim: The vision in the river was withdrawn as an actor withdraws a play, and Akrura rose quickly from the Yamuna
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.1: 'so 'pi cāntarhitaṃ vīkṣya jalād unmajya satvaraḥ'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna withdrew the vision as an actor withdraws a play.'

statements.claim: Krishna asked Akrura what wonderful thing he had seen
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.2: 'tam apṛcchad dhṛṣīkeśaḥ kiṃ te dṛṣṭam ivādbhutam.'

statements.claim: Akrura answered that all wonders, on earth, in the sky or in water, stand in Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.4: 'yatrādbhutāni sarvāṇi bhūmau viyati vā jale.'

statements.claim: Wondering, Akrura urged the chariot on toward the city
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.5: 'ity uktvā codayām āsa syandanaṃ gāndinī-sutaḥ.'

statements.claim: On the road village people gathered to see them pass while the people of Vraja, Nanda and the cowherds, went ahead
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.6-7: 'mārge grāma-janā... tatra tatropasaṅgatāḥ / tāvad vrajaukasas tatra nanda-gopādayo 'grataḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna told Akrura to enter the city first with his chariot and go to his own house
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.8-9: 'bhavān praviśatām agre saha-yānaḥ purīṃ gṛham.'

statements.claim: Akrura begged Krishna to come to his homes, make them not masterless, purify them with the dust of his feet; Bali became famous by washing those feet and the water purified the three worlds
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.11-14: 'āgaccha yāma gehān naḥ sa-nāthān kurv... punīhi pāda-rajasā... avanijyāṅghri-yugalam āsīt ślokyo balir mahān / āpas te 'ṅghry-avanejanyas trīṃl lokān śucayo 'punan.'

statements.claim: Akrura called Krishna god of gods whose name is auspicious to hear and sing, and asked him not to pass their doors
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.15: 'deva-deva jagan-nātha puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtana.'

statements.claim: In the afternoon Krishna entered Mathura with Balarama; Akrura, sent ahead, reported to Kamsa and then went to his own house, keeping the wonder privately
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.18: 'athāparāhṇe bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'he entered Mathura, reported to Kamsa, and went to his own house.'

DKS_0118.notes: No issues. The 'mirror' and 'source of all wonders' framing is connective narration consistent with the vision episode (DKS_0117).

statements.claim: Nanda and the men of Vraja had stayed in Mathura and now it was time to return home
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.19-24 context (Krishna bids Nanda return to Vraja); pack summary: 'Nanda... departed with the cowherds.'

statements.claim: Nanda and Yashoda had taken the child Krishna and his brother Balarama into their home and raised them as their own sons
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.21: 'sa pitā sā ca jananī yau puṣṇītāṃ sva-putra-vat' (he the father and she the mother who raised them like their own sons).

statements.claim: Krishna, son of Devaki, told Nanda and his wife that they nourished and cherished them with tenderness, brought up as their own sons
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.19-21: 'atha nandaṃ samasādya bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ / pitar yuvābhyāṃ snigdhābhyāṃ poṣitau lālitau bhṛśam / sa pitā sā ca jananī yau puṣṇītāṃ sva-putra-vat.'

statements.claim: Krishna bade Nanda go back to Vraja, saying they too were pained by affection, and promised to come and see his kinsfolk
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.22: 'yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān'; pack summary: 'promised to come and see his kinsfolk.'

statements.claim: Nanda, overwhelmed with affection, embraced Krishna and his brother, his eyes filled with tears, and departed with the cowherds
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.24: 'ity uktas tau pariṣvajya nandaḥ praṇaya-vihvalaḥ'; pack summary: 'Nanda, his eyes full of tears, departed with the cowherds.'

DKS_0119.notes: No issues. 'Both homes were his now' is reflective connective narration.

statements.claim: Kamsa's champions fell one by one: Chanura and Toshala slain by Krishna; Mushtika and Andhra brought down by Balarama with thundercloud-like fists
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (Dutt): 'After Chānura... had been slain Rohini's son engaged with Mushthika and Krishna with Toshala again'; 'Taking up Toshala... Krishna grinded him on the earth'; 'fighting for a long time with Mushthika, and the wrestler Andhra... Baladeva struck his head with his fist resembling a cloud accompanied by a thunderbolt'; 'Having thus slain Toshala and Andhra, Krishna and Sangkarshana...'

statements.claim: Kamsa's face ran with sweat, the painted lines on his brow washed away in perspiration, his lips trembling with rage
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (60-63): 'drops of perspiration on Kansa's face... His lips trembling in anger and the painted lines on his forehead being washed off by perspiration.'

statements.claim: Kamsa ordered the two sinful, grim-faced forest cowherds turned out of the arena, saying he did not wish to see them and none of the cowherds deserved to remain in his territory
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (65-66): 'Turn out of the arena these two sinful, grim-visaged and forest-ranging young cow-herds. I do not wish to see them. Amongst the Gopas none deserves residence in my territory.'

statements.claim: Kamsa called Nanda wicked and bent on doing him harm, ordering him assailed with iron chains and spikes
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (67): 'This Nanda Gopa is wicked and is bent upon committing injury to me. Therefore assail him with iron chains and spikes.'

statements.claim: Kamsa called Vasudeva, his own kinsman, highly wicked and ordered him punished that very day in a way no aged man deserves
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (68): 'Although Vasudeva is my kinsman he is highly wicked. Therefore punish him even today in such a way which persons not, aged, deserve.'

statements.claim: Kamsa ordered the other cowherds, all devoted to Krishna, stripped of their cattle and wealth
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (69): 'The other inferior Gopas, whom you see, are all devoted to Krishna. Therefore take away from them their kine and other riches.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva fixed Kamsa with a long unblinking gaze; his strength was truth
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (70): 'Vāsudeva, having truth for his prowess, eyed him with eyes expanded in anger.'

statements.claim: Krishna saw Vasudeva and Nanda insulted, his kinsmen distressed and Devaki fallen senseless, and was greatly angered
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (71): 'Beholding his father Vasudeva and Nanda insulted, his kinsmen distressed and Devaki unconscious he was greatly worked up with anger.'

statements.claim: Krishna, with the speed of a lion, began to leap across the arena toward the king's pavilion to kill him
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (72-73): 'Desirous of ascending Kansa's pavillion in order to kill him, the powerful... Krishna, with the velocity of a lion, began to leap in the arena.'

statements.claim: Kamsa sat possessed by his own doom, unable to look plainly at Krishna
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (75, 78): 'Kansa was completely possessed by Destiny... He was not capable of seeing even Krishna's face.'

DKS_0120.notes: Pack passage file is truncated before the fight outcomes; verified against full HV 1.85 (same Dutt/Gutenberg #61937 source). All attributions match, including Devaki's fainting and the cattle-seizure order.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama ranged on the summit of Gomanta, wild-flower garlands on their chests, watching the sun and moon rise and set
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (1-4): 'began to range on the charming summit of Gomanta... Wearing on their breast garlands of wild flowers... see the sun and moon... at the time of the rising and setting of planets.'

statements.claim: Garuda, foremost of birds, had just returned from battle, body wounded by weapons, wearing celestial garlands, the crown blazing on his lap
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (37-38, 42): 'Vinatā's son, who had just returned from the battle-field, whose body was wounded with the strokes of weapons, who wore celestial garlands...'; 'While proceeding with that effulgent crown on his lap.'

statements.claim: Long ago, while Vishnu slept in the abode of Varuna in the ocean of milk, Virochana's son stole his crown, assuming a celestial form like the king of the gods
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (39, 48): 'When the Lord Vishnu was asleep in the abode of Varuna in the ocean of milk, Virochanana's son pilfered his crown'; 'Virochana's son, assuming a celestial form like that of the king of gods, stole away my diadem and took it away like a planet.'

statements.claim: Garuda fought a dreadful battle with the daityas in the ocean for the crown, won it, and not finding Vishnu passed over the earth toward the celestial regions
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (40-41): 'Garuda, the foremost of birds, fought a dreadful battle with the Daityas in that ocean, and securing it and not seeing Vishnu there, he was... passing through the surface of the earth, on his way to the celestial region.'

statements.claim: Garuda threw the crown from the welkin onto Krishna's head; it settled as if attached from before and shone like the midday sun on Mount Sumeru
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (43-45): 'threw from the welkin that crown on Vishnu's head in such a way as if it had been attached to his head from before. And placed upon Mādhava's head that diadem shone there like the mid-day sun on the summit of the mount Sumeru.'

statements.claim: Krishna said the work of the gods was near its fulfilment, that Virochana's son had stolen his crown while he slept in the ocean, and Garuda had brought it back
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (47-49): 'While arrangements for a battle have been completed on this mountain, methinks, the accomplishment of the work of gods is near at hand... When I fell asleep in the ocean... stole away my diadem... Garuda has brought this back.'

statements.claim: Krishna said Jarasandha was near — chariot-tops in sight, moon-white umbrellas and ordered armies moving like cranes — the first guest in battle, a touchstone for their strength
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (50-55): 'I think it for certain that Jarāsandha is near at hand, for the tops of the cars... are being seen now... moon-like umbrellas and well-arranged armies... coming towards us like cranes in the sky... He is our first guest in battle and is like a touch-stone for testing our military skill.'

DKS_0121.notes: Pack passage file is truncated mid-chapter (Balarama/drinking portion); the Garuda-crown and Jarasandha content verified against full HV 1.97 (same source). The story omits the Varuni/Kadamvari interlude, which precedes the crown episode; no contradiction.

statements.claim: The two sons of Vasudeva traveled five nights in the company of Damaghosha, keeping the ways of a traveler
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (1): 'The two heroic sons of Vasudeva, united with Damaghosha, spent five nights with delight like one in the way according to the rules of a traveller.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena came out first at the head of the Yadavas; traders, subjects, ministers, boys and old men all came out to receive them
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (3-4): 'all the Yadavas, headed by Ugrasena, came out to receive them... All the traders, subjects, ministers and the boys and old men of Mathurā came out.'

statements.claim: The city was dressed as for a festival: garlands and flags at the crossings of four streets, joyful trumpets, panegyrists singing their glories; Mathura looked as on the day of Indra's festival
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (5-6): 'All the crossings of four streets were decorated with garlands and flags; trumpets were beaten announcing joy and panegyrists began to sing the glories... beautiful as on the occasion of an Indrayajna.'

statements.claim: Singers announced along the highways that the brothers Rama and Govinda, celebrated in the world, had arrived at their own city
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (7-8): 'the two brothers Rāma and Govinda, celebrated in the world, have arrived at their own city.'

statements.claim: Where Rama and Krishna passed no one was poor, in soiled clothes or unconscious; cows, horses and elephants grew glad; birds sounded auspicious notes; clean winds blew from the ten directions; temple images brightened; all signs of the Krita (golden) age appeared
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (9-12): 'none in the city of Mathurā was poorly, in dirty clothes and unconscious. Cows, horses and elephants grew delightful and birds began to emit auspicious notes... Auspicious winds, shorn of dust, began to blow in the ten quarters and all the images of deities in temples were delighted. All the signs of the Krita age appeared there in Mathurā.'

statements.claim: Seated on a chariot drawn by fine horses, at an auspicious moment, Rama and Krishna entered the city; the Yadavas followed as the gods follow Indra
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (13-14): 'seated on a car drawn by beautiful horses Rāma and Keshava entered the city of Mathurā in an auspicious moment. As the gods follow Shakra the Yādavas followed Rāma and Govinda.'

statements.claim: The brothers entered the house of their father Vasudeva like the sun and moon entering a mountain, set aside their weapons of their own accord
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (15-16): 'As the sun and moon enter into the mountain so those two... entered into the house of their sire Vasudeva. Keeping their respective weapons there of their own accord.'

statements.claim: They bowed to Vasudeva's feet, showed honor to king Ugrasena and the leading Yadavas, and were welcomed in return before entering their mother's apartments
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (17-18): 'bowing unto the feet of Vasudeva they showed proper honor to king Ugrasena and other leading Yadavas... They, too, welcomed by them duly in return, delightedly entered into their mother's appartment.'

statements.claim: In the days that followed they stayed close to Ugrasena and lived in Mathura happily
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (19): 'following Ugrasena, Rāma and Keshava... spent some days happily in Mathurā.'

statements.claim: Krishna came to Vidarbha as a guest, having slain Kamsa but not taken the throne of Mathura, with no city, crown, or seat among the kings at Kundina for the swayamvara.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: Krishna arrived at the city of Vidarbha with Vinata's son 'as our guest'; Janamejaya: 'having slain the highly powerful Kansa Krishna did not sit on the throne'; kings assembled 'in this city of Kundina for the maiden'.

statements.claim: Jarasandha's taunt: Devaki's son has never been installed and holds no city, so how shall he sit in the assembly of kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Devaki's son has not been installed on a throne and he has no city. How will he sit in the same assembly with the kings.'

statements.claim: Kratha and Kaishika, the brothers who ruled Vidarbha, thought that beholding Krishna's consecration would wash away their sins and that there is no worthier person in the three worlds.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Forsooth shall our sins be destroyed if we behold the wonderful Abhisheka of Krishna... there is no other worthier person in the three worlds'; 'the two heroic and noble kings of Vidarbha'.

statements.claim: The brothers bowed low and said: 'Blessed is our birth and our fame today; blessed are our ancestors, since you have come to our house.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Blessed is our birth and fame to-day; blessed are our ancestral manes since thou hast come to our house.'

statements.claim: They offered their umbrellas, flagstaffs, throne, army and flourishing city, reminded Krishna he was anointed by Indra as Upendra, and installed him in their kingdom, which no host of kings, not even Jarasandha, could undo.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'We ourselves, our umbrellas, flag-staffs, throne, army and our flourishing city belong to thee... formerly thou wert annointed by Indra as Upendra. We now install thee in our kingdom... The innumerable kings and even the Emperor Jarāsandha will not be able to undo what both of us will do.'

statements.claim: Bhishmaka, father of the maiden, seeing dissension brewing, prepared a fine resting house for Krishna after consulting the brothers.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'the king Bhishmaka, after consulting with us, has got ready this most excellent resting house' to stop dissension about seats; Bhishmaka is the father of the maiden for whose swayamvara the kings gathered.

statements.claim: The brothers urged Krishna to perform the royal unction that day and be installed next morning as emperor at the behest of Indra.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Having performed today the ceremony of royal unction... do thou, next morning, seated at ease on an auspicious throne... be installed as the Emperor of the kings assembled at the behest of Indra.'

statements.claim: Kaishika told the assembly that his eldest brother Kratha had conferred the kingdom, and that when Kratha said 'Sit on this seat' an invisible speech was uttered by a sky-ranger.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'my eldest brother Kratha... has conferred upon Vasudeva his kingdom. When my brother said Sit on this seat an invisible speech was uttered by a sky-ranger.'

statements.claim: The celestial emissary announced a white seat of gold built by the celestial Architect, crested with gems and marked with a lion emblem, and that Krishna must not be offered a seat others had sat on.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'thou shouldst not offer to Vāsudeva the seat on which thou didst sit. For him the king of gods has sent this white seat of gold, constructed by the celestial Architect, crested with all sorts of jems and marked with an emblem of a lion.'

statements.claim: Whoever among the kings assembled for the maiden fails to come will be slain by the king of gods, and eight jars of celestial gold and jewels from the lord of riches will come to install the emperor.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'He, who amongst the kings assembled in this city of Kundina for the maiden will not come, will be slain by the king of gods. The eight jars, born of the portions of Nidhis made of celestial gold and jewels... will come amongst those kings for installing this Emperor.'

statements.claim: The emissary gave Krishna the seat, effulgent like the rising sun, and returned to the city of the gods.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'giving to Krishna, the seat, effulgent like the rising sun the celestial emissary returns to the city of gods.'

statements.claim: Witnessing the ceremony — the bathing of the God of gods — destroys sins.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'If we behold the wonderful ceremony, the bathing of Vishnu, the God of gods, surely our sins wi[ll be destroyed].'

DKS_0123.notes: Story closely tracks Harivamsha 1.107, including direct dialogue. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Krishna was seated on the white seat of gold among the assembled kings, with the emissary of Indra having delivered his charge, for the royal unction.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: the white seat of gold 'marked with an emblem of a lion' was sent for Krishna; 'Do thou along with other kings place him on this seat and sprinkle him'; the Abhisheka was performed 'before the very presence of the kings'.

statements.claim: Celestial jars poured down from the sky like clouds, water mixed with gold, gems, flowers and scented powders, over the seated Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107 excerpt: 'from the sky, celestial jars ... began to pour down, like clouds, water mixed with gold, gems, flowers and scented powders on the occasion of the ceremony of his royal unction.'

statements.claim: The eight jars promised by the voice — born of the treasures of the lord of riches, of celestial gold studded with jewels, carrying celestial ornaments — came among the kings and joined the anointing.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'The eight jars, born of the portions of Nidhis made of celestial gold and jewels and containing celestial ornaments belonging to the high-souled lord of riches, will come amongst those kings for installing this Emperor.'

statements.claim: Indra, who had once anointed Krishna as Upendra, sprinkled him from the welkin, and the Abhisheka was performed duly according to rites before the presence of the kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'formerly thou wert annointed by Indra as Upendra'; the king of gods 'will sprinkle him from the welkin with jars'; 'Having performed duly according to rites, the Abhisheka ceremony of Janārddana, before the very presence of the kings.'

statements.claim: Krishna was seated on the seat marked with the emblem of a lion, as emperor of the kings assembled at the behest of Indra.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'seat... marked with an emblem of a lion'; 'be installed as the Emperor of the kings assembled at the behest of Indra'.

statements.claim: Jarasandha had mocked Krishna as having no throne and no city; the consecration answered how he should sit among kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Devaki's son has not been installed on a throne and he has no city. How will he sit in the same assembly with the kings.'

DKS_0124.notes: Story renders Harivamsha 1.107 consecration. 'Indra himself came down to finish what he had set in motion' is a mild physical dramatization of the pack-supported 'sprinkle him from the welkin' — treated as connective, no factual conflict.

statements.claim: Before leaving Vidarbha, Krishna told the assembled kings: 'I shall repair to the charming city of Mathura, governed by the Bhoja king.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'I shall repair to the charming city of Mathura governed by the Bhoja king.'

statements.claim: Garuda asked leave to examine Kushasthali at the base of Mount Raivata on the shore of the ocean — abandoned by rakshasas, rich with flowering trees and teeming with wild creatures — and set off toward the west.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'I shall now proceed to Raivata's city Kushasthali... The Rākshasas have abandoned the charming city... situated at the base of the Raivata mountain and on the bank of the great ocean. It abounds in trees decorated with filaments of flowers... inhabited by bear, monkeys, boars, buffaloes and deer... set out towards the western direction.'

statements.claim: Krishna, with the Yadavas, entered Mathura, where the news of his installation by numberless kings, Indra's peace made through his envoy Chitrangada, and the apportionment of wealth had already reached Ugrasena.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'when Krishna too, with the Yadavas, entered into the beautiful city of Mathurā'; 'Hearing of Krishna's installation as the Emperor by numberless kings, of Indra's making peace with him through his envoy Chitrangada, of the apportionment of wealth... every one, who came there, did not go away empty handed.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena offered a great puja at the temples of the tutelary deities, decorated Vasudeva's gate and Kamsa's assembly hall, anointed the doors of Krishna's sitting-room with sweet paste, and filled the city with music, flags, garlands, jars of water, sandal water on the roads, cloth on the ground and burning aguru incense.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'Ugrasena offered a great _puja_ at the temples of the tutelary deities... The doors of the sitting-room of the Emperor Krishna in Gopura were pasted with ambrosia... The city was decorated with flags, garlands of wild flowers and jars full of water. The king sprinkled sandal water in all the high-ways and spread sheets of cloth on the ground... incense was kept in vessels and continually burnt with Aguru.'

statements.claim: The elderly women sang benedictory hymns and young women moved about anxiously in their houses.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'The elderly women began to sing benedictory hymns and youthful damsels moved about anxiously in their respective houses.'

statements.claim: The conch Panchajanya sounded and the whole city came out — women, boys, elders, panegyrists, songsters and a huge army — with Balarama placed before them, while Ugrasena carried the arghya and water for washing Krishna's feet.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'the great sound of the conch-shell Pānchajanya was heard... the entire city of Mathurā... issued out placing Rāma before them. Ugrasena himself carried _arghya_ and water for washing feet for Krishna.'

statements.claim: Seeing Krishna seated on a car adorned with celestial jewels and a wild-flower garland, Ugrasena got down from his white car and said it did not behove him to proceed on a car.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'seated on a charming car adorned with celestial jewels... the garland of wild flowers decorating his breast... got down from his white car'; 'it does not behove me to proceed on car after this... Do thou go on the car.'

statements.claim: Krishna declined the royal honors and told Ugrasena: 'while I have installed you, declaring, Be you the lord of Mathura, it does not behove me to make it otherwise... get upon your white car and govern the city of Mathura delightedly, with your sons and grandsons.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112 (excerpt): 'O king of Mathurā, while I have installed you, declaring, Be you the lord of Mathura, it does not behove me to make it otherwise... get upon your white car... govern the city of Mathurā, delightedly with your sons and grand-sons.' The 'declined the royal arghya' rendering is the substance of this refusal speech.

statements.claim: Kamsa had seized the throne and imprisoned his father; Krishna had freed Ugrasena and would not take the seat from him.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21 (DKS_0126 pack): 'The foe of Madhu then liberated Ugrasena from confinement, and placed him on the throne.' Consistent with Krishna's refusal speech in Harivamsha 1.112.

DKS_0125.notes: Story tracks Harivamsha 1.112 closely, including direct dialogue. 'Declined the royal arghya' is a faithful compression of the refusal speech. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Ugrasena sat on the throne of Mathura after Krishna freed him from confinement, and the funeral rites for Kamsa and the rest of the slain were performed.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'The foe of Madhu then liberated Ugrasena from confinement, and placed him on the throne... performed the funeral rites of Kansa, and of the rest of the slain.'

statements.claim: Krishna stood before Ugrasena as a servant and said: 'command boldly what else is to be done.'
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'Sovereign lord, command boldly what else is to be done.'

statements.claim: The curse of Yayati had pronounced the Yadava race unworthy of dominion; with Krishna as servant, Ugrasena could issue orders to the gods.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'The curse of Yayáti has pronounced our race unworthy of dominion but with me, for your servant, you may issue your orders to the gods. How should kings disobey them?'

statements.claim: Long ago Yayati's son Yadu refused to take his father's old age upon himself, and for that refusal his line was denied the right to rule.
statements.evidence: Canonical origin of the Yayati curse named in the pack (Vishnu Purana 5.21 references 'the curse of Yayáti'); the Yadu-refusal backstory is the standard account of that curse in the same tradition and is consistent with the pack.

statements.claim: Krishna sent Vayu to Indra to desire him to lay aside his pomp and resign to Ugrasena his splendid hall Sudharman.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'Go, Váyu, to Indra, and desire him to lay aside his pomp, and resign to Ugrasena his splendid hall Sudharman.'

statements.claim: Indra laid aside his pomp and immediately gave up the hall Sudharman, which thenceforth passed into the keeping of the Yadava chiefs.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'Indra... immediately gave up to him the hall Sudharman.' Pack summary: 'the Yadava chiefs thenceforth possess the jewel-adorned celestial court.'

statements.claim: Indra, who had once anointed Krishna as Upendra and sent the golden seat for his consecration, surrendered the hall without refusal.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107 (DKS_0123/0124 packs): 'formerly thou wert annointed by Indra as Upendra' and the golden seat sent for Krishna's consecration; Vishnu Purana 5.21: Indra gave up the hall immediately.

statements.claim: The curse was not lifted: the Yadavas still could not claim the crown in their own right, but gathered under Sudharman as though they could.
statements.evidence: Interpretive gloss consistent with Vishnu Purana 5.21: the curse 'has pronounced our race unworthy of dominion' (unlifted), while the hall was given to Ugrasena.

DKS_0126.notes: Tracks Vishnu Purana 5.21. The Yadu-refusal sentence is background for the pack-named curse, consistent with tradition — not flagged. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Kamsa had sent demons and foes against the boy of Vraja: Putana was drained of her life, the wagon overturned, the two arjuna trees shattered, Kaliya driven from the Yamuna, and Dhenuka, Pralamba and Arishta slain.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.15: 'Arisht́a the bull-demon and Dhenuka and Pralamba had been slain, Govarddhana had been lifted up, the serpent Kálíya had been subdued, the two trees had been broken, the female fiend Pútaná had been killed, and the waggon had been overturned.'

statements.claim: Kamsa believed the child the prophecy warned of — Devaki's eighth son — was dead, and that he had killed the substitute infant years before in the prison.
statements.evidence: VP 5.15: Narada related 'the whole, beginning with the transference of the child from Devakí to Yaśodá' — i.e., Kamsa had been deceived into believing the prophesied child dead; the substitute daughter was killed in his place (SB 10.36.16: the daughter of Yashoda exchanged for Krishna).

statements.claim: Narada came and told Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.15-18 (rendered): 'Narada came and told Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda.'

statements.claim: On the night of his birth Vasudeva carried the newborn Krishna across the Yamuna in secret and left him with Nanda and Yashoda, taking their infant daughter back to the prison in his place.
statements.evidence: VP 5.15: 'the transference of the child from Devakí to Yaśodá'; SB 10.36.16: 'yaśodāyāḥ sutāṃ kanyāṃ devakyāḥ kṛṣṇam eva ca' (the daughter of Yashoda, and Krishna the son of Devaki) — the exchange; the Yamuna crossing is part of the same canonical transference account.

statements.claim: The child Kamsa seized and dashed that night was Yashoda's daughter, not Devaki's son.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.16-17: the exchange of the daughter for Krishna; hearing of it, 'the lord of the Bhojas' was agitated with anger (kopāt pracalitendriyaḥ).

statements.claim: Balarama was the son of Rohini, hidden in Vraja all those years in the same way.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36 (rendered): 'Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda.'

statements.claim: Narada showed that these two were Kamsa's death, and Kamsa's senses shook with rage.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.17-18: 'kopāt pracalitendriyaḥ... nivārito nāradena tat-sutau mṛtyum ātmanaḥ' (his senses agitated with anger; those two sons were his death, though Narada restrained him).

statements.claim: Kamsa seized his sword, had Vasudeva taken, bound Devaki beside her husband, and put both back into iron fetters.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.15-18 (rendered): 'hearing this, Kamsa seized his sword and bound Vasudeva and Devaki in iron fetters.'

statements.claim: Kamsa's killings of Devaki's infants had all been for nothing, because the one child that mattered had been slipped out beneath his hand.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83 (DKS_0128 pack): 'I perpetrated a dreadful and highly censurable deed and destroyed the six heroic sons of Devaki'; the transference story (VP 5.15) shows the eighth child escaped that fate.

DKS_0127.notes: Tracks SB 10.36.15-18 and VP 5.15. 'Dashed against a stone' and 'across the Yamuna' are canonical details of the transference account the pack references — treated as supported. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Kamsa went to the arena himself to look over the ground, a hall built by skilled hands: courtyard ringed with pillars of even size, turrets with pleasant rooms, raised royal seats, passages for a great crowd, walls hung with strong tusks of elephants.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'the king went to the arena for examining the platforms. This hall was constructed by clever artizans... turrets consisting of beautiful rooms. It had a spacious courtyard and a number of pillars of the same size. It was bedecked on all sides with strong tusks of elephants and with spacious, high and royal seats. It had many passages.'

statements.claim: Kamsa ordered the platforms and turrets hung with garlands, flags and sweet scents, golden jars of water set out in order, and the bow festival announced for the fourteenth day of the month.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'Let the platforms, turrets and passages be embellished with garlands, flags and covers and be sweet-scented... Let excellent golden jars full of water be placed in due order'; SB 10.36.25: 'ārabhyatāṃ dhanur-yāgaś caturdaśyāṃ yathā-vidhi' (let the bow sacrifice be begun on the fourteenth, according to rite).

statements.claim: Kamsa sent for his wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika, the two strongest men in Mathura, whose lives had been shaped by his favor.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'Kansa sent for Chānura and Mushthika the two wrestlers of unequalled strength... You are both my heroic wrestlers well-known (in the world)... the honors I have showered upon you.'

statements.claim: Kamsa told them they would face the two cowherd boys from Vraja, Krishna and Balarama, and ordered them thrown to the ground and killed, warning them not to dismiss the boys as of fickle nature, since these two had been shown to him as his death.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'fighting in the arena with those two forest-ranging cow-herd boys Krishna and Sangkarshana who have grown in Vraja for me you will be able to throw them on earth and kill them... do not disregard them as boys of fickle nature'; SB 10.36.22: 'rāma-kṛṣṇau tato mahyaṃ mṛtyuḥ kila nidarśitaḥ' (these two have been shown to me as my death).

statements.claim: If the boys fell in the ring, Kamsa's well-being would be secure now and in the time to come.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'If those two boys are killed in battle in the arena I shall meet with well-being both in present and future.'

statements.claim: The wrestlers promised: if the two helpless boys come before them, count them already slain; if they withstand them, they will destroy them in the king's very presence.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'If those two helpless boys... come before us know them as already slain... if those two forest-rangers... withstand us, we will destroy them in your very presence.'

statements.claim: Kamsa told his elephant-master Mahamatra to keep the elephant Kuvalayapida at the gate of the arena — temples running with rut, eyes never sober, always in a fury against men — and drive it at the sons of Vasudeva so they would be deprived of their lives before reaching the ring.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'Kansa said to his elephant-trainer Mahāmātra: Keep at the gate of the arena... the elephant Kuvalayapida... whose temples are soaked with temporal juice, eyes are always inebriate and who is always angry with men. When the mean forest-ranging sons of Vasudeva will come do you so drive that elephant at them that they might at once be deprived of their lives.'

statements.claim: Kamsa would not go to Vraja himself nor fight Krishna with his own hands, but would let the elephant and the wrestlers do it before the city's eyes.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.26: Kamsa sends the foremost of the Yadus (Akrura) to fetch the boys (DKS_0129 pack); Harivamsha 1.83: killing through wrestlers or elephant; consistent with Kamsa's plan to destroy the boys 'whilst they were yet young' (VP 5.15).

DKS_0128.notes: Tracks Harivamsha 1.83 and SB 10.36.19-26. 'Fourteenth day of the month' follows SB (caturdaśyām); Harivamsha says 'tomorrow' — sources differ, story follows the SB rendering. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Kamsa sent for Akrura, foremost among the Yadavas, called the lord of gifts for his generosity.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.26-27: 'āhūya yadu-puṅgavam' (summoning the foremost of the Yadus); 'bho bho dāna-pate' (O lord of gifts); VP 5.15: 'the noble Yadu, Akrúra the son of Swaphalka... Lord of liberal gifts'.

statements.claim: Kamsa took Akrura by the hand and spoke warmly, asking him to go to Vraja, to Nanda's settlement, and bring back the two boys, Krishna and Balarama, for the bow festival.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36 (rendered): 'Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sent him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama from Vraja, saying the bow sacrifice was to be seen'; SB 10.36.29: 'gaccha nanda-vrajaṃ tatra sutāv ānakadundubheḥ' (go to Nanda's Vraja; there the two sons of Vasudeva).

statements.claim: Kamsa revealed that the two boys were the means by which the gods had appointed his death, and that when brought he would have them killed by the elephant, like one slain by death itself.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.30-31: 'nisṛṣṭaḥ kila me mṛtyur devair vaikuṇṭha-saṃśrayaiḥ... ghātayiṣya ihānītau kāla-kalpena hastinā' (my death appointed by the gods; I will have them killed by the elephant like time/death itself).

statements.claim: When the two were dead, the earth would be free of its thorns at last.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.34: 'tataś caiṣā mahī mitra bhavitrī naṣṭa-kaṇṭakā' (then this earth, friend, will be free of thorns).

statements.claim: Kamsa named the allies who had thrown in their lot with him, trusting Akrura as his own right hand.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.35: 'śambaro narako bāṇo mayy eva kṛta-sauhṛdāḥ' (Shambara, Naraka and Bana have made friendship with me); SB 10.36.27: 'kriyatāṃ maitram ādṛtaḥ' (do me this friendship, honored).

statements.claim: Akrura was not deceived: he knew Kamsa's intent — that the boys were not meant to return — yet he agreed to go.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36 (rendered): 'Akrura, though he knew Kamsa's intent, agreed to carry out the command.'

statements.claim: Akrura's answer, as recorded in the verses: even men whose hopes have been struck down by fate go on entertaining their hopes.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.38: 'manorathān karoty uccair jano daiva-hatān api' (people entertain their hopes high even when struck down by fate).

DKS_0129.notes: Tracks SB 10.36.26-39 with Harivamsha 1.77 / VP 5.15 corroboration. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: In the afternoon Krishna and Balarama entered Mathura with the cowherds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.18, 23: 'athāparāhne bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ' (in the afternoon the blessed Krishna with Samkarshana); 'tāṃ sampraviṣṭau vasudeva-nandanau vṛtau vayasyair naradeva-vartmanā' (the two sons of Vasudeva entered, surrounded by companions, along the kings' road).

statements.claim: The city rose before them dressed for a festival: a gateway of crystal with doors of gold and golden arches, crossroads of gold, high mansions and terraced gardens, rows of houses and open assembly halls, doves and peacocks calling in the lattice windows.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.19-21: 'sphāṭika-tuṇga-gopura-dvārāṃ bṛhad-dhema-kapāṭa-toraṇām... sauvarṇa-śṛṅgāṭaka-harmya-niṣkuṭaiḥ śreṇī-sabhābhir bhavanair upaskṛtām... āviṣṭa-pārāvata-barhi-nāditām'.

statements.claim: Water pots stood full along the streets; the ground was sprinkled with curd and sandalwood; garlands of flowers and strings of lamps hung among fresh green leaves.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.22: 'āpūrṇa-kumbhair dadhi-candanokṣitaiḥ prasūna-dīpāvalibhiḥ sa-pallavaiḥ' (full water-pots, sprinkled with curd and sandalwood, garlands of flowers and rows of lamps with fresh leaves).

statements.claim: The women of the city came running; in their haste one dressed with clothes and ornaments inside out, another forgot one of a pair (a single earring, a single anklet), another lined only one eye with kajal, some set down their food halfway, some left off being rubbed with oil before the bath was done.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.24-25: 'viparyag-dhṛta-vastra-bhūṣaṇā... vismṛtya caikaṃ yugaleṣv... kṛtaika-patra-śravanaika-nūpurā... nāṅktvā dvitīyaṃ... locanam... aśnantya ekās tad apāsya... abhyajyamānā akṛtopamajjanāḥ'.

statements.claim: The lotus-eyed Krishna's bold, easy smiles and teasing glances were like nectar poured out; the women drank the sight of him and embraced his form with their eyes, their skin thrilling, their long-carried sorrow loosening and falling away.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.26-27: 'manāṃsi tāsām aravinda-locanaḥ pragalbha-līlā-hasitāvalokaiḥ... tat-prekṣaṇotsmita-sudhokṣaṇa-labdha-mānāḥ... ānanda-mūrtim upaguhya dṛśātma-labdhaṃ hṛṣyat-tvaco jahur anantam arindamādhim' (lotus-eyed, bold playful smiles and glances; nectar-sprinkling; embracing the blissful form with their eyes; skin thrilling; they gave up their endless sorrow).

statements.claim: Those who could not reach the street climbed to the rooftops and showered down curd and unbroken rice and water, garlands and sweet scents, like offerings.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.28-29: 'prāsāda-śikharārūḍhāḥ prīty-utphulla-mukhāmbujāḥ... dadhy-akṣataiḥ soda-pātraiḥ srag-gandhair abhyupāyanaiḥ' (climbing to palace tops, faces blossoming with joy; curd, unbroken rice, water-pots, garlands, scents as offerings). The 'could not reach the street' motive is connective.

statements.claim: The people of the city called out in wonder: what great austerities must these gopis have performed, that they can see him whenever they wish?
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.30: 'ūcuḥ paurā aho gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran mahat' (the citizens said: aho, what great austerities did these gopis perform).

DKS_0130.notes: Tracks SB 10.41.18-30 closely, following the Sanskrit passage (citizens/paurāḥ shower offerings) rather than the pack's rendered note mentioning brahmins — story matches the authoritative passage. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama came that very day from Vrindavan with Akrura, who drove them in his chariot and went ahead to the palace, leaving the brothers to walk the city.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.82: Akrura set out with Krishna and Sankarshana, reached Mathura before evening, then went to Kamsa leaving the two to visit the highways; consistent with Bhagavata 10.41 chain.

statements.claim: They walked through Mathura like two elephants loosed from their posts.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.82: 'went on visiting all the high-ways like two elephants let free from their posts'.

statements.claim: They met the king's washerman carrying the king's own dyed cloth, gathered from many countries.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.82: 'I dye, as he desires, all the clothes of the king Kansa which he gets from various countries'; Vishnu Purana 5.19: washerman was Kamsa's servant.

statements.claim: Krishna asked the washerman for clothes that would suit the two of them.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.41.32: 'dehy āvayoḥ samucitāny aṅga vāsāṃsi'.

statements.claim: The washerman refused and abused them, calling them forest rangers born among the deer, stupid, of inferior understanding, and warning them to drop the request if they valued their lives.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.41.33-35; Harivamsha 1.82: 'born in a forest you have grown up with the deer... stupid and of inferior intellect... Perhaps giving up all hopes of your life you have come here'.

statements.claim: Destiny was against that washerman.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.82: 'Destiny was against that stupid washer-man of feeble understanding'.

statements.claim: Krishna, his anger rising, struck him a single blow of his open hand across the head, and the man fell and lay still.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.41.36 (struck off his head with his hand); Harivamsha 1.82: struck him on the head with his fist, 'with his head sundered he fell down lifeless on earth'.

statements.claim: The washerman's attendants dropped their bundles of dyed cloth and ran.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.41.37: 'tasyānujīvinaḥ sarve vāsaḥ-kośān visṛjya'.

statements.claim: The brothers chose garments for themselves and gave the rest away to the cowherds who had come from Vrindavan.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.41.38 (Krishna and Sankarshana wore garments dear to themselves); pack summary: 'took the garments and distributed them to the cowherds'.

statements.claim: The dye sat freshly on the cloth, red and yellow and deep blue.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric colour detail; pack confirms the cloth was dyed in many colours (Harivamsha 1.82).

DKS_0131.notes: All factual claims supported by Bhagavata 10.41.31-38 / Harivamsha 1.82 / Vishnu Purana 5.19. Story follows Bhagavata variant (attendants flee; garments distributed to cowherds), which the pack endorses.

statements.claim: In a hall in Mathura stood a great bow, the most guarded thing in the city, standing on a stand, worshipped and decked with offerings, ringed by armed men.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.15: 'puruṣair bahubhir guptam arcitaṃ paramarddhimat' (guarded by many men, worshipped, most splendid).

statements.claim: The bow was the centrepiece of the festival the king was preparing.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.82 refers to the 'bow-sacrifice' Krishna came to witness; festival context of the arc.

statements.claim: Krishna asked the townspeople where the famous bow was kept.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.14: 'tataḥ paurān pṛcchamāno dhanuṣaḥ sthānam acyutaḥ'.

statements.claim: The guards forbade him, but he took the great bow in his left hand, lifted it easily, and strung it in a single moment.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.16: 'kareṇa vāmena sa-līlam uddhṛtaṃ sajyaṃ ca kṛtvā nimiṣeṇa paśyatām'; pack excerpt: seized it though the guards forbade him.

statements.claim: He bent it and it snapped in two at the middle like a stalk of sugarcane, and the sound filled the sky, the earth and every direction, so that all Mathura heard it.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.16-17 (sugarcane simile; 'śabdaḥ khaṃ rodasī diśaḥ'); Vishnu Purana 5.20: 'all Mathurá resounded with the noise'.

statements.claim: The guards and their followers came at them, and Krishna and Balarama struck down the whole force Kamsa had sent, using the two broken halves of the bow.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.18-20: 'tad-rakṣiṇaḥ sānucaraṃ kupitā ātatāyinaḥ... balaṃ ca kaṃsa-prahitaṃ hatvā'.

statements.claim: The townspeople marvelled, and the sun was going down as they walked out into the city.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.21-22 (townsfolk saw the wonderful valour; 'ādityo 'stam upeyivān').

statements.claim: No archer's hand had drawn the bow in living memory.
statements.evidence: Rhetorical framing of the bow's sacred, unused status; not contradicted by the pack.

statements.claim: By nightfall there was not a household that had not heard the tale told twice.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric hyperbole following 10.42.21 (townspeople witnessed and spoke of the feat).

DKS_0133.notes: All key events match Bhagavata 10.42.13-22 (left-hand lift, stringing, sugarcane snap, noise filling Mathura, guards struck down with the two halves).

statements.claim: The news reached Kamsa that the great bow was broken and the men he had set to guard it were dead.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.25: 'kaṃsas tu dhanuṣo bhaṅgaṃ rakṣiṇāṃ sva-balasya ca'.

statements.claim: He had known the two young men were coming for years and watched for them fearfully.
statements.evidence: Canonical arc background (Kamsa's long-standing fear of the prophecy, established in earlier corpus stories); consistent with the pack, not contradicted.

statements.claim: That night Kamsa did not sleep; fear kept him awake.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.26: 'dīrgha-prajāgaro bhīto durnimittāni durmatiḥ' (long wakefulness, terrified, evil omens).

statements.claim: He looked into a mirror and could not see his own head in the reflection, though his face should have been there.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.27: 'adarśanaṃ sva-śirasaḥ pratirūpe ca saty api'.

statements.claim: He looked at his shadow and saw a hole running through it, and strained to hear his own breathing and heard nothing.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.28: 'chidra-pratītiś chāyāyāṃ prāṇa-ghoṣānupaśrutiḥ'.

statements.claim: In dreams he embraced a corpse and rode an ass through the night, and a heaviness and dejection settled over everything.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.29: 'svapne preta-pariṣvaṅgaḥ khara-yānaṃ viṣādanam'.

statements.claim: By morning he had seen his own death in every sign; the omens all said the same thing.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: omens and dreams 'all foretelling his death'; Bhagavata 10.42.30 ('anyāni cetthaṃ-bhūtāni svapna-jāgaritāni ca').

DKS_0134.notes: All omens map directly to Bhagavata 10.42.23-30 verses. The 'known for years' line reflects the arc's established prophecy background (previous stories), not the pack passage, but is consistent and uncontradicted.

statements.claim: When the night ended and the sun rose out of the waters, Kamsa gave his order: let the wrestling begin.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.31-32: 'vyuṣṭāyāṃ niśi... sūrye cādbhyaḥ samutthite... tūrya-bheryaś ca jaghnire'.

statements.claim: The arena was prepared with drums and kettledrums sounding, the noise reaching every corner of Mathura.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.32: 'ānarcuḥ puruṣā raṅgaṃ tūrya-bheryaś ca jaghnire'.

statements.claim: Citizens and country folk poured in, brahmins and kshatriyas at their head, until the stands were full.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.33: 'teṣu paurā jānapadā brahma-kṣatra-purogamāḥ'.

statements.claim: Kamsa climbed to the royal dais with his ministers around him.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.34: 'kaṃsaḥ parivṛto 'mātyai rāja-mañca upāviśat'.

statements.claim: The wrestlers took their places: Chanura, Mushtika, Kuta, Shala and Toshala.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.36: 'cāṇūro muṣṭikaḥ kūtaḥ śalas tośala eva ca'.

statements.claim: Summoned by the Bhoja king, Nanda and the cowherds arrived bearing their offerings.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.42.37: 'nanda-gopādayo gopā bhoja-rāja-samāhutāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'arrived with their offerings'.

statements.claim: Ropes were drawn around the wrestling ground.
statements.evidence: Plausible arena detail; not explicitly in the pack verses, no contradiction.

DKS_0135.notes: Matches Bhagavata 10.42.31-37 point by point, including the 'sun risen from the waters' detail and the full wrestler list.

statements.claim: At the gate of the wrestling arena stood the elephant Kuvalayapida; Kamsa had ordered 'let it wait at the gate'.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.1 ('raṅga-dvāraṃ samāsādya tasmin nāgam avasthitam'); Harivamsha 1.84: 'Having ordered "Let the elephant Kuvalyapida wait at the gate"'.

statements.claim: The arena rose on octagonal pillars painted in many colours, hung with festoons of flowers and the banners of every guild, with gold and gems and seats and couches; Kamsa's pavilion shone like a mountain of snow.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.84 (2-15): octagonal painted pillars, festoons of flowers, banners of the crafts, gold and gems, cushioned seats; Kamsa's pavilion 'like mount Meru in radiance', the king shining 'like the moon... on the white summit of the white mountain'.

statements.claim: The king entered in white with white chowries waving, took his throne, and the citizens shouted his praises; the wrestlers, loose-garmented, took the ground on three sides.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.84 (18-20): two white chowries, white raiment and turban, citizens' shouts of victory, wrestlers with loose garments on three sides.

statements.claim: Krishna tied back his garments and gathered his curling hair before approaching.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.2: 'baddhvā parikaraṃ śauriḥ samuhya kuṭilālakān'.

statements.claim: He told the elephant's keeper to stand aside and make way; the keeper, stung, goaded the beast, which came forward with trunk folded to crush them.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.3-4; Harivamsha 1.84: 'that wicked elephant, folding up its trunk, attempted to destroy Rama and Krishna'.

statements.claim: Krishna slipped beneath it, took hold of its tail, and dragged it back the length of twenty-five bows; he moved between its tusks and under its legs like the wind troubling the sea.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.7-8 ('pucche pragṛhyāti-balaṃ dhanuṣaḥ pañca-viṃśatim'; 'savya-dakṣiṇato'); Harivamsha 1.84: 'agitated him as does wind the ocean'.

statements.claim: He roared like a lion, slapped his arms, and let the elephant's trunk come against his chest; the enraged beast, seeing only by smell, could not find him.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.5-6 ('ghrāṇa-dṛṣṭiḥ'); Harivamsha 1.84 (26-27): roaring like a lion, slapping arms, taking the trunk on his breast.

statements.claim: He sported with the elephant in a childlike way, smiling, and said Kamsa, in trying to kill him through the elephant, was only hurrying himself to the abode of Yama.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.10-11 ('sa dhāvan kṛīdayā'); Harivamsha 1.84 (24-25): 'he is eager to repair to the abode of Yama'; 'sporting with that elephant under the pretext of a childish freak'.

statements.claim: On the second charge he pressed it down and set his foot on it like a lion settling its prey, tore out both tusks with his two hands and beat it with them; it discharged must like a cloud in the rains and lay still, blood dark at its temples.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.12-14; Harivamsha 1.84 (31-35): foot on the lower lip, uprooting the tusks with both hands, must discharged 'like a cloud in the rains', blood from the temples.

statements.claim: Its keepers fell with it.
statements.evidence: Pack summary of Bhagavata 10.43.1-15: 'slew the beast and its keepers'.

statements.claim: Krishna took up one of the tusks, and he and Balarama, surrounded by the cowherds, entered the arena covered with the elephant's blood and must.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.14-15 ('danta-pāṇiḥ samāviśat'; 'vṛtau gopaiḥ katipayair baladeva-janārdanau'); Harivamsha 1.85 and Vishnu Purana 5.20: 'covered with must and blood' entered the arena.

statements.claim: Kamsa watched from his high seat as the two came forward.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.84: the king seated on his throne in the arena; consistent with the narrative.

DKS_0136.notes: Follows the Bhagavata variant (Krishna alone slays the elephant), as the tradition_note states; all details including the 25-bow drag and tusk removal are verse-backed.

statements.claim: Krishna walked into the arena holding the elephant's tusk, Balarama at his side, the two great-armed, in bright garments, garlands and ornaments.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.14, 17-18: tusk in hand ('danta-pāṇiḥ'); 'mahā-bhujau vicitra-veṣābharaṇa-srag-ambarau'.

statements.claim: The galleries were full — townsmen and countrymen, kings and commoners, wrestlers and merchants, women at the screened windows — and the people drank the two in with their eyes and as if with their tongues.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.19-20 ('nāgara-rāṣṭrakā nṛpa'; 'pibanta iva cakṣurbhyāṃ lihanta iva jihvayā'); Harivamsha 1.84: women viewing through 'delicate jealousies' (screened windows).

statements.claim: Each person saw him according to his own heart: a thunderbolt to the wrestlers, best of men to ordinary men, embodied love to the women, a kinsman to the cowherds, a chastiser to the wicked among the kings, the highest truth to the ignorant, the goal of the yogis, the supreme deity of the Vrishnis, a child to his parents, and death to the lord of the Bhojas, Kamsa.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.16: 'mallānām aśanir nṛṇāṃ nara-varaḥ strīṇāṃ smaro mūrtimān / gopānāṃ sva-jano 'satāṃ kṣiti-bhujāṃ śāstā sva-pitroḥ śiśuḥ / mṛtyur bhoja-pater virāḍ aviduṣāṃ tattvaṃ paraṃ yogināṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ para-devatā'.

statements.claim: The people recounted his deeds: born to Devaki and carried to Gokula; the end of Putana and the whirlwind demon; saving the cows and cowherds from the forest fire; holding up a great hill on one hand for seven days; the gopis' delight in his smiling glance; the fame of the Yadu line; and the elder brother, the glorious lotus-eyed Rama.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.23-29: 'eṣa vai kila devakyāṃ jāto nītaś ca gokulam / pūtanānena nītāntaṃ cakravātaś ca dānavaḥ / gāvaḥ sa-pālā etena dāvāgneḥ parimocitāḥ / saptāham eka-hastena dhṛto 'dri-pravaro 'munā / gopyo 'sya nitya-mudita-hasita-prekṣaṇaṃ mukham / vadanty anena vaṃśo 'yaṃ yadoḥ su-bahu-viśrutaḥ / ayaṃ cāsyāgrajaḥ śrīmān rāmaḥ kamala-locanaḥ'.

statements.claim: The city had come to watch them die, and for a moment forgot it.
statements.evidence: Framing of the crowd's wonder; consistent with the pack's theme (delight and rejoicing before the fight).

DKS_0137.notes: The multi-perspective description and the entire remembered-deeds catalogue map directly onto Bhagavata 10.43.16-30.

statements.claim: Chanura, a wrestler and Kamsa's champion, walked into the centre of the arena and addressed the two brothers, calling them 'Son of Nanda' and 'Rama', saying heroes are counted as such, that those who please the king find their welfare, that the cowherds are always cheerful, and proposing that both they and he do what pleases the king.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.31-34: 'he nanda-sūno he rāma bhavantau vīra-sammatau / priyaṃ rājñaḥ prakurvatyaḥ śreyo vindanti vai prajāḥ / nityaṃ pramuditā gopā... / tasmād rājñaḥ priyaṃ yūyaṃ vayaṃ ca karavāma he'.

statements.claim: Krishna's reply was fitted to the time and place: 'We are subjects of this lord of the Bhojas, but we are forest-dwellers; we are boys and will play with those of equal strength, as is proper.'
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.35-37: 'deśa-kālocitaṃ vacaḥ / prajā bhoja-pater asya vayaṃ cāpi vane-carāḥ / bālā vayaṃ tulya-balaiḥ krīḍiṣyāmo yathocitam'.

statements.claim: Chanura insisted the fight must go forward and that there was no injustice in it, saying he would meet Krishna and Mushtika would face Balarama.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.43.38-39 ('tasmād bhavadbhyāṃ balibhir yoddhavyaṃ nānayo 'tra vai'); pack summary: 'Chanura urged, "Fight me, and let Mushtika fight Balarama"'.

statements.claim: Chanura was a wrestler who had made his name breaking the men he was set against.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.85: Chanura 'has put a stigma on the ways of wrestlers by destroying many of them after their discomfiture'.

statements.claim: High above the ring Kamsa watched from his throne and said nothing, letting his champion press the match.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric; consistent with Kamsa seated on the royal dais (10.42.34) and the events' intent. Not explicitly stated in 10.43.30-39.

DKS_0138.notes: The dialogue closely tracks Bhagavata 10.43.30-39; the Mushtika-pairing detail is endorsed by the pack summary.

statements.claim: After Kamsa lay dead and the wrestlers had fallen, his eight younger brothers — Kanka, Nyagrodha and the rest — came rushing at Krishna in fury.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.44.39: 'tasyānujā bhrātaro 'ṣṭau kaṅka-nyagrodhakādayaḥ'; pack summary: 'rushed at Krishna in fury'.

statements.claim: Balarama, the elder, son of Rohini, stepped between them and Krishna and slew all eight with his club, like a lion moving through cattle.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.44.40: 'tathāti-rabhasāṃs tāṃs tu saṃyattān rohiṇī-sutaḥ'; pack summary: 'Balarama slew them all with his club, like a lion among cattle'.

statements.claim: He took the proudest of them in his two hands and felled him as easily as the rest.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.85: 'Holding powerfully by his hands the proud brother of Kansa, by name Urgita, the virtuous-souled Baladeva killed him'.

statements.claim: The elephant's tusk was still in Krishna's hand when the brothers charged.
statements.evidence: Consistent with Bhagavata 10.43.14 (tusk in hand at the arena entrance) and 10.44 sequence; uncontradicted.

statements.claim: The house of Kamsa had spent years sending its killers after a child.
statements.evidence: Canonical arc background (Kamsa's attempts on the infant Krishna, prior stories); consistent with the pack, uncontradicted.

statements.claim: The verses give the brothers only a line of names and the single motion of their charge; one club, eight men, and then silence.
statements.evidence: Rhetorical compression of Bhagavata 10.44.39-40, which indeed devotes only two verses to the episode.

DKS_0141.notes: Follows the Bhagavata (parents' greeting kept separate, per tradition_note); the Urgita detail from Harivamsha is used only where it fits ('the proudest of them').

statements.claim: Kamsa lay dead with his brothers, and the men of Mathura stood stunned among the fallen while the wives of the slain warriors wept and lamented over their husbands on the field.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.44.41-48: the women, grieving at the slaying of their friends/husbands, lament over the husbands lying on the heroes' bed (v.42-43 'teṣāṃ striyo... śayānān vīra-śayāyāṃ patīn āliṅgya śocatīḥ'); Kamsa's death and his brothers' fall are the immediately preceding canonical events (DKS_0141, Bhagavata 10.44.36-40).

statements.claim: The widows called to the dead by tender epithets — lord, beloved, knower of righteousness, kind to the shelterless — and mourned the city left without its protector.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.44.44-45: 'hā nātha priya dharma-jña karuṇānātha-vatsala / tvayā virahitā patyā purīyaṃ puruṣarṣabha'.

statements.claim: Even Kamsa's wives wept, and the sound reached the palace and the streets.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.87: Ugrasena hears 'the heart-rending lamentations of Kansa's wives' bewailing their husbands; pack excerpt (SB 10.44.41-48) covers the royal women's weeping.

statements.claim: Krishna did not turn away; he walked among the royal women, comforted them, and had the customary funeral rites prepared for the dead.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (Bhagavata 10.44.41-48, confidence 5): 'Krishna comforted the royal women and had the customary funeral rites performed for the dead'.

statements.claim: Ugrasena, burning with grief and breathing like a man who had drunk poison, came and reproached himself in the assembly of the Yadavas for having made widows of these thousand women.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.87 (1-4): 'Breathing like a person who has drunk poison, Ugrasena, burning with grief for his son, approached Krishna... censuring his own self in that assembly of the Yādavas... I have... made widows of these thousand women.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena reflected that Kamsa was sinful, hated by the pious and ruthless of temper, so that death was better than such a life, and that the wicked reap their fruits by death while the pious reach auspicious ones.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.87 (7-12): 'Death is preferable to life unto him who... is of a degraded conduct, ruthless temper... Kansa was highly sinful, never liked by the pious... Those, who are wicked, are constrained by Death to reap the proper fruits. The pious attain to auspicious fruits.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena asked leave to perform Kamsa's after-death rites — to build the pyre, put fire to it and offer the water-oblation — after which he would range in the forest with his wife and daughters-in-law.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.87 (26-30): 'Having performed the after-death ceremonies of that king... I shall, along with my wife and daughters-in-law, range in the forest with the animals... having made his funeral pyre, putting fire to it and offering oblation of water I shall have discharged debt to Kansa... This is my only prayer.'

statements.claim: Krishna was filled with surprise at Ugrasena's words and answered with consolation: what Ugrasena said befitted his age, family and nature; the inevitable work being done, Kamsa would still receive funeral honors befitting a king, and destiny is inevitable.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.87 (31-34): 'Hearing the words of Ugrasena, Krishna was filled with surprise. And consoling him he said: ...what you have said behoves your age and family... Although dead, Kansa will receive funeral honors befitting a king... Why do you not then understand that destiny is inevitable?'

statements.claim: Kamsa's body was placed in a palanquin and carried to the northern bank of the Yamuna, where the pyre was raised, fire set, and the obsequial rites performed.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.87 (58-59) excerpt: 'desirous of performing the obsequial rites of king Kansa according to the ritualastic laws they placed his body in a palanquin and took it to the northern bank of Yamuna... setting fire to the pyre.'

statements.claim: The day that began with the wrestling match ended with the funeral, and Mathura had to bury its dead before enjoying its freedom.
statements.evidence: Framing close to the story; the corpus treats the lament and rites as the same aftermath event (evt_0146); the Harivamsha has the cremation on the following morning, but the pack's own Bhagavata-based summary presents the rites within this episode, so no contradiction is asserted.

DKS_0142.notes: Faithful to Bhagavata 10.44.41-48 and Harivamsha 1.87; the long Ugrasena/Krishna exchange maps verse by verse to the pack's Dutt translation.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama walked into the prison where Vasudeva and Devaki were still bound, released them from their bonds themselves, and bowed to touch their parents' feet.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.44.49-50: 'mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva mocayitvātha bandhanāt'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna and Balarama released Vasudeva and Devaki from their bonds and bowed, touching their feet'.

statements.claim: Vasudeva and Devaki, knowing their sons to be the lords of the world, embraced them without fear.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.44.50: 'devakī vasudevaś ca vijñāya jagad-īśvarau' ('knowing [them to be] the lords of the world'); pack excerpt: 'the parents, knowing their sons to be the lords of the world, embraced them without fear'.

statements.claim: Kamsa killed Devaki's children one by one as they were born, and the last two sons were smuggled out of the prison on the night of their birth — Krishna carried across the Yamuna by his father, Balarama taken to safety before him.
statements.evidence: Canonical arc background established in earlier corpus events (the six slain children and the night transfers of Balarama and Krishna, per Bhagavata 10.2-10.3 and prior stories); consistent with this pack, uncontradicted.

statements.claim: For eighteen years those gates had held Vasudeva and Devaki, and the cell had been a cage for nearly two decades.
statements.evidence: No support in the pack (Bhagavata 10.44.49-50 / Vishnu Purana 5.20) or anywhere in the corpus chain. The corpus only establishes that Krishna dwelt in Vraja for eleven years (DKS_0016, SB-based) and that the imprisonment began before the children's births; the total duration is nowhere quantified, so the specific figure 'eighteen years'/'nearly two decades' is unsupported.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: She had been told, on the night Krishna was born, that her eighth child would be the death of Kamsa.
statements.evidence: The corpus's own canonical event (DKS_0003, Bhagavata 10.1.28-33, Vishnu Purana 5.1, Harivamsha 1.56) places the eighth-child prophecy at Vasudeva and Devaki's WEDDING, when Kamsa drove the chariot and heard the bodiless voice — years before Krishna's birth. The story shifts the prophecy to Krishna's birth night, which contradicts the established account.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: The parents remembered the words Krishna spoke at his birth, when the chains fell from their hands and he promised to return when the time came, and the promise had been kept.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.20 (pack): Vasudeva and Devaki bowed to Krishna, 'recalling to recollection what he had said to them at his birth'; consistent with the birth-night release of the chains in the earlier corpus chain.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama had grown up in Gokula knowing their parents only as names, and came to their parents before the throne, the city, or anything else victory might have claimed.
statements.evidence: Framing of the reunion (Vraja upbringing is canonical chain background); the ordering against the throne/city is the story's reflective framing, not a sourceable assertion.

corrections.original_sentence: For eighteen years those gates had held Vasudeva and Devaki — the couple whose children Kamsa had feared so much that he killed them one by one, and whose last two sons had been smuggled out of that very prison on the night of their birth.
corrections.suggested: All the years of Kamsa's reign those gates had held Vasudeva and Devaki — the couple whose children Kamsa had feared so much that he killed them one by one, and whose last two sons had been smuggled out of that very prison on the night of their birth.

corrections.original_sentence: She had been told, on the night Krishna was born, that her eighth child would be the death of Kamsa, and she had watched Kamsa take her children from her, one after another, as they were born.
corrections.suggested: She had been told, on the night of her wedding, that her eighth child would be the death of Kamsa, and she had watched Kamsa take her children from her, one after another, as they were born.

corrections.original_sentence: Every fear she had carried for eighteen years had been about these two young men who now knelt at her feet.
corrections.suggested: Every fear she had carried through all the years of her imprisonment had been about these two young men who now knelt at her feet.

corrections.original_sentence: The chains lay on the floor of the cell, and the room that had been a cage for nearly two decades had become, in the space of a few breaths, the place where a family stood whole.
corrections.suggested: The chains lay on the floor of the cell, and the room that had been a cage for so many years had become, in the space of a few breaths, the place where a family stood whole.

DKS_0143.notes: Core reunion is faithful (SB 10.44.49-50 + VP 5.20). Two issues: (1) 'eighteen years'/'nearly two decades' duration is unsupported anywhere in the pack or corpus (corpus only gives 11 years in Vraja, DKS_0016); (2) the prophecy is misdated to Krishna's birth night — the corpus canon (DKS_0003) has the voice at the wedding procession.

statements.claim: Krishna, who had broken the great bow, felled the wrestlers and ended Kamsa, stood bowed before his parents asking their pardon, with Balarama at his side.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.45.1: 'uvāca pitarāv etya sāgrajaḥ sātvanarṣabhaḥ' (the best of the Satvatas, with his elder brother, approaching the parents, spoke); bow/wrestlers/Kamsa are the established preceding events of the arc.

statements.claim: Krishna told his parents they had ever longed for them, but struck by fate they could not dwell near them, though the parents wished it with all their hearts.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.45.2-3: 'nāsmatto yuvayos tāta nityotkaṇṭhitayor api / na labdho daiva-hatayor vāso nau bhavad-antike'.

statements.claim: Krishna said the body that becomes the seat of every purpose is born and nourished from the parents, and the debt owed to a mother, father, aged parent, devoted wife and young son no one can repay with himself or all his wealth.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.45.4-6: 'sarvārtha-sambhavo deho janitaḥ poṣito yataḥ / ... mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vṛddhaṃ bhāryāṃ sādhvīṃ sutam śiśum'; v.5 'ātmanā ca dhanena ca'.

statements.claim: He confessed that kept from them by Kamsa, their minds never at peace, they could not serve their parents as sons should, and asked forgiveness — 'we were in the power of another'.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.45.7-8: 'tan nāv akalpayoḥ kaṃsān nityam udvigna-cetasoḥ / tat kṣantum arhathas tāta mātar nau para-tantrayoḥ'.

statements.claim: Vasudeva and Devaki could not answer at first; they reached out and held their sons, their tears fell on the sons' heads, and the old rope of affection bound the four of them together.
statements.evidence: Bhagavata 10.45.10 (given in the following episode's passage): 'siñcantāv aśru-dhārābhiḥ sneha-pāśena cāvṛtau' (the two, pouring streams of tears, bound by the rope of affection); parents' tears and embrace are the pack's depicted response.

statements.claim: The two parents had been helpless for eighteen years in the prison.
statements.evidence: Specific duration appears in no source: this pack covers Bhagavata 10.45.1-9 only, and the corpus nowhere quantifies the imprisonment (cf. DKS_0143 note); the corpus only establishes eleven years in Vraja (DKS_0016) plus unquantified pre-birth years.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: There was no anger or settling of accounts in the prison that day; the sons who had been taken came back asking forgiveness rather than giving it, and asked only that their parents forgive them for the childhood they had missed.
statements.evidence: Reflective commentary on the plea; consistent with the pack's account of the humble request for forgiveness, no new factual assertion.
