DKS_0226.notes: No unsupported/contradicted claims. Every recited grievance and the final challenge map to HV 1.127. The Nandana-garden naming is cross-corroborated by HV 1.220 (used for DKS_0227).

statements.claim: Krishna left Dwaraka under the pretext of a hunt, rode out to the Raivataka mountain with Satyaki, handed his chariot to Daruka, and promised to re-enter the city on that very car
statements.evidence: HV 1.220 (Dutt): 'a moment after sun rise, went to the Raivataka mountain, under the pretext of hunting, taking up... Satyaki... O Daruka, take charge of my chariot... I shall re-enter Dwarka on this very car.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna followed behind on a separate car capable of coursing over hills
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Pradyumna followed Krishna from behind on a separate car capable of coursing on hills.'

statements.claim: Krishna mounted Garuda with Satyaki and within the twinkle of an eye arrived at the Nandana forest, pleasure park of the gods
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Within the twinkle of an eye the intelligent Hari arrived at the pleasure park of the gods, the Nandana forest.'

statements.claim: Hosts of celestial warriors, indomitable and armed with various weapons, kept watch in the garden
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the illustrious Adhokshaja saw hosts of celestial warriors, indomitable, courageous and armed with various weapons.'

statements.claim: Krishna tore the Parijata from the earth before the guards could gather and set it on Garuda's back
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the mighty Krishna uprooted the Parijata tree and placed it on the back of Garuda even before their eyes.'

statements.claim: The tree embodied itself and approached in prayer, and Krishna consoled it: 'Do not fear, O tree'
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the Parijata, having embodied itself, approached (with prayer) Kesava and Garuda... was consoled... Do thou not fear, O tree.'

statements.claim: Krishna circled the stronghold of the gods once, the tree riding behind him on Garuda
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Adhokshaja began to go round that best of strong-holds, the abode of the gods.'

statements.claim: The garden keepers ran to Indra with the news that the finest tree in heaven was being carried away
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the keepers of the garden of gods, had run to Mahendra and informed him... the most excellent of trees, the Parijata, is being carried away.'

statements.claim: Indra rode out on Airavata, Jayanta following on a chariot, and found Krishna at the eastern gate of heaven
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the subduer of Paka (Indra) came out mounted on Airavata being followed from behind by Jayanta on a car... Vásudeva, who had by that time reached the Eastern gate.'

statements.claim: Krishna saluted his elder and said he was taking the excellent tree for a ceremonious observance for his sister-in-law
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Kesava, seated on the back of Garuda, saluted Sakra with his head and said:—I am only taking away this excellent tree for a ceremonious observance of your sister-in-law.'

statements.claim: Indra answered that Krishna should not take the tree without challenging him, and bade him deal the first blow and hurl the Kaumodaki mace
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'thou shouldst not take away this tree... without challenging me to fight... let thy promise be fulfilled by your hurling the Koumodaki mace at me.'

statements.claim: Krishna pierced the great elephant with arrows fierce like thunder; Indra pierced Garuda with heavenly arrows and cut off Krishna's shafts; Krishna smilingly cut off Indra's in turn
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Krishna began to pierce the excellent elephant of the king of the celestials, with sharp arrows fierce like thunder itself... the wielder of the thunder-bolt began to pierce Garuda... Madhava cut off all those arrows... smiling.'

statements.claim: At the twang of the Sharanga and the thunder of Indra's bow together, the inhabitants of heaven swooned away
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'at the sound of Mahendra's bow and at the twang of the Sranga bow, the inhabitants of heaven swooned away.'

statements.claim: Jayanta slipped toward Garuda and tried to remove the Parijata; Krishna told Pradyumna to prevent him, and a fierce duel blazed between the two sons while gods, sages, Siddhas and Charanas looked on amazed
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the highly powerful Jayanta tried to remove the Parijata tree from the back of Garuda... the slayer of Kansa said to Pradyumna Prevent him... a fierce combat raged between the heroic Jayanta and the son of Rukshmini... The gods, the sages, the Siddhas and the Charnas... struck with wonder.'

statements.claim: A messenger of the gods named Pravara, of great strength, advanced toward the tree on Garuda's back, and Krishna told Satyaki: 'Even from this place, oppose him'
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'a messenger of the gods, named Pravara, of great strength, tried to take away the Parijata from the back of Garuda... Krishna told Satyaki;—O Satyaki, even from this place do thou oppose Pravara.'

DKS_0227.notes: Faithful to HV 1.220. VP 5.30 (pack variant: Krishna defeats the gods with his discus) is not narrated and nothing contradicts it. 'By evening' in the Daruka promise is a light connective gloss on the source's half-day wait.

statements.claim: Pravara, a warrior of heaven whom no weapon could slay, had been born a Brahmana on Jambu island, won heaven through the merit of penances, and earned the friendship of Indra himself
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'this Pravara was the friend of the ruler of the gods... Formerly he was a Brahmana inhabiting the Jamva Island, whence through the merit of religious penances, he attained to heaven... earned the friendship of the slayer of Vala.'

statements.claim: Brahma granted Pravara a boon that he could never be killed
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'he was incapable of being slain by virtue of a boon obtained from Brahma.'

statements.claim: In Indra's service Pravara had become a messenger of heaven, accomplished in mighty weapons and able to subdue all foes
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'a messenger of the gods, named Pravara, of great strength... accomplished in the use of mighty weapons and able to subdue all his foes.'

statements.claim: Pravara came forward in the battle over the Parijata, making for the tree on Garuda's back
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Pravara... tried to take away the Parijata from the back of Garuda.'

statements.claim: Krishna marked him and said: 'O Satyaki, even from this place, oppose him'
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'On beholding him advance, Krishna told Satyaki;—O Satyaki, even from this place do thou oppose Pravara.'

statements.claim: Satyaki had stood beside Krishna through the wars of Mathura and Dwaraka and had never refused his lord
statements.evidence: General character continuity not asserted in this pack (the pack shows only Satyaki accompanying Krishna on the Raivataka outing); biographical background, not a plot fact.

statements.claim: In the duel Pravara cut down Satyaki's shafts in mid-air and repeatedly struck the bow from his hand, disarming him before the watching gods
statements.evidence: Pack canonical summary for this story: 'Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him.' (The 1.220 passage shown in the pack truncates mid-duel; summary covers the disarming sequence.)

statements.claim: Satyaki could not wound the boon-protected champion, yet he gave him no rest and never gave ground
statements.evidence: Pravara's invulnerability is in-source (boon from Brahma); the 'refusal to yield' drama is connective narration of the duel.

statements.claim: Pravara tired of the duel, turned his mount, and made for the Parijata, reaching for the tree on Garuda's back
statements.evidence: HV 1.220 (continuation) and pack summary: 'when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.'

statements.claim: One blow of Garuda's wing hurled Pravara and his chariot a full four miles back through the sky; he struck the ground and lay senseless
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.220): 'Garuda struck him with his wings so vehemently that he, with his car, fell full four miles back and there fainted away.'

statements.claim: Satyaki, bow in hand, took his place beside the tree as its guard
statements.evidence: Connective; consistent with Satyaki's charge of protecting the tree (HV 1.221: Satyaki and Pradyumna went 'to protect the Parijata tree').

statements.claim: The king of birds was already turning his eyes toward the elephant below
statements.evidence: Bridge to the next beat; Garuda's attack on Airavata follows in the same chapter (pack DKS_0229 excerpt).

DKS_0228.notes: Duel details rely on the pack's canonical summary + excerpt because the quoted HV 1.220 passage is truncated at the moment Krishna orders Satyaki to oppose Pravara; nothing in the story exceeds what the summary and excerpt cover.

statements.claim: Through the morning the duel raged above heaven, Krishna on Garuda against Indra on Airavata, the air crossed with arrows
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: Indra came out mounted on Airavata; Krishna pierced the elephant with sharp arrows; Indra pierced Garuda with heavenly arrows; each cut off the other's shafts.

statements.claim: Airavata was the banner of the king of the gods, carrier through a hundred asura wars, his presence meaning heaven would not lose, his tusks the pride of the celestial world
statements.evidence: Traditional descriptive lore about Indra's war-elephant; hedged ('was said to mean') and not asserted by the pack excerpt.

statements.claim: In the first exchange Krishna drove arrows into the elephant's flanks, sharp arrows fierce like thunder
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Krishna began to pierce the excellent elephant of the king of the celestials, with sharp arrows fierce like thunder itself.'

statements.claim: Airavata stood shaking off the arrows as a mountain shakes off rain
statements.evidence: Connective flourish; the pack shows the elephant's wounds come from Garuda's claws (see next statements), and no text shows it shrugging off Krishna's arrows.

statements.claim: Garuda had borne the Parijata through the whole battle and had just hurled Pravara four miles with a sweep of his wings
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: tree placed on Garuda's back (v9); Pravara fell 'full four miles back and there fainted away'.

statements.claim: Garuda struck Airavata on the head with his fierce claws furnished with fearful talons
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.220): 'Garuda, of mighty strength, struck Airavata on the head with his fierce claws furnished with fearful talons.'

statements.claim: The elephant screamed and reared, sorely afflicted by the wound, as Garuda struck again until the beast began to stagger
statements.evidence: The excerpt confirms the wound afflicted Airavata sorely and that it fell; screaming/rearing/staggering are connective dramatization.

statements.claim: The elephant fell from the heights of heaven, striking the top of the Parijatra mountain, where it lay
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.220): 'Afflicted sorely with the wound... the elephant fell from the heights of heaven on the top of that best of mountains the Parijatra.'

statements.claim: Indra stood in the sky without his mount, and even the arrows between the brothers ceased to fly
statements.evidence: The pack records only the elephant's fall; nothing has Indra dismounted or stranded in the sky. The source's own continuation (HV 1.221, quoted in the corpus for DKS_0230) opens with 'the mighty Lord of the immortals... remaining on the back of the Airavata' at the Parijatra — Indra stays with the fallen elephant on the mountain.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: The gods stared at the mountain where their banner had fallen, and the battle paused
statements.evidence: Aftermath framing; the wonder of the watchers and the lull are connective, consistent with the source moving the scene to the mountain.

statements.claim: The might of the king of the gods had been measured against the might of the bird who carried Krishna, and the bird prevailed
statements.evidence: Interpretive closing reflection on the episode, not a new factual assertion.

corrections.original_sentence: Indra stood in the sky without his mount, and even the arrows between the brothers ceased to fly.
corrections.suggested: Indra remained with his great elephant Airavata, who now lay fallen on the top of the Parijatra mountain, and even the arrows between the brothers ceased to fly.

DKS_0229.notes: One unsupported claim: Indra is depicted standing alone in the sky after Airavata falls, whereas the pack excerpt and the source's continuation (HV 1.221.1: Indra remaining on Airavata's back at the Parijatra) keep Indra with his mount on the mountain. Correction offered. All battle mechanics otherwise map to HV 1.220.

statements.claim: Recap: all day the gods' king fought from Airavata's back over the uprooted Parijata, and Garuda wounded the elephant sorely
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'beholding the elephant Airavata sorely afflicted with the wounds inflicted on him' (wounds inflicted by Garuda per v8).

statements.claim: At nightfall, when the sun had gone down behind the Parijatra mountain, the battle began again
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'By that time the sun went down the horizon and night set in. But the battle between Sakra and Keshava commenced anew.'

statements.claim: Krishna called to Indra: Airavata is sorely wounded and night grows apace; let us refrain from fighting and do as you wish tomorrow morning — and Indra agreed
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the foremost of elephants Airavata has been sorely wounded by Garuda: night also grows on apace. Let us refrain from fighting (now). Do as thou wishest to-morrow morning again... Let it be so then.'

statements.claim: The Parijatra mountain made itself small as a grinding stone for sandal when Krishna came, and he was pleased with it
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the Parijatra, that knew the powers of the high-souled son of Valadeva, on beholding Janarddana approach, entered into the earth, becoming as small as a stone for grinding sandal. Keshava was then highly pleased with the mountain.'

statements.claim: Indra erected a temporary shelter of stones for the night near the sacred Pushkara
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the king of the gods Purandara... erecting a temporary shade with stones, stopped there near the Puskara for the night.'

statements.claim: Brahma, the sage Kashyapa with Aditi, and the hosts of heaven — Sadhyas, Vasus, the Ashwini twins, Adityas and Rudras — assembled there
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Brahma, the mighty sage Kasyapa, Aditi, and other gods and sages came to him there... the Sadhyas, Viswadevas, the Aswini Kumaras, the Adityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus also assembled there.'

statements.claim: Krishna stayed on the mountain with Pradyumna and Satyaki, the Parijata resting on Garuda's back behind him
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Narayana also remained on that delightful mountain Parijatra accompanied by his son and Satyaki' and Garuda with the Parijata followed him, Satyaki and Pradyumna riding to protect the tree.

statements.claim: Krishna blessed the mountain: it shall be called Sanapada, auspicious and holy as the Himalaya, abounding in gems, outvying Meru
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'thou shalt be called Sanapada; and thou shalt be auspicious and holy like the Himalaya Mountain... abounding in numerous kinds of gems, do thou outvie the celebrated Meru mountain.'

statements.claim: Saluting the god whose emblem is the bull, Krishna thought of the Ganga, and the river that has its source in Vishnu's feet (Vishnupadi) came; he worshipped her and bathed in her water
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Keshava, after due salutation to the God having the emblem of the bull, remembered that foremost of rivers, the Ganges... the river Vishnupadi (having the feet of Vishnu for its source) came there, and Krishna, having worshipped her, performed his ablutions.'

statements.claim: Taking up the sacred water and bilva leaves, Krishna invited Rudra, lord of all lords, to be present
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the Eternal Hari, taking up the water of that sacred river Ganga and leaves of Bilwa, invited therewith the god Rudra, lord of all lords.'

statements.claim: Shiva appeared with Uma at his side and his followers, manifest on the surface of the Ganga's water and on the bel leaves
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the God Mahadeva, accompanied by Uma and attended by their followers, revealed himself there on the Ganga's water and the Bel leaves.'

statements.claim: Krishna worshipped him with flowers of the Parijata and eulogized the lord of lords
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Keshava worshipped him with the flowers of the Parijata tree and that eloquent speaker then began to eulogise that lord of lords.'

statements.claim: The hymn: Rudra who binds beings in maya and manifests through the sound pervading the universe; Pasupati, lord of all creatures; performer of all acts; God of gods; Bhava, self-created creator of all creators; Maheswara, crowned by the defeated gods and asuras; 'I resign myself entirely to your protection. Crown me... with fame'
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 v22-26 matches the epithets and their etymologies closely (Rudra/maya/sound, Pasupati, God of gods, Bhava/self-create, Maheswara/coronated by defeated gods and Asuras, and the closing request for fame).

statements.claim: Shiva declared: 'O best of gods, you shall obtain the things you desire. You shall carry away the Parijata tree. And you shall be invincible'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.221): 'O best of gods, thou shalt obtain the things desired by thee; thou shalt carry away the Parijata tree... thou shalt be invincible.'

statements.claim: Shiva and Uma faded back into the night, leaving Krishna certain the tree would go home with him
statements.evidence: Shiva's departure is the source's close (he 'disappeared on the spot' in the continuation); Krishna's certainty is narration.

DKS_0230.notes: Clean. Hymn is a faithful condensation of HV 1.221 v22-34; boon wording matches the excerpt verbatim. The 'wish-giving tree' and garden recap are connective.

statements.claim: Recap: on the night mountain Krishna summoned the Ganga at his thought, bathed in her waters, offered bilva leaves and sacred water, eulogized Shiva, and won the boon that he would carry away the Parijata and remain invincible
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 v17-38 (see DKS_0230 evidence); recap matches the same chapter.

statements.claim: Shiva told Krishna that on the summit of this mountain there is a stronghold of the Danavas called Satpura, and hidden inside it live mighty Danavas of wicked soul
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.221): 'on the summit of this mountain... there is a stronghold of the Danavas called Satpura. Hidden inside that fastness live mighty Danavas of wicked soul.' Full source adds: 'within the caves underneath the ground.'

statements.claim: The Danavas were invincible to the gods by a boon of Brahma — no weapon of the celestials could touch them, and no god could prevail
statements.evidence: Pack canonical summary: 'invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon'; HV 1.221 continuation: 'through the virtue of a boon bestowed on them by Brahma, they are... incapable of being slain by the celestials.'

statements.claim: Shiva charged Krishna: 'Do you, O Krishna, slay them' — a task no god could carry out, given to Krishna alone
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.221): 'do thou, O Keshava, slay them'; source adds 'disguised as you are now in a human semblance'.

statements.claim: The mountain was a gate: the stronghold lay hidden under the very ground where Krishna stood
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 continuation: 'within the caves underneath the ground there is a stronghold of the Danavas'; Krishna later says 'underneath you live mighty Asuras' (v48). 'Gate' is connective metaphor.

statements.claim: The day's war for a tree had been one the gods could fight; this hidden war was one they could not
statements.evidence: Connective framing of the revelation, consistent with the boon making them invincible to the celestials.

statements.claim: Before dawn, on the summit where the stronghold's gate was hidden, a shrine was raised and Krishna was enshrined within it
statements.evidence: The enshrinement itself is supported (pack summary: 'Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain'; HV 1.221: Krishna declares 'I shall also be enshrined on you... holding in check the dreadful Asuras' and 'thenceforward that infallible God is enshrined there'). The 'before dawn' timing is a light gloss — the source has Krishna address the mountain 'on the dawn of day'.

statements.claim: The mountain kept Krishna's presence as a place of worship, a watch kept over the fastness in its heart
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 continuation: 'I shall live on your heights holding in check the dreadful Asuras'; those who climb the top and behold his image gain merit; thenceforward he is enshrined and worshipped there.

statements.claim: When morning came the fight with Indra would resume on the slopes below, with the Parijata still the prize
statements.evidence: Bridge to the next episode; the resumption of the Indra battle opens HV 1.222.

DKS_0231.notes: Satpura details verified against the full source (Vishnu Parva ch. 75): stronghold on the summit within caves underneath the ground — the story's 'beneath the summit / under the ground' wording is accurate. Enshrinement supported by the pack summary and source.

statements.claim: The quarrel over the Parijata was ended by the elders of the gods, the sage Kashyapa and his wife Aditi, parents to both brothers
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: Brahma sent Kashyapa with Aditi to prevent the two sons; they halted the battle and reconciled the brothers.

statements.claim: Aditi told Krishna: take this Parijata, go to Dwaraka and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife; when the ceremony is over, bring the tree back and place it as before in the garden of Nandana
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'O Upendra! take this Parijata, go to Dwarka and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife. But... when that ceremony will be over, you are to bring back this tree and place it as before in the garden of Nandana.'

statements.claim: Krishna accepted the tree together with its condition
statements.evidence: The pack passage truncates at 'Hearing this Krishna said to the illustrious...'; acceptance is the natural continuation and matches the story outcome (tree carried to Dwaraka).

statements.claim: Satyaki and Pradyumna, guards of the Parijata through all the fighting, kept their watch as it traveled, and Garuda bore the tree
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: Satyaki and Pradyumna went on Garuda 'in order to protect the Parijata tree'; HV 1.220-222 show Garuda carrying it throughout.

statements.claim: On the way home Krishna set the tree down at Raivataka before carrying it the last stretch into Dwaraka itself
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'Krishna plants it at Raivataka and carries it into Dwarka.' (The quoted HV 1.222 passage is truncated before this leg of the journey; Raivataka is where Daruka waits with Krishna's chariot.)

statements.claim: Arriving over Dwaraka, Krishna blew his conch and the sound delighted every inhabitant
statements.evidence: VP 5.31 (Wilson): 'When Krishna arrived over Dwaraka, he blew his shell, and delighted all the inhabitants with the sound.'

statements.claim: Krishna alighted from Garuda and, with Satyabhama at his side, walked to her garden and planted the great Parijata there
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'alighting from Garuda, he proceeded with Satyabhama to her garden, and there planted the great Parijata tree.'

statements.claim: The tree's fragrance perfumed the earth for three furlongs in every direction
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'the smell of which perfumed the earth for three furlongs.'

statements.claim: Anyone who approached the tree could recall the events of a prior existence, and the Yadavas, beholding their faces in the tree, contemplated themselves in their original celestial forms
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'an approach to which enabled every one to recollect the events of a prior existence; so that, on beholding their faces in that tree, all the Yadavas contemplated themselves in their (original) celestial forms.'

statements.claim: Satyabhama received the tree joyfully — this was the auspicious festival she had longed for, the rite she had spoken of
statements.evidence: Aditi names it 'the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife' (HV 1.222); HV excerpt: Krishna entered Satyabhama's palace with the tree. The 'rite she had spoken of' refers to the established chain premise.

statements.claim: The tree was a loan, not a gift: when the rite was done it was to return to the garden of Nandana
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'you are to bring back this tree and place it as before in the garden of Nandana.'

DKS_0232.notes: Blends the two cited variants as the pack's variant_notes describe: HV's conditional grant by Aditi (frame) with VP's planting in Satyabhama's garden (three-furlong scent, prior-existence memory). Nothing asserted contradicts either source. Source chronology note: HV places this homecoming after the reconciliation narrated in DKS_0233, so the corpus order 0232->0233 reads the resolution twice; each story individually matches its pack.

statements.claim: On the Parijatra mountain, in the first light, the battle over the tree began again, Krishna and Indra fighting from their cars while neither struck the other directly
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'there took place an encounter between those two celestials mounted on their cars on account of the Parijata... Indra did not strike Upendra in battle nor the latter the former.'

statements.claim: Krishna's arrows scattered Indra's soldiers, with ten sharpened shafts striking each of the horses of the king of gods
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'With straight-coursing arrows Vishnu... struck the soldiers of the king of gods... with ten sharpened arrows Janarddana struck each of the horses of the king of gods.'

statements.claim: Indra's arrows covered the horses of Krishna's car and buried Garuda's wings in shafts, while a thousand arrows cloaked the great elephant
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'Vasava... covered Shaiyya and other horses... With a thousand of arrows Krishna covered the elephant (of Indra) and the highly powerful slayer of Bali covered Garuda too.'

statements.claim: As the heroes fought, the earth shook like a boat adrift in water, the quarters blazed with lustre, mountains trembled, hundreds of trees were uprooted and pious mortals fell
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'the earth shook like a boat sunk in water and the quarters were fully enshrouded with lustre. Mountains shook, hundreds of trees were uprooted and pious mortals fell down on earth.'

statements.claim: Hurricanes blew, rivers ran backward, fire burned even in water, planets fought in the sky, hundreds of stars fell, and the elephants of the quarters quivered while cranes cried dreadfully overhead
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'hundreds of hurricane blew... the course of the rivers was changed in an opposite direction... fire was lighted even in the water and planets fought with planets in the sky. And hundreds of stars fell down on earth... Elephants of the quarters... began to quiver. The welkin was covered with cranes emitting loud cries.'

statements.claim: It seemed that earth, heaven, and sky had vanished from view
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'beholding those two heroic gods engaged in fighting with each other the earth, heaven and sky as if disappeared from view.'

statements.claim: The ascetics recited mantras and the brahmanas gave themselves to meditation, praying for the sake of all creatures
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'for the behoof of the world the ascetics began to recite Mantras and the Brahmanas speedily engaged in carrying on meditations.'

statements.claim: Brahma told Kashyapa: go with your wife Aditi and prevent your two sons
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'Brahma said to Kashyapa:—O you of firms vows, go with your wife Aditi and prevent your two sons.'

statements.claim: Seeing Kashyapa and Aditi in the battlefield, both heroes climbed down from their cars, laid down their arms, and saluted the feet of their parents
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'Beholding Kashyapa with Aditi in the battle-field those two heroic... got down from their cars, and leaving off their arms, saluted the feet of their parents.'

statements.claim: Aditi took both by the hands and said: born of the same parents you are trying to slay each other as if you were not brothers; let pass what has happened; if you obey your mother and father, lay down your arms and hear what I say
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'holding them both by the hands Aditi said:—Born of the same parents you are trying to slay each other as if you are not brothers. Let pass what has happened... lay down your arms and hear what I say.'

statements.claim: The two walked together to the bank of the Jahnvi river, where Indra said: O Krishna, you are the Lord and Creator of the universe and I have been placed by you in my kingdom; having accepted me as your elder brother, why do you wish to destroy me?
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'conversing with each other, went to the bank of the river Janhavi. Sakra said:—O Krishna, thou art the Lord Creator of the universe and I have been placed by thee in my kingdom... having accepted me as thy elder brother why dost thou wish to destroy me?'

statements.claim: The two bathed together in the Jahnvi, and the ascetics named the place the union ground of dear ones, where the brothers were united with their parents
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'having bathed in the water of the river Janhavi they both returned to... Kashyapa... and Aditi. The ascetics designate that place as the union ground of dear ones where those two lotus-eyed brothers were united with their parents.'

statements.claim: Krishna promised safety to Indra before the assembled celestials; the gods repaired to heaven, with Kashyapa, Aditi, Indra and Krishna riding together on one car, and Sachi adored the sage and his wife
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'after Krishna had promised safety unto Indra in the very presence of the pious celestials... seated on one car Kashyapa, Aditi, Indra and Upendra set out for the celestial region... Sachi... adored the high souled Kashyapa along with his wife.'

statements.claim: When the night had passed, Aditi gave the tree to Krishna to carry to Dwaraka for his wife's festival, on condition that it return to the garden of Nandana when the rite was done
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'after the night had elapsed Aditi... said to Hari... take this Parijata, go to Dwarka and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife... you are to bring back this tree and place it as before in the garden of Nandana.'

statements.claim: The war ended not with a victor but with a mother's gift — the tree given, not taken — and the brothers went home at peace
statements.evidence: Interpretive close on the reconciliation and Aditi's gift.

DKS_0233.notes: Fully grounded in HV 1.222, including the omens, both mothers' speeches, and the Jahnvi reconciliation. Note: in source order this episode precedes the homecoming narrated in DKS_0232, which the corpus runs immediately before it; each story matches its own pack.

statements.claim: Krishna thought of Narada and the sage arrived as soon as he was thought of.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'as soon as he was thought of by Krishna, that foremost of Munis... Nārada... arrived there'.

statements.claim: At the appointed hour Krishna and Satyabhama bathed the great muni Narada, anointed him with scents and garlands and fed him, honouring him for the Punyaka ceremonies.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'when the appointed hour came, the eternal Vāsudeva... along with the beloved Satyā... worshipped the great Muni Nārada... with scents and garlands and fed him'. Pack title itself is 'Satyabhama's Punyaka Rite'.

statements.claim: Satyabhama bound Krishna to the Parijata tree with a garland of flowers and, with his permission, dedicated him to Narada.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'the lucky damsel, having put a garland of flowers around Krishna's neck, bound him to the Pārijāta tree... obtaining his permission she dedicated Keshava unto Nārada'.

statements.claim: Satyabhama gave away sesame seeds gleaming like jewels, gold mixed with rice and other plants, mountains of gold, and a thousand cows.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'she gave away sessamum seeds illumined with the lustre of jems and jewels, gold mixed with rice and other plants, mountains of gold and a thousand kine'.

statements.claim: Narada accepted everything and told Krishna that, given by Satya with water, he had become his, ordering him to follow and obey; Krishna replied 'This is the first stage' and followed.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'given by Satya together with water thou hast become mine. Do thou follow me and do what I say.' ... Janārddana said 'This is the first stage' and began to follow Nārada.

statements.claim: Narada cut jokes, said 'do thou wait here, I shall go', took the garland from Krishna's neck and demanded a Kapila cow with a calf and a black-antelope skin full of sesame seeds and gold as the fee of release, a means laid down by the god whose emblem is the bull (Shiva).
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): verbatim verses 11-13, including 'This means of release has been laid down by the god (Siva) having a bull for his emblem'.

statements.claim: Krishna said 'So be it', offered the fee, then smilingly offered Narada a boon.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'Janārddana said "So be it" and offered him the same fee of release... Pray for a desired-for boon and I will grant it'.

statements.claim: Narada asked that Vishnu always remain pleased with him and grant him habitation with him, and that any rebirth be as a Brahmana born of no woman; Krishna granted it.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): verses 16-18 verbatim; 'the Lord Vishnu said "So it will be"'.

statements.claim: Satyabhama had invited all sixteen thousand wives of Krishna to the Punyaka ceremony and, at its close, distributed among them the celestial garments and ornaments Shachi had previously given to Vasudeva.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'Satyabhāmā... had invited... the sixteen thousand wives of the highly powerful Vishnu. And at the termination of the ceremony she distributed amongst them all those celestial raiments and ornaments which Sachi had previously given to Vāsudeva'.

statements.claim: The Parijata, at Krishna's command, displayed its own accomplishments while friends and relations invited by Narada and Keshava witnessed its power.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'Living there, Pārijāta, at the command of Vāsudeva, began to display its own accomplishments... all their friends and relations began to witness the power of Pārijāta'.

statements.claim: Krishna brought the Pandavas with Pritha, Draupadi and Subhadra; Shrutasrava came with her son and Bhishmaka with his, along with other friends and relations.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'the highly powerful Hari had brought there the Pandavas along with Prithā, Draupadi, and Subhadrā... Shrutasravā, with her son, Bhishmaka with his son and other friends and relations were also brought there'.

statements.claim: For a year Krishna stayed happily in Dwaraka with Arjuna and the ladies of his household; at the end of that year he returned the Parijata to the city of the celestials.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'after a year had elapsed the highly powerful Keshava... returned with Pārijāta to the city of the celestials and saluted Sakra, Aditi, and Kashyapa'.

DKS_0234.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims. The pack passage supports every named event, quote, and number. The opening line's framing ('all within the same afternoon', garland as binding/ransom) is atmosphere over a rite the passage narrates continuously; the pack title itself frames it as 'Satyabhama's Punyaka Rite'.

statements.claim: Recap: the battle over the Parijata had ended only when Kashyapa and Aditi, sent by Brahma, halted it and the two 'brothers' bathed in the Jahnvi and made peace.
statements.evidence: Prior-story summary carried in the DKS_0234 pack chain: 'Kashyapa and Aditi Reconcile Krishna and Indra || Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two "brothers" lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled'. Aditi's words in this pack ('may you both always entertain such a brotherly feeling') confirm the fraternal frame.

statements.claim: After a year of festival Krishna carried the Parijata from Dwaraka up to heaven and saluted Indra (Sakra), Aditi and Kashyapa.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'after a year had elapsed... Keshava... returned with Pārijāta to the city of the celestials and saluted Sakra, Aditi, and Kashyapa'.

statements.claim: Aditi, after Krishna bowed to her, asked that the two always keep brotherly feeling and that Krishna satisfy this desire; he said 'It shall be so'.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): verses 28-29 verbatim ('may you both always entertain such a brotherly feeling... It shall be so').

statements.claim: Krishna told Indra he had been commanded by the high-souled Shiva to destroy all the unslayable Danavas living on earth and would kill all those Asuras within ten days.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'I have been commanded by the high-souled Siva, to destroy all the unslayable Dānavas living on earth. From to-day within ten days I will kill all those Asuras'.

statements.claim: Krishna said Pravara with the heroic Jayanta must wait in the sky at the time of the battle to slay the Danavas, one of them a god in human form and the other the son of a god.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'Pravara, together with the heroic Jayanta, shall have to wait in the sky for slaying those Dānavas. Of them one is a god in a human form and the other is the son of a god'.

statements.claim: Krishna explained the Danavas, proud of Brahma's boon, were unslayable by the gods, but he would kill them 'for I am now a man'.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'Although those Dānavas, proud of the boon conferred on them by Brahmā, are unslayable by the gods, still we will kill them for I am now a man'. Also the pack's evidence excerpt, verbatim.

statements.claim: Indra, pleased, said 'So it will be', and he and Krishna embraced each other.
statements.evidence: HV 1.223 (Dutt, Gutenberg #61937): 'Then Indra, pleased, said to Krishna "So it will be." And then... they embraced each other'.

statements.claim: Connective reflections — that Krishna's human form was his weapon against a boon that shielded the Danavas from every god, and that the ten days had begun to run unknown to the world below.
statements.evidence: Exegesis of the quoted vow; the pack confirms the boon from Brahma and the ten-day promise but does not itself editorialize.

DKS_0235.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims. The pack passage (HV 1.223) carries the entire scene verbatim; dialogue quotes in the story match. Note: the opening recap of the earlier Parijata battle is verified against the previous-story summary in the DKS_0234 pack chain, not against this pack's own passage.

statements.claim: The inhabitants of Shatpura, Nikumbha and other Daityas, proud of their boon, assembled and demanded: 'Give us our share in the Yajna. We will drink Soma and Brahmadatta must give us his daughters', plus his most valuable jewels, threatening not to allow the yajna if he transgressed.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): verses 6-12 quoted nearly verbatim, incl. 'If he transgresses this order we will not allow him to celebrate this Yajna. This is our order'.

statements.claim: The setting was the city of Shatpura on the sacred bank of the river Avarta, resorted to by munis, where the Vajasaneyi Brahmana Brahmadatta, a disciple of Yajnavalkya, well-read in the four Vedas and six Angas and endued with morality, was initiated into a yajna extending over a year.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): verses 1-3, including 'Brahmadatta, a disciple of Yajnawalka, well-read in the four Vedas and six Angas and endued with morality, was initiated into a Yajna extending over a year'.

statements.claim: Brahmadatta answered that no portion of sacrificial offerings was laid down for them in the Vedas (they could ask the assembled munis), that he would give his daughters to proper bridegrooms following the Vedas, and that if they came to terms he might give his entire collection of jewels but if they used force he would give nothing, 'for Devaki's son is my supporter'.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): verses 13-16 nearly verbatim.

statements.claim: The Danavas chose force: they scattered the articles of the yajna and began carrying away his daughters.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'the wicked Dānavas of Shatpura, Nikumbha and others began to scatter the articles of Yajna and carry away his daughters'.

statements.claim: Vasudeva and Devaki were at Shatpura because Brahmadatta was a class-friend and preceptor of Vasudeva, and Vasudeva had come with Devaki to protect him, as Indra guards Brihaspati, his own preceptor.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'as Sakra... protects Vrihaspati so... Vasudeva, with Devaki, repaired there for protecting him, for he was a class friend and preceptor of Anakadundubhi (Vasudeva)'.

statements.claim: At the yajna were present the munis Vyasa, Yajnavalkya, Sumantu, Jaimini, Dhritiman, Jajali, Devala and others of firm devotion, and Devaki distributed among the beggars whatever each wanted, proportionate to Vasudeva's wealth.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'were present Vyasa, Yajnawalka, Sumantu, Jaimini, Dhritimān, Jajali, Devala and other great and leading Munis of firm devotion... the pious Devaki distributed amongst the beggars various articles they wanted proportionate to the wealth of the intelligent Vasudeva'.

statements.claim: Seeing the sacrificial articles robbed by the Asuras, Vasudeva thought of Krishna, Balabhadra and Gada, and as soon as he was thought of Krishna came to know everything.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'Anakadundubhi thought of the great Krishna, Balabhadra and Gada. As soon as he was thought of Krishna came to know of every thing'.

statements.claim: Krishna ordered Pradyumna to proceed and save the maidens by his illusive powers, saying he himself would soon go to Shatpura with the Yadava army.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'Proceed, O my son, and save the maidens by virtue of your illusive powers... I myself too will soon go to Shatpura with the Yādava army'.

statements.claim: Pradyumna, ever obedient, went within a moment, took away the maidens by illusion, created illusory figures which he left before the Daityas, and told Devaki 'Be not afraid'; the Daityas carried off the illusory maidens and entered their city with satisfaction while Brahmadatta's real daughters were safe.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): verses 17-23 nearly verbatim ('leaving aside Brahmadatta's daughter the irrepressible Daityas carried away the illusory maidens and entered their city with satisfaction').

statements.claim: The great yajna continued according to proper rites, and all the kings invited by Brahmadatta — Jarasandha, Shishupala, Dantavakra, the Pandavas, the sons of Dhritarashtra, the Malava and Tangana kings, Rukmi, Ahvriti, Neela, Narmada, Vinda, Anuvinda, Avantya, Shalya, Shakuni and others — arrived and encamped near Shatpura.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'that great and glorious Yajna was being celebrated according to proper rites... all the kings, invited by the intelligent Brahmadatta, arrived at the sacrificial ground... encamped near Shatpura' (name list verbatim).

statements.claim: The sacrifice now wore a ring of armies around it — 'and the year was not yet half done', with every new arrival making the encampment thicker.
statements.evidence: No pack passage states how far the year-long yajna had progressed when the kings encamped; the pack says only that the yajna was 'extending over a year' and that the kings arrived and encamped. The visible passage (and its excerpt) contains no elapsed-time figure.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

corrections.original_sentence: The sacrifice that had begun as a year of offerings now wore a ring of armies around it — and the year was not yet half done, and every new arrival made the encampment thicker and the air heavier.
corrections.suggested: The sacrifice that had begun as a year of offerings now wore a ring of armies around it, and every new arrival made the encampment thicker and the air heavier.

DKS_0236.notes: 1 UNSUPPORTED (the 'year was not yet half done' timing claim — the pack gives no elapsed-time figure; kings simply 'encamped near Shatpura' while the year-long yajna went on). Everything else is verbatim-supported, including dialogue and the king list. Passages truncated mid-chapter ('[...]' markers) in the pack did not affect these claims.

statements.claim: Narada's quoted thought: 'At this Yajna all the Kshatriyas and the Yadavas have assembled. Surely this will lead to a conflict. I shall therefore try to bring it about.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'Seeing this the beautiful Nārada thought:—"At this Yajna all the Kshatryas and Yādavas have assembled. Surely this will lead to a conflict. I shall therefore try to bring it about." Thinking this he repaired to Nikumbha's house'.

statements.claim: The assembled kings (Jarasandha, Shishupala, Dantavakra, the Pandavas, the sons of Dhritarashtra, the Malava and Tangana kings, Rukmi, Shalya, Shakuni and more) camped around the sacrificial ground where Brahmadatta's year-long rite burned, with the Yadavas on the other side.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): king list and 'encamped near Shatpura' (verses 24-28). The Yadava presence at the ground follows from the same chapter and from ch. 231's 'the Pandavas in charge of the Yajna'.

statements.claim: Framing gloss: in the city the Danavas nursed the grievance of the maidens they had thought to carry off.
statements.evidence: Motive/state-of-mind framing, not a stated source fact. The same chapter says the Daityas carried away the illusory maidens and 'entered their city with satisfaction', so the 'nursed a grievance' gloss is the story's interpretation (they never obtained the real daughters, which is the seed of the dissension Narada refers to).

statements.claim: The Danavas received Narada with worship and seated him; he asked Nikumbha how he could sit at ease after causing a dissension with the Yadavas, since Brahmadatta was the friend of Krishna's father.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): 'He was worshipped there by Nikumbha and other Dānavas... Having caused a dissension with the Yadavas how are you sitting here at ease? Do you not know that Brahmadatta is the friend of Krishna's father?'

statements.claim: Narada told Nikumbha that Brahmadatta's five hundred wives had been brought to the sacrificial ground (200 of Brahmana origin, 100 Kshatriya, 100 Vaishya, 100 Shudra); all had worshipped Durvasa, who booned that each would get a son and a daughter one by one, and by that boon they had all given birth to fair daughters of matchless beauty, tender, ever youthful, chaste, fragrant with the scent of all flowers.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt): verses 33-38 verbatim, including the varna breakdown (200/100/100/100) and Durvasa's boon.

statements.claim: Narada drew the conclusion that jewels would open the ears of the kings and maidens would seal the bargain (the Asuras were to win the assembled kings with jewels and maidens).
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Narada... prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas'. Pack excerpt: Nārada tells Nikumbha 'O hero, you invite in proper order the help of other kings'. (Passage itself truncates at verse ~38.)

statements.claim: Narada urged Nikumbha to invite, in proper order, the help of the other kings.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt) pack evidence excerpt: 'O hero, you invite in proper order the help of other kings'.

statements.claim: Returning through the encampment, Narada prevented the heroic sons of Pandu, holding the Pandavas back so they would not stand with the Yadavas when trouble came.
statements.evidence: HV 1.230 (Dutt) pack evidence excerpt: '...returning... the great Nārada prevented the heroic sons of Pandu'. Consistent with ch. 231 where 'the Pandavas [are] in charge of the Yajna' rather than on the battlefield.

statements.claim: Closing stage-setting: the Danavas had allies among the kings, and everything had been arranged for a battle without Narada raising his voice.
statements.evidence: Summary/connective restatement of the incitement; no new factual assertion.

DKS_0237.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims. One connective-narration question: the gloss that the Danavas 'nursed the grievance of the maidens they had thought to carry off' — interpretive, since the pack has them satisfied with the illusory maidens. All substantive claims (Narada's incitement, the 500 wives' varna breakdown, Durvasa's boon, inviting the kings' help, preventing the Pandavas) are supported by the passage or the pack's own summary/excerpt where the passage is truncated.

statements.claim: At sunrise the Danavas came out of Shatpura roaring, on asses, elephants, crocodiles, hares, horses, buffaloes, lions and tortoises, many chariots drawn by the same beasts, with the sound of trumpets, car wheels and conches.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'Within a moment of the clear sun coming within the range of people's vision... the Dānavas... came out of Shatpura... on asses, elephants, crocodiles, hares, horses, buffaloes, lions and tortoises. Many of their cars were drawn by those animals... the sound of trumpets, rattle of car wheels, and the blowing of conches'.

statements.claim: Krishna, Baladeva and Satyaki rode to the field on Garuda's back, bathed in the waters of the sacred river Avarta, and worshipped Shiva before the battle.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'Baladeva, Krishna and Satyaki delightedly got upon Garuda's back. Having bathed in the water of the sacred river Avarta... worshipped the god Siva'.

statements.claim: Pradyumna stood at the head of the army, the Pandavas were in charge of the yajna (guarding the sacrifice ground), and remaining soldiers were at the door of the cave; Jayanta and Pravara were summoned by Krishna's thought, arrived instantly, were visible only to Krishna, and were kept above.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'having placed Pradyumna above in front of the army, the Pandavas in charge of the Yajna and the remaining soldiers at the door of the cave... thought of Jayanta and Pravara... they arrived there as soon as they were recollected. The Lord only could see them and they were kept above along with Pradyumna'.

statements.claim: At Krishna's mandate war-bugles and other instruments were sounded; Samba and Gada arranged the soldiers in the shape of a makara (crocodile-like sea monster), and Sharana, Uddhava, Viprithu, Prithu, Sudangshthra, Vichakshu and others helped Aniruddha protect the rear.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'at Krishna's mandate, war-bugles... were sounded... Sāmva and Gada arranged the soldiers in the shape of a Makara. Shārana, Uddhava... Viprithu, Prithu... Sudangsthra, Vichakshu... began to help Aniruddha and protect the rear of the army'. ('Makara' glossed as 'great crocodile' is a standard rendering.)

statements.claim: The kings siding with the Asuras included the followers of the Chedi king Shishupala, the hundred brothers headed by Duryodhana, and Bhagadatta, Shalya, Shakuni and Jarasandha.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'the soldiers of the Chedi and other kings were bent upon assisting the Asuras... amongst the followers of the Chedi king Shishupāla, the hundred brothers headed by Duryodhana stood there... the king Bhagadatta, Shalya, Shakuni, Jarāsandha... got themselves ready for the encounter'.

statements.claim: Nikumbha came out at the head of the Asura army as the lord of gods issues out at the head of the celestial host.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'as the lord of gods issues out at the head of the celestial host so Nikumbha came out at the head of that Asura army'.

statements.claim: Nikumbha assailed the Yadava army with arrows like serpents; Anadhrishti, commander-in-chief of the Yadu army, could not bear it and answered shaft for shaft until everything was covered with arrows and Nikumbha, his chariot, standard and horses became invisible; seeing this, the foremost of the illusory-possessed was filled with anger.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'Nikumbha began to assail the dreadful army of the Bhaimas with arrows like serpents, Anādhristhi, the commander-in-chief of the Yadu army, could not bear it... when everything was covered with arrows, Nikumbha, his chariot, standard and horses became invisible. Seeing it the heroic Nikumbha... was filled with anger'.

statements.claim: By his illusive powers Nikumbha bewildered Anadhrishti, carried him to the cave named Shatpura and imprisoned him, then returned and took Kritavarma, Charudeshna, Vaitarana of Bhoja's race, Sanatkumar, Arksha (Jambavati's son), Nishatha, Ulmukha and numerous other Yadavas one by one into the dreadful cave, so covering himself that no one could see him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): verses 27-29 nearly verbatim; 'when he led the Yadavas to the dreadful cave of Shatpura he so covered himself by his illusive powers that no body could see him'.

statements.claim: Krishna, Baladeva, Satyaki, Samba, the irrepressible Aniruddha, Pradyumna especially, and many other Yadavas were filled with anger at the onslaught.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'the Lord Krishna, Baladeva, Sātyaki, Sāmva, the slayer of inimical heroes, the irrepressible Aniruddha and numerous other Bhaimas, especially Pradyumna, were greatly filled with anger'.

statements.claim: Krishna set string to his Sarnga bow and began to move among the Danavas as the god of fire ranges on grass.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'setting string to his Srānga bow and shooting arrows the holder of the Srānga (Krishna) began to move about amongst the Dānavas as the god of fire ranges on grass'.

DKS_0238.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims and no connective questions. All characters, mounts, formations, ally lists, the imprisonment sequence and the Sarnga image map verbatim to HV 1.231. 'Great crocodile' for makara and the 'war fought by subtraction' passages are imagery, not sourceable facts.

statements.claim: Anadhrishti and the other captains had been swallowed into the cave of Shatpura one by one through Nikumbha's illusion, so the Yadava army's heart was inside the mountain.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'bewildering Anadhristhi and bringing him to the cave named Shatpura the heroic Nikumbha imprisoned him there... took there Kritavarmā... Nishatha, Ulmuku and numerous other Yādavas' (verses 27-29, present in this pack's passage).

statements.claim: With the Sarnga strung, Krishna moved among the Danavas as fire ranges over dry grass, his arrows flying before him in sheets.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'setting string to his Srānga bow and shooting arrows the holder of the Srānga (Krishna) began to move about amongst the Dānavas as the god of fire ranges on grass'.

statements.claim: The Danavas took up thousands of sataghnis, parighas, fiery lances and burning axes, tore up dreadful rocks and great stones, hurled infuriated elephants, chariots and horses, and ran at Krishna like locusts driven by the noose of Death into a burning fire.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'taking up thousands of Sataghnis, Parighas, fiery lances, burning axes, dreadful rocks, and huge stones and throwing up infuriated elephants, cars and horses the Danavas ran towards the effulgent god as the locusts, drawn by the noose of Death, run towards the burning fire'.

statements.claim: The Narayana-fire consumed all those weapons, stones, elephants and chariots, and the smiling Krishna baffled them all with the fire of his arrows, standing like a bull suffering an autumn downpour.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt): 'Narayana-fire consumed all those things. And smiling the highly effulgent Yadu chief... baffled them all with the fire of his arrows. And as a bull suffers the downpour of rain in the autumn so he bore the shower [of weapons]'.

statements.claim: As soon as any Asura rose into the sky, Jayanta and Pravara — summoned by Krishna's thought before the battle and visible only to him — met them with arrows and every one fell.
statements.evidence: HV 1.231 (Dutt) pack evidence excerpt: 'as soon as they rose up into the sky Jayanta and Pravara killed them all with arrows'; the pair's summoning and stationing above is in verses 1-6 of the same chapter (in this pack's passage).

statements.claim: The Danava host was routed and burned; the rout Nikumbha's illusion had postponed came in full, and the cave of Shatpura still held its prisoners.
statements.evidence: The rout of the Asuras continues into ch. 232 ('Completely routed by Krishna... the heroes fled away on all sides' — DKS_0240 pack); the imprisoned Yadava heroes in the Shatpura cave are per ch. 231 verses 27-29. 'The cave was not [won]' is connective.

DKS_0239.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims. Similes and mood ('smiling since he strung the bow', 'the sky became a wall') are imagery over supported events. The pack passage truncates at verse ~36 ('[...]') but the sky-slaying claim is carried by the pack's own evidence excerpt.

statements.claim: When the kings and their followers were imprisoned, fear entered the minds of the Asuras; completely routed by Krishna and the Yadavas, the heroes fled on all sides.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): 'when the kings, with their followers, were imprisoned fear entered into the mind of the Asuras. Completely routed by Krishna, Anarta and other Yadavas... the heroes fled away on all sides'.

statements.claim: Nikumbha rebuked the fleeing host: they broke their promise to avenge their slain kinsmen; heroes slain in battle live happily in the region of the celestials, while cowards must face their wives at home — 'Shame on you'.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): Nikumbha's speech (verses 1-6) closely paraphrased; 'Why do ye... break your promise and take to your heels? You promised to avenge the destruction of your kinsmen... If you however fly away whose face will you behold in your house? What will your wives say? Oh fie on you!'

statements.claim: The Asuras, filled with shame, returned with double vigour and engaged the Yadavas again; Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva destroyed all who went to the sacrificial ground.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): 'the Asuras, filled with shame, returned with double vigour and again engaged in an encounter with the Yādavas. Dhananjaya, Bhima, Nakula, Sahadeva and Dharma's son, the king Yudhishthira destroyed all who went to that sacrificial ground'.

statements.claim: Those who rose up into the sky were slain by Indra's son (Jayanta) and the foremost of the twice-born Pravara, still on watch above the field.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): 'Those, who rose up into the sky, were slain by Indra's son and the foremost of the twice-born Pravara'. The story's naming of Indra's son as Jayanta follows the pair's identity established in ch. 223/231.

statements.claim: A river of blood flowed down from the mountain Govinda, its fishes the swords of the fallen.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): 'there flew a river of blood... It took its rise from the mountain Govinda and its water was the blood of the Asuras... The swords were the fishes'.

statements.claim: Nikumbha leaped up and fought on; Jayanta and Pravara met him with thunderbolt-like arrows; he struck Pravara down with his parigha (iron club); Indra's son caught Pravara, embraced him, found him alive, set him down, then wounded Nikumbha's person with numerous shafts.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): verses 13-19 closely followed; 'Nikumbha struck Pravara with his Parigha who fell down on earth. As soon as he fell down Indra's son held him up and embraced him with his arms. Knowing him alive he at once let him off and ran towards the Asura... Indra's son wounded Nikumbha's person with numerous shafts'.

statements.claim: The wounded Nikumbha, thinking of Krishna who had killed his kinsmen, broke off the fight and vanished, going to where Krishna stood.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): 'the great Asura thought:—"I shall fight in the battle-field with my enemy Krishna who has killed my kinsmen..."... Nikumbha disappeared from that place and went where the highly powerful Krishna was'.

statements.claim: Indra, seated on Airavata, came down with the gods to witness the battle; pleased with his victorious son, he embraced him and Pravara (freed from stupefaction) and had celestial trumpets sounded.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt): 'Seated on his Airāvata the virtuous destroyer of Bala, Vāsava, had come there with the gods to witness the battle... he embraced him and Pravara who was freed from stupifaction... celestial trumpets were struck at the command of the king of gods'.

statements.claim: When the last Asura had fallen or fled the war was over, and Krishna gave the victory away: the captive kings were brought before him and instead of punishment received jewels and fine raiment from his hand.
statements.evidence: Pack summary/index: 'After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta'. (Passage truncated at verse 33 before the distribution scene.)

statements.claim: To the Yadavas Krishna gave the hundreds of Daitya maidens of the conquered city; to the Pandavas he gave six thousand chariots with their horses.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt) pack evidence excerpt: 'Keshava... conferred upon the Yadavas hundreds of Daitya maidens... he gave the Pāndavas six thousand cars with horses'.

statements.claim: In conquered Shatpura there lived the brahmana Brahmadatta (the yajna-performer of ch. 230), and Krishna summoned him and granted him the city itself, caves and walls and all.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 (Dutt) pack evidence excerpt: 'gave that city of Shatpura to the Brāhmana Brahmadatta'; ch. 230 (this story's lineage) establishes Brahmadatta the Vajasaneyi Brahmana in Shatpura.

DKS_0240.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims. Story compresses the sequel (Nikumbha's renewed attack on Krishna/Arjuna, verses 24-33 and beyond, dealt with in later stories) into 'the war was over'; the pack's own summary frames the distribution as 'after the victory', so no assertion contradicts the pack. The ch. 232 passage in the pack is truncated ('[...]') before the spoils scene; spoils are supported by the pack summary + evidence excerpt.

statements.claim: After the battles the Yadavas took to the sea, and Balarama, drunk on Kadamvari wine with reddened eyes, fair as the moon in cloud-dark raiment, sported with Revati, daughter of King Revata, delighted by looking at her face.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'Having lost all control over himself... for drinking Kadamvari wine and with his eyes reddened the highly beautiful Bala... began to sport with Revati... clad in raiments black like clouds the divine Rāma, fair like the rays of the moon... attained to an excess of delight by repeatedly looking at the countenance of his beloved consort'. Arjuna 'had come there for the sea-voyage' confirms the maritime setting.

statements.claim: At Krishna's command the beautiful Apsaras came to please Rama and Revati; dressed as the women of the Yadava country, they saluted Revati and Rama, danced in time with gestures expressive of every emotion, and sang, in the Yadava tongue, songs set to thousands of tunes.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'at the command of Keshava... the beautiful Apsaras approached... saluted Revati and Rāma and began to dance in accompaniment with time... Having dressed themselves after the women of the country of the Yādavas those... damsels sang, in their language, songs set to thou sands of tunes'.

statements.claim: The songs recounted Krishna's deeds: the destruction of Kamsa, Pralamba and Chanura; the tying to the mortar that earned the name Damodara; Putana's destruction; the uprooting of the two trees; Kaliya pressed down in the lake; Govardhana upheld for Gokula; the hump-backed woman cured; the dwarfish form assumed; the wolves created; Saubha slain; Subhadra carried away; the battle with Valahaka and Jamvumali; and the jewels carried off in Indra's very presence.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): verses 7-14 enumerate all of these nearly item for item ('destruction of Kansa, Pralamva, and Chanura... tied to the mortar... obtained the name of Damodara... destruction of Putana... uprooting of the trees Yamala and Arjuna... creation of wolves... suppression of the wicked king of serpents Kalya by Krishna in the lake... upholding of the mount Govardhana for the benefit of Gokula... cured the hump-backed woman... assumed the most wretched dwarfish form... how Soubha was slain... the carrying away of Subhdrā; the battle with Vālāhaka and Jamvumāli; and how he carried away all the jewels in the very presence of Sakra after defeating him').

statements.claim: Balarama, drunk with Kadamvari wine, sang with his wife Revati with sweet clapping of hands; Krishna, to please his brother, sang with Satyabhama.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'the highly beautiful Balarāma, drunk with Kadamvari wine, began to sing with his wife Revati accompanied with sweet clapping of hands... Madhusudana, in order to please him, began to sing with Satya'.

statements.claim: Arjuna, who had come for the sea-voyage, joined his sister Subhadra and Krishna in singing; Gada, Sarana, Pradyumna, Samba, Satyaki, Charudeshna, Rama's sons Nishatha and Ulmukha, the commander Akrura, Sankha and other leading Yadavas sang in a chorus.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'Pārtha, who had come there for the sea-voyage, also delightedly joined the beautiful Subhadrā and Krishna in their singing... Gada, Sārana, Pradyumna, Shāmva, Satyaki... Chārudeshna also sang there in a chorus. Rāma's sons... Nishatha and Ulmukha, the commander, Akrura, Sankha and other leading Bhaimas also sang there'.

statements.claim: By Krishna's power the boats increased in size, and when the Yadu chiefs sang the whole world was filled with joy and sins were dissipated.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'by Krishna's power the boats increased in size and Janarddana sang to his best along with the leading Bhaimas... the whole world was filled with joy and sins were dissipated'.

statements.claim: Narada, the guest of the celestials, sang for Krishna with such intensity that a portion of his matted hair melted away; composing the songs on the spot, he sang them again and again with various gestures and motions.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'Narada, the guest of the celestials, began to sing in such a way amongst the Yadavas that a portion of his matted hairs melted away... composing the songs there and then, that Muni... sang them amongst the Bhaimas again and again with various gestures and motions'.

statements.claim: Narada smiled on Baladeva, Revata's daughter, Krishna, Pritha's son Arjuna, Satyabhama and Subhadra; though Krishna's wives were patient by nature, the joking sage made them laugh; he sang tunes high and low, laughed aloud and shed tears of joy.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'beholding Baladeva, the daughter of the king Revata, Keshava, Pritha's son, Satyabhānā and Subhadrā, the intelligent Rishi smiled repeatedly. Although the wives of Keshava were patient by nature still the intelligent Nārada, ever fond of joking... made them laugh... sang various tunes high and low... began to laugh aloud and shed tears of joy'.

statements.claim: Krishna danced: to the music of his own flute he performed the Hallishaka before them all, and the Apsaras answered him, the beautiful Rambha rising to dance before Rama and Keshava, with Urvashi.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt) pack evidence excerpt: 'Narada began to play on his Vinā... Krishna began to perform Hallishaka accompanied with the music of his flute... the beautiful Rambhā... rose up, played and pleased Rāma and Keshava'. Urvashi is named alongside Rambha as a performer in the pack's own index entry/summary.

statements.claim: The celestial song called the Chhalikya, previously heard only in heaven, was brought down that day and sung for mankind.
statements.evidence: Pack title and summary: 'Krishna Brings the Celestial Chhalikya Song to the Yadavas... the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind'. ('Heard only in heaven' is the natural gloss on 'celestial'.) Passage truncated ('[...]') before this scene.

statements.claim: When the music ended, the damsels at Krishna's command gave away the best jewels of the world, beautiful raiments and garlands, until every guest was laden with gifts.
statements.evidence: HV 1.236 (Dutt): 'the youthful damsels, conversant with gestures, gave away, at Krishna's command, the best jewels of the world, beautiful raiments, garlands made in hea[ven]...' (passage truncates mid-verse; the giving is verbatim in the visible text).

DKS_0241.notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims and no connective questions. Every detail — Balarama and Revati, the Apsaras' dress and dance, the catalogue of Krishna's deeds in song, the singers, the swelling boats, Narada's melting locks and laughter, the Hallishaka and Rambha/Urvashi, the Chhalikya, the gift-giving — maps verbatim to HV 1.236 or the pack's summary/excerpt where the passage is truncated. One map note: 'in the Yadava tongue' glosses the pack's 'in their language'; harmless.

statements.claim: The garden attached to Bhanu's women's quarters was unapproachable and stood unguarded while the Yadava heroes were busy with their sports, the moment Nikumbha chose to strike.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237: 'Although the garden, attached to the female appartment of Bhanu, was unapproachable, still at that time there were no guards for the Yadavas were busy with their sports.'

statements.claim: Years before, Pradyumna had carried off Prabhavati, daughter of Nikumbha's brother Vajranabha, and the demon had never forgiven the insult.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237: 'the daughter of his brother Vajranabha, by name Prabhavati, had been taken away by Pradyumna... Remembering this former enmity.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha slipped into the garden and seized Bhanumati, the beautiful daughter of Bhanu.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237: 'stole away the beautiful daughter of Bhanu by name Bhanumati.'

statements.claim: On hearing the lamentation Vasudeva and Ahuka rushed out in fury, found no offender, and went to Krishna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (7-8): 'the heroes, Vasudeva and Ahuka issued out, filled with wrath. And not seeing the offender before them... went where the highly powerful Krishna was.'

statements.claim: Krishna mounted Garuda with Arjuna beside him and ordered Pradyumna, whose banner bore the makara, to follow in his chariot.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (9-10): 'rode, together with Partha, Garuda... Having commanded the hero having the emblem of a Makara on his flag to follow him on his car.'

statements.claim: They overtook Nikumbha before he could reach the city of Vajra and the safety of his kinsmen.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (11): 'before Nikumbha... could reach the city of Vajra, Partha and Krishna... overtook him in the way.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha fought smiling, a heavy club in his right hand and the weeping Bhanumati in his left, so none could strike him in earnest.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (13-15): 'Nikumbha... smilingly fought with them all with heavy clubs. Holding the maiden Bhanumati by his left hand... hurled the club with his right hand.'

statements.claim: Krishna, Pradyumna and Arjuna, though capable of slaying the demon, could not bear to wound the maiden.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (16): 'although capable of slaying that irrepressible enemy they began to sigh piteously out of their excessive compassion for the maiden.'

statements.claim: Arjuna solved the riddle like a man striking a serpent coiled around a camel, wounding the demon with his thin arrows without ever touching the girl.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (17-18): 'As when a serpent gets round a camel, a man... strikes the serpent leaving the camel to itself, so Partha, the foremost of archers, began to strike the Daitya with his arrows... wounded the Danavas with their cane-like arrows.'

statements.claim: By his illusory powers Nikumbha vanished with the maiden so completely that none could tell where they had gone, assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture as he fled.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (19-20): 'resorting to his illusory powers Nikumbha so disappeared with the maiden... he, however, went on assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture.'

statements.claim: The chase carried them across all seven continents of the earth until Nikumbha dropped onto the summit of Mount Gokarna, on the bank of the river Chela Ganga, which no god, Asura or ascetic could cross, being guarded by the energy of Mahadeva.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (22-24): 'travelled all over the earth consisting of seven insular continents and dropped down... on the bank of the river Chela Ganga flowing on the summit of the mount Gokarna. None amongst the gods, Asuras or great ascetics could cross that mountain protected by the energy of Mahadeva.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, a master of illusion himself, snatched Bhanumati away while Krishna and Arjuna assailed the demon, who fled from the northern range of Gokarna to the southern.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (25-26): 'Finding this weak point of Nikumbha, the Bhaima chief Pradyumna... got hold of the maiden Bhanumati. And Krishna, and Arjuna began to assail the Asura greatly with arrows. Then leaving the northern range of the mount Gokarna, Nikumbha fled to the southern range.'

statements.claim: With Krishna's permission Pradyumna carried the maiden home to Dwaraka and returned to find Krishna and Arjuna at the mouth of the cave that was the entrance to Shatpura, Nikumbha's city.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (26-29): 'the great Asura entered into Shatpura, the abode of his kinsmen... With Krishna's permission the heroic son of Rukshmini... took... the maiden to the city of Dwaraka. And keeping her there he returned to Shatpura... and beheld the two Krishnas... at the mouth of the cave.'

statements.claim: All night the three kept watch at the cave's mouth; at dawn the demon came out to fight.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (27-30) says 'those two heroes spent the night at the mouth of the cave' (Krishna and Arjuna) while Pradyumna was taking the maiden to Dwaraka, then all three 'waited there with Pradyumna' at the entrance. Minor timeline compression, no contradiction of events.

statements.claim: At dawn Nikumbha broke through Arjuna's Gandiva arrows, struck him on the head with his thorn-covered club; the hero vomited blood and lost consciousness, and the master of illusions carried him off.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (31-33): 'Dhananjaya, with arrows shot off his Gandiva bow, obstructed the thorough-fair. In spite of it Nikumbha... took up his club covered with thorns and struck Partha on his head. Thus assailed... Pritha's son vomitted blood and lost his consciousness.' Arjuna's abduction confirmed by pack summary: Krishna 'frees the abducted Arjuna.'

statements.claim: Thousands of Nikumbhas filled earth and sky, but Krishna perceived the true form of the creator of illusions and cut off his head with the discus, whereupon every false form dissolved and Arjuna was free.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, HV 1.237: 'they saw all over the earth and welkin thousands of Nikumbha... the Divine Lord Krishna... saw the true form of Nikumbha, the creator of illusions... with his discus, cut off his head'; index title: 'Krishna Destroys a Body of Nikumbha with the Discus... frees the abducted Arjuna.'

statements.claim: Krishna gathered Arjuna onto Garuda and turned toward Dwaraka, leaving Shatpura's master destroyed.
statements.evidence: Closing connective narration consistent with the pack outcome (Nikumbha's head cut off, Arjuna freed); the specific departure scene is not in the visible passage.

DKS_0242.notes: Fully grounded in HV 1.237. Minor compression: the night watch at the cave mouth is attributed to all three though the source places it on Krishna and Arjuna with Pradyumna rejoining; treated as connective. Atmosphere (smiles, weeping, dawn) is narrative texture.

statements.claim: Vajranabha practised hard austerities on the summit of Mount Sumeru, and pleased Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, asked him to pray for a boon.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (5-6): 'a great Asura, celebrated by the name of Vajranabha, practised hard austerities on the summit of the mount Sumeru. Pleased with his penances the Divine Brahma, the grand-father of the world, asked him to pray for a boon.'

statements.claim: Vajranabha asked two gifts: that even the gods might never kill him, and that he might possess the city Vajra, where even the air could not enter without his will, a city that gave its lord whatever he desired unasked, ringed by gardens and walls, surrounded by branch cities, full of peerless gems.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (7-9): 'prayed for two boons that even the gods might not kill him, and that he might get the city Vajra where even the air cannot easily enter, which gives every sort of desired-for objects even when they are not thought of, which has gardens encircled by walls, many branch cities, and peerless jems of every description'; the 'without his will' condition appears at 1.238 (23): 'even the wind cannot enter into his city if Vajranabha does not wish it.'

statements.claim: Brahma granted both, Vajranabha lived in Vajra, and millions of demons dwelt there in his garden and the branch cities, healthy, well-fed and contented.
