statements.evidence: BP 10.59.4-5: 'śaṅkha-nādena yantrāṇi hṛdayāni manasvinām' and 'pāñcajanya-dhvaniṃ śrutvā yugāntaśani-bhīṣaṇam' (by the conch-sound the machines and the hearts of the proud; the Panchajanya sound terrible as the end-of-age thunderbolt).

statements.claim: By the time Krishna and Satyabhama reached the inner walls, nothing stood between them and the citadel but one defender rising from the girdling waters.
statements.evidence: Bridge to the Mura episode; BP 10.59.5 has Mura hearing the conch, and BP 10.59.7 has him rising from the waters with five heads.

DKS_0260.notes: Defense-by-defense breach maps exactly to BP 10.59.1-5 (mace/mountains, arrows/weapon-forts, discus/fire-water, sword/nooses, conch/engines+hearts). No issues.

statements.claim: Mura, the last guardian, heard the conch and rose from the depths of the waters girdling the citadel.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.5: 'pāñcajanya-dhvaniṃ śrutvā' (having heard the sound of Panchajanya); BP 10.59.7-10 has Mura rising from the waters (papātāmbhasi) - pack rendering: 'Mura, roused by Krishna's conch, rose from the waters.'

statements.claim: Mura had five heads, all of which roared at once, blazing like the fire of the end of the ages and harsh as the sun of the world's last day.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.6-7: 'yugānta-sūryānala-rocir ulbaṇaḥ' (blazing with the fire of the end-of-age sun) and 'vyanadat sa pañcabhiḥ' (he roared with five mouths).

statements.claim: He hurled his trident, so fierce no eye could rest on it, and Krishna broke it in mid-air with two arrows, the three-pronged weapon splitting apart.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.6-8: the trident 'su-durnirīkṣaṇaḥ' (very hard to look at); 'hariḥ śarābhyām abhinat tri-dhojasā' - Krishna split the trident with two arrows (pack rendering: 'Krishna shattered it with two arrows').

statements.claim: Mura's mace came next and Krishna shattered it into a thousand splinters.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.9: 'gadāṃ mṛdhe gadāgrajo nirbibhide sahasradhā' (he shattered the mace into a thousand pieces).

statements.claim: Krishna's discus cut off Mura's five heads, and he fell lifeless into the waters like a mountain whose peaks have been struck off by Indra's thunderbolt.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.10: 'vyasuḥ papātāmbhasi kṛtta-śīrṣo nikṛtta-śṛṅgo 'drir ivendra-tejasā' (lifeless he fell into the water, head cut off, like a mountain with peaks struck off by Indra's power).

statements.claim: Mura had seven sons - Tamra, Antariksha, Sravana, Vibhavasu, Vasu, Nabhasvan and Aruna - who came out armed to avenge their father and flung themselves at Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.11-12: the seven names appear verbatim (tāmro 'ntarikṣaḥ śravaṇo vibhāvasur vasur nabhasvān aruṇaś ca saptamaḥ); pack rendering: 'slew Mura's seven sons who attacked to avenge their father'; verse 12 lists their arrows, swords, maces, śaktis, ṛṣṭis and tridents.

statements.claim: Krishna brought all seven down, cutting through arms and armor, until all seven lay with Mura before the citadel.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.13: 'tān pīṭha-mukhyān anayad yama-kṣayaṃ nikṛtta-śīrṣoru-bhujāṅghri-varmaṇaḥ' (he sent them to Yama's abode, heads, thighs, arms and armor cut off).

statements.claim: From the citadel heights Narakasura watched Krishna on Garuda with Satyabhama, blazing like a storm cloud crowned with lightning above the sun, and hurled the sataghni (hundred-killer) while all his warriors loosed their shafts.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.14: 'dṛṣṭvā sa-bhāryaṃ garuḍopari sthitaṃ sūryopariṣṭāt sa-taḍid ghanaṃ yathā... vyasṛjac chata-ghnīṃ' (seeing him with his wife atop Garuda, above the sun, like a cloud with lightning, he released the sataghni); 'yodhāś ca sarve yugapac ca vivyadhuḥ' (all his warriors struck simultaneously).

statements.claim: When the air cleared the rider was still there, unharmed.
statements.evidence: Not stated in the quoted verses, but consistent with Naraka's defeat in the immediately following episode (BP 10.59, next corpus story 'Krishna Slays Narakasura').

DKS_0261.notes: Sequence and details (trident broken by two arrows, mace shattered, discus beheading, seven sons' names, sataghni) match BP 10.59.5-14 exactly. No issues.

statements.claim: In the aftermath, Narakasura, the son of the earth who had harried the gods and hoarded the treasures of heaven, lay dead in his fortress city of Pragjyotisha.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.22 opens with the earth goddess approaching Krishna after the slaying; Naraka's death, thefts and hoard are the established cluster facts (previous corpus story: 'Krishna Slays Narakasura').

statements.claim: Bhumi, the goddess of the earth, came before Krishna, the slayer of her son.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.22-23: 'tataś ca bhūḥ kṛṣṇam upetya' (then Earth approached Krishna); Bhumi is Naraka's mother (Bhauma = son of the earth).

statements.claim: In her hands she carried Aditi's earrings blazing with refined gold and precious stones, Varuna's great umbrella, and the great jewel, and gave them back.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.22: 'kuṇḍale pratapta-jāmbūnada-ratna-bhāsvare... prācetasaṃ chatram atho mahā-maṇim' (the earrings blazing with refined gold and jewels, the umbrella of Varuna [son of Pracetas] and the great jewel).

statements.claim: She praised Krishna: homage to the lotus-navelled one, wearer of the garland of lotuses; to Vasudeva, Vishnu, the unborn creator of endless power; who bears the great darkness for its destruction and is not touched by it; who upholds goodness; who is time, primal matter and the supreme person.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.24-28: 'namaḥ paṅkaja-nābhāya namaḥ paṅkaja-māline... vāsudevāya viṣṇave... ajāya janayitre 'sya brahmaṇe 'nanta-śaktaye... tamo nirodhāya bibharṣy asaṃvṛtaḥ... kālaḥ pradhānaṃ puruṣo bhavān paraḥ.'

statements.claim: She counted herself among his works: 'I am the water, the fire, the wind, the sky; the elements, the gods, the mind, the senses.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.29: 'ahaṃ payo jyotir athānilo nabho mātrāṇi devā mana indriyāṇi.'

statements.claim: The purpose of her visit was her frightened son Bhagadatta (son of Naraka), who had come for refuge at Krishna's lotus feet, and Krishna granted him fearlessness.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.30-31: 'tasyātmajo 'yaṃ tava pāda-paṅkajaṃ bhītaḥ prapannārti-haropasāditaḥ' (this son of his, frightened, has approached your lotus feet, O remover of the affliction of the surrendered); pack excerpt: 'begged Krishna to protect her son Bhagadatta; Krishna granted him fearlessness.' Bhagadatta as Naraka's son matches BP 3.3.5, where the kingdom is given to Naraka's son after the slaying.

statements.claim: The treasures of heaven were free of the demon's vault; the earrings of Aditi would travel onward to be returned in the courts of heaven, and a new king sat on Naraka's throne, placed there by mercy.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.37 has Krishna restore the earrings to Aditi in Indra's abode after this scene; BP 3.3.5: after slaying Naraka, Krishna gave the remainder (the kingdom) to Naraka's son (āmantritas tat-tanayāya śeṣaṃ dattvā).

statements.claim: The city watched in silence as its master's body was borne away; Bhumi did not weep for Naraka nor ask vengeance.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere/framing; the pack records Bhumi's prayer for Bhagadatta but no grief or vengeance plea - the framing does not contradict it.

DKS_0263.notes: Bhumi's offering (earrings/umbrella/great jewel), her hymn and the plea for Bhagadatta with the grant of fearlessness all track BP 10.59.22-31. The story's genealogy (Bhagadatta = Naraka's son, Bhumi = his mother) is the standard one and matches BP 3.3.5; the pack excerpt's loose 'her son Bhagadatta' is not followed as the primary reading. No issues.

statements.claim: In Naraka's treasury were diamonds, pearls, corals, sapphires and emeralds, heaps of gold and jewels gathered from gods, gandharvas and serpents, a bed shining like the moon, a lion-shaped throne bright as burning fire, and Varuna's great umbrella, cloud-colored and moon-lustered with a standard of gold.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'diamonds, pearls, corals, sapphires, emeralds... a highly costly bed shining like the moon, a lion-shaped throne effulgent like burning fire, and a huge and beautiful umbrella of the hue of the clouds of the rainy season, of the lustre of the moon and with a golden standard'; jewels formerly with 'the gods, Gandharvas and Pannagas (serpents).'

statements.claim: Krishna took the great umbrella of Varuna for himself, as his share of the hoard.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'Taking himself the Varuni umbrella capable of showering gold, he rode Garuda.'

statements.claim: In the inner chambers Naraka had shut away 16,100 royal princesses, daughters of kings seized from their families; seeing Krishna they were captivated, and in that first glance each mentally chose him: 'May this man be my husband; may the creator ratify my choice.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.32-34: 'rājanya-kanyānāṃ... striyo vīkṣya nara-varyaṃ vimohitāḥ... bhūyāt patir ayaṃ mahyaṃ dhātā tad anumodatām' (pack rendering: 16,100 royal princesses; seeing him they were enchanted; 'may this man be my husband, may the creator ratify my choice').

statements.claim: They came to him thin from fasting and vows, wearing the single braid of a woman whose husband is absent, dressed in silk, with folded hands, standing around him without fear because word of Naraka's death had reached them.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'emaciated on account of the observance of vows and fastings, clad in silken raiments and with one braid of hairs approached Janarddana with folded hands and stood encircling him. They fearlessly surrounded Krishna because they had learnt of the death of the great Asuras.'

statements.claim: They had lived in the seraglio deprived of every enjoyment yet unharmed, like celestial maidens lodged in a city of the gods, and the elder guardians of the palace bowed to Krishna as he passed.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'Although deprived of all sorts of enjoyments, still residing there as if in the city of the celestials, they lived happily like celestial damsels... The elderly Mānavas who were their guards... bowed to Krishna.'

statements.claim: They told him that the sage Narada and the wind-god had long ago promised that Narayana himself would slay Naraka and become their husband.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'What the celestial saint Nārada... and the Wind-god had said to us before... They said that the Universal Lord Nārāyana... slaying Bhumi's son Naraka, would in no time become our husband.'

statements.claim: Krishna consoled them and sent the treasures ahead to Dwaraka - Naraka's twenty thousand war elephants carrying bows and lances, forty thousand she-elephants and eight hundred thousand horses - while sixty-four four-tusked white elephants of the breed of Airavata bore the maidens and their wealth toward Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'twenty thousand grim-visaged elephants carrying bows, Tomaras... forty-thousand she-elephants, and eight lacs of horses'; BP 10.59.35-36: Krishna sent the maidens to Dvaraka with 'airāvata-kulebhāṃś ca catur-dantāṃs tarasvinaḥ' (pack rendering: sixty-four white elephants of Airavata's breed, four-tusked and swift).

statements.claim: In Dwaraka the news stirred the streets: 16,100 royal brides were on the road and the riches of a demon king were arriving.
statements.evidence: Framing of the aftermath; consistent with the maidens and treasures being sent to Dvaraka ahead of Krishna.

DKS_0264.notes: Follows BP 10.59.31-36 with Harivamsha 1.121 corroboration (treasury inventory, maiden's description, Narada/wind-god prophecy, elephant/horse counts). The tradition note correctly acknowledges the Harivamsha's Mount Mani variant while following the BP location. No issues.

statements.claim: Krishna came up to Indra's heaven carrying Aditi's earrings, which the demon Naraka had torn from her; Indra and the gods received him with worship, and Aditi, pleased, took back what was hers.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.37: 'gatvā surendra-bhavanaṃ dattvādityai ca kuṇḍale' (going to Indra's abode, he gave Aditi the earrings); Harivamsha 1.121: 'Giving to the king of gods the pair of ear-rings belonging to Aditi... Aditi was pleased.'

statements.claim: Satyabhama had seen the Parijata tree, the wish-fulfilling tree of the gods, and wanted it for her own garden in Dwaraka; wishing to please his beloved like an ordinary man, the Lord went for the celestial tree.
statements.evidence: BP 3.3.4: 'priyaṃ prabhur grāmya iva priyāyā vidhitsur ārcchad dyutaruṃ' (the Lord, like a common man, desiring to please his beloved, went for the celestial tree); BP 10.59.38: 'codito bhāryayotpāṭya pārījātaṃ garutmati' (urged by his wife, he uprooted the Parijata onto Garuda).

statements.claim: The ruler of the universe uprooted the tree from the middle of heaven, whole, roots and all, and set it on Garuda.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.121: 'Krishna of unlimited powers, forcibly up-rooted it and placed it on Garuda's head'; Harivamsha 1.220: 'uprooted the Pārijāta tree and placed it on the back of Garuda'; BP 10.59.38.

statements.claim: Shachi protested that the tree belonged to her; it was not proper, Govinda, to remove it.
statements.evidence: VP 5.30: 'This Párijáta tree belongs to Śachí... it is not proper, Govinda, for you to remove it.'

statements.claim: Indra, blind with rage, rushed at Krishna with all his host, as though Krishna were a plaything of the women; Krishna turned aside the thunderbolt and defeated host after host of the immortals.
statements.evidence: BP 3.3.4: 'vajry ādravat taṃ sa-gaṇo ruṣāndhaḥ krīḍā-mṛgo nūnam ayaṃ vadhūnām' (the thunderbolt-wielder rushed at him with his host, blind with rage: 'surely this is a plaything of the women'); BP 10.59.37-40 rendering: 'overcame Indra and the gods'; VP 5.31 has Krishna return Indra's cast thunderbolt.

statements.claim: In the end Indra let the Parijata go, and the wish-fulfilling tree of heaven was given to the earth.
statements.evidence: VP 5.31 (Indra consents: 'Let this Párijáta tree be transferred to Dwáraká'); BP 10.59.39 has it planted in Satyabhama's garden.

statements.claim: Over Dwaraka Krishna blew his conch and the whole city rose at the sound; he planted the Parijata in Satyabhama's garden, where it perfumed the earth for three furlongs, let those who approached recall past lives, and showed the Yadavas their original celestial forms.
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'he blew his shell, and delighted all the inhabitants... planted the great Párijáta tree, the smell of which perfumed the earth for three furlongs, and an approach to which enabled every one to recollect the events of a prior existence; so that... all the Yádavas contemplated themselves in their (original) celestial forms.'

statements.claim: Uddhava remembered the episode later with wonder - the lord, wishing to please his beloved like a common man, carrying the celestial tree home for his wife.
statements.evidence: BP 3.3.4 is Uddhava's own recall of exactly this episode (priyaṃ prabhur grāmya iva priyāyā...).

DKS_0265.notes: All beats (earrings restoration, Satyabhama's wish, uprooting, Shachi's protest, Indra's attack and defeat, planting in Satyabhama's garden with its three-furlong perfume and past-life recall) supported by BP 10.59.37-40, BP 3.3.4, HV 1.121/1.220 and VP 5.30-31. No issues.

statements.claim: In Dwaraka 16,100 brides were waiting - the maidens Krishna had freed from Naraka's palace, princesses, daughters of kings from many lands, who had come to the city with the demon's treasures.
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'the wealth, elephants, horses, and women, which he had recovered from Naraka... brought to Dwáraká by the servants of the demon'; count 'Sixteen thousand and one hundred' per VP 5.31 and BP 10.59.32.

statements.claim: They had chosen him with their own eyes the moment they saw him standing in the demon's hall, before a word was spoken.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.33-34: seeing him the women were captivated and each wished 'may this man be my husband.'

statements.claim: Krishna took possession of the wealth, the elephants and the horses recovered from Naraka.
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'Then Krishńa took possession of the wealth, elephants, horses, and women, which he had recovered from Naraka.'

statements.claim: At an auspicious season the wedding came; in separate mansions across Dwaraka, in a single moment, Krishna multiplied himself into as many forms and received the hand of every one of the 16,100 brides according to the ritual, each bride believing he was hers alone.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.41: 'muhūrta ekasmin nānāgāreṣu' (in a single moment, in separate mansions); VP 5.31: 'at an auspicious season he espoused all the maidens... at one and the same moment he received the hands of all of them, according to the ritual, in separate mansions. Sixteen thousand and one hundred was the number... into so many different forms did the foe of Madhu multiply himself; so that every one of the damsels thought that he had wedded her in his single person.'

statements.claim: Krishna took up residence in each of those houses, living with each wife as a householder, undivided, in a way beyond all reckoning and comparison; none but the Lord could perform such a feat.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.42: 'gṛheṣu tāsām anapāyy atarka-kṛn nirasta-sāmyātiśayeṣv avasthitaḥ' (he dwelt in their homes, never absent, unthinkable, beyond all comparison); VP 5.31: 'the creator of the world, Hari... abode severally in the dwelling of each of these his wives.'

statements.claim: Even Brahma and the other gods cannot trace his path - cannot follow how one man is wholly present to 16,100 wives.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.43: 'brahmādayo 'pi na viduḥ padavīṃ yadīyām' (even Brahma and the others do not know his path).

statements.claim: The brides rose to greet him and offered seats; they worshipped him, washed his feet, brought betel, rest, cooling fans, garlands and perfumes, and tended his hair, bed and bath; hundreds of maidservants served each household, and their love only grew.
statements.evidence: BP 10.59.44: 'pratyudgamāsana-varārhaṇa-pada-śauca-tāmbūla-viśramaṇa-vījana-gandha-mālyaiḥ keśa-prasāra-śayana-snapanopahāryaiḥ dāsī-śatā api vibhor vidadhuḥ sma dāsyam' (rising, seats, worship, foot-washing, betel, rest, fanning, perfumes, garlands, hair-dressing, beds, baths - even hundreds of maidservants served the Lord); v.43: their love grew ceaselessly (edhitayānurāga).

statements.claim: Each marriage was complete: each bride had her husband fully, not a fraction of him divided among thousands - a king might marry many wives by proxy, but this was different.
statements.evidence: Theological reflection consistent with the text's insistence on Krishna's undivided, simultaneous presence (BP 10.59.42-43); the proxy-marriage contrast is the narrator's framing, not a pack claim.

DKS_0266.notes: The simultaneous mass wedding, the multiplication into as many forms, residence in every house, Brahma's inability to trace his path, and the wives' loving service all track BP 10.59.41-44 and VP 5.31. No issues.

statements.claim: The war at Kurukshetra was over and the Pandavas had won it; Krishna was preparing to return to Dwaraka when Uttara cried out.
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.7-8 (Sanskrit): gantuṃ kṛtamatir brahman dvārakāṃ ratham āsthitaḥ — Krishna resolved to go to Dwaraka and mounted his chariot; pack index places the scene as Krishna departing Hastinapura after the war.

statements.claim: Uttara cried 'Protect me, protect me, great yogin, Lord of gods, master of the world! May this blazing iron-tipped arrow burn me, but let my embryo not fall.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt of SB 1.8: 'Uttara cries: Protect me, protect me, great yogin, Lord of gods, master of the world! May this blazing iron-tipped arrow burn me, but let my embryo not fall.'

statements.claim: Uttara was the daughter of King Virata.
statements.evidence: Pack: 'the womb of Virata's daughter.'

statements.claim: Drona's son Ashvatthama had loosed his weapon so that the Pandavas would be left without an heir, targeting the unborn child.
statements.evidence: Pack: 'the Lord... understood that Drona's son's weapon was aimed to leave the Pandavas without heir'; index: 'the unborn Parikshit.'

statements.claim: The weapon was the Brahmashira, unerring and beyond any counter.
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.14 (Sanskrit in pack): 'yadyapyastraṃ brahmaśirastvamoghaṃ cāpratikriyam' — the brahmashira weapon is unerring (amogha) and not to be counteracted (apratikriya).

statements.claim: By his own maya Krishna entered the womb and shielded the child with the Sudarshana disc, extinguishing the unerring Brahmashira.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Krishna enters her womb by his yoga-maya and shields the unborn Parikshit with the Sudarshana disc, extinguishing the unerring Brahmashira.' Verse excerpt states the womb was covered by his maya to preserve the Kuru line — summary is the pack's intended reading.

statements.claim: 'Do not be astonished, for all wonders have their home in him.'
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.15: 'mā maṃsthā hyetadāścaryaṃ sarvāścaryamaye ñcyute' — do not think this a wonder, for all wonders abide in Acyuta.

statements.claim: The child was born whole and would be called Parikshit, heir of the Kuru line; Uttara kept her own life and the child's.
statements.evidence: Pack title/index: 'Krishna Shields Parikshit in Uttara's Womb'; maya covered the womb 'to preserve the Kuru line.'

statements.claim: 'The war had won them a kingdom and cost them nearly everything else; the next generation of their house had been cut down in the terrible days after the fighting.'
statements.evidence: Background framing consistent with the pack's 'leave the Pandavas without heir' and the SB context of Ashvatthama's night attack; the specific killings are not detailed in the pack verses.

DKS_0267.notes: All factual claims supported by SB 1.8.7-15 pack. The Sudarshana-disc shielding follows the pack summary (verses themselves say maya covered the womb); no contradiction. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Hearing that Krishna and his warriors were coming and thinking they would attack, King Shrigala of Karavira rode out of the city to strike first.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v1: 'Being informed of their arrival and thinking that they would attack the city, king Shrigāla, terrible in battle and endued with the prowess of Indra, issued (out of the city).'

statements.claim: Shrigala's chariot had golden axles, was packed with weapons and inexhaustible quivers, was drawn by swift horses, coursed like Garuda, shone like the sun and resembled the car of Indra.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v2-6: car 'filled with weapons... filled with inexhaustible arrows and quivers... drawn by quick-coursing horses, embellished with strong golden axles, coursing like Garuda... effulgent like the sun and resembling the car of Indra.'

statements.claim: The earth was said to sink beneath Shrigala's weight, and he approached Krishna like an insect approaching a flame.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v7, v11: 'Shrigāla approached Krishna like an insect approaching a flame'; 'Stricken with fear at his shouts... the Earth sank under his weight.'

statements.claim: Krishna was not pained and sat at ease as Shrigala approached.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v12-13: 'Vāsudeva was not pained'; 'Shrigāla ran towards him like unto clouds ranging towards a mountain... Vāsudeva... seated at ease.'

statements.claim: Shrigala taunted Krishna about his work among the weak kings on Mount Gomanta and the useless Kshatriyas, declared himself emperor of the world, and offered a fair single combat: 'If thou art slain... I shall be the only Vāsudeva in the world. And if I am slain thou shalt be the only one.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v17-22, quoted nearly verbatim in the pack passage.

statements.claim: Krishna replied 'Strike me as you wish' and held up his discus.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v23: 'Hearing those words of Shrigala and saying Strike me as you wish the forgiving Mādhava held up his discus.'

statements.claim: The encounter resembled two infuriated elephants meeting in a forest.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v14-15: 'a dreadful encounter between them like that of two infuriated elephants in a forest.'

statements.claim: Shrigala lost his senses in anger, loosed a net of arrows and hurled maces and flaming weapons at Krishna, who stood motionless like a mountain.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v24-26: net of arrows, 'showered on Krishna mace and various other weapons... covered with flames of fire Krishna stood there motionless like a mountain.'

statements.claim: Krishna hurled the discus at Shrigala's breast; his heart pierced, the king fell bleeding like a cleft mountain.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v27-29: 'holding up his discus he hurled it at Shrigala's breast... Shrigala too, having his heart pierced by the discus... fell down, bleeding like a cleft mountain.'

statements.claim: The soldiers fled or wept in the city; Krishna said 'Do not fear! Do not fear!' to the people; the subjects, ministers and queens with their sons wept over the fallen king.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v30-40: soldiers fled, some entered the city weeping, some performed rites; Krishna declared safety and said 'Do not fear! Do not fear!'; subjects/ministers/queens with sons wept.

DKS_0268.notes: Story tracks HV 1.100 (Dutt) almost scene-for-scene, including the dialogue verbatim. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: The routed Asuras broke and ran; Nikumbha shamed them: 'You promised to avenge the destruction of your kinsmen... What will your wives say? Fie on you! Fie on you!'
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v1-6: Nikumbha, filled with anger, asked why they broke their promise to avenge their kinsmen and cried 'What will your wives say? Oh fie on you! fie on you!'

statements.claim: Filled with shame, the Asuras returned with double vigour and re-engaged the Yadavas at the sacrificial ground of the martial festival; Dhananjaya, Bhima, Nakula, Sahadeva and Yudhishthira destroyed those who came; sky-borne foes were slain by Indra's son and Pravara.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v7-9: Asuras 'returned with double vigour'; the five Pandava brothers 'destroyed all who went to that sacrificial ground where took place the martial festivity'; 'Those, who rose up into the sky, were slain by Indra's son and the foremost of the twice-born Pravara.'

statements.claim: The field ran with a river of blood thick as a rainy-season stream.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v10-12: 'there flew a river of blood like a stream filled with water in the rainy season.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha struck Pravara down with his iron club (parigha); Indra's son Jayanta caught and embraced his comrade, then ran back at the Asura; wounded by shafts, Nikumbha resolved to fight Krishna, who had killed his kinsmen, rather than exhaust himself on Indra's son.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v13-19: Nikumbha struck Pravara with his Parigha; Indra's son held him up, embraced him, and ran at the Asura; 'the great Asura thought: I shall fight... with my enemy Krishna who has killed my kinsmen. Why do I make myself exhausted by fightlng with Indra's son.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha vanished and reappeared where Krishna stood; Indra on Airavata had come with the gods to watch, and celestial trumpets sounded for Jayanta's victories.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v20-23: Nikumbha 'disappeared from that place and went where the highly powerful Krishna was'; 'Seated on his Airāvata... Vāsava, had come there with the gods to witness the battle'; 'celestial trumpets were struck at the command of the king of gods.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha set up a leonine shout and attacked Krishna, Arjuna, Bhima, Yudhishthira, the brothers, the Yadava chiefs and the kings, and by his illusory powers none of those masters of weapons could see him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v24-28: Nikumbha with a leonine shout attacked Garuda, Baladeva, Satyaka, Nārāyana, Arjuna, Bhima, Yudhisthira, Sahadeva, Nakula, Vasudeva, Shāmva and Pradyumna; 'none among those heroes, masters of all sorts of weapons, could see him.'

statements.claim: Krishna meditated on Vilwodakeshwara, the lord of goblins, and by that lord's power everyone could see Nikumbha standing like the summit of Kailasa.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v28-30: 'Hrishikesha (Krishna) meditated upon Vilwodakeshwara, the lord of goblins'; all 'could at once see Nikumbha... stationed before them like the summit of the Kailāsa.'

statements.claim: Arjuna had strung Gandiva and his shafts struck Nikumbha's body but shattered and fell broken; he asked Krishna, 'My arrows, resembling thunderbolts, pierce even the mountains. But why are they useless here?'
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v31-33: 'Pārtha had set string to his Gāndiva bow... they fell down on earth shattered and broken'; Dhananjaya asked 'My arrows... pierce even the mountains. But why are they useless here?'

statements.claim: Nikumbha fled to the cave of Shatpura, stronghold of his kin; Krishna followed; commanded by an invisible voice to use the discus and saluting Mahadeva, Krishna discharged the Sudarshana, which sundered Nikumbha's head with its earrings from his body.
statements.evidence: Pack title/summary: Krishna 'follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana'; excerpt: 'saluting Mahādeva he discharged his discus Sudarshana... sundered Nikumbha's head adorned with most beautiful ear-rings.'

DKS_0269.notes: Every beat maps to HV 1.232 passage (v1-33) + pack excerpt and title. Krishna's reply 'O son of Kunti, hear' begins exactly where the printed passage truncates; the cave/voice/discus ending is covered by the pack title and excerpt. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: While the Yadavas were absorbed in their sports and Dwaraka lay unguarded, the wicked, unapproachable Danava Nikumbha, enemy of the gods and bent on his own destruction, stole away Bhanumati, the beautiful daughter of Bhanu.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v1-2: 'While the virtuous Yadavas were thus sporting the highly wicked and unapproachable Dānava, Nikumbha, the enemy of the gods, desirous of bringing on his self-destruction, finding a loop-hole, stole away the beautiful daughter of Bhānu by name Bhānumati.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha was avenging an old enmity: Pradyumna had earlier carried off Prabhavati, daughter of Nikumbha's brother Vajranabha, and Vajranabha had been killed.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v3-4: 'formerly, the daughter of his brother Vajranābhā, by name Prabhāvati, had been taken away by Pradyumna and Vajranābha had been killed. Remembering this former enmity... he... stole away Bhānumati.'

statements.claim: Bhanumati was taken from the garden attached to her father Bhanu's women's quarters — a garden that was unapproachable but stood without guards because the Yadavas were busy with their sports.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v4-5: 'played upon the women of the Yādavas'; 'Although the garden, attached to the female appartment of Bhānu, was unapproachable, still at that time there were no guards for the Yadavas were busy with their sports.'

statements.claim: As the weeping maiden was carried away a great tumult arose in the women's quarters.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v6: 'while that weeping maiden was being carried away there arose all on a sudden a great tumult in the female appartment.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva and Ahuka rushed out filled with wrath and, finding no offender, went in their sport dress to Krishna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v7-8: 'the heroes, Vasudeva and Ahuka issued out, filled with wrath. And not seeing the offender before them, they, in that dress, went where the highly powerful Krishna was.'

statements.claim: Krishna, hearing of the insult, rode Garuda (enemy of serpents) with Arjuna, commanded Pradyumna (whose banner bore the Makara) to follow in his chariot, and bade Garuda fly.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v9-10: 'Janārddana... rode, together with Pārtha, Garuda the enemy of the serpents. Having commanded the hero having the emblem of a Makara on his flag to follow him on his car he asked Kashyapa's son Garuda to proceed.'

statements.claim: 'The whole city of Dwaraka at leisure, its palaces open, its gardens unwatched... was exactly what Nikumbha had been waiting for.'
statements.evidence: Atmosphere consistent with v1-5 (Yadavas sporting, no guards); motive framing not stated verbatim in pack.

statements.claim: Nikumbha was a master of illusion who knew a hundred ways to vanish, so finding him would take all the speed of Garuda, all the arrows of Arjuna and all the cunning of Pradyumna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v4, v12: Nikumbha 'proficient in illusions'; Pradyumna 'the foremost of those conversant with illusions.'

DKS_0270.notes: Faithful to HV 1.237 v1-11 and the pack summary (ocean sport, unguarded garden, revenge motive). Story ends where the pursuit begins; the overtaking/rescue is the next story's content. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Before Nikumbha could reach the city of Vajra, Krishna and Arjuna overtook him on the way.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v11: 'before Nikumbha, unconquerable in battle, could reach the city of Vajra, Pārtha and Krishna... overtook him in the way.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, foremost of those conversant with illusions, divided himself into three portions.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v12: 'the highly powerful Pradyumna, the foremost of those conversant with illusions, divided himself into three portions.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha, smiling, fought all three with heavy clubs while holding the weeping maiden in his left hand.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v13: 'Nikumbha, like unto an immortal, smilingly fought with them all with heavy clubs. Holding the maiden Bhānumati by his left hand... repeatedly hurled the club with his right hand.'

statements.claim: Krishna, Pradyumna and Arjuna could not strike ruthlessly lest they wound the maiden; they sighed with compassion for her and, following the rules of their art, struck the demon with cane-like arrows without touching the maiden.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v14-18: none 'could strike him ruthlessly lest they might wound the maiden'; they 'began to sigh piteously out of their excessive compassion'; 'Pārtha, Kāma and Krishna did not strike the maiden but wounded the Danavas with their cane-like arrows.'

statements.claim: Arjuna shot as a man strikes a serpent coiled round a camel, leaving the beast untouched.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v17: 'As when a serpent gets round a camel... so Pārtha, the foremost of archers, began to strike the Daitya with his arrows.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha vanished with the maiden by illusion and went on assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture; Arjuna assailed him with arrows piercing his vitals.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v19-21: Nikumbha 'so disappeared with the maiden... nobody could know it'; 'he, however, went on assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture'; Dhananjaya 'assailed him again with cane-like arrows piercing his very vitals.'

statements.claim: Pursued across the whole earth of seven insular continents, Nikumbha dropped down on the bank of the river Chela Ganga on the summit of Mount Gokarna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v22-23: 'that great Asura... travelled all over the earth consisting of seven insular continents and dropped down with the maiden at last on the bank of the river Chela Gangā flowing on the summit of the mount Gokarna.'

statements.claim: No god, Asura or great ascetic could cross that mountain, protected by the energy of Mahadeva; Pradyumna found the weak point and snatched Bhanumati away.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v24-25: 'None amongst the gods, Asuras or great ascetics could cross that mountain protected by the energy of Mahadeva. Finding this weak point of Nikumbha... Pradyumna... got hold of the maiden Bhānumati.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Arjuna assailed Nikumbha with arrows; he fled from the northern range of Gokarna to the southern range, pursued by the two Krishnas on Garuda.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v25-26: 'Krishna, and Arjuna began to assail the Asura greatly with arrows. Then leaving the northern range of the mount Gokarna, Nikumbha fled to the southern range. Both the Krishnas however, riding on Garuda, pursued him.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha entered Shatpura, the abode of his kinsmen; Krishna and Arjuna spent the night at the mouth of the cave; Pradyumna, with Krishna's permission, took Bhanumati back to Dwaraka and returned; the three heroes then occupied the entrance of Shatpura waiting for Nikumbha.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v27-30: Nikumbha 'entered into Shatpura, the abode of his kinsmen'; the two heroes spent the night at the cave mouth; 'With Krishna's permission the heroic son of Rukshmini... took... daughter to the city of Dwārakā... and returned'; Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna 'waited there.'

DKS_0271.notes: Scene-for-scene match with HV 1.237 v11-30 including the serpent-camel simile and cane-like arrows detail. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Bhanumati, daughter of Bhanu, had been snatched from the women's garden by the demon Nikumbha while the city was absorbed in its sports; Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna chased him across the earth and brought her safely home; the demon was shut up in his mountain stronghold.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v1-30 (pack): abduction from the unguarded garden, pursuit, rescue at Gokarna, Nikumbha confined in Shatpura; recap is consistent with the same chapter.

statements.claim: The sage Narada came to Dwaraka and supplied the explanation that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a curse.
statements.evidence: Pack title/summary: 'Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages.'

statements.claim: Long before, the girl had excited the anger of Durvasa, the foremost of sages, who imprecated a curse that she must fall into the hands of an enemy.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.237, Narada's speech): 'this your daughter excited the anger of the foremost of Munis Durvāsā who... imprecated a curse on her saying:— she must fall into the hands of an enemy.'

statements.claim: The sages had softened the curse: Bhanumati would fall into an enemy's hands as the words demanded, but that is where its working ended — she would be taken, and she would be restored.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'a Durvasa curse softened by the sages'; chapter narrative has the abduction followed by rescue and restoration, matching the limited working.

statements.claim: The abduction by Nikumbha, the long chase and the rescue at Mount Gokarna were the curse doing exactly what it had been permitted to do, and no more.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the pack summary's softened-curse reading and the HV 1.237 events (abduction → pursuit → rescue at Gokarna → return).

statements.claim: Bhanu gave his daughter in marriage to Sahadeva, the youngest of the five Pandava brothers, in Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: '...do you now confer her on Sahadeva.' Sahadeva is the youngest Pandava (standard corpus fact); wedding location Dwaraka follows from the Dwaraka setting of the chapter.

statements.claim: 'The demon had believed he was avenging an old wrong and choosing his own hour. Perhaps he was. But beneath his malice had run an older current, set in motion years before by a sage's anger.'
statements.evidence: Interpretive commentary that synthesizes the pack's two strands (Nikumbha's revenge motive v3-4 and the Durvasa curse excerpt); no separate factual assertion.

DKS_0272.notes: Supported by pack summary + excerpt (HV 1.237 Narada passage: Durvasa curse, 'confer her on Sahadeva'). No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Krishna was hidden under a growing mound of rocks where his chariot had stood — buried by torrents of rocks.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'torrents of rocks falling upon me covered me up... covered along with my horses and charioteer and flagstaffs, with crags on all sides, I disappeared from sight altogether.'

statements.claim: Salwa came to war from his flying city Saubha, a fortress of costly metal that could move through the sky wherever he willed, and devastated Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'that car of precious metals capable of going anywhere at will'; Daruka: 'he... devastated Dwaraka'; story's pack title/locations: Saubha (aerial city).

statements.claim: Krishna had gone out to meet Salwa in single combat in the air; the fight began as a duel of archery against the enemies who crowded the aerial city.
statements.evidence: Framing for the excerpted battle (MBh 3.22 begins mid-duel with Krishna cutting off heads 'from off that car of costly metals'); the specific 'single combat in the air' staging is not within the pack passage itself but is consistent with the Salwa episode.

statements.claim: Krishna loosed arrows shaped like serpents, capable of great height and intense energy, cutting down the enemies of the celestials.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'I began to discharge from the Sharanga many well-looking arrows of the forms of snakes, capable of going at a great height and possessing intense energy.'

statements.claim: The car vanished through illusion; Krishna was filled with wonder; Danavas of frightful visages and hair set up a loud howl; Krishna slew them with the weapon that strikes at sound, answering yells from all ten directions with mantra-charged arrows until the invisible hosts were silent.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: car 'had vanished, through illusion... I was then filled with wonder'; 'host of Danvas... of frightful visages and hair, set up a loud howl'; shafts 'capable of striking at the perception of sound alone'; yells from 'all the ten quarters above and across' answered with 'arrows of diverse forms, and celestial weapons inspired with mantras.'

statements.claim: The car of precious metals reappeared at Pragjyotisha and the Danavas drowned Krishna in a mighty shower of rocks, so that he grew like an ant-hill with summits and peaks.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'that car of precious metals... bewildering my eyes, reappeared at Pragjyotisha'; 'the destroying Danavas of fierce forms suddenly drowned me with a mighty shower of rocks... I began to grow like an ant-hill (with its summits and peaks).'

statements.claim: Krishna's Vrishni army, struck with panic, fled in all directions; heaven, firmament and earth were filled with cries of 'Oh!' and 'Alas!'; friends wept while enemies rejoiced.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'those foremost of heroes of the Vrishni race who were of my army were, struck with panic, and all on a sudden began to fly in all directions'; 'the heaven, the firmament, and the earth were filled with exclamation of Oh! and Alas!'; 'my friends... began to weep and wail... delight filled the hearts of the enemies.'

statements.claim: Wielding the thunderbolt, Indra's favourite weapon capable of riving stones, Krishna destroyed the entire mass of crags; his horses stood trembling, almost at the point of death, and his friends rejoiced as at the sun dispersing clouds.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'wielding the thunderbolt, that favourite (weapon) of Indra, capable of riving stones, I destroyed that entire mass of crags'; 'my steeds, afflicted with the weight of the stones and almost on the point of death began to tremble'; friends 'rejoiced... even as men rejoice on seeing the sun rise in the sky, dispersing the clouds.'

statements.claim: Charioteer Daruka urged Krishna: 'Behold Salwa... Do not disregard him... Slay Salwa — do not let him live... this one has devastated Dwaraka.'
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22, Daruka's speech quoted near-verbatim in the pack passage: 'behold Salwa the owner of the car of precious metals sitting (yonder)... Slay Salwa... do not let him live... he... devastated Dwaraka.'

statements.claim: Krishna fixed his blazing weapon of fire to the bowstring, bade Daruka stay a moment, and hurled the discus Sudarshana — sharp-edged as a razor, unstained, reducing Yakshas, Rakshasas and Danavas to ashes — which rose like a second sun, went through the town of Saubha as a saw divides a tall tree, and cut the flying city in twain.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'saying unto Daruka, Stay a moment I fixed on my bow-string my favourite weapon of fire... the great powerful discus Sudarsana which reduceth to ashes in battle Yakshas and Rakshasas and Danavas... sharp-edged like the razor, and without stain'; 'rising into the sky, it seemed like a second sun... the discus went right through it, even as a saw divideth a tall tree. And cut in twain by the energy of the Sudarsana.'

DKS_0273.notes: Near-verbatim rendering of MBh 3.22 (Ganguli). The 'single combat in the air' opening line is connective framing outside the excerpted passage (flagged RCN); everything else directly supported. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Krishna held the reins of Arjuna's chariot at Kurukshetra, having come as a charioteer, not a fighter.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 excerpt: 'Vasudeva's son, abandoning (the reins of) the steeds, jumped down from the car'; the army trembled 'in the very presence of Vasudeva and the high-souled Partha' — Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer is the fixed frame of the battle narrative.

statements.claim: After the forenoon had passed and the Pandavas had won the first part of the day, Devavrata (Bhishma, son of Santanu) was carried by his fleetest steeds into the mass of his enemies, and a dreadful engagement followed.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'After the forenoon of that day... had passed away... and after the high-souled Pandavas had won the victory, thy sire Devavrata... rushed carried by the fleetest steeds, towards the army of the Pandavas... commenced a dreadful battle, making the hair stand on end.'

statements.claim: The battle sounds — twang of bows like splitting hills, cries of 'Stay! Here I stand!' and 'Turn back!', fall of golden armour and diadems like stones on stony ground — and a river of blood miry with the bodies of men, horses and elephants, with vultures and jackals at its edges.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: uproar 'resembling that of splitting hills'; words 'Stay--Here I stand... Turn back' heard everywhere; falling coats of gold mail 'resembled the sound of falling stones on a stony ground'; 'dreadful river of blood... miry with flesh and blood... Flowing from the bodies of steeds, men, and elephants, and delightful to vultures and jackals.'

statements.claim: Bhishma's bow, drawn into a circle, shot blazing shafts like venomous snakes; not one arrow was futile; he smote the Pandava car-warriors, naming each one beforehand; his lightness of hands made him seem to dance like a circle of fire present everywhere.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'Bhishma... with bow incessantly drawn to a circle, shot shafts of blazing points, resembling snakes of virulent poison'; 'smote the Pandava car-warriors naming each beforehand'; 'displaying his extreme lightness of hands, and dancing (as it were) along the track of his car, he seemed... to be present everywhere like a circle of fire'; 'Not a single shaft of that light-handed warrior was futile.'

statements.claim: The Pandavas and Srinjayas saw Bhishma, though really alone, multiplied a thousand-fold, now east, now west, now north, now south; they could not even look at him and saw only the countless shafts.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'the Pandavas in that battle, along with the Srinjayas, beheld that hero, though really alone, as multiplied a thousand-fold'; 'Having seen him now on the east, the next moment they saw him on the west... on the north... on the south'; 'There was no one amongst the Pandavas capable of even looking at him. What they all saw were only the innumerable shafts.'

statements.claim: Thousands of kings fell upon the enraged Bhishma like flights of senseless insects upon a blazing fire; a single straight shaft despatched a single elephant as a hill is riven by thunderbolt, and one arrow pierced two or three armoured riders standing together.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'kings in thousands came in contact with thy sire... and fell upon that fire represented by the enraged Bhishma like flights of senseless insects'; 'With a single straight shaft... he despatched a single elephant like hill riven by the thunderbolt. Two or three elephant-riders at a time, cased in mail and standing together, thy sire pierced with one shaft.'

statements.claim: Whoever approached Bhishma was seen for a moment and the next moment was seen falling; the vast host of King Yudhishthira gave way in a thousand directions and trembled in the presence of Vasudeva and Partha.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'Whoever approached Bhishma... seen for a moment, was next beheld to fall down on the ground'; 'that vast host of king Yudhishthira the just... gave way in a thousand directions'; 'the vast army began to tremble in the very presence of Vasudeva and the high-souled Partha.'

statements.claim: Krishna abandoned the reins, jumped down from the car whirling the discus Sudarshana — beautiful nave, edge sharp as a razor, effulgent as the sun — and rushed impetuously toward Bhishma like a lion springing upon a prince of elephants blinded with fury.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 excerpt: 'Vasudeva's son, abandoning (the reins of) the steeds, jumped down from the car, whirling with his (right) arm his discus of beautiful nave with edge sharp as a razor, effulgent as the sun... the high-souled Krishna rushed impetuously towards Bhishma... like a lion from desire of slaying upon a prince of elephants blinded with fury.'

statements.claim: The grandsire, who had named every warrior before he shot, had not named this one (Krishna).
statements.evidence: Closing flourish tying v11 (Bhishma named Pandava car-warriors beforehand) to Krishna's unannounced charge; consistent with the excerpt.

DKS_0274.notes: MBh 6.59 (Ganguli) rendered almost clause-for-clause, including Bhishma's feats and the closing charge. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: As the cowherds of Vraja slept in Ambika forest keeping a vow, the chief Nanda was seized by a great hungry serpent and cried out 'Krishna! Krishna!'
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.4-6: 'kaścin mahān ahis tasmin vipine 'ti-bubhukṣitaḥ' (a certain great serpent, very hungry, in that forest), 'sa cukrośāhinā grastaḥ kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahān ayam'; v18 confirms the cowherds completed their vow there ('samāpya tasmin niyamaṃ').

statements.claim: The cowherds beat and burned the serpent with firebrands, but it would not release Nanda.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.7: 'alātair dahyamāno 'pi nāmuñcat tam uraṅgamaḥ' (though burnt by firebrands the serpent did not release him).

statements.claim: Krishna touched the serpent with his foot, which destroyed its evil and released Nanda.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.8: 'sa vai bhagavataḥ śrīmat pāda-sparśa-hatāśubhaḥ' (its evil destroyed by the Lord's foot-touch); pack excerpt: 'Nanda was released'.

statements.claim: The serpent was in truth Sudarshana the Vidyadhara, who had mocked the Angirasa sages in pride of his beauty and been cursed by them as a grace — bound in the serpent body until the blessed one's touch should free him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.12-13: 'ṛṣīn virūpāṅgirasaḥ prāhasaṃ rūpa-darpitaḥ / śāpo me 'nugrahāyaiva kṛtas taiḥ karuṇātmabhiḥ'; identity as 'Sudarshana the Vidyadhara' comes from the pack's own source excerpt (SB 10.34.4-17 rendering), which the verses shown presuppose.

statements.claim: Krishna asked who he was, and the radiant being praised Krishna as the remover of fear for the refuge-seeking, the great yogi, then took leave, circumambulated him and bowed.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.9-10 ('ko bhavān parayā lakṣmyā rocate 'dbhuta-darśanaḥ'), v14-15 ('bhava-bhītānāṃ prapannānāṃ bhayāpaham... mahā-yogin mahā-puruṣa sat-pate'), v17 ('ity anujñāpya dāśārhaṃ parikramyābhivandya ca').

statements.claim: The being then rose into the night sky (a Vidyadhara, sky-farer).
statements.evidence: The pack verses end with the circumambulation and homage (10.34.17); his skyward departure is not stated in the excerpted verses but is consistent with Vidyadhara nature and uncontradicted.

statements.claim: The cowherds, astonished at Krishna's glory, completed their vow and returned to Vraja telling the story.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.18: 'niśāmya kṛṣṇasya tad ātma-vaibhavaṃ... samāpya tasmin niyamaṃ punar vrajaṃ... kathayanta ādṛtāḥ'.

DKS_0275.notes: Faithful verse-by-verse to SB 10.34.4-18. The name/status 'Sudarshana the Vidyadhara' is carried by the pack's excerpt; dialogue paraphrase matches v9-16.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama, brought by Akrura, entered Mathura on foot along the royal road and were regarded with pleasure by men and women, like two young elephants.
statements.evidence: VP 5.19 (pack): 'You must now journey on foot... left them... whilst Ráma and Krishńa continued to walk along the royal road. Regarded with pleasure by men and women, they went along sportively, looking like two young elephants.'

statements.claim: A weaver gladly fitted both brothers with garments of many colours, each bearing its own mark/device.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.39-40: 'vāyakaḥ prītas tayor veṣam akalpayat / nānā-lakṣaṇa-veṣābhyāṃ kṛṣṇa-rāmau virejatuḥ'.

statements.claim: Pleased with the weaver, Krishna gave him a form like his own (sārūpya).
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.41: 'tasya prasanno bhagavān prādāt sārūpyam ātmanaḥ'.

statements.claim: At the garland-maker Sudama's house the brothers were honoured with seats, foot-washing water, arghya and other rites, and with garlands and sandal paste.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.42-43 ('sudāmno bhavanaṃ mālā-kārasya... āsanam ānīya pādyaṃ cārghyārhaṇādibhiḥ') and pack excerpt ('honoring them with garlands and sandal paste').

statements.claim: Sudama declared their birth and family purified, called them the supreme cause of the world with no partial glance, the soul of all beings, and offered himself as their servant.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.44-47: 'naḥ sārthakaṃ janma pāvitaṃ ca kulaṃ... viśvasya jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ param... na hi vāṃ viṣamā dṛṣṭiḥ suhṛdor jagad-ātmanoḥ / tāv ajñāpayataṃ bhṛtyaṃ kim ahaṃ karavāṇi vām'.

statements.claim: Asked what he wanted, Sudama chose only unshakable devotion, and Krishna granted it along with fortune that grows in his line.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.50-51: 'so 'pi vavre 'calāṃ bhaktiṃ tasminn evākhilātmani / iti tasmai varaṃ dattvā śriyaṃ cānvaya-vardhinīm'.

statements.claim: The older telling adds that the blessing extended beyond this life to a heavenly region at the end.
statements.evidence: VP 5.19 (pack excerpt): 'you shall finally obtain... a heavenly region, the consequence of my favour'; tradition_note correctly flags this as the VP-only framing.

statements.claim: Word of the strangers spread through Mathura that night; the city wondered what the cowherd boys would do next.
statements.evidence: Closing scene-setting consistent with the canonical sequence (the brothers are in Kamsa's city before the arena events); not a sourceable assertion in the pack.

DKS_0276.notes: Blends BP 10.41.39-51 (weaver + Sudama, sārūpya and devotion/fortune boons) with VP 5.19 (foot-entry, heavenly region), cleanly attributed; tradition_note matches the pack's variant note.

statements.claim: The radiant being before Krishna had been a giant lizard in a dry well, drawn out by Krishna's left hand and restored by his touch — King Nriga of the Ikshvaku line.
statements.evidence: Recap of the canonical prior event (corpus chain, previous title): 'The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga'; Nriga's Ikshvaku lineage per pack index.

statements.claim: Nriga gave cows beyond counting — as many as the sands of the earth and stars of the sky: milch and young cows of fine form, tawny with gold-tipped horns, to virtuous, vow-keeping brahmanas and needy families.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.11-13: 'yāvatyaḥ sikatā bhūmer yāvatyo divi tārakāḥ / payasvinīs taruṇīḥ śīla-rūpa-guṇopapannāḥ kapilā hema-sṛṅgīḥ / sv-alaṅkṛtebhyo guṇa-śīlavadbhyaḥ sīdat-kuṭumbebhya ṛta-vratebhyaḥ'.

statements.claim: He also gave land, gold, houses, horses, elephants, maidens with their servants, sesame, silver and beds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.14: 'go-bhū-hiraṇyāyatanāśva-hastinaḥ kanyāḥ sa-dāsīs tila-rūpya-śayyāḥ'.

statements.claim: A cow of a foremost brahmana strayed into Nriga's herd and was being led out to another brahmana when its owner cried 'That cow is mine!'; both brahmanas disputed the cow before the king.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.15-17: 'kasyacid dvija-mukhyasya bhraṣṭā gaur mama go-dhane / tāṃ nīyamānāṃ tat-svāmī dṛṣṭvovāca mameti tam / viprau vivadamānau mām ūcatuḥ svārtha-sādhakau'.

statements.claim: Nriga propitiated both brahmanas with wealth gained by righteous means, begging them to forgive the unknowing servant; the owner refused all compensation and walked away, and neither would yield.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.18-20: 'anunītāv ubhau viprau dharma-kṛcchra-gatena vai / bhavantāv anugṛhītāṃ kiṅkarasyāvijānataḥ / nāhaṃ pratīcche vai rājann ity uktvā svāmy apākramat'; pack summary: 'both brahmanas claimed it and refused all compensation'.

statements.claim: Yama's messengers took Nriga to Yama's court, where Yama asked whether he would first taste the good or the bad of his deeds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.21-22: 'etasminn antare yāmair dūtair nīto yama-kṣayam / pūrvaṃ tvam aśubhaṃ bhuṅkṣa utāho nṛpate śubham'.

statements.claim: Nriga chose to suffer the bad first, and so fell as a lizard.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.23: 'pūrvaṃ devāśubhaṃ bhuñja iti prāha pateti saḥ'; pack excerpt: 'he fell as a lizard'. The dry-well imprisonment is the established prior-event state (corpus chain).

statements.claim: The moralizing gloss on Nriga's motives ('perhaps because the merit of a life of giving could wait...') is offered as the narrator's speculation.
statements.evidence: Explicitly framed as conjecture ('He did not argue it. Perhaps...'); no factual claim.

DKS_0278.notes: Follows SB 10.64.9-23 closely; well/left-hand/lizard details belong to the preceding canonical event and are consistent with the pack chain.

statements.claim: Nriga praised Krishna as the witness of every being's heart, the lord of yoga seen in the pure hearts of those guided by scripture, beyond the senses, whose very sight ends worldly existence.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.24-25: 'kiṃ nu te 'viditaṃ nātha sarva-bhūtātma-sākṣiṇaḥ... parātmā yogeśvaraḥ śruti-dṛśāmala-hṛd-vibhāvyaḥ sākṣād adhokṣaja... yasya bhavāpavargaḥ'.

statements.claim: Nriga asked Krishna's permission to go to the celestial world, bowed, circumambulated him and touched his feet with his head.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.26-29: 'anujānīhi māṃ kṛṣṇa yāntaṃ deva-gatiṃ prabho... ity uktvā taṃ parikramya pādau spṛṣṭvā sva-maulinā'.

statements.claim: Krishna taught the gathered citizens that a brahmana's property, even a little enjoyed, is indigestible fire — worse than hālāhala poison (which has an antidote; poison kills only the eater and fire is quenched by water), for brahmana wealth taken without leave destroys three generations.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.31-34: 'durjaraṃ bata brahma-svaṃ bhuktam agner manāg api / nāhaṃ hālāhalaṃ manye viṣaṃ yasya pratikriyā / hinasti viṣam attāraṃ vahnir adbhiḥ praśāmyati / brahma-svaṃ duranujñātaṃ bhuktaṃ hanti tri-pūruṣam'.

statements.claim: Krishna warned that kings blinded by royal fortune do not see their own fall, paying in years for every handful of dust and every tear of those they rob.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.35-37: 'rājāno rāja-lakṣmyāndhā nātma-pātaṃ vicakṣate / gṛhṇanti yāvataḥ pāṃśūn krandatām aśru-bindavaḥ / rājāno rāja-kulyāś ca tāvato 'bdān niraṅkuśāḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna declared that whoever takes a brahmana's livelihood — given by his own hand or another's — covets what makes men short-lived; that one must never harm even an erring brahmana; and that wealth torn from a brahmana drags the taker down.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.38-42: 'sva-dattāṃ para-dattāṃ vā brahma-vṛttiṃ harec ca yaḥ / na me brahma-dhanaṃ bhūyād yad gṛdhvālpāyuṣo narāḥ / vipraṃ kṛtāgasam api naiva druhyata māmakāḥ / yathāhaṃ praṇame viprān anukālaṃ samāhitaḥ / brāhmaṇārtho hy apahṛto hartāraṃ pātayaty adhaḥ'.

statements.claim: A celestial car descended, Nriga boarded it and ascended out of sight above Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Nriga praised Krishna, bowed, and ascended to heaven in a celestial car'; consistent with SB 10.64's continuation beyond the excerpted v43 ('evaṃ viśrāvya bhagavān mukundo dvārakaukasaḥ').

statements.claim: The two teachings — the poison-with-no-antidote warning and Nriga's tale — were retold in Dwaraka long after.
statements.evidence: Closing reflection; not a sourceable assertion.

DKS_0279.notes: Teaching matches SB 10.64.30-43 near-verbatim. Note: the pack's one-line excerpt condenses the order (ascent before the teaching); the passage itself (and this story) place Krishna's address to the people first, the car/ascent after — passage treated as authoritative.

statements.claim: Paundraka, king of Karusha, deluded by flatterers who called him the descended Lord Vasudeva, lost recollection of his real self and believed himself the one true Vasudeva.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.1-2 ('tvaṃ vāsudevo bhagavān avatīrṇo jagat-patiḥ', 'dūtaṃ ca prāhiṇon mandaḥ'); VP 5.34: 'flattered by ignorant people as the descended deity... Losing all recollection of his real character'.

statements.claim: He sent a messenger to Krishna at Dwaraka demanding that Krishna give up the divine marks he bore and surrender the name and character of Vasudeva, coming to do homage in return for means of subsistence.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.4-5 ('vāsudevo 'vatīrṇo 'ham eka eva na cāparaḥ / yāni tvam asmac-cihnāni mauḍhyād bibharṣi sātvata'); VP 5.34 message: 'Relinquish... the discus; lay aside all my insignia, my name, and the character of Vāsudeva; and come and do me homage; and I will vouchsafe thee means of subsistence.'

statements.claim: The assembly laughed at the message, and Krishna replied in jesting words that he would hurl those very signs at the fool and slay him, and that Paundraka's face would lie covered by cranes and vultures.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.7-9: 'uvāca dūtaṃ bhagavān parihāsa-kathām anu / mukhaṃ tad apidhāyājña kaṅka-gṛdhra-vaṭair vṛtaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'the assembly laughed, and Krishna replied that he would hurl those signs at the fool and slay him'; VP 5.34: the assembly/jesting reply and ironic discus promise.

statements.claim: The messenger carried the whole reply back to Paundraka, unsoftened.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.10 (pack v9): 'iti dūtas tam ākṣepaṃ svāmine sarvam āharat'.

statements.claim: Paundraka had made ready for a penitent Krishna — the welcome, the ceremonies.
statements.evidence: Nothing in the pack (SB 10.66.1-9 and excerpt) or in the fuller account (SB 10.66.10-11 shows Paundraka instead appearing with two akṣauhiṇīs to meet Krishna's battle preparations; VP 5.34 likewise has him march out with his army) supports any prepared welcome or ceremonies for a submitting Krishna.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

statements.claim: The story's closing note that his delusion left no room for the possibility that his embassy was absurd.
statements.evidence: Dramatization consistent with the delusion the pack establishes; not itself a sourceable event.

corrections.original_sentence: He had made ready for a penitent Krishna — the welcome, the ceremonies — and the thought that the demand might be refused had never once crossed his mind.
corrections.suggested: He had been certain of his own divinity, and the thought that the demand might be refused had never once crossed his mind.

DKS_0280.notes: Core episode faithful to SB 10.66.1-9. One invented embellishment: the welcome/ceremonies prepared for a 'penitent Krishna' — no source has Paundraka preparing ceremonies; both SB and VP show him arming for battle instead.

statements.claim: Krishna had slain the impostor Paundraka and the king of Kashi who had sheltered him; the king's son Sudakshina performed his father's funeral rites.
statements.evidence: Prior canonical event (corpus chain: 'Krishna Slays Paundraka and the King of Kashi'); VP 5.34: Paundraka 'supported by the king of Káśí. Krishńa marches against, and destroys them.'; SB 10.66.25-26: 'rājñaḥ kāśī-pater... mahiṣyaḥ putra-bāndhavāḥ / sudakṣiṇas tasya sutaḥ kṛtvā saṃsthā-vidhiṃ pateḥ'.

statements.claim: With his teachers Sudakshina worshipped Shiva at Avimukta, and the pleased lord granted him a boon: to serve the southern (dakṣiṇa) fire with brahmana priests in an abhicāra rite against the enemy he called impious.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.27-30: 'ity ātmanābhisandhāya sopādhyāyo maheśvaram / prīto 'vimukte bhagavāṃs tasmai varam adād vibhuḥ / dakṣiṇāgniṃ paricara brāhmaṇaiḥ samam ṛtvijam / sādhayiṣyati saṅkalpam abrahmaṇye prayojitaḥ'.

statements.claim: From the fire pit rose an embodied, terrible fire-demon — fierce with fangs, furrowed brows and a harsh face, tongue licking, feet of palm-tree size shaking the earth — which set out toward Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.31-34: 'tato 'gnir utthitaḥ kuṇḍān mūrtimān ati-bhīṣaṇaḥ / daṃṣṭrogra-bhru-kuṭī-daṇḍa-kaṭhorāsyaḥ sva-jihvayā / padbhyāṃ tāla-pramāṇābhyāṃ kampayann avanī-talam / tam ābhicāra-dahanam āyāntaṃ dvārakaukasaḥ'.

statements.claim: The frightened citizens of Dwaraka ran to Krishna, who was playing dice in the assembly hall; Krishna, witness within and without all things, saw the fear of his people and sent the Sudarshana discus, blazing like ten million suns and like the fire of cosmic dissolution.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.35-38: 'akṣaiḥ sabhāyāṃ krīḍantaṃ bhagavantaṃ bhayāturāḥ... sarvasyāntar-bahiḥ-sākṣī vibhuḥ / tat sūrya-koṭi-pratimaṃ sudarśanaṃ jājvalyamānaṃ pralayānala-prabham'.

statements.claim: The demon, its face shattered by the discus, turned back and, reaching Varanasi, burned Sudakshina and the priests — his own abhicāra consumed its master.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.39: 'kṛtyānalaḥ pratihataḥ... bhagna-mukho nivṛttaḥ / vārāṇasīṃ parisametya sudakṣiṇaṃ taṃ sartvig-janaṃ samadahat sva-kṛto 'bhicāraḥ'.

statements.claim: The discus then entered Varanasi — through its ramparts, halls and markets — and burned the whole city, which even the gods could not enter, with all its princes and followers.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.40-42: 'cakraṃ ca viṣṇos tad-anupraviṣṭaṃ vārāṇasīṃ sāṭṭa-sabhālayāpaṇām / dagdhvā vārāṇasīṃ sarvāṃ'; VP 5.34: 'Thus was Vārāṇasī burnt, with all its princes and their followers... a city, that was inaccessible to the gods, was thus wrapped in flames.'

statements.claim: The closing moral — that the discus undid in a single night what no army or god had ever done to the city he loved — is rhetorical summation.
statements.evidence: The 'single night' duration is not stated in the pack; the sentence is a moralizing close (compare VP's 'inaccessible to the gods'), not an event report.

DKS_0282.notes: Faithful to SB 10.66.25-42 and VP 5.34; Sudakshina's name follows BP while the pack's variant note flags VP leaves the son unnamed.

statements.claim: At the svayamvara of Lakshmana, daughter of Duryodhana, Samba — son of Jambavati and a Yadava of Dwaraka — carried her off in his chariot.
statements.evidence: VP 5.35 (pack): 'At the choice of a husband by the daughter of Duryodhana, the princess was carried off by the hero Śámba, the son of Jámbavatí'; BP 10.68.1ff, Kauravas' outcry follows (v1-2, 5).

statements.claim: The furious Kauravas called him an ill-mannered boy, demanded he be bound, and asked what the Vrishnis would dare do.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.1-3: 'kauravāḥ kupitā ūcur durvinīto 'yam arbhakaḥ / badhnītemaṃ durvinītaṃ kiṃ kariṣyanti vṛṣṇayaḥ'.

statements.claim: Karna, Shala, Bhuri, Yajnaketu and Duryodhana himself gave chase, shouting 'Stop! Stop!'
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.4-6: 'iti karṇaḥ śalo bhūrir yajñaketuḥ suyodhanaḥ / dṛṣṭvānudhāvataḥ sāmbo dhārtarāṣṭrān mahā-rathaḥ / taṃ te jighṛkṣavaḥ kruddhās tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti bhāṣiṇaḥ'; story follows BP's five chiefs (tradition_note correct that VP adds Bhishma and Drona).

statements.claim: Samba turned, twanged his handsome bow and pierced them all — four arrows into the horses of each foremost chariot and one arrow into each charioteer.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.8-9: 'visphūrjya ruciraṃ cāpaṃ sarvān vivyādha sāyakaiḥ / caturbhiś caturo vāhān ekaikena ca sārathīn'.

statements.claim: The Kurus cut down his four horses and, with great effort, seized and bound him, chariot-less, taking him prisoner with Lakshmana taken from him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.10-11: 'taṃ tu te virathaṃ cakruś catvāraś caturo hayān / taṃ baddhvā virathī-kṛtya kṛcchreṇa kuravo yudhi'; the recovery of Lakshmana into Kuru hands is implied by the failed abduction at Hastinapura (uncontradicted in the pack; VP 5.35 later has the Kurus surrender 'Śámba and his wife').

statements.claim: The attitude among Kauravas that the Yadu race had no claim to royal dignity.
statements.evidence: VP 5.35 (pack): 'Báhlíka and other friends of the Kauravas, who looked upon the Yadu race as not entitled to regal dignity'; echoed in BP's 'kiṃ kariṣyanti vṛṣṇayaḥ'.

statements.claim: When the Yadavas heard of the capture, their wrath was kindled and Dwaraka's councils grew hot with talk of war.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.12: 'tac chrutvā nāradoktena rājan sañjāta-manyavaḥ'; VP 5.35: 'their wrath was kindled against Duryodhana and his associates, and they prepared to take up arms against them'.

DKS_0283.notes: Faithful to SB 10.68.1-12 following the BP chief-list; VP variant (Bhishma/Drona among pursuers) correctly noted in tradition_note.

statements.claim: Narada, astonished that Krishna with a single body had married so many women, came to Dwaraka to see it for himself.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.1-2: 'citraṃ bataitad ekena vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak... ity utsuko dvāravatīṃ devarṣir draṣṭum āgamat'.

statements.claim: Dwaraka was adorned with nine hundred thousand palaces of crystal and silver, with well-laid roads, squares and marketplaces.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.4-5: 'prāsāda-lakṣair navabhir juṣṭāṃ sphāṭika-rājataiḥ / vibhakta-rathyā-patha-catvarāpaṇaiḥ śālā-sabhābhī rucirāṃ surālayaiḥ'.

statements.claim: The inner quarter held sixteen thousand mansions of coral pillars and beryl floors, canopies hung with pearls, jewel lamps dispelling darkness, peacocks on the roofs, and maidservants in gold necklaces and fine robes.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.7-11: 'ṣoḍaśabhiḥ sadma-sahasraiḥ... viṣṭabdhaṃ vidruma-stambhair vaidūrya-phalakottamaiḥ / vitānair... muktā-dāma-vilambibhiḥ / dāsībhir niṣka-kaṇṭhībhiḥ su-vāsobhir alaṅkṛtam / ratna-pradīpa-nikara-dyutibhir nirasta-dhvāntaṃ vicitra-valabhīṣu śikhaṇḍino'.

statements.claim: In the first mansion Narada saw Krishna on a couch fanned by Rukmini; the Lord rose, bowed, seated the sage, washed his feet and took that water on his own head, then asked what he might do for him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.12-15: wife fanning him with a gold-handled chowrie; 'sahasotthita... ānamya pāda-yugalaṃ śirasā... sāñjalir avīviśad āsane sve / tasyāvanijya caraṇau tad-apaḥ sva-mūrdhnā bibhraj... prāha prabho bhagavate karavāma he kim'. The first queen is identified as Rukmini in the standard expanded telling (Krishna Book, ch. 69) and the pack lists Rukmini among the event's characters.

statements.claim: Narada praised Krishna — friendship to all beings, restraint toward the wicked, a free descent for the world's good — and asked that he might always remember the Lord's feet, the refuge of those fallen in the well of the world.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.16-17: 'maitrī janeṣu sakaleṣu damaḥ khalānām... svairāvatāra urugāya... dṛṣṭaṃ tavāṅghri-yugalaṃ janatāpavargaṃ... saṃsāra-kūpa-patitottaraṇāvalambaṃ dhyāyaṃś carāmy anugṛhāṇa yathā smṛtiḥ syāt'.

statements.claim: Palace by palace Narada saw Krishna at once playing dice with a wife and Uddhava (asked 'when did you arrive?' as if unaware), cuddling small children, pouring oblations in the five great sacrifices, at twilight japa, riding horses/elephants/chariots, counselling ministers including Uddhava, giving adorned cows to brahmanas, laughing at a jest with his beloved, meditating alone on the Person beyond nature, warring and making peace, performing weddings and thread ceremonies of his children, worshipping the gods, and hunting on a Sindhu horse.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.18-34: 'dīvyantam akṣais tatrāpi priyayā coddhavena ca / pṛṣṭaś cāviduṣevāsau kadāyāto bhavān iti / lālayantaṃ sutān śiśūn / juhvantaṃ ca vitānāgnīn yajantaṃ pañcabhir makhaiḥ / sandhyām upāsīnaṃ japantaṃ brahma vāg-yatam / aśvair gajai rathaiḥ... vicarantaṃ / mantrayantaṃ... mantribhiś coddhavādibhiḥ / dadataṃ gāḥ sv-alaṅkṛtāḥ / hasantaṃ hāsa-kathayā... priyayā / dhyāyantam ekam āsīnaṃ puruṣaṃ prakṛteḥ param / kurvantaṃ vigrahaṃ kaiścit sandhiṃ cānyatra / prasthāpanopanayanair apatyānāṃ mahotsavān / yajantaṃ sakalān devān... / carantaṃ mṛgayāṃ... hayam āruhya saindhavam'.

statements.claim: In every mansion Krishna was wholly present, and in none was he diminished; each greeted the sage with complete attention.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.35 ('avyakta-lingaṃ prakṛtiṣv antaḥ-pura-gṛhādiṣu') and the repeated greeting motif of v20-22; pack excerpt: 'saw Krishna everywhere at once... in each of the 16,000 mansions'.

statements.claim: Narada laughed, said he knew Krishna's yoga-maya, which even clever illusionists cannot see, and asked leave to wander the worlds flooded with Krishna's glory.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.36-38: 'nāradaḥ prahasann iva / vidāma yoga-māyās te durdarśā api māyinām / anujānīhi māṃ deva lokāṃs te yaśasāplutān'; Krishna's assent and bidding him wander is the following canonical event (corpus chain next title).

DKS_0284.notes: Closely follows SB 10.69.1-38; each household activity maps to its verse. Rukmini's identification in the first palace is standard in the tradition (Krishna Book) and consistent with the pack's character list.

statements.claim: Narada, having heard reports of Dwaraka, came to see Krishna's city and household for himself, walking among the palaces of Krishna's sixteen thousand queens and finding Krishna present and fully engaged in every palace.
statements.evidence: Corpus chain: previous story DKS_0284 (SB 10.69.1-35, evt_0257) — 'Narada Sees Krishna in Every Palace of Dvaraka... simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.'

statements.claim: Narada declared he now understood Krishna's yoga-maya, which even the masters of illusion cannot see, revealed to him through serving Krishna's feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.37 'vidāma yoga-māyās te durdarśā api māyinām'; pack excerpt: 'I understand your yoga-maya, hard to see even for the master of maya, revealed to me by serving your feet'.

statements.claim: Krishna was following the path of men in Dwaraka — living a mortal king's life — while carrying the power that upholds all worlds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.43 'evaṁ manuṣya-padavīm anuvartamāno nārāyaṇo 'khila-bhavāya gṛhīta-śaktiḥ' (Narayana following the path of men, having assumed power for the good of all).

statements.claim: Krishna bade Narada wander the worlds singing of his pastimes, and the telling of them purifies whoever hears.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Krishna bade him roam the worlds singing his purifying pastimes'; SB 10.69.38 (Narada seeks leave to flood the worlds with Krishna's glory); 10.69.44 'yo gāyati śṛṇoty anumodate... bhaktir bhaved bhagavati hy apavarga-mārge'.

statements.claim: Narada departed and went singing through the worlds, and those who sing of, hear of, or delight in these deeds turn toward the path of liberation.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Narada departed remembering him'; SB 10.69.44 ties singing/hearing/delighting to devotion on the path of liberation (apavarga-mārga).

statements.claim: The scenes of Krishna at ease with ministers, listening to singers, beside queens at lamps, and laughing with children are the ordinary texture of his Dwaraka days.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric elaboration of Krishna's simultaneous presence in each palace (corpus chain DKS_0284); generic domestic vignettes, no independent factual assertion.

DKS_0285.notes: All event claims (yoga-maya declaration, command to roam and sing, departure) directly supported by SB 10.69.36-44 excerpt and verses; multi-palace simultaneity carried by corpus chain DKS_0284.

statements.claim: The birds of Dwaraka sang at dawn like bards awakening Krishna.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.1 'vayāṁsy aroruvan kṛṣṇaṁ bodhayantīva vandinaḥ' (the birds cried out, awakening Krishna as it were, like bards).

statements.claim: In the brahma-muhurta, Rukmini lay awake beside Krishna and could not bear the coming moment (the end of their night together).
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.2 'muhūrtaṁ taṁ tu vaidarbhī nāmṛṣyad ati-śobhanam' (Vaidarbhi/Rukmini could not endure that most beautiful moment); 10.70.3 'brāhme muhūrta utthāya vāry upaspṛśya mādhavaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna rose in the brahma-muhurta, touched water, and meditated on the one self-effulgent reality that is secondless, immutable, and free of all impurity.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.3-4 'ekaṁ svayaṁ-jyotir ananyam avyayaṁ... nitya-nirasta-kalmaṣam'.

statements.claim: He bathed in clear water according to rite, put on fresh garments, performed the sandhya worship and fed the sacred fire while keeping his speech still.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.5 'athāpluto 'mbhasy amale yathā-vidhi... cakāra sandhyopagamādi... hutānalo brahma jajāpa vāg-yataḥ'.

statements.claim: He saluted the rising sun and offered the first worship of the day to his own senses.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.6 'upasthāyārkam udyantaṁ tarpayitvātmanaḥ kalāḥ' (worshiped the rising sun, gratifying his own senses). The story's gloss ('asking them to serve him rather than rule him') is interpretive.

statements.claim: Every day Krishna gave away herds of milk-giving cows with horns of gold, hooves of silver, strung with pearls, together with linen and sesame.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.7-8 'dhenūnāṁ rukma-śṛṅgīnāṁ sādhvīnāṁ mauktika-srajām... dadau rūpya-khurāgrāṇāṁ kṣaumājina-tilaiḥ saha'.

statements.claim: He honored the cows, brahmanas, gods, elders, teachers, and every living being, then adorned himself, ornament of the human world.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.9-10 'go-vipra-devatā-vṛddha-gurūn bhūtāni sarvaśaḥ... ātmānaṁ bhūṣayām āsa nara-loka-vibhūṣaṇam'.

statements.claim: He looked into the mirror at the auspicious objects — clarified butter, cows and bulls, brahmanas, images of the gods — and gave garlands, betel leaf and unguents to the brahmanas.
