DKS_0469.notes: The pack's prose passage is a duplicate of the MBh 7.147 passage used for DKS_0468 (Bhima-carless episode) and does not itself contain the quoted speech; the pack excerpt is clearly the intended evidence for this event and matches the story's quotations verbatim. Per instructions, the excerpt/summary reading was treated as authoritative.

statements.claim: At night Duryodhana reproached Karna and Drona: the battle had been set on foot by them in rage after the ruler of the Sindhus fell to Arjuna's arrows; they watched the slaughter of his army with indifference though competent to vanquish it; they had told him 'We two shall vanquish the sons of Pandu,' and had they said otherwise he would never have provoked these hostilities.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 (pack passage, near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Pierced by the goad of his speech, Karna and Drona went back into battle like snakes vexed with sticks; the Pandavas united and advanced with all their troops.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage.

statements.claim: Drona pierced Satyaki with ten arrows, Karna with ten more, Duryodhana with seven, Vrishasena with ten and Suvala's son with seven, so that the grandson of Sini stood in an impervious wall of Kauravas.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage: 'Drona... pierced (Satyaki)... with ten arrows. And Karna pierced him with ten arrows, and thy son with seven, and Vrishasena pierced him with ten, and Suvala's son with seven. In that impervious wall of Kauravas around the grandson of Sini...'

statements.claim: The Somakas pierced Drona from every side with showers of arrows, and Drona, enraged, began taking the lives of Kshatriyas like the sun destroying darkness with his rays.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage.

statements.claim: A loud uproar rose among the Panchalas; some abandoned sons, fathers, brothers, uncles and kinsmen and fled, some ran senseless at Drona himself; that night the Pandava host fled throwing down blazing torches in the very sight of Bhima, Arjuna, Krishna, the twins, Yudhishthira and Dhrishtadyumna; only the light among the Kaurava troops showed where the fugitives ran; Drona and Karna pursued the flying host scattering shafts.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Krishna, becoming cheerless, told Arjuna that Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki with the Panchalas had gone against Drona and Karna, that the host was broken and routed and could not be rallied, and urged: 'Seeing the host fly away through fear — you Pandava warriors, cast away your fears! With all the forces arrayed in good order, the two of us, with uplifted weapons, are even now proceeding against Drona and the son of the Suta, to withstand them.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage and pack excerpt (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Krishna then pointed out Bhima advancing against Drona and Karna, surrounded by the Somakas and Pandavas, and told Arjuna to fight, supported by Bhima and the many mighty car-warriors, to assure all his troops.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna and Krishna approached Drona and Karna and took their station at the head of battle; the vast force of Yudhishthira saw them and returned to the fight; at dead of night a fierce encounter took place like two oceans swelling at moonrise; the Kaurava warriors threw away their blazing lamps and fought fearlessly and madly under gloom and dust.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage (near-verbatim).

DKS_0470.notes: Rendering tracks MBh 7.172 almost verbatim throughout, including both of Krishna's rallying speeches. Closing line ('Krishna was looking past Drona and Karna... at a time that had not come yet') is foreshadowing connective.

statements.claim: Karna struck Dhrishtadyumna on the chest with ten shafts that pierced to the very vitals, and Dhrishtadyumna pierced him back with five, crying 'Wait! Wait!'; the two shrouded each other with showers of arrows from bows drawn to their fullest stretch.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 (pack passage, near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Karna despatched Dhrishtadyumna's driver and four steeds to Yama's abode, cut his foremost bow with keen arrows and felled his driver with a broad-headed shaft; Dhrishtadyumna, deprived of car, steeds and driver, jumped down, took up a mace and, though struck by Karna's straight shafts, approached and slew Karna's four steeds.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage.

statements.claim: Dhrishtadyumna climbed onto Arjuna's car and would have gone back at Karna, but Yudhishthira bade him desist.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage: 'quickly ascended the car of Dhananjaya... desired to proceed towards Karna. Dharma's son (Yudhishthira), however, bade him desist.'

statements.claim: Karna mingled leonine shouts with his bow's twang and blew his conch with great force; the Panchalas and Somakas, seeing their prince vanquished, rushed at him making death itself their goal; Karna's driver had yoked fresh steeds, white as conchs, of the Sindhu breed, well-broken and swift, and Karna afflicted the Panchala warriors like a cloud pouring rain on a mountain, so that the Panchala host fled like a doe frightened by a lion.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: With razor-faced arrows Karna cut off the arms of flying combatants and heads decked with ear-rings, and cut the thighs of men on elephants, horses and the earth; many fled without feeling the loss of their limbs, took the motion of a straw for Karna, and fled from their own friends mistaking them for him; Karna pursued the broken retreating host shooting shafts on all sides.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, beholding his army flying, told Arjuna that Karna stood there like Rudra armed with his bow, scorching everything like the blazing sun at dead of night, that the wails were the cries of their helpless friends mangled by his shafts, that he aimed and loosed with no interval between the acts, and asked Arjuna to do what should next be done about the slaughter of Karna, 'for the time may have come.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna told Krishna that the son of Dharma was frightened by Karna's prowess, that the army was flying broken and mangled by Drona's shafts and frightened by Karna, that he could not bear seeing Karna careering fearlessly (like a snake that cannot bear the tread of a man), and asked to be taken to Karna: 'I will either kill him — or let him slay me.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim, including the snake simile and 'I will either kill him... or let him slay me').

statements.claim: Krishna held Arjuna back: he beheld Karna careering like the chief of the celestials himself and there was none else who could stand against him, but the time had not come for Arjuna to encounter the son of the Suta, for the blazing dart given by Vasava (Indra) was still with him, still unused; instead Krishna commanded Ghatotkacha, Hidimva's son: 'Slay Karna in battle, at this dead of night.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 7.173): 'I behold Karna, O son of Kunti... I do not, however... regard the time to have come... for thee to encounter the Suta's son in battle. The blazing dart... given him by Vasava, is still with him... Let the mighty Ghatotkacha proceed against the son of Radha.' ... 'addressed Hidimva's son... "Slay Karna in battle, at this dead [of night]."' The purpose — that the dart be spent on Ghatotkacha before Arjuna ever meets Karna — is the pack summary's own reading.

DKS_0471.notes: Rendering is near-verbatim to the pack's MBh 7.173 passage through Yudhishthira's and Arjuna's speeches and Krishna's reply (the pack passage truncates at 'there is none else'; the excerpt completes Krishna's speech and the command to Ghatotkacha). The 'pierced to the very vitals' phrasing slightly strengthens the source's 'capable of penetrating into the very vitals' — immaterial to the outcome, not flagged.

statements.claim: Krishna saw Bhima being assailed/overwhelmed by the Rakshasa Alayudha and rode to Ghatotkacha instead of to Bhima's aid
statements.evidence: Pack 7.178: 'Seeing Bhima in that battle assailed by the cannibal, Vasudeva, approaching Ghatotkacha, said unto him these words.'

statements.claim: Alayudha was brother of Vaka, and Vaka had been slain by Bhima years before (grudge backstory)
statements.evidence: Pack calls Alayudha 'that prince of cannibals and brother of Vaka'; the Vaka-slain-by-Bhima backstory is canonical corpus background (7.181 pack: 'Hidimva and Vaka and Kirmira have all been slain by Bhimasena') rather than this pack's passage.

statements.claim: Ghatotkacha, Bhima's son by Hidimva, was fighting Karna that night
statements.evidence: Passage calls him 'the son of Hidimva'/'mighty son of Bhimasena' and Krishna tells him 'Abandoning Karna for the present, quickly slay Alayudha… Thou can afterwards slay Karna.'

statements.claim: Krishna's order: abandon Karna, slay Alayudha first, Karna afterwards — Ghatotkacha obeyed and met Alayudha
statements.evidence: Quoted verbatim in passage: 'Behold… Bhima is violently assailed by the Rakshasa in battle… Abandoning Karna for the present, quickly slay Alayudha…' followed by 'the valiant Ghatotkacha, abandoning Karna, encountered Alayudha'.

statements.claim: While they duelled: Satyaki, Nakula, Sahadeva pierced Alayudha's Rakshasa warriors with arrows; Arjuna overthrew Kshatriyas
statements.evidence: 'the mighty car-warrior Yuyudhana, and Nakula, and Sahadeva, pierced with keen shafts the warriors of Alayudha…'; 'the diadem-decked Vibhatsu… began to overthrow many foremost of Kshatriyas.'

statements.claim: Karna fell on the Panchalas under Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandin; Bhima rushed at Karna; Nakula/Sahadeva/Satyaki joined; Panchalas faced Drona
statements.evidence: 'Karna… agitated many kings and many mighty car-warriors amongst the Panchalas headed by Dhrishtadyumna and Sikhandin… Bhima… rushed speedily towards Karna… Nakula and Sahadeva and Satyaki… proceeded to that place where the Suta's son was… while the Panchalas encountered Drona.'

statements.claim: Alayudha struck Ghatotkacha on the head with a gigantic iron club (Parigha); Ghatotkacha sat down motionless, then shook it off
statements.evidence: 'Alayudha… struck Ghatotkacha… on the head, with a gigantic Parigha. With the stroke… he seemed to be in a state of partial swoon and sat down motionless. Recovering consciousness… he hurled at his foe a gold-decked mace adorned with a hundred bells and looking like a blazing fire' which 'crushed into pieces the steeds, the driver, and the loud-rattling car of Alayudha.'

statements.claim: Alayudha used illusion — shower of blood, black clouds with lightning, thunder — destroyed by Ghatotkacha's own illusion; shower of stones met by shower of arrows
statements.evidence: 'Relying on his illusion, he poured a copious shower of blood. The sky then seemed to be overspread with a mass of black clouds adorned with flashes of lightning… Ghatotkacha, soaring aloft, destroyed it by means of his own illusion… he began to pour a heavy shower of stones… Ghatotkacha dispelled by means of a shower of arrows.'

statements.claim: They exchanged weapons, tore up trees (sami, pilu, champaka, banian, peepul) and hurled mountain-summits; like the old combat of Vali and Sugriva
statements.evidence: Passage lists 'Parighas and spears and maces…' and 'trees such as Sami and Pilu… banian and peepul' plus 'mountain-summits'; 'the battle… was… like that in days of old… between Vali and Sugriva.'

statements.claim: The two giants seized each other by the hair; Ghatotkacha whirled Alayudha down and cut off his head, lifting it by the earrings, and roared
statements.evidence: 'those two gigantic warriors… seized each other by the hair… whirling the Rakshasa on high and dashing him down, Hidimva's son cut off his large head. Then taking that head decked with a pair of ear-rings, the mighty Ghatotkacha uttered a loud roar.'

statements.claim: Panchalas and Pandavas answered with leonine shouts, drums and conches; the torchlit night declared the Pandavas' victory
statements.evidence: 'the Panchalas and the Pandavas began to utter leonine shouts… beat and blew thousands of drums and ten thousands of conchs. That night then clearly indicated the victory of the Pandavas. Illumined with torches all around…'

statements.claim: 'By the light of a thousand torches' night battle and Alayudha taller than his chariot
statements.evidence: Atmosphere: pack confirms torchlit night battle and giant combatants, not the specific comparisons.

DKS_0472.notes: Faithful retelling of MBh 7.178; no unsupported or contradicted factual claims.

statements.claim: Pandavas grieved over Ghatotkacha's body lying like a riven mountain; only Krishna showed delight
statements.evidence: 'Beholding Hidimva's son slain and lying like a riven mountain, all the Pandavas became filled with grief… Only Vasudeva filled with transports of delight, began to utter leonine shouts.'

statements.claim: Ghatotkacha was slain by the dart Karna had saved/intended for Arjuna
statements.evidence: Passage: the dart given by Sakra 'has slain Ghatotkacha'; 'Vrisha, having obtained it, had always regarded thee as slain in battle.'

statements.claim: Troops began to fly in panic at Ghatotkacha's fall
statements.evidence: Arjuna's words in passage: 'Our troops are flying away, beholding Ghatotkacha slain.'

statements.claim: Krishna embraced Arjuna, tied the steeds, roared, danced like a tree shaken by a tempest, slapped his armpits, shouted from the chariot terrace
statements.evidence: 'uttering loud shouts he embraced Arjuna. Tying the steeds and uttering loud roars, he began to dance in a transport of joy, like a tree shaken by a tempest… repeatedly slapping his own armpits… standing on the terrace of the car.'

statements.claim: Arjuna rebuked the joy as unfit for an occasion of sorrow, comparing it to the drying up of the ocean or Meru learning to move
statements.evidence: 'thou showest great joy at a time scarcely fit for it… This lightness of heart… seems to me like the drying up of the ocean or the locomotion of Meru.'

statements.claim: Krishna's reply: 'Karna, his dart being baffled through Ghatotkacha, is already slain in battle.'
statements.evidence: Quoted verbatim in passage.

statements.claim: No man could stand before Karna armed with that dart, looking like Kartikeya in battle
statements.evidence: 'The man does not exist in this world that could not stay before Karna armed with that dart and looking like Kartikeya in battle.'

statements.claim: With his natural armour and ear-rings Karna could singly vanquish the three worlds; neither Indra (Vasava), Varuna nor Yama would approach him; even Arjuna with Gandiva or Krishna with the Sudarshana discus could not conquer him
statements.evidence: 'could singly vanquish the three worlds with the very gods. Neither Vasava, nor Varuna… nor Yama, could venture to approach him… neither thyself, bending the Gandiva, nor myself, uplifting my discus, called Sudarsana, could vanquish him in battle.'

statements.claim: Armour, ear-rings, and the dart were successively taken away; Karna called Vaikartana because he cut off and gave his natural armour and ear-rings to Sakra for the dart
statements.evidence: 'By good luck, his (natural) armour had been taken away. By good luck, his earrings also had been taken away. By good luck, his infallible dart also is now baffled, through Ghatotkacha… because Karna, cutting off his (natural) armour and his brilliant ear-rings, gave them unto Sakra, it is for that he came to be called Vaikartana.'

statements.claim: Stripped of armour, ear-rings and the dart, Karna is 'like a man' — like a snake stupefied by incantation or a fire of mild flames
statements.evidence: 'Karna now seems to me to be like an angry snake of virulent poison stupefied by power of incantation, or like a fire of mild flames… Deprived, however, of his armour… and divested also of the dart given him by Vasava, Karna is now like a man (and no longer like a god).'

statements.claim: Karna's virtues (devotion to Brahmanas, truthfulness, penances, kindness even to foes) earned him the name Vrisha; he could not be vanquished by the gods themselves
statements.evidence: 'Devoted to Brahmanas, truthful in speech, engaged in penances, observant of vows, kind even unto foes, for these reasons Karna is called Vrisha… He is incapable of being vanquished in battle by the gods.'

statements.claim: Krishna foretold one opportunity: when Karna's car-wheels sink in the earth Arjuna should slay him; Krishna would make a sign beforehand
statements.evidence: 'There will occur one opportunity for his slaughter. When his car-wheels will sink in the earth… thou shouldst slay him in that distressful situation. I will make thee a sign beforehand.'

statements.claim: Closing interpretation: Ghatotkacha's death spent the weapon meant for Arjuna and Krishna danced seeing Arjuna alive and Karna now mortal
statements.evidence: Synthesis of the passage's explicit statements ('his dart being baffled through Ghatotkacha, is already slain in battle'); framing, not new facts.

DKS_0473.notes: Close paraphrase of MBh 7.180 including long quoted speeches; no unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Setting: on the night of the fleeing troops Krishna answered Arjuna's question how Jarasandha and the others were slain
statements.evidence: Passage opens with Arjuna's question: 'How, O Janardana, for our good, and by what means, were those lords of the earth, viz., Jarasandha and the others, slain?' and closes 'Thy troops also are flying away on all sides.'

statements.claim: Had Jarasandha, the Chedi ruler (Sisupala), and the Nishada king's son (Ekalavya) lived, Duryodhana would have chosen them; hostile to the Pandavas, they would have joined the Kauravas and protected Dhritarashtra's sons; with Karna they could have conquered the whole earth
statements.evidence: 'If Jarasandha, and the ruler of the Chedis, and the mighty son of the Nishada king, had not been slain, they would have become terrible. Without doubt, Duryodhana would have chosen those… they would all have adopted the side of the Kauravas… the Suta's son, and Jarasandha, and the ruler of the Chedis, and the son of the Nishada… would have succeeded in conquering the whole earth.'

statements.claim: Without means even the gods could not conquer them; each could fight the whole celestial host protected by the Regents
statements.evidence: 'without the employment of means, the very gods could not have conquered them in battle. Each of them… could fight in battle with the whole celestial host protected by the Regents of the world.'

statements.claim: Jarasandha's mace: hurled when assailed by Balarama (Valadeva), blazing like fire, parting the sky like the line parting a woman's tresses, with the impetus of Indra's thunder
statements.evidence: 'assailed by Valadeva, Jarasandha… hurled for our destruction a mace capable of slaying all creatures. Endued with the splendour of fire, that mace coursed towards us dividing the welkin like the line on the head that parts the tresses of a woman… with the impetuosity of the thunder hurled by Sakra.'

statements.claim: Balarama baffled the mace with the weapon Sthunakarna; the mace fell, splitting the earth and making mountains tremble, slaying the Rakshasa woman Jara with her son and kinsmen
statements.evidence: 'the son of Rohini hurled the weapon called Sthunakarna for baffling it… that mace fell down on the earth, splitting her… making the very mountains tremble… That Rakshasa woman… was slain with her son and kinsmen by means of that mace and the weapon of Sthunakarna.'

statements.claim: Jara had joined the two halves of the child, hence the name Jarasandha
statements.evidence: 'Jarasandha had been made up of two halves of one child. And because it was Jara that had united those two halves, it was for this that he came to be called Jarasandha.'

statements.claim: Deprived of his mace, Jarasandha was slain by Bhimasena in Arjuna's presence; armed with the mace, even the gods with Indra could not have slain him
statements.evidence: 'Deprived of his mace in that great battle, Jarasandha was afterwards slain by Bhimasena in thy presence… If the valiant Jarasandha had stood armed with his mace, the very gods with Indra at their head could not have slain him in battle.'

statements.claim: Ekalavya was deprived of his thumb by Drona by guile, Drona posing as his preceptor
statements.evidence: 'for thy good, the Nishada's son also… was, by an act of guile, deprived of his thumb by Drona, assuming the position of his preceptor.'

statements.claim: With fingers cased in leathern gloves Ekalavya shone like a second Rama; undeprived of his thumb he was invincible to gods, Danavas, Rakshasas and Uragas, able to shoot day and night
statements.evidence: 'with fingers cased in leathern gloves, looked resplendent like a second Rama. Undeprived of thumb, Ekalavya… was incapable of being vanquished in battle by the gods, the Danavas, the Rakshasas, and the Uragas… capable of shooting incessantly day and night.'

statements.claim: 'For your good, he was slain by me on the field of battle' — Krishna claims Ekalavya's battlefield death
statements.evidence: Passage: 'For thy good, he was slain by me on the field of battle.'

statements.claim: Sisupala, the Chedi ruler, was invincible to gods and Asuras together and was slain by Krishna before Arjuna's eyes; Krishna was born to slay him
statements.evidence: 'Endued with great prowess, the ruler of the Chedis was slain by me before thy eyes. He also was incapable of being vanquished in battle by the gods and the Asuras together. I was born to slay him as also the other enemies of the gods, with thy assistance…'

statements.claim: Hidimva, Vaka and Kirmira — Rakshasas of might equal to Ravana's, destroyers of Brahmanas and sacrifices — were slain by Bhimasena; Alayudha by Hidimva's son
statements.evidence: 'Hidimva and Vaka and Kirmira have all been slain by Bhimasena. All those Rakshasas were endued with might equal to that Ravana and all of them were destroyers of Brahmanas and sacrifices… Alayudha… had been slain by Hidimva's son.'

statements.claim: Krishna slew Ghatotkacha by means, through Karna's dart; had Karna not, Krishna would have had to slay him himself
statements.evidence: 'Hidimva's son also, I have slain by the employment of means, viz., through Karna with his dart. If Karna had not slain him with his dart in great battle, I myself would have had to slay Bhima's son Ghatotkacha.'

statements.claim: Ghatotkacha was inimical to Brahmanas and sacrifices and of sinful soul; by his death Indra's dart was rendered futile
statements.evidence: 'That Rakshasa was inimical to Brahmanas and sacrifices. Because he was a destroyer of sacrifices and of a sinful soul, therefore hath he been thus slain… by that act as a means, the dart given by Sakra, hath also been rendered futile.'

statements.claim: Krishna's vow: destroyers of righteousness are all slayable by him; he remains wherever the Vedas, truth, restraint and the rest abide
statements.evidence: 'they that are destroyers of righteousness are all slayable by me. Even that is the vow made by me, for establishing righteousness. Whither the Vedas and truth and self-restraint… thither I myself always remain.'

statements.claim: Krishna promised the means to slay Karna and that Vrikodara (Bhima) would slay Suyodhana (Duryodhana)
statements.evidence: 'Thou needst not be at all anxious about Karna's slaughter. I will tell you the means by which you will slay him. Vrikodara also will succeed in slaying Suyodhana.'

DKS_0474.notes: Very close to MBh 7.181 passage; tradition_note already flags the epic-specific Ekalavya variant the story follows. No unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Karna carried the dart through the war without ever hurling it at Arjuna, and Krishna explained why to Satyaki (Yuyudhana)
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (7.181): 'I, however, O foremost of warriors, always used to stupefy the son of Radha. It was for this that he did not hurl the dart at Pandu's son.'

statements.claim: Scene-setting: Krishna spoke 'as the night's uproar died down'
statements.evidence: Transitional framing; the underlying 7.181 passage has the uproar increasing ('the uproar made by the hostile army is increasing. Thy troops also are flying away'), which the story itself restates correctly later. Minor connective inconsistency, not a factual assertion about the source.

statements.claim: Indra gave Karna the dart long ago in exchange for his natural armour and ear-rings; it was meant for Arjuna and never failed
statements.evidence: Corroborated in the corpus chain's 7.180 passage (DKS_0473 pack): 'Sakra gave that dart unto Karna in exchange for the latter's ear-rings and celestial armour… Vrisha, having obtained it, had always regarded thee as slain in battle.'

statements.claim: The secret was that Krishna always stupefied Karna so the dart was never hurled at Arjuna
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'always used to stupefy the son of Radha. It was for this that he did not hurl the dart at Pandu's son.'

statements.claim: Elaboration that the moment of the throw came many times and each time slipped away before the Pandavas knew
statements.evidence: Consistent dramatisation of the stupefaction claim; supported by 7.183 (DKS_0476 pack) where nightly resolutions to hurl the dart were forgotten by morning.

statements.claim: Krishna valued Arjuna (Vibhatsu) above his sire, mother, brothers and his very life
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'I do not regard my sire, my mother, yourselves, my brothers—ay, my very life—so worthy of protection as Vibhatsu in battle.'

statements.claim: Krishna's dance was because he beheld Dhananjaya alive, 'like one returned from the dead'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Beholding Dhananjaya, therefore, like one returned from the dead, these transports of delight, O Yuyudhana, have seized me.'

statements.claim: Armour, ear-rings and dart were each stripped away in turn; the dart was spent through Ghatotkacha
statements.evidence: Synthesis of the 7.180/7.181 material (each loss is stated in the corpus packs); presentational summary rather than new claim.

statements.claim: Final image: Karna unaware the weapon was gone, stripped of armour and 'charm', now mortal
statements.evidence: Close of the 7.180 statement that Karna 'is now like a man (and no longer like a god)'; rhetorical flourish.

DKS_0475.notes: Mostly a direct gloss of the 7.181 excerpt quoted in the pack's index entry. The one scene-timing phrase ('uproar died down') is connective and self-corrected later in the same story; not counted as contradicted.

statements.claim: The dart could slay any one person, could not be borne or baffled even by the gods, and was saved for Krishna or Arjuna
statements.evidence: Dhritarashtra in pack: 'that dart could always slay one person in battle, and… it was incapable of being either borne or baffled by the very gods with Vasava at their head… was it not hurled by Karna at Devaki's son, or Phalguna'.

statements.claim: The dart was spent on Ghatotkacha, son of Bhima and the Rakshasa princess Hidimba; Dhritarashtra would call that death as insignificant as the crushing of straw
statements.evidence: 'Vasava's dart is lost, having effected the slaughter of Ghatotkacha who was as insignificant as straw.'

statements.claim: Kaurava troops, filled with joy, shouted in the dark night and fell impetuously on the Pandava ranks
statements.evidence: 'Upon the slaughter, that night… of the Rakshasa, Ghatotkacha, by Karna, thy troops, filled with joy, uttered loud shouts. In that dark hour of the night, they fell impetuously upon the Pandava troops and began to slay them.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, cheerless, ordered Bhima to resist the Dhartarashtra host, saying a great stupefaction overwhelmed him, then sat down on his car, tearful, sighing, staring at Karna's prowess
statements.evidence: 'resist the Dhritarashtra host. In consequence of the slaughter of Hidimva's son, a great stupefaction overwhelms me.' Having ordered Bhimasena thus, he sat down on his car. With tearful face and sighing repeatedly, the king became exceedingly cheerless at the sight of Karna's prowess.

statements.claim: Krishna's counsel: grief and cheerlessness do not become the chief of the Bharatas; 'Rise, O king, and fight… If cheerlessness overtakes thee, our victory becomes uncertain.'
statements.evidence: Quoted verbatim in pack excerpt and passage.

statements.claim: Yudhishthira wiped his eyes and answered that the excellent path of duty was not unknown to him
statements.evidence: 'Dharma's son, Yudhishthira, wiping his eyes with his hands, replied… the excellent path of duty is not unknown to me.'

statements.claim: Ghatotkacha's services: while the Pandavas lived in the woods, though a mere child, he came to Yudhishthira at Kamyaka when Arjuna left for weapons and dwelt with them till Dhananjaya's return
statements.evidence: 'Whilst we were living in the woods the high-souled son of Hidimva, although then a mere child did us many services… Learning that Partha… had departed for the acquisition of weapons, that great bowman… came to me at Kamyaka. He dwelt with us till Dhananjaya's reappearance.'

statements.claim: Ghatotkacha carried the tired princess of Panchala (Draupadi) on his back over inaccessible fastnesses; his feats showed skill in all modes of warfare
statements.evidence: 'Whilst proceeding over many inaccessible fastnesses, he himself carried on his back the tired princess of Panchala. The feats he achieved… show that he was skilled in all modes of warfare.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira's affection for Ghatotkacha was twice what he bore Sahadeva; the boy was devoted to him and dear to him
statements.evidence: 'My affection for Ghatotkacha… is twice that… which I naturally bear towards Sahadeva. That mighty-armed one was devoted to me. I was dear to him and he was dear to me.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira pointed to troops afflicted and routed by the Kauravas and car-warriors broken before Karna's shafts
statements.evidence: 'Behold… our troops afflicted and routed by the Kauravas. Behold, those mighty car-warriors broken before Karna's shafts.'

statements.claim: Closing reflection that Krishna waited, letting the grief speak itself out, and the counsel was the first step of bearing the burden
statements.evidence: Interpretive close consistent with Krishna's speech; no new factual assertions.

DKS_0476.notes: Verbatim-faithful to MBh 7.183 (Yudhishthira's grief, Krishna's counsel, the king's reply); no unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Drona caused great carnage among the Panchalas and Srinjayas; he was wrathful at the slaughter of Bhurishravas and Jayadratha
statements.evidence: Pack 7.191: 'Drona caused a great carnage among the Panchalas…'; the wrath motive appears in the corpus's 7.183 passage (DKS_0476 pack): Drona 'excited with wrath at the slaughter of Bhurisravas and Jayadratha.'

statements.claim: Panchala and Srinjaya car-warriors rushed at Drona and were slaughtered with shafts and darts; fear entered the Pandavas and they despaired of victory
statements.evidence: 'those mighty car-warriors, viz., the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, all rushed against Drona himself… were slaughtered by him with shafts and darts… fear entered the hearts of the Pandavas… the Pandavas… became hopeless of victory.'

statements.claim: None was competent even to look at Drona; Arjuna, his only match, would not fight his teacher, being conversant with morality
statements.evidence: 'There is none competent to even look at him in battle. Conversant with the ways of morality, Arjuna (who alone is a match for him) will not fight with him.'

statements.claim: Krishna's plan: Drona is invincible by force (even to the gods with Vasava) but slayable by humans once he lays aside his weapons; on Ashvatthama's fall he will cease to fight
statements.evidence: 'This foremost of all bowmen is incapable of being ever vanquished by force in battle, by the very gods with Vasava at their head. When, however, he lays aside his weapons, he becomes capable of being slain on the field even by human beings… Upon the fall of (his son) Aswatthaman he will cease to fight, I think.'

statements.claim: Krishna urged Yudhishthira: if Drona fights in rage even half a day the army will be annihilated; 'Under such circumstances, falsehood is better than truth.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'If Drona fighteth, filled with rage, for even half-a-day, I tell thee truly, thy army will then be annihilated… Under such circumstances, falsehood is better than truth.'

statements.claim: Arjuna did not approve the advice; others did; Yudhishthira accepted it with great difficulty
statements.evidence: 'This advice… was not approved by Kunti's son, Dhananjaya. Others approved of it. But Yudhishthira accepted it with great difficulty.'

statements.claim: Bhima slew a huge elephant of their own army named Ashvatthama, belonging to Indravarman, chief of the Malavas
statements.evidence: 'the mighty-armed Bhima… slew with a mace a foe-crushing, terrible and huge elephant named Aswatthaman, of his own army, belonging to Indravarman, the chief of the Malavas.'

statements.claim: Bhima, with bashfulness, exclaimed 'Ashvatthama hath been slain!', keeping the true fact within his mind
statements.evidence: 'Approaching Drona then in that battle with some bashfulness Bhimasena began to exclaim aloud, 'Aswatthaman hath been slain.'… Keeping the true fact within his mind, he said what was untrue.'

statements.claim: Drona's limbs dissolved like sands in water, but recalling his son's prowess he deemed the news false and was comforted
statements.evidence: 'Drona's limbs seemed to dissolve like sands in water. Recollecting however, the prowess of his son, he soon came to regard that intelligence as false… he became comforted.'

statements.claim: Drona rushed at Dhrishtadyumna (son of Prishata), covered him with a thousand arrows, was covered in turn by twenty thousand Panchala car-warriors
statements.evidence: 'Rushing towards the son of Prishata… he covered him with a thousand keen shafts… Then twenty thousand Panchala car-warriors of great energy covered him.'

statements.claim: Drona invoked the Brahma weapon and looked like a smokeless blazing fire; he felled Panchala heads and cut off golden-ornamented arms; Kshatriyas lay like trees uprooted by the tempest; earth grew miry with flesh and blood
statements.evidence: 'invoked into existence the Brahma weapon… Drona looked resplendent like a smokeless, blazing fire… he felled the heads of the Panchalas and cut off their massive arms… lay scattered like trees uprooted by the tempest… the earth, miry with flesh and blood, became impassable.'

statements.claim: Drona slew twenty thousand Panchala car-warriors, cut off Vasudana's head with a broad-headed arrow, slew five hundred Matsyas, six thousand elephants and ten thousand steeds
statements.evidence: 'Having slain twenty thousand Panchala car-warriors… cut off, with a broad-headed arrow, the head of Vasudana… slaying five hundred Matsyas, and six thousand elephants, he slew ten thousand steeds.'

statements.claim: The Rishis — Viswamitra, Jamadagni, Bharadwaja, Gautama, Vasishtha, Kasyapa, Atri — gathered to behold Drona, who stood as if for the extermination of the Kshatriya race
statements.evidence: 'Beholding Drona stationed on the field for the extermination of the Kshatriya race, the Rishis Viswamitra, and Jamadagni, and Bharadwaja, and Gautama, and Vasishtha, and Kasyapa, and Atri…'

statements.claim: The closing line that the rishis could not turn Drona from his course
statements.evidence: Consistent with the passage's continued slaughter (and next story's 'Krishna's stratagem had not ended Drona's fury'); the excerpt truncates before any rishi speech.

statements.claim: Opening simile of Drona as a springtime fire through dry straw
statements.evidence: Pandavas' own words in passage: Drona 'will consume us all like a raging conflagration consuming a heap of straw in the season of spring.'

DKS_0478.notes: Near-verbatim account of MBh 7.191 including the elephant deception and Drona's continuing slaughter; no unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna pointed out Yudhishthira pursued by many Dhartarashtra bowmen desiring to slay him, with the Panchalas proceeding to rescue him
statements.evidence: Pack 8.60: 'Yonder, O son of Pandu, your brother (Yudhishthira) is being pursued by many mighty and great bowmen amongst the Dhartarashtras… The mighty Pancalas… are proceeding after the high-souled Yudhishthira from desire of rescuing him.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana, king of the whole world, clad in mail with a large car force, pursued the Pandava king with his brothers, whose weapon-touch was fatal as poisonous snakes
statements.evidence: 'Duryodhana, O Partha, the king of the whole world, clad in mail and accompanied by a large car force, is pursuing the Pandava king… accompanied by his brothers, the touch of whose weapons is as fatal as that of poisonous snakes.'

statements.claim: Elephants, horses, car-warriors and foot-soldiers of the Dhartarashtras advanced to seize Yudhishthira like poor men after a precious gem
statements.evidence: 'Those Dhartarashtra elephants and horses and car-warriors and foot-soldiers are advancing to seize Yudhishthira like poor men after a precious gem.'

statements.claim: Checked for a moment by Satyaki and Bhima, they were stupefied like the Daityas seeking the Amrita made motionless by Sakra and Agni, then pressed on again like rain-season water rushing to the ocean, roaring and shaking their bows
statements.evidence: 'checked by Satyaki and Bhima, they have again been stupefied, like the Daityas, that desired to take away the Amrita, made motionless by Sakra and Agni… are again proceeding towards Yudhishthira like a vast quantity of water in the season of rains rushing towards the ocean… uttering leonine roars, blowing their conchs, and shaking their bows.'

statements.claim: Krishna regarded Yudhishthira as within the jaws of Death or poured as a libation on the sacrificial fire; even Sakra could scarcely escape the arrayed army's arrows
statements.evidence: 'I regard Kunti's son Yudhishthira… to be already within the jaws of Death or already poured as a libation on the sacrificial fire… Sakra himself, coming within the range of its arrows, can scarcely escape.'

statements.claim: The shafts of Duryodhana, Drona's son, Kripa or Karna would break down the very mountains
statements.evidence: 'The force of the heroic Duryodhana's shafts, or Drona's son's or Kripa's or Karna's would break down the very mountains.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira had once been compelled by Karna to turn his back on the field; Karna, great of might and lightness of hand, could afflict him, especially with Duryodhana
statements.evidence: 'king Yudhishthira was once compelled by Karna to turn his back upon the field. The son of Radha is endued with great might and great lightness of hand… He is competent to afflict the eldest son of Pandu in fight, specially when he is united with the mighty and brave son of Dhritarashtra.'

statements.claim: The king was emaciated from fasts, endued with Brahma-force but little Kshatriya-might; assailed by Karna he was in great peril
statements.evidence: 'The king… is exceedingly emaciated in consequence of his fasts. He is endued with Brahma-force, but the puissant one is not endued with much of Kshatriya-might. Assailed, however, by Karna… hath been placed in a situation of great peril.'

statements.claim: Krishna thought Yudhishthira had fallen, reasoning from Bhimasena coolly hearing the Dhartarashtra roars, that Pandu's son was dead
statements.evidence: 'I think, O Partha, that king Yudhishthira has fallen. Indeed, since… the wrathful Bhimasena, coolly heareth the leonine roars… I think… that Pandu's son Yudhishthira is dead.'

statements.claim: Karna urged the Dhartarashtra car-warriors against Yudhishthira with Sthunakarna, Indrasjaha and Pasupata weapons and clubs; the king's standard was no longer visible, probably struck down
statements.evidence: 'Yonder Karna urges forward the mighty car-warriors of the Dhartarashtras towards the son of Pritha with the weapons called Sthunakarna, Indrasjaha and Pasupata, and with clubs… The king's standard is no longer visible. It has probably been struck down by Karna with his shafts.'

statements.claim: In the sight of the twins, Satyaki, Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Bhima, Satanika and all Panchalas and Cedis, Karna destroyed the Pandava division like an elephant destroying lotuses; car-warriors fled and elephants fled crying
statements.evidence: 'In the very sight of the twins… and of Satyaki and Shikhandi, and Dhrishtadyumna and Bhima and Satanika… yonder Karna is destroying the Pandava division with his arrows, like an elephant destroying an assemblage of lotuses… those car-warriors of thy army… are flying away… Those elephants… are flying away… uttering cries of pain.'

statements.claim: Karna's standard bore the device of the elephant's rope and moved all over the field; he rushed against Bhimasena, routing Panchala car-warriors as Sakra routed the Daityas
statements.evidence: 'that foremost of standards, of the Suta's son, on his car, bearing the device of the elephant's rope, is seen to move all over the field. There, the son of Radha is now rushing against Bhimasena… those mighty car-warriors of the Pancalas are being routed (by Karna) even as the Daityas had been routed by Sakra.'

statements.claim: Closing exhortation: 'Righteously setting thy heart on battle, advance against that leader of car-warriors.'
statements.evidence: Final line of the pack's index excerpt.

DKS_0479.notes: Extended paraphrase of Krishna's speech in MBh 8.60; nearly every clause maps to the passage. No unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Ashvatthama, with a large car-force, suddenly proceeded to where Arjuna was; Arjuna with Krishna withstood him like a continent the surging ocean
statements.evidence: Pack 8.64: 'Drona's son, surrounded by a large car-force… suddenly proceeded to that spot where Partha was. Like the continent withstanding the surging ocean, the heroic Partha having Saurin (Krishna) for his help-mate withstood the impetuously rushing Ashvatthama.'

statements.claim: Ashvatthama covered both Arjuna and Vasudeva with shafts; onlookers wondered at the two Krishnas shrouded with arrows
statements.evidence: 'the valiant son of Drona, filled with rage, covered both Arjuna and Vasudeva with his shafts. Beholding the two Krishnas shrouded with arrows… wondered exceedingly.'

statements.claim: Arjuna, as if smiling, invoked a celestial weapon; the brahmana Ashvatthama baffled it and all weapons Arjuna sped
statements.evidence: 'Arjuna, as if smiling, invoked into existence a celestial weapon. The Brahmana Ashvatthama… baffled that weapon… all those weapons that Arjuna sped from desire of slaying the son of Drona were baffled by the latter.'

statements.claim: During the encounter Ashvatthama resembled the Destroyer with gaping mouth; he covered all points of the compass with straight arrows and pierced Vasudeva with three arrows in the right arm
statements.evidence: 'we beheld the son of Drona to resemble the Destroyer himself, with gaping mouth. Having covered all the points of the compass… with straight arrows, he pierced Vasudeva with three arrows in the right arm.'

statements.claim: Arjuna slew all of Ashvatthama's steeds, covering the earth with a river of blood; Ashvatthama's division's car-warriors were slain; Ashvatthama in turn caused a terrible river of blood flowing to Yama's domains
statements.evidence: 'Arjuna, slaying all the steeds of his high-souled assailant, caused the Earth… to be covered with a river of blood… a large number of car-warriors… belonging to the division of Ashvatthama, slain… Ashvatthama also… caused a terrible river of blood to flow there that led to Yama's domains.'

statements.claim: Ashvatthama pierced Arjuna all over and struck him cruelly at the chest with a winged arrow; Arjuna covered him with arrows and cut off his bow
statements.evidence: 'shook his formidable bow decked with gold, and then pierced him from every side with many sharp arrows… cruelly struck Arjuna, aiming at the chest, with a winged arrow… the wielder of Gandiva forcibly covered the son of Drona with showers of arrows, and then cut off his bow.'

statements.claim: Ashvatthama hurled a spiked mace like thunder; Arjuna, as if smiling, cut it off and it fell like a mountain broken by the thunderbolt
statements.evidence: 'taking up a spiked mace whose touch resembled that of thunder's, hurled it… at the diadem-decked Arjuna. The son of Pandu… suddenly cut off that spiked mace… it fell down on the Earth, like a mountain… broken into pieces, struck with the thunderbolt.'

statements.claim: Ashvatthama covered Arjuna with the Aindra weapon; Arjuna, fixing an Indra-created weapon on Gandiva, destroyed the arrowy shower and covered Ashvatthama's car; Ashvatthama pierced Krishna with a hundred shafts and Arjuna with three hundred small arrows
statements.evidence: 'Drona's son… began to cover Vibhatsu, aided by the energy of the Aindra weapon… Partha… fixing on his bowstring a mighty weapon created by Indra, destroyed that Aindra-shower of arrows… approached the latter, invoked a mighty weapon and suddenly pierced Krishna with hundred shafts and Arjuna with three hundred small arrows.'

statements.claim: Arjuna pierced Ashvatthama with a hundred arrows in his vital limbs, showered arrows on his steeds, driver and bowstring, and felled his driver with a broad-headed arrow
statements.evidence: 'Arjuna pierced the son of his preceptor with a hundred arrows in all his vital limbs… poured many arrows on the steeds and driver and the bowstring of Drona's son… felled his adversary's driver… with a broad-headed arrow.'

statements.claim: Ashvatthama himself took the reins and covered Krishna with arrows while guiding his steeds and fighting Phalguni — applauded by all the warriors
statements.evidence: 'Drona's son, however, himself taking up the reins, covered Krishna with many arrows. The activity of prowess that we then beheld… he guided his steeds while he fought with Phalguni. That feat… was applauded by all the warriors.'

statements.claim: Vibhatsu (Jaya), smiling, cut the traces of Ashvatthama's steeds with a razor-faced arrow; the steeds ran away and a loud noise arose from the troops
statements.evidence: 'Then Vibhatsu, otherwise called Jaya, smiling the while, quickly cut off the traces of Ashvatthama's steeds… with a razor-faced arrow. Already afflicted… the steeds of Drona's son thereupon ran away. Then a loud noise arose from thy troops.'

statements.claim: Arjuna asked Krishna to take him against Karna; Krishna replied that the royal son of Kunti had been deeply wounded and mangled by Karna — see and comfort him first, then slay Karna
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'The royal son of Kunti hath been deeply wounded and mangled by Karna. Having seen him first and comforted him, thou wilt then, O Partha, slay Karna.'

statements.claim: Scene close: 'the field… fell suddenly quiet' after the duel
statements.evidence: Rhetorical beat; the passage itself ends with a loud noise from the troops, so 'quiet' is a stylised pause rather than a sourced fact.

DKS_0480.notes: Detailed faithful rendering of the Arjuna–Ashvatthama duel in MBh 8.64 with Krishna's closing counsel; no unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Arjuna had just won victory over the son of Drona and searched his own troops because Yudhishthira was gone from the field
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Having vanquished the son of Drona... Dhananjaya... cast his eyes among his own troops... Not seeing his brother Yudhishthira...'

statements.claim: Bhima told Arjuna the king had left the field, his limbs scorched by Karna's shafts, and whether he still lived was doubtful
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: Bhima said, 'King Yudhishthira the just, hath gone away from this place, his limbs scorched with Karna's shafts. It is doubtful whether he still liveth!'

statements.claim: Arjuna recalled that the king had stayed in battle, pierced by Drona's arrows, expectant of victory, until Drona was slain
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'though deeply pierced by Drona with keen shafts, the king... had still stayed in battle, expectant of victory, until Drona was slain!'

statements.claim: Arjuna judged the king had gone to the camp and asked Bhima to go for news while he stayed to check the foes
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Without doubt... the king hath gone to the camp!... quickly go hence, O Bhima! I will stay here, checking all our foes!'

statements.claim: Bhima refused to go, saying heroes would call him frightened in battle, and offered to fight all the samsaptakas himself so Arjuna could go
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'If, O Arjuna, I go there, many foremost of heroes will then say that I am frightened in battle!'... 'I will fight with all the samsaptakas in battle! Therefore, O Dhananjaya, do thou go thyself!'

statements.claim: Arjuna asked Krishna to urge the steeds and leave the sea of troops so he could see king Ajatasatru
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Urge the steeds, O Hrishikesha, leaving this sea of troops! I desire, O Keshava to see king Ajatasatru!'

statements.claim: Krishna told Bhima the feat was not wonderful for him and bade him slay the assembled foes of Partha
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'This feat is not at all wonderful for thee, O Bhima! I am about to go (hence). Slay these assembled foes of Partha!'

statements.claim: Krishna drove at great speed on Garuda-like steeds to where the king lay alone on his bed; both alighted and worshipped Yudhishthira's feet
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'Then Hrishikesha proceeded with very great speed to the spot where king Yudhishthira was... borne by those steeds that resembled Garuda... approached the king who was lying alone on his bed. Both of them, alighting from that car, worshipped the feet of king Yudhishthira the just.'

statements.claim: Seeing the king safe, the two were filled with joy, and the king, thinking Karna had been slain, spoke with voice choked with delight
statements.evidence: MBh 8.65: 'the two Krishnas became filled with joy... King Yudhishthira the just, thinking that Karna had been slain, became filled with joy... addressed them in these words in a voice choked with delight.'

statements.claim: 'He was wrong' - the king's belief that Karna had fallen (narrator's comment closing the scene)
statements.evidence: The joy was based on a mistaken belief ('thinking that Karna had been slain'); corpus chain next story has the duel with Karna continuing, so Karna was not slain at this point.

DKS_0481.notes: Close, nearly verbatim rendering of MBh 8.65 dialogue and action; only the 'he was wrong' coda is editorial commentary, factually consistent with the continuing duel.

statements.claim: Arjuna and Karna, both owning white steeds, met in combat like two infuriated elephants fighting for a she-elephant
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'those two foremost of men, both owning white steeds... closed with each other like two infuriated Himalayan elephants, both of full-grown tusks, fighting... for the sake of a she-elephant in her season.'

statements.claim: They poured showers of arrows like clouds meeting clouds or mountain meeting mountain, with twanging bows and clattering car-wheels, while both armies watched
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Like a mass of clouds encountering another mass, or a mountain encountering a mountain, those two warriors, both pouring showers of arrows, encountered each other, their bows loudly twanging... and the wheels of their cars producing a deafening clatter.' Armies/welkin struck with fear: same passage.

statements.claim: Karna first pierced Arjuna with ten shafts; Arjuna pierced him in return with ten shafts in the centre of the chest
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Then Karna first pierced Partha in that encounter, with ten mighty shafts. Arjuna pierced him in return with ten keen-pointed shafts... in the centre of the chest.'

statements.claim: Limbs of the heroes, drivers and horses were mangled and blood flowed like a river whose water none would drink
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'marked by a river whose distasteful water consisted of blood, the limbs of those two heroes, as also their drivers and animals, became exceedingly mangled.'

statements.claim: Arjuna rubbed his arms and Gandiva's string and sped cloth-yard shafts, nalikas, boar's-ear-headed arrows, razors, anjalikas and crescent arrows, all cut off by Karna
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Rubbing his two arms and the string also of Gandiva... Arjuna, then sped showers of cloth-yard shafts, and Nalikas and arrows equipped with heads like boar's ears and razors, and Anjalikas, and crescent-shaped arrows... all those successive showers... were cut off by the Suta's son.'

statements.claim: Spectators raised leonine shouts and waved fingers and cloths when Arjuna rushed against Karna
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'Others among the spectators, filled with joy and uttering leonine shouts, raised their arms, waving their fingers or the pieces of cloth they held, when Arjuna rushed against the son of Adhiratha.'

statements.claim: Arjuna loosed a fiery weapon covering earth, welkin and compass points and hiding the sun; warriors' robes caught fire and they fled
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'The son of Indra then sped at Karna a fiery weapon... Covering the earth and the welkin and the ten points of the compass and the very course of the sun... The robes of all the warriors took fire, at which they fled away.'

statements.claim: Karna quenched the conflagration with the varunastra - clouds dark as mountains flooded the field and the fire was quenched in a trice
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'the Suta's son Karna... shot... the varunastra for quenching it... Those clouds whose extremities presented the aspect of mountains, surrounding every side, flooded the earth with water. That fierce conflagration... was still quenched by those clouds in a trice.'

statements.claim: The Somakas urged Arjuna to pierce Karna and cut off his head; the Kauravas urged Karna to slay Arjuna and send the sons of Pritha to the woods forever
statements.evidence: MBh 8.89: 'The Somakas then loudly shouted to Partha... pierce Karna. Cut off his head...' and Karna's side: 'slay Arjuna with keen shafts. Let the sons of Pritha once more go to the woods forever.'

statements.claim: Krishna rebuked Arjuna for letting Karna crush his weapons and offered him the razor-edged Sudarsana to strike off Karna's head, like Sakra slaying Namuci with the thunderbolt
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt from MBh 8.89: 'Then Vasudeva, beholding Partha's shafts baffled by Karna, said... What is this, O diadem-decked Arjuna, that Karna should succeed in crushing thy weapons today... strike off the head of that foe of thine with this Sudarsana, of edge keen as a razor, that I give unto thee, like Sakra striking off the head of his foe Namuci, with the thunderbolt.'

DKS_0482.notes: Story mirrors MBh 8.89 closely; pack passage truncates after the varunastra quench, but the Sudarsana offer is verbatim in the pack excerpt. Closing line is narrative pause, not a factual claim.

statements.claim: The broken Kaurava divisions fled before Arjuna's arrows and watched from a distance his weapon careering with the effulgence of lightning
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'Flying away in consequence of the falling of Arjuna's arrows, the broken divisions of the Kauravas, staying at a distance, continued to gaze at Arjuna's weapon... careering around with the effulgence of lightning.'

statements.claim: Karna crushed Arjuna's burning weapon with his foe-killing weapon received from Rama, resembling an Atharvan rite
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'the Suta's son now crushed [that weapon] with his shafts winged with gold... destroyed that burning weapon of Arjuna with his own foe-killing weapon of great power which he had obtained from Rama, and which resembled (in efficacy) an Atharvan rite.'

statements.claim: Scorched and mangled, unable to prevail, Karna reached for a single shaft that lay alone in his quiver, and did not know that the snake Aswasena had entered it
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'When at last Karna found that he could not prevail over Partha... set his heart upon that shaft of his which lay singly within a quiver.' Full text of same section: 'The Suta's son did not know that the snake Aswasena had entered his arrow by the aid of his Yoga powers.'

statements.claim: Aswasena, whose mother Arjuna slew at Khandava, had hidden in the nether region and now rose, took arrow form and entered Karna's quiver
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'the snake Aswasena, who was hostile to Arjuna, was passing his time in the nether region... recollecting the death of his mother... he quickly entered into Karna's quiver... in the form of an arrow.'

statements.claim: The shaft was snake-mouthed, blazing, polished according to rule, long kept for Partha's destruction, in a golden quiver amid sandal dust; Karna aimed it at Phalguna's head
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'that foe-killing, exceedingly keen, snake-mouthed, blazing, and fierce shaft... long kept for the sake of Partha's destruction... within a golden quiver amid sandal dust... aimed it at Partha... for cutting off Phalguna's head in battle.'

statements.claim: When the snake-arrow was fixed on the string, the Regents of the world including Sakra set up loud wails
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'When that snake of the form of an arrow was fixed on the bow-string, the Regents of the world, including Sakra, set up loud wails.'

statements.claim: Fatigued, the two heroes were fanned by apsaras with palm-leaf fans sprinkled with sandal-water while Sakra and Surya brushed their faces
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90: 'those two heroes, fatigued with their exertions in battle, looked at each other. Both of them were then fanned with excellent and waving fans made of young (palm) leaves... by many Apsaras... And Sakra and Surya, using their hands, gently brushed the faces of those two heroes.'

statements.claim: The chariot stood sunk in the earth, where Krishna had pressed it down in the moment the arrow flew
statements.evidence: Full text of MBh 8.90 (same source chapter; pack passage truncated just before this scene): 'Madhava, with great speed... pressed down with his feet that excellent car, causing it to sink about a cubit deep.' Pack excerpt confirms the car was in the earth and Krishna raised it afterwards.

statements.claim: Krishna explained to Arjuna the snake's Khandava origin and told him to slay it; Arjuna cut the snake down
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90 pack excerpt: 'Whilst thou, armed with bow, wert engaged at Khandava in gratifying the god Agni, this snake was then in the sky, his body ensconced within his mother's... Remembering that act of hostility done by thee, he cometh towards thee today for thy destruction.' Full text: Krishna said 'Slay that great snake inimical to thee' and 'Jishnu... cut off, with six keen shafts, that snake in the welkin.'

statements.claim: After the snake was cut off, Krishna himself raised the car from the earth with his arms
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90 pack excerpt: 'After that snake had been cut off by Arjuna, the lord Keshava himself... raised up with his arms that car from the earth.'

statements.claim: Karna was left wounded and failing and the duel was not over
statements.evidence: MBh 8.90 continues with the duel: after raising the car, Karna pierced Krishna with ten shafts and the exchange resumed; corpus chain next story: 'Krishna Urges Arjuna to Slay the Distressed Karna.'

DKS_0484.notes: Pack passage is truncated mid-chapter (ends at the Regents' wails); the chariot-pressing and slaying details were verified against the full Ganguli text of the same section 8.90, which the pack cites. Story omits the diadem-striking episode but asserts nothing contradicting it.

statements.claim: News of the war of the Kurus and Pandavas and the slaughter of the warrior kings reached Balarama from the mouths of brahmins, and he deemed the earth's burden lifted
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.21-22 (pack): 'Hearing of the battle of the Kurus and Pandavas and the slaughter of the warrior kings, Balarama, deeming the earth's burden lifted, goes to the field where Bhima and Duryodhana are fighting with maces.' Sanskrit v.21: 'srutva dvijaih kathyamanam kuru-pandava-samyuge.'

statements.claim: Balarama went to Kurukshetra where Bhima and Duryodhana were locked in their mace-duel, to stop it
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.22-23: Balarama goes to where Bhima and Duryodhana fight with maces; Vedabase 10.79.23: 'Wanting to stop the club fight then raging... Lord Balarama went to Kurukshetra.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, the twins, Krishna and Arjuna went to greet Balarama when they saw him coming
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.23 (Sanskrit): 'yudhisthiras tu tam drstva yamau krsnariunav api.'

statements.claim: Balarama told the two equal champions - addressing the king and Vrikodara - that neither could win and bade them desist
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.25-26: 'yuvaam tulya-balau virau he rajan he vrikodara / tasmad ekatarasyeha yuvayoh sama-viryayoh'; pack excerpt: 'He tells the equal champions that neither can win and to desist.'

statements.claim: The two, bound by enmity and remembering mutual insults, did not heed his words
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.27: 'na tad-vakyam jagrihatur baddha-vairau nrparthavat'; pack excerpt: 'the two, bound by enmity and remembering mutual insults, do not heed his words.'

statements.claim: Accepting it as destiny, unable to part them, Balarama turned away and returned to Dwaraka
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.28: 'distam tad anumanvano ramo dvaravatim yayau' ('accepting that as destiny, Rama went to Dvaravati'); pack excerpt: 'Balarama, accepting it as destiny, returns to Dwaraka.'

statements.claim: He came from Dwaraka (as his point of departure for Kurukshetra)
statements.evidence: No support in the pack; SB 10.79.1-22 places Balarama on a pilgrimage tour of holy places (from Naimisharanya through southern India to Prabhasa) when he heard the brahmins' news and went to Kurukshetra; the text has him return TO Dvaraka after the duel (v.28), not set out from it.
statements.resolution: Corrected in story text via consolidation pass.

corrections.original_sentence: He came from Dwaraka, and as he rode, the news was still turning in his mind — the war done, the kings fallen, and two champions yet beating each other to death.
corrections.suggested: He had been journeying through the holy places when the news reached him, and as he rode, the news was still turning in his mind — the war done, the kings fallen, and two champions yet beating each other to death.

DKS_0486.notes: One unsupported detail: the story has Balarama set out from Dwaraka, but SB 10.79 (the pack's source) has him hear the news mid-pilgrimage and go to Kurukshetra from there, returning to Dvaravati afterwards. Rest of the story tracks the pack closely.

statements.claim: Freed from the brahma weapon of Ashvatthama, Kunti addressed Krishna as he turned to depart
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.16-17 (pack): 'Freed from the brahma weapon, Kunti addressed Krishna as he turned to depart.' Sanskrit v.16: 'brahma-tejo-vinirmuktair atmajaih saha krsnaya.'

statements.claim: She bowed to the primal Person, veiled by his own play, unknowable to the ignorant, imperishable, the goal of the pure-hearted sages
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.18-19: 'mayajavanikacchannam ajnadhyaksajam avyayam / ... paramahamsanam muninam amalatmanam.'

statements.claim: She bowed to Krishna son of Vasudeva and Devaki, lotus-navelled, garlanded with lotuses
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.20: 'krsnaya vasudevaya devaki-nandanaya ca / namah pankajanabhaya namah pankajamaline.'

statements.claim: She remembered Devaki shut up for a very long time in Kamsa's prison, given over to sorrow
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.22: 'yatha hrsikesa khalena devaki kamsena ruddhaticiram sucarpita.'

statements.claim: She recalled that he freed her and her children again and again from poison, the great fire, the cruel assembly of the dice hall, the hardships of forest exile and the weapons of mighty warriors
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.23 and pack summary: 'from poison, from the great fire, from the cruel assembly, from the hardships of forest exile, from the weapons of great chariot-warriors'; v.23: 'visan mahagneh purusadadarsanad asatsabhaya vanavasakrcchratah.'

statements.claim: 'May those dangers remain with me forever, teacher of the world, for it was in danger that I saw you' - a man puffed up by birth, wealth, learning and beauty does not see him
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.24-25: 'vipadah santu tah sasvat tatra tatra jagad-guro' and 'janmaisvarya-sruta-sribhir edhamana-madah puman.'

statements.claim: She called him the wealth of those who own nothing, beyond the world's moods, and considered him Time itself, lord without beginning and end; no one can read his intention as he moves in the guise of a man
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.26-28: 'namo 'kincana-vittaya nivrtta-guna-vrttaye / manye tvam kalam isanam anadi-nidhanam vibhum / na veda kascid bhagavams cikirsitam tavehamanasya nrinam vidambanam.'

statements.claim: Even the rope with which a gopi of Vrindavan bound him as a child, eyes blurred with tears and running collyrium, was his play
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.30: 'gopy adade tvayi krtagasi dama tavad ya te dasasru-kalilanjana-sambhramaksam.'

statements.claim: Some said the unborn one was born to give glory to the virtuous, others that Vasudeva prayed for him to come to Devaki, others that he came to lift the earth's burden like a boat on the ocean
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.31-33: 'kecid ahur ajam jatam punya-slokasya kirtaye / apare vasudevasya devakyam yacito 'bhyagat / bharavatarayanvanye bhuvo nava ivodadhau.'

statements.claim: 'Will you abandon us today...? What are we, Pandavas and Yadavas alike, without you, but name and form? This land will not shine as it shines now, bearer of the mace' - she named him Shri Krishna, friend of Arjuna, bull of the Vrishnis, of unending valor
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.36-38, 42: 'apy adya nas tvam... jihasasi svit suhrdo 'nujivinah / ke vayam nama-rupabhyam yadubhih saha pandavah / neyam sobhisyate tatra yathedanim gadadhara' and 'srikrsna krsna-sakha vrsny-rsabhavani-dhrug rajanya-vamsa-dahananapavarga-virya.'

statements.claim: She asked only that her mind be fixed on him alone, lord of Madhu, again and again
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.40-41: 'tvayi me 'nanya-visaya matir madhu-pate 'sakrt.'

statements.claim: Krishna, whose every glory she had praised, smiled gently and answered 'So be it', then turned back toward the city
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.44: 'tam badham ity upamantrya pravisya gajasahvayam' ('assuring her, 'So be it,' he entered Hastinapura'); pack excerpt: 'And the Lord, whose every glory she had praised, smiled gently.'

DKS_0487.notes: The hymn's content maps verse-by-verse onto SB 1.8.16-44. The departure frame ('as Krishna prepares to leave Hastinapura for Dwaraka') matches the pack summary; Krishna re-entering the city at the close matches SB 1.8.44 and sets up the next story (SB 1.10 departure).

statements.claim: Krishna stayed in Hastinapura several months after the war, to gladden his friends and comfort his sister
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.6-7 (pack excerpt): 'Having stayed in Hastinapura some months to gladden his friends and please his sister, Hari took his leave, embraced and bowed to all, and mounted his chariot.'

statements.claim: Subhadra, Draupadi, Kunti, Gandhari and Dhritarashtra could not bear the separation, their eyes fixed on him as he departed
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.8, 12 (pack): 'Subhadra, Draupadi, Kunti, Gandhari, Dhritarashtra and the others could not bear the separation, their eyes fixed on him as he departed'; v.12: 'sarve te 'nimesair aksais tam anu druta-cetasah.'

statements.claim: The wise who have tasted true company cannot give it up; the Pandavas, whose minds were fixed on Krishna, could not endure his absence
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.10-11: 'satsangan mukta-duhsango hatum notsahate budhah / tasmin nyasta-dhiyah parthah saheran viraham katham.'

statements.claim: Tears rose in their eyes and were held back from longing for Devaki's son
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.13: 'nyarundhann udgalad-baspam autkanthyad devaki-sute.'

statements.claim: Mridangas, conches, bheris and vinas sounded; Kuru women climbed to the palace roofs to see him
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.14-15: 'mrdanga-sankha-bheryas ca vina-panava-gomukhah' and 'prasada-sikhararudhah kuru-naryo didrksaya.'

statements.claim: A white umbrella adorned with pearl garlands was held over him, Uddhava and Satyaki waved chauris, and brahmins' blessings were heard along the way
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.16-18: 'sitatapatram jagraha mukta-dama-vibhusitam / uddhavah satyakis caiva vijane paramadbhute / asruyantasisah satyas tatra tatra dvijeritah.'

statements.claim: The people spoke of him as the ancient Person who alone existed before all distinctions, who sets creation turning, whose feet sages seek, whose deeds are sung in the hidden Vedas, who descends when kings grow unrighteous
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.20-24: 'sa vai kilayam purusah puratano ya eka asid avisesa atmani... sa vayam yat padam atra surayo jitendriya... vedeSu guhyesu ca guhya-vadibhih... yada hy adharmena tamo-dhiyo nrpa jivanti tatraisa hi sattvatah kila.'

statements.claim: The women praised the clan of Yadu, the forest of Madhu, and Kushasthali which dims heaven's glory; the women won by valor at the svayamvara after defeating the fierce Chedi king make womanhood glorious
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.25-29: 'aho alam slaghya-tamam yadoh kulam... madhor vanam... kusasthali punya-yasaskari bhuva... ya virya-sulkena hrtah svayamvare pramathya caidya-pramukhan hi susminah... etah param stritvam... sadhu kurvate.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira rode with him part of the way to protect the army and escort; at the edge of the city the Kurus stood at a distance, tormented by separation
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.31-32: 'ajata-satruh prtanam gopithaya madhu-dvisah / atha duragatan saurih kauravan virahaturan.'

statements.claim: He travelled through Kuru-jangala, Panchala, Shurasena, the lands along the Yamuna, across the Maru desert, through the far reaches of Sauvira and Abhira, honored at every kingdom he crossed
statements.evidence: SB 1.10.33-35: 'kuru-jangala-pancalan surasenan sa-yamunan / maru-dhanvam atikramya sauvirabhira-yoh paran / tatra tatra ha tatratyair harih pratyudyat-arhanah.'

DKS_0488.notes: Rendering of SB 1.10.6-35 is close and verse-faithful. Minor details (city children running beside the wheels; 'dead of two houses') are connective color that the source neither asserts nor contradicts.

statements.claim: Crossing into his own prosperous realm of Anarta, Krishna blew his conch, white-bellied and reddened by his lips, and the sound removes the fear of the world
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.1-2 and pack summary: 'Approaching his own prosperous land of Anarta, Krishna blew his conch to dispel his people's sorrow'; v.1-2: 'sa uccakase dhavalodaro daro 'py urukramasyadhara-sona-sonimah' and 'tam upasrutya ninadam jagad-bhaya-bhayavaham.'

statements.claim: Hearing it, the citizens rushed out to see their lord, faces blooming with joy, voices choked with delight
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.3-4: 'tatropanita-balayo raver dipam ivadrtah / prity-utphulla-mukhah procur harsa-gadgadaya gira.'

statements.claim: 'We bow to your lotus feet, worshipped by Brahma, Shiva and the kings of the gods... you alone are our mother, our friend, our husband, our father'
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.5-6: 'natah sma te natha sadanghri-pankajam virinca-vairincya-surendra-vanditam / bhavaya nas tvam bhava visva-bhavana tvam eva mata tha suhrt-pati-pita.'

statements.claim: 'When you went away to the Kurus or the Madhus to see your friends, how could we live... your glance dries up every sorrow'
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.8-9: 'yarhy ambujaksa apasasara bho bhavan kurun madhun vatha suhrd-didrksaya / katham vayam natha cirosite tvayi prasanna-drstya-khila-tapa-sosanam.'

statements.claim: Krishna, tender to his devotees, heard them all
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.10: 'iti codirita vacah prajanam bhaktavatsalah.'

statements.claim: The city was decked with arches at gates and along the roads, avenues swept, lanes, markets and squares freshened; at every door were pots of curds, unbroken rice, fruits and sugarcane
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.12-15: 'gopura-dvara-margesu krta-kautuka-toranam / sammarjita-mahamarga rathya-pana-katvaram / dvari dvari grhanam ca dadhy-aksata-phaleksubhih.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva, Akrura, Ugrasena, Balarama, and Pradyumna, Charudeshna and Samba (Jambavati's son) came out to meet him
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.16-17 and pack excerpt: 'Vasudeva, Akrura, Ugrasena and the wondrous Rama, with Pradyumna and others, came forth on chariots to meet him'; v.17: 'pradyumnas carudesnas ca sambo jambavati-sutah.'

statements.claim: The foremost elephant led the procession, brahmins chanted blessings, hundreds of courtesans rode out in vehicles, and actors, dancers, bards and panegyrists filled the road
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.18-20: 'varnendram puraskrtya brahmanaih sa-sumangalaih / varamukhayas ca sataso yanair tad-darsanotsukah / nata-nartaka-gandharvah suta-magadha-vandinah.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered the bows, embraces, hand-touches, smiles and glances of relatives and citizens, and himself honored the elders, brahmins with wives and the aged
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.21-23: 'bhagavan... prahva-bhivadana-slesa-kara-sparsa-smiteksanaih / svayam ca gurubhir vipraih sa-daraih sthavirair api.'

statements.claim: The noble women of Dwaraka watched from the terraces along the royal road; his chest was the home of fortune, his face the drinking vessel of their eyes
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.24-26: 'raja-margam gate krsne dvarakayah kula-striyah / sriyo nivaso yasyorah pana-patram mukham drsam.'

statements.claim: He passed beneath the white umbrella and waving fans, showered with flowers, to his father's house, where his mothers led by Devaki lifted him onto their laps
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.27-29: 'sitatapatra-vyajanair upaskrtah prasuna-varsair abhivarsitah pathi / pravisyas tu grham pitroh parisvaktah sva-matrbhih / tah putram ankam aropya sneha-snuta-payodharah.'

statements.claim: Then he entered his own palace fulfilling every desire; his wives, seeing their husband home after his long absence, embraced him with their children, and even to those who saw him constantly his two feet were always new
statements.evidence: SB 1.11.30-33: 'athavisat sva-bhavanam sarva-kamam anuttamam / patnyah patim prosya grhan-upagatam vilokya sanjata-mano-mahotsavah / ... yady apy asau parsva-gato raho-gatas tathapi tasyanghri-yugam navam navam.'

DKS_0489.notes: Very close rendering of SB 1.11.1-33. Only loose spots are devotional paraphrase ('mother, friend, husband, father' list matches v.6) and generic crowd color ('rose and ran', joy 'like a tide'), which the passage supports in substance.

statements.claim: Arjuna came to Dwaraka, found the bodies of Krishna and Balarama and performed the obsequial rites for them and the rest of the slain
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (Wilson, pack): 'ARJUNA having found the bodies of Krishna and of Rama, performed for them, and the rest of the slain, the obsequial rites.'

statements.claim: The eight queens of Krishna, Rukmini at their head, embraced his body and entered the funeral fire; Revati, embracing Rama's corpse, entered the blazing pile, which was cool to her
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The eight queens of Krishna... with Rukmini at their head, embraced the body of Hari, and entered the funeral fire. Revati also, embracing the corpse of Rama, entered the blazing pile, which was cool to her, happy in contact with her lord.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena and Vasudeva, with Devaki and Rohini, hearing this, committed themselves to the flames, and Arjuna performed their rites too
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Hearing these events, Ugrasena and Anakadundubhi, with Devaki and Rohini, committed themselves to the flames. The last ceremonies were performed for all these by Arjuna.'

statements.claim: Arjuna took Vajra and led the thousands of Krishna's wives and all the people from Dwaraka with tenderness and care
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The son of Kunti conducted the thousands of the wives of Krishna, with Vajra, and all the people, from Dwaraka, with tenderness and care, and travelled slowly away.'

statements.claim: The Sudharman palace and the Parijata tree, brought down to earth by Krishna, went back to heaven; on the day Hari left the earth the dark Kali age descended
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The Sudharman palace and the Parijata tree, which had been brought to earth by Krishna, both proceeded to heaven; and on the same day that Hari departed from the earth the powerful dark-bodied Kali age descended.'

statements.claim: The ocean rose and submerged Dwaraka except one temple of the Yadu deity, never washed away, where Kesava abides and visitors are freed from sins
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'The ocean rose, and submerged the whole of Dwaraka, except alone the dwelling of the deity of the race of Yadu... there Kesava constantly abides... Whoever visits that holy shrine... is liberated from all his sins.'

statements.claim: Arjuna halted the people in the Panchanada country, a rich and fertile spot, and robbers gathered the lawless Abhiras against the single warrior guarding widowed women and great riches
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Arjuna halted the people... in the Panchanada country, in a rich and fertile spot; but the desires of the robbers... were excited, when they observed so many widowed females... in the possession of Arjuna alone. Inflamed by their cupidity, they assembled the villainous Abhiras.'

statements.claim: The robbers mocked Arjuna as rich and proud of slaying Bhishma, Drona and Karna, ignorant of villagers' prowess, and rushed on the people with cudgels and clods of earth
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Here is this Arjuna, immensely rich... His pride is raised by the death of Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha, Karna, and others... he does not know the prowess of simple villagers. Up, up; take your long thick staves... they rushed, armed with cudgels and clods of earth, upon the people.'

statements.claim: Arjuna told them to retire unless they wished to die; they ignored him and seized the treasure and the women
statements.evidence: VP 5.38 (pack): 'Arjuna encountered them, and said to them in derision, Retire, wretches, ignorant of what is right, unless ye are desirous of dying. But they disregarded his menaces, and seized his treasures and his women.'
